title: [Performance] Fuse GLM-5.3-Flash KDA decode output writeback
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

For ordinary decode-only GLM-5.3-Flash KDA batches, combine recurrent-output padding masking, destination zeroing and the final copy into one Triton writeback kernel. The native recurrent operator still computes its usual temporary output and state. Mixed prefill/decode and speculative paths retain their existing behavior.

DP validation exposed two issues in the initial implementation. Fully masked blocks beyond the source allocation could fault on Ascend; the kernel now skips these loads, including the empty-source case. Varying request counts and DP padding lengths also caused repeated compilations; these dimensions are now non-specialized runtime scalars. Tiles are limited to 16KB (8192 FP16/BF16 or 4096 FP32 elements) to amortize bounds checks without exceeding FP32 local-memory limits.

The Triton kernel and its Python entry point live together in `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/kda/output_writeback.py`; the model imports `write_recurrent_output` from this operator module.

The [output_writeback.md operator document](https://github.com/lijiahang226/vllm-ascend/blob/0d472b0421a170635f0fc425d5ab2865cb740a7e/vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/output_writeback.md) follows the repository Triton template and describes the formula, parameter/layout contract, padding behavior, graph replay constraints, hardware validation scope and existing test entry point.

Refs #15665.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Reduces decode writeback and dynamic-shape compilation overhead without changing recurrent arithmetic or adding a configuration option.

The current optimized implementation completed a focused TP4 × DP2 / EP8 comparison: input 3500/output 256, global concurrency 8 and 64. At concurrency 8, mean TPOT decreased **2.95%–5.23%** relative to the two baselines; every candidate round was faster than every accepted baseline round. At concurrency 64, the mean difference was **0.14%–0.96%**, within observed variation, so no stable high-concurrency benefit is claimed.

### How was this patch tested?

- **Relocation validation:** The recurrent output writeback operator was relocated intact to vllm_ascend/ops/triton/kda/output_writeback.py; after line-ending normalization, its bytes match the previous module exactly (SHA256 b0052b9a0965156bf90ca94a0cc3c78d8d702397a1169cf8f666c554260c5110). The caller and existing nine NPU cases change only their import path, and no obsolete output_writeback import remains in this branch. The current test file LF-normalized SHA256 is abafbd9a4493413ccfb241b68583bacc25b810faec95ce67500779ecf0821b38. Changed-file Ruff check, Ruff format --check, and git diff --check passed after correcting import order and mixed line endings. Post-relocation NPU tests and local CPU UT were not run: node 167 reset three authorized SSH sessions before remote command execution, and the local environment lacks torch_npu and vllm. Previously reported nine-case NPU results predate this relocation and are historical evidence only; current-head Linux CI is reported separately below.

- **Committed operator coverage:** following the existing Triton single-card pattern (for example `test_precopy.py`, #15032), add only `tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_glm5next_output_writeback.py`: **before this relocation, 9 real-NPU cases passed on node 167, Ascend A3, in 36.43 seconds**. The 70-line file compares against a CPU PyTorch reference with zero tolerance: FP16/BF16/FP32 valid-row copies and padding zeros, empty source/output, single-token decode, unaligned destination guards, and the allocation-end 63-to-1771-token DP regression with graph replay after updating input values and query ends. NaNs poison invalid rows and destinations. This is a compact operator suite, not the previous 129-case matrix. No new PR tests, CI runtime registration, or UT were added. The existing 18 CPU contract/dispatch cases remain unchanged from their passing run. The current automatic PR selector does not collect this nightly directory; the NPU result is an explicit hardware run, not a claimed PR CI gate. It used the existing operator conftest and `--confcutdir` at the ops directory, with the then-current test-file hash and production operator hash recorded. The relocation changes the test import path; that historical run is not a new-path NPU execution.
- Validated implementation `a06119e4f93debd21caf08b9fbc180d3feaa9be5`: **142 NPU cases and 21 CPU contract/dispatch tests passed** on node 167, Ascend A3 (163 total, 101.63 seconds). Production/test SHA256 match the committed files. Covers FP16/BF16/FP32, empty/ragged shapes, storage guards, allocation-end large padding, changing query counts and graph replay. All output comparisons are exact. This is a historical broader shape sweep; current committed coverage is the compact suite above.
- Fresh-cache dynamic-length comparison: eight combinations of source length, destination length and query count produced **8 kernel variants before versus 1 after**. Their cumulative first-call time was **28.515 seconds versus 4.432 seconds**, with exact outputs. This measures compilation plus first execution, not end-to-end model throughput.
- Warm microbenchmark: seven alternating-order samples, each graph containing 128 writes, across 16/32/64 heads. At 63 source → 1771 destination tokens, median graph time fell **130.58→33.96 / 260.72→66.64 / 519.99→131.51 microseconds**, respectively. Single-token graph time remained approximately 2.3 microseconds. Host eager dispatch can add about 1 microsecond for small cases; the completed DP comparison below shows a low-concurrency benefit but no clear high-concurrency benefit.
- An earlier runtime-scalar/1024-element draft removed recompilation but slowed large writes, so it was rejected. An unconditional 8192-element tile failed FP32 compilation because of local-memory limits; the final dtype-sized tile passed the complete suite. Failure evidence and tuning measurements are retained.
- Allocation-end reproduction of the former DP failure (63 source → 1771 destination, 16 heads) faulted before the safety guard and passed with it. Previous head `c2b15544` also completed TP4×DP2/EP8, input/output 256, concurrency 128: two warmups plus three compilation-free rounds (768 measured requests), no device fault and zero preemptions. Its next concurrency-256 sweep exposed the recompilation problem; that matrix was intentionally interrupted to prioritize this fix, with all results preserved.
- The focused TP4 x DP2 / EP8 campaign is complete: input 3500 / output 256, global concurrency 8 and 64, two full-output warmups and three accepted rounds per cell. Temperature 0, seed 1024; FULL_DECODE_ONLY plus breakable graphs, captures 1/2/4/8/16/32/64/128, max batched tokens 2048. Prefill is not fully captured. All eight workers used the intended source hashes, the same #17109 host fix, 791 cache blocks and a common frozen cache seed. All 432 accepted fixed-output requests in each arm matched the first baseline token-for-token; both engines recorded zero preemptions. All 200 sampled ownership records across four arms (including the original before-baseline performance run) had no external occupants. The original six before-baseline performance rounds were reused after the Docker working-directory client-launch failure; they were not rerun or reported as new measurements.

| Global concurrency | Before / candidate / after TPOT (ms) | Reduction vs before / after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | 55.4755 / 52.5740 / 54.1705 | 5.23% / 2.95% |
| 64 | 196.6617 / 196.3902 / 198.3028 | 0.14% / 0.96% |

At concurrency 8 all three candidate rounds (52.4806/52.6318/52.6097 ms) were below all six accepted baseline rounds (minimum 53.3453 ms), supporting a benefit for this measured configuration. The baseline means drifted by -2.35%, so the headline reduction is a range rather than a single universal percentage. At concurrency 64, candidate rounds were 192.5977/202.3217/194.2513 ms; the slower round remains included. The 0.14%-0.96% mean difference is small relative to the candidate variance and +0.83% baseline drift; no stable high-concurrency benefit is claimed.

- Full GSM8K: **1259 / 1266 / 1266 out of 1319** (before / candidate / after), zero request errors. The unchanged baselines differ on 21 question grades. The candidate is wrong on 6 questions correct in both baselines and correct on 5 wrong in both. These are genuine numeric-answer differences, not format-only failures; equal aggregate scores do not establish per-question equivalence or attribute all differences to scheduling. Raw answers/grades are preserved.
- All accepted rounds had no changed Triton cache metadata. One separate candidate attempt with new metadata was excluded under the declared rule. No slow accepted round was removed. TP2 x DP4 / EP8 and TP1 x DP8 / EP8 are not claimed complete for this head. The independent conv DP16 result is not evidence for this candidate.
- Earlier TP8 accuracy audit: fixed-cohort runs of two baselines and the original candidate all scored 1254/1319 with identical final numeric answers/grades. Normal-concurrency repetitions varied; these historical runs do not establish latest-head DP accuracy equivalence. An earlier real-native KDA audit also matched outputs/state in 100/100 cases and all 65,280 finite BF16 encodings.
- **Current source:** `0d472b0421a170635f0fc425d5ab2865cb740a7e`, based on main `972fcd5c974d55a7970ebe630329daa4b4049c49`. This follow-up only clarifies in the operator document that `write_recurrent_output` is the stable public ABI and the kernel/tile/grid policy are implementation details. Product code and tests are unchanged from `f5668dfbb8cf3b8ae9dec418d59c33a3d3fdb5c4`. No new UT/nightly cases, runtime behavior, or hardware validation claims are introduced.
- **Current-head CI:** At current head 0d472b0421a170635f0fc425d5ab2865cb740a7e, [pre-commit](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35845953660/job/107132347253) succeeded. Its complete job log shows all 18 pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff and markdownlint, and mypy succeeded for vllm_ascend, examples, and tests on Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12 (nine successful checks). The main merge-conflict check, PR create action, and DCO succeeded; [CPU UT](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35845953660/job/107133755650) was in progress in the final snapshot. No failed or skipped check was reported in that snapshot, and no device test result was yet reported. GitHub marked the PR mergeable but BLOCKED while checks remained outstanding.

Baseline: vllm-ascend `9ad52992c9682f4f640048eb0753f5626e475d50`, vLLM `84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c`.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [Performance] Optimize GLM-5.3-Flash convolution state copies
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Reduce GLM-5.3-Flash conv-state copy cost by computing the source/destination addresses in the existing Triton copy kernels. The bounded grid covers each sequence's actual state elements without launching over the full padded physical page. The model's conv-state layout, state values, and cache capacity are unchanged.

The model calls the tensor-level `copy_conv_state(...)` API in `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/kda/conv_state.py`. That module owns shape/stride derivation, block size, grid policy and the private Triton launch. The model retains temporary-state allocation and the ordered pack/convolution/writeback flow.

The [conv_state.md operator document](https://github.com/lijiahang226/vllm-ascend/blob/f97fe949540e54c5e5eeb4705803489cfa1d4158/vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/conv_state.md) follows the repository Triton template and describes the formula, parameter/layout contract, padding behavior, graph replay constraints, hardware validation scope and existing test entry point.

Refs #15665.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Improves conv-state copy latency without a new configuration or checkpoint conversion. The optimized implementation at `1ab020889e593ae67e9f9cc9d5a7ba674a346840` completed the requested compact TP1 × DP16 / EP16 long-input comparison on Ascend A3.

| Input / output tokens | Global concurrency | Before / conv / after TPOT (ms) | TPOT reduction vs before / after | Output throughput improvement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 32768 / 1024 | 16 | 56.850 / 49.664 / 56.745 | 12.64% / 12.48% | 10.70%–10.76% |
| 65536 / 4096 | 16 | 56.796 / 49.626 / 56.829 | 12.62% / 12.67% | 12.55%–12.61% |
| 65536 / 1024 | 64 | 179.196 / 149.039 / 179.229 | 16.83% / 16.84% | 15.09%–15.30% |

Before baseline and candidate have three accepted rounds per case. The after baseline has one accepted round per case under the predeclared adaptive rule: add two more if drift exceeds 3%, the candidate's margin is under 3%, or preemption occurs. None triggered after excluding compilation-affected rounds. The after-baseline sample is consequently weaker than a full three-round comparison. Baseline TPOT drift was -0.185%, +0.057%, and +0.019%; every candidate round was faster than every accepted baseline round in its case. These are observed improvements, not confidence intervals, and are not additive with independent PRs.

### How was this patch tested?

- **Launch ABI validation:** The conv-state kernel AST is identical to the previous head after its private rename. A local host-only fake-launcher contract check covered state-row-major and channel-major cache layouts, strided indices, a page stride above 2^31, the 65,535-program grid cap, both write_back values, and an empty request batch; every nonempty launch preserved the previous grid, tensor/scalar argument order, and compile-time options. The model still allocates the same temporary tensors only for noncontiguous states and calls the same AscendC operator between pack and writeback, with no new synchronization or dynamic cache. Changed Python files pass Ruff check/format and git diff --check. Both worktrees attempted format.sh ci once, but Git Bash could not find pre-commit; the local environment also lacks torch_npu, vllm, and triton, so no CPU integration test was run. The one node-167 preflight connection reset before remote command execution, so neither device availability nor NPU correctness was validated in this round.

- **Committed test scope:** only the two existing `test_glm5next_conv_state.py` layout cases remain. They now call the public `copy_conv_state` API; their inputs, assertions and case count are unchanged, and they no longer duplicate kernel arguments or a launch-grid formula. No UT/nightly cases or CI routes are added. The earlier broad A3 shape sweep is historical validation, not a hardware rerun of this API follow-up.
- **DP16 long-input performance:** physical devices 0–15 on node 167; same W8A8 checkpoint, vLLM `84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c`, model runner v1, FULL_DECODE_ONLY with breakable capture sizes 1/2/4/8/16, max batched tokens 2048, temperature 0, seed 1024. Async scheduling, prefix caching, and MTP were disabled. Prefill was not claimed to run wholly in a graph. Each measured round submitted twice the global concurrency with fixed output length. Prior full-length baseline warmups were reused; candidate/after used a 32-token warmup and excluded rounds with new compilation. One candidate and one after-baseline round were excluded and retained as evidence.
- **Capacity and ownership:** all 16 workers in all three arms had matching source provenance, the same loaded KDA host library, and 166 cache blocks. Accepted measurements had zero preemption and no foreign-device occupancy. Candidate TTFT and p95/p99 TPOT were also lower in all three cases. The test controller and its three model services have exited.
- **Fixed long-output token checks:** all 576 candidate sequences across nine accepted rounds matched the corresponding before-baseline token sequences exactly, including every token of 4096-token outputs. All 192 paired after-baseline sequences also matched. This tests those fixed prompts, not universal generation identity.
- **Long-context accuracy:** 32/32 numerical answers for all three arms. Original strict `ANSWER:` formatting scores remain 27/32, 28/32, and 27/32; the other answers were correct bare numbers. The numerical audit is separate from, and does not overwrite, the strict scoring.
- **Full GSM8K:** all 1319 questions at global concurrency 64, temperature 0, seed 1024: before **1260/1319**, candidate **1263/1319**, after **1262/1319**, with zero request errors. Before versus candidate had 8 correct-to-incorrect and 11 incorrect-to-correct answers; the two baselines themselves had 9 and 11. After versus candidate had 11 and 12. Six candidate errors were correct in both baselines. There is no observed aggregate accuracy regression; individual generations differ, so this is not a claim of universal numerical equivalence or improved accuracy.
- **Copy correctness:** 229 NPU shape cases passed. In the previously failing mixed batch, 34 layers × 2 steps × 4 TP ranks produced 272 paired comparisons with bitwise-identical copy outputs and complete state storage.
- **Individual kernel timing:** on A3, TP8 / 8 sequences, current bounded-grid implementation: state read **27.92 → 22.01 us**, writeback **218.14 → 21.80 us** per device call. Measured with 128 calls per captured graph and seven alternating-order device-event samples; these are individual kernels, not the whole wrapper or model latency.
- **Shared correctness dependency:** the earlier mixed-batch failure also reproduced on unmodified baseline. Its AscendC KDA workspace overlap is fixed separately in #17109. All three DP16 arms used the same verified fixed host library (`fe38d957bdde50008fef782228cab468c7521ee9fd0afcab0f05ed6544cea0a2`), so its benefit is not attributed to this PR. The captured failure fixture passed 40/40 after that fix and controlled baseline/conv replays both passed 26/26.
- **Current source:** `f97fe949540e54c5e5eeb4705803489cfa1d4158`, based on main `972fcd5c974d55a7970ebe630329daa4b4049c49`. The public tensor ABI now owns launch-parameter derivation, and the model and existing tests no longer launch a raw Triton kernel. Kernel arithmetic, nonempty launch policy, temporary allocations and convolution ordering are preserved; empty request batches return without a launch. No hardware performance or whole-model accuracy result is claimed for this refactor.
- **Current-head CI:** At current head f97fe949540e54c5e5eeb4705803489cfa1d4158, [pre-commit](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35845937840/job/107132257869) succeeded. Its complete job log shows all 18 pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff and markdownlint, and mypy succeeded for vllm_ascend, examples, and tests on Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12 (nine successful checks). The main merge-conflict check, PR create action, and DCO succeeded; [CPU UT](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35845937840/job/107133331938) was in progress in the final snapshot. No failed or skipped check was reported in that snapshot, and no device test result was yet reported. GitHub marked the PR mergeable but BLOCKED while checks remained outstanding.

Scope: this completes the user-approved reduced three-case DP16 comparison. It does not claim completion of the abandoned eight-case matrix, other hardware, or combined-optimization performance.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [CI] Add non-Flash GLM5.x reduced-checkpoint builder and gates (11-layer logits + performance)
body:
Draft PR adding CI gates for the **non-Flash GLM-5.x** reduced checkpoint (11 main
layers plus one retained MTP layer). Three commits:

- `36e93d504` GLM reduced-model nightly gates and prefix parity probes
- `72a3fb0a3` truncated-logits gate: fixed 200 GSM8K samples, all 20,693
  prediction positions, A1 argmax agreement >= 90%
- `313b11baa` 11-layer offline performance gate (this change)

## What is in this PR

- The profile-based reduced-checkpoint builder/preparer under `tools/glm_reduced`
  (`profiles.py`, `reducer.py`, `prepare.py`, `safetensors_io.py`).
- The fixed-position truncated-logits gate (11-layer GLM-5.2 W4A8, 20,693
  positions, A1 argmax agreement >= 90%).
- The offline 11-layer performance gate (this change).

The builder is the provisioning prerequisite for both gates; the three are kept
in one PR on purpose rather than split.

## Scope: non-Flash GLM5.x only

- Both gates target non-Flash GLM5.x DSA checkpoints. The currently registered
  model is `Eco-Tech/GLM-5.2-w4a8` reduced to 11 main layers plus one retained
  MTP layer (MTP disabled in the gate).
- Flash and hybrid/linear-attention models are rejected before any measurement:
  both gates run the shared `validate_model`, which raises
  "Flash models are excluded from this gate" when the model id or the config
  mentions flash, and which requires `model_type == glm_moe_dsa` with every
  `layer_types` entry equal to `deepseek_sparse_attention`.
- The reduction tooling under `tools/glm_reduced` is profile-based and can
  describe other families, but neither gate applies a GLM5.x baseline to another
  family. Other non-Flash GLM5.x models need their own registered baseline, and
  this PR claims nothing about Flash models.

## Performance gate

- Offline single-round runner (no OpenAI server), mirroring the logits gate.
- Compares a fresh run against a pinned, host-scoped baseline; model, hardware
  tag, runner architecture, engine settings, workload shapes and iteration
  counts must match exactly or it fails closed.
- Thresholds: output throughput >= 90% of baseline; TTFT/TPOT/whole-workload
  latency <= 120%. Derived from a three-start A/A calibration, not chosen to let
  a candidate pass.
- CI never writes or bootstraps a baseline; evidence directories are never
  overwritten.

## Calibration

Three independent starts on the lab x86_64 A3 host, one warmup plus three
measured iterations each. Cross-start relative MAD: 4.22% throughput, 10.19%
TTFT, 4.42% TPOT, 4.40% whole-workload latency. The earlier single-launch
baseline was an optimistic outlier (8.7%-13.3% above the three-start median), so
the baseline is now the median of three starts.

## Boundaries

- The baseline is scoped to `linux-x86_64-a3-800i-8-167`; there is no aarch64
  calibration yet, so the nightly registration is left commented out in
  `nightly_config.yaml`. Enabling it on aarch64 would fail closed by design.
- `enforce_eager=True` and MTP disabled: this is a regression baseline, not a
  deployment peak, and it does not extrapolate to the full 78-layer model.
- The 3% relative-MAD stability cap used by the earlier Reduced8 gate is not met
  on this shared host, so the thresholds carry roughly twice the worst observed
  one-sided ratio (0.9578 low-side throughput, 1.1019 high-side latency).
- A confirmation round with the calibrated baseline was not completed: the
  attempt hit resource contention on the shared host. The runner pipeline itself
  was exercised end-to-end once.

## Testing

- 15 CPU gate tests (`tests/ut/tools/glm_reduced/test_perf_gate.py`); ruff check
  and ruff format clean.
- Logits gate: 20 CPU tests, single-round NPU agreement 20,693/20,693, exit 0.
- No GitHub nightly has been run.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [Performance][Revert] Revert prioritizing SAS metadata before QLI (#15949)
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Reverts #15949, squash commit `5b875b36fd8d7fc0768c1f289657ed6fc066bf05` (`[Performance] Prioritize SAS metadata before QLI`).

This removes the SAS-before-QLI prioritization in `vllm_ascend/worker/device_metadata.py` and the `one_card/aclgraph/test_device_metadata.py` e2e coverage added with it.

Conflict-resolution note: `.github/workflows/scripts/estimated_times.yaml` keeps the refreshed timings from later CI commits (e.g. #17230) and only drops the `test_device_metadata.py` entry, since that e2e file is deleted by this revert.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Internal device-metadata task scheduling order returns to the pre-#15949 state.

title: [Performance][Ops] Add FLA NPU backend for GDN prefill on A5
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds an opt-in FLA NPU fused backend for Gated Delta Net (GDN) prefill on Ascend A5.

- Adds a dedicated `ascend_gdn_prefill_backend` additional-config key so the Ascend selector does not conflict with vLLM's upstream-injected `gdn_prefill_backend` key.
- Keeps the existing Ascend GDN prefill behavior when the new option is unset: use the built-in CANN fused operator when available and supported, otherwise fall back to the Triton Ascend implementation.
- Accepts only `fla_npu` as an explicit value. 
- Dynamically loads `fla_npu.ops.ascendc.chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd` from the external `flash-linear-attention-npu` package only when `fla_npu` is configured. This path targets Ascend A5 and currently requires PCP world size 1.
- Documents the configuration contract and default behavior.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Users can opt in to the external FLA NPU backend with:

```bash
vllm serve MODEL --additional-config='{"ascend_gdn_prefill_backend":"fla_npu"}'
```

When `ascend_gdn_prefill_backend` is omitted, existing users keep the automatic CANN-to-Triton fallback behavior. If the option is specified, the only valid value is `fla_npu`.

### How was this patch tested?

Added CPU unit-test coverage for:

- the unset default and preservation of the existing backend path;
- loading the external FLA operator through a fake module, without installing or cloning the external repository in standard CI;
- the missing-dependency error path;
- the external operator's extended return tuple and forwarded kernel arguments;
- recurrent-state scattering when empty sequences are filtered from the kernel batch.

CI results for commit `8e2805715`:

- pre-commit: passed;
- mypy: passed;
- CPU unit tests: passed;
- DCO, PR validation, documentation link checks, and Read the Docs builds: passed.

A real A5 end-to-end numerical and performance validation with a compatible `flash-linear-attention-npu` package is still required before merge. The remaining `ci-gate` check requires a maintainer to add one of the repository's ready labels.

title: [Feature][EC Transfer] Add MemCache-backed L1 encoder cache
body:
[Feature][EC Transfer] Add MemCache-backed L1 encoder cache
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR introduces `ECMemcacheConnector`, a MemCache-backed L1 cache
for multimodal encoder outputs. It integrates with vLLM through the
existing EC connector framework and uses the multimodal feature
identifier (`mm_hash`) as the cache key.

Repeated image or video inputs can reuse previously computed encoder
embeddings instead of running the multimodal encoder again.

- Add a scheduler-side MemCache client that checks multiple `mm_hash`
  values in one request and records cache hits and misses.
- Send per-step load/save metadata from the scheduler to workers:
  cache hits are loaded from MemCache, while misses run the encoder and
  publish the resulting embeddings.
- Load multiple encoder outputs directly into preallocated NPU tensors
  with `batch_get_into`.
- Use `KeyInfo.size()` together with the model dtype and encoder hidden
  dimension to reconstruct each cached tensor as
  `[num_encoder_tokens, hidden_dim]`.
- Publish newly computed encoder outputs directly from NPU memory with
  `put_from`.
- Record an NPU event before dispatching the put operation to a background
  thread, so MemCache waits for encoder computation without blocking the
  model-runner thread.
- Save only from TP rank 0 and PCP rank 0. Encoder outputs are identical
  across TP/PCP ranks, so publishing from every rank would duplicate data
  and cause concurrent writes to the same `mm_hash`.
- Keep eviction management inside MemCache. The connector does not add a
  separate local eviction policy.
- Track cumulative cache hits, misses, and hit rate for debugging and
  observability.

This PR also extends MemcacheBackend with:
- batch_get_into, for copying multiple values into flat destination
  buffers.
- put_from, for publishing one value directly from a device buffer.
- Optional transfer-direction arguments for the existing get and put
  wrappers while preserving their previous default directions.
When the connector is not configured, the existing encoder execution and
cache behavior remain unchanged.

Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?
Yes, when ECMemcacheConnector is explicitly enabled.

The connector can be enabled without modifying vLLM:

```bash
vllm serve <model> \
  --ec-transfer-config '{
    "ec_connector": "ECMemcacheConnector",
    "ec_connector_module_path":
      "vllm_ascend.distributed.ec_transfer.ec_memcache_connector",
    "ec_role": "ec_both"
  }'
```

title: [Performance][MoE] Use bf16 router GEMM with fp32 accumulation for bf16-origin weights
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it

`AscendGateLinear` (PR #9617) forces fp32 weights and fp32 computation for the MoE router gate, because the previous `bf16×bf16→bf16` path (bf16 accumulation, no fp32 output) caused expert-selection errors in agent workloads on NPU.

However, the fp32 path (`aclnnMatmulV2`) is ~6x slower than necessary for bf16-origin weights — the common case for models like Kimi K3, whose gate weights are stored as bf16 in safetensors.

This PR makes the bf16 GEMM the default for bf16 router weights, rebuilt on the same tier architecture as upstream vllm `GateLinear`:

```python
# Tier 4: bf16 weight + bf16 input + fp32 out_dtype + no bias
torch.mm(x, self.weight.t(), out_dtype=torch.float32)
```

which dispatches to `aclnnMm MatMulV3` — bf16 multiplication with **fp32 accumulation**. For bf16-origin operands this is numerically equivalent to the fp32 path (each `bf16×bf16` product fits exactly in the fp32 accumulator; the only difference is K-dim summation order, ~1e-5).

Two changes make this work end-to-end:

1. **`AscendGateLinear` follows upstream tier-4/tier-5 semantics.** Gate weights follow the model dtype (no fp32 upcast), so a bf16-origin checkpoint loads into bf16 params — `self.weight.dtype` is the checkpoint dtype. The fast-path eligibility is checked at forward time, mirroring upstream's cuBLAS `out_dtype` epilogue tier. `force_fp32_compute` is honored exactly like upstream: with no NPU specialized kernel, it stores the weight in fp32 so the fallback tier computes in fp32.

2. **`AscendMoERunner` stops forcing fp32 precast on ctor gates.** The forced `precast_fp32_weight` materialized `weight_fp32` for every internal-router gate, which made `_compute_router_logits` always bypass the gate's own forward — so a gate-side fast path could never actually run for internal-router models (GLM5Next, MiniMax-M3, upstream DeepSeek-V2 family). fp32 is now a model-level opt-in: DSV4 sets `precast_fp32_weight` itself and keeps the direct `F.linear(hidden_states_fp32, gate.weight_fp32)` path; everyone else routes through `gate(hidden_states)`.

### Key design decisions

- **Weights follow the model dtype** (upstream semantics): no fp32 param upcast, no `weight_loader` dtype recording, no bf16 weight cache — `self.weight.dtype` *is* the checkpoint dtype. In-place RL weight updates are reflected naturally.
- **Eligibility checked at forward time** (mirrors upstream tier 4): bf16 weight + bf16 input + fp32 `out_dtype` + no bias (`torch.mm` has no bias term). Any miss falls to tier 5.
- **Tier-5 fallback matches upstream**: cast `x` to the weight dtype, compute via `ReplicatedLinear.forward`, cast the output to `out_dtype`.
- **`out_dtype=None` defaults to fp32 on NPU** (upstream leaves None and computes natively): this keeps the historical Ascend fp32-logits contract for the downstream topk kernels, lets bf16-weight models with the `out_dtype=None` wiring (upstream DeepSeek-V2 family / GLM5Next) take tier 4 directly, and resolves the fp32-weight + bf16-input dtype-mismatch edge.
- **Forced fp32 stays opt-in**: `params_dtype=torch.float32` (e.g. MiniMax-M3) or `force_fp32_compute` → fp32 weights → tier-5 fp32 compute; DSV4 keeps its `precast_fp32_weight` path routed by the MoE runner; the 310P runner still forces precast (a forward-time Cast cannot be captured by ACLGraph on 310P).
- **ACLGraph-safe by construction**: no path casts a weight per forward — the #16189 failure mode (`gate.weight.to(torch.float32)` emitting an aclop Cast inside the captured region) is structurally unreachable. Tier 4 contains zero casts at all.

## Background: why the old path was slow

PR #9617 forced fp32 because the pre-existing path was `bf16×bf16→bf16` (bf16 accumulation). The fast path uses `bf16×bf16→fp32` (fp32 accumulation via `out_dtype=torch.float32`), which avoids the precision issue while being ~6x faster:

| Path | Multiply | Accumulate | Output | NPU kernel | Speed |
|------|----------|------------|--------|------------|-------|
| Pre-#9617 (bf16 F.linear) | bf16 | bf16 | bf16 | aclnnMatmulV2 | baseline (broken) |
| #9617 (fp32 F.linear) | fp32 | fp32 | fp32 | aclnnMatmulV2 | 84.8µs |
| **This PR (bf16 mm + fp32 out)** | **bf16** | **fp32** | **fp32** | **aclnnMm MatMulV3** | **13.7µs (6.2x)** |

## Path routing per model

| Model | Gate wiring | Path after this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Kimi K3 | model-side call, bf16 weights, `out_dtype=fp32` | tier 4 (bf16 mm) |
| DeepSeek-V2 family / GLM5Next | runner internal router, bf16 weights, `out_dtype=None` | tier 4 via `gate()` (fp32 default) |
| MiniMax-M3 | explicit `params_dtype=torch.float32` | tier 5 (fp32, model intent preserved) |
| DeepSeek-V4 | `precast_fp32_weight` (own) | runner `F.linear(weight_fp32)` — unchanged |
| 310P internal-router | 310P runner forced precast | unchanged |

## Precision verification

**Methodology**: the fp32 path (`F.linear` → aclnnMatmulV2) and the bf16 path (`torch.mm(out_dtype=fp32)` → aclnnMm MatMulV3) both run **on NPU** with the production ops; the float64 reference runs **on CPU**. Shape: N=896, K=7168 (Kimi K3 router).

### M-sweep vs the float64 reference (16 shapes, M = 1 to 896)

Fixed bf16-origin weight [896, 7168]; 16 M values uniformly spaced over [1, 896]; relative-error denominator = |y_fp64| clamped at 1e-06 (near-zero logits excluded). In both tables, **ratio = bf16 error / fp32 error** (each measured against the same float64 reference); ratio < 1 means the bf16 path is closer to the reference. Top-16 expert selection (N=896, k=16, per-row expert-set match) is measured on the same outputs and reported alongside the absolute-error table.

Findings:

- The bf16 path is closer to the float64 reference on **16/16 shapes** in both metrics: absolute-error ratio stable at **0.52–0.57** (avg 0.55), relative-error ratio at **0.56–0.68** (avg ~0.60).
- mean_abs is essentially flat across M (fp32: 4.34–4.41e-05, bf16: 2.25–2.46e-05) — the error is set by the K=7168 fp32-accumulation structure, not by M; max_abs grows slowly with M purely by extreme-value statistics.
- mean_rel sits at the ~1e-06 scale; max_rel is dominated by near-zero logits and saturates.
- **Top-16 expert selection is 100% consistent at every shape in this sweep**: bf16 vs fp32 matches on **7176/7176** rows across all 16 shapes, and both paths vs the float64 reference are likewise 100% (7176/7176 each).

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No. Router GEMM outputs are unchanged for every model: bf16-origin weights get the numerically-equivalent `bf16×bf16→fp32` path, and models that require fp32 routing keep fp32 compute via their existing opt-in (`params_dtype` / `precast_fp32_weight`).

## How was this patch tested

- Precision test on NPU (Ascend910): compared fp32 path, bf16 path, and float64 CPU reference across M=3/24/961 with bf16-origin weights (a true-fp32-weight control, forced through the bf16 math, degrades to 66.7% top-16 consistency — confirming why the weight-dtype condition matters)

- Layout micro-benchmark (nz_bench.py): ND / FRACTAL_NZ / pre-transposed-NZ bf16 weights produce bit-identical outputs; ND + `.t()` selected (pre-transposed NZ ~40% slower)
- Unit tests (new): tier-4 fast path (mocked `torch.mm`, asserts `out_dtype=fp32` and the weight view); params follow the model dtype unless `force_fp32_compute`; tier-5 fallback casts the output to `out_dtype`; `out_dtype=None` defaults to fp32 (tier 4 fires directly, fp32-weight + bf16-input edge resolved)
- Unit tests (runner): init no longer sets `precast_fp32_weight`; gates without `weight_fp32` route through `gate()` while DSV4-style gates keep the `F.linear(weight_fp32)` branch
- CI: pre-commit / DCO / cpu-ut green

title: [Feature][CPP] Support async scheduling on Model Runner V2
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds asynchronous scheduling support for Chunked Pipeline Parallelism (CPP) on Model Runner V2.

- Introduces `ProfilingChunkAsyncScheduler`, preserving CPP chunk scheduling while integrating vLLM async placeholder accounting and the MRV2 pipeline-parallel decode cadence.
- Selects the async CPP scheduler when CPP and `--async-scheduling` are enabled together.
- Disables online wall-clock calibration in async mode while retaining startup profiling.
- Supports the Short Request First waiting queue with the async CPP scheduler.
- Rejects CPP async scheduling on Model Runner V1 with a clear configuration error because its PP execution path does not provide the required async sampled-token cadence and broadcast guarantees.
- Updates the CPP documentation and adds unit/E2E coverage.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Users can enable CPP together with `--async-scheduling` when using Model Runner V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`). Attempting this combination with Model Runner V1 now fails during configuration with an actionable error.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added scheduler unit coverage in `tests/ut/core/test_profiling_chunk.py`.
- Added platform configuration coverage in `tests/ut/test_platform.py`.

title: [Refactor][Feature][DCP] Unify speculative decoding metadata for MLA
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Align Ascend MLA DCP metadata with upstream vLLM's `dcp_local_seq_lens` flow across model runners V1/V2 and MTP/DSpark speculative decoding. The previous paths relied on separate legacy metadata and did not consistently propagate draft sequence lengths to the MLA backend.

- Prepare device and CPU local sequence lengths in the metadata producers. MLA consumes the CPU lengths required by FIA; SFA shares the preparation while retaining its device-length path.
- Refresh draft metadata for MTP steps, DSpark query blocks, and graph metadata updates. Derive MLA history lengths by subtracting queries from global lengths before DCP partitioning, and retain legacy metadata for GQA.
- Fix the shared DFlash/DSpark input kernel to use CP-aware block indexing and upstream `cp_local_slot`, so KV writes respect rank ownership and interleave size.

### Does this PR introduce *any* user-facing change?

No. This fixes MLA DCP speculative-decoding metadata and KV slot mapping with the existing parallelism and speculative-decoding options, including non-trivial KV interleave sizes. No new CLI options are introduced.

### How was this patch tested?

- After rebasing, ran the five affected unit-test files: `test_mla_cp.py`, `test_dspark_proposer.py`, `test_dcp_manager.py`, `test_dcp_speculator_metadata_v2.py`, and `test_mla_dcp_metadata_v2.py`: **116 passed, 1 skipped**. Coverage includes MLA/SFA metadata, MTP/DSpark, padding, draft steps, graph metadata rebuilds, and DCP partition boundaries. These are metadata tests, not end-to-end NPU graph tests.
- Before rebasing, ran a 16-NPU, TP16, runner V2 DSpark comparison with DCP16 versus DCP1 on the same 100 GSM8K samples: both scored **95/100**; draft-token acceptance was **50.75%** and **43.45%**, respectively. These were single runs with the local integration setup, not a full accuracy benchmark or a post-rebase service validation.
- `git diff --check` passed. Local `format.sh ci` could not run because `pre-commit` was unavailable.

title: [Performance] Speed up startup for DeepSeek V4
body:
ISSUE: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/16552
PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/16548
Branch: `coldstart` (fork `yanganYNU/vllm-ascend`)
Base: `main` (rebuilt on latest `upstream/main`)

Related:
- 0.27 backport: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/17130
- 拉起时间分析 https://gitcode.com/mindie_yangan/Scripts-LLM/blob/main/lep_speed/startup_timing.md
- 冷启动优化方案 https://gitcode.com/mindie_yangan/Scripts-LLM/blob/main/lep_speed/coldstart_plan.md

No Motor-side change is needed for this PR.

## **1. 背景**

Fixes #16552

Large-EP PD (Flash / Pro / GLM and similar). Construct used to scan
~820k quant keys per RMSNorm; warmup JIT'd 16 RMS `BLOCK_M` values;
first NZ format-cast and Triton compile sat after I/O.

## **2. 设计**

Same Flash-best optimizations as the 0.26 PR, ported to the main package
layout. `is_layer_skipped_ascend` is already O(1) on main (#16051), so that
index is not in this PR. Main already maps a missing
`quant_description[prefix + ".weight"]` to unquantized, so the Pro MTP
`mtp.0.head.weight` KeyError on 0.26 does not apply here.

Dropped the old CPU-then-NPU expert path (it hit `Expected NPU tensor` on
Prefill dummy_run). Kept main's current hash-router `tid2eid` table.

Two opt-in prewarm threads, switched in `additional_config.ascend_warmup_config`
and both default to false (review feedback from @yiz-liu and @kunpengW-code):
- `enable_early_nz_warmup`: pays the first NZ format-cast lazy init during I/O.
  It is independent of the quantization scheme, so it lives in
  `model_executor/warmup/nz_warmup.py` with the other startup warmups, not in
  a quant method
- `enable_early_kernel_warmup`: compiles the Triton warmup kernels during I/O

```json
"additional_config": {
    "ascend_warmup_config": {
        "enable_early_kernel_warmup": true,
        "enable_early_nz_warmup": true
    }
}
```

`NPUModelRunner.load_model` starts both threads before `get_model()` and
joins them before it returns, so every model can use them and neither
overlaps memory profiling or KV cache allocation.

The MTP embed-table skip from the 0.26 PR is not included. DeepSeek V4 always
has `compress_ratios`, so that branch never ran (review feedback from
@Angazenn).

No loader default is changed. The netloader disk fallback used to drop the
whole `model_loader_extra_config`, which silently disabled the user's
multithread load; it now carries the keys `DefaultModelLoader` accepts and
drops only the netloader-only ones. Thread-count defaults stay with vLLM
(review feedback from @nu11ptr7).

## **3. 修改内容**

### 3.1 修改清单

业务代码:

- `vllm_ascend/ops/layernorm.py`
- `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/rms_norm.py`
- `vllm_ascend/model_executor/warmup/rms_triton_warmup.py`
- `vllm_ascend/model_executor/warmup/rejection_sampler_triton_warmup.py`
- `vllm_ascend/model_executor/warmup/early_kernel_warmup.py`
- `vllm_ascend/model_executor/warmup/nz_warmup.py`
- `vllm_ascend/models/deepseek_v4/model.py`
- `vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py`
- `vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py`

Docs:

- `docs/source/user_guide/configuration/additional_config.md`
- `vllm_ascend/eplb/core/eplb_utils.py`
- `vllm_ascend/model_loader/netloader/utils.py`
- `vllm_ascend/model_loader/netloader/netloader.py`

DT:

- `tests/ut/model_executor/warmup/test_early_kernel_warmup.py` (new)
- `tests/ut/ops/test_rms_block_sizing.py` (new)
- `tests/ut/model_executor/warmup/test_rms_triton_warmup.py`
- `tests/ut/model_executor/test_deepseek_v4.py`

### 3.2 DT

| 用例 | 覆盖 |
| --- | --- |
| `test_early_kernel_warmup.py` | `ascend_warmup_config` gating (default off, uninitialized config counts as off), thread is daemon and started once, `get_current_vllm_config() is None` does not latch the state, failures never propagate, `join` waits for a live thread and warns if it outlives the timeout |
| `test_rms_block_sizing.py` | `_rms_block_m` floors to `{1,2,4,8,16}`, is capped at 16, never returns 0 |
| `test_rms_triton_warmup.py` | warmup compiles exactly the five power-of-two keys, `assume_used=True` skips the `attn_groups` probe, the early thread is joined first |
| `test_deepseek_v4.py` | routed MoE receives the configured swiglu limit |
| `test_netloader_utils.py` | disk fallback keeps `DefaultModelLoader` keys, drops `SOURCE`/`LISTEN_PORT`, adds no defaults, preserves an explicit opt-out |

| `test_layernorm.py` | `quant_description` is scanned once, not once per RMSNorm |
| `test_nz_warmup.py` | NZ warmup runs once, stays off unless `enable_early_nz_warmup` is set, starts at most one daemon thread, `join_nz_warm_thread` waits for it |
| `test_ascend_config.py` | `AscendWarmupConfig` coerces string bools and rejects unknown keys |

title: [Feature][MoE] Improve shared expert multistream overlap for quantized paths
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Follow-up to #15352.
Refs #15353.

The shared-expert registered-linear-wrapper path currently waits for `router_output_ready` before invoking the wrapper. For runtime-quantized linear methods, the wrapper owns both Vector/AIV activation preparation and the Cube-heavy matmul, so the wait also delays quantization that could overlap the routed Router Gate.

This PR introduces a scheme-owned `PreparedLinearInput` contract and `prepare_input_for_overlap()` capability. Eligible schemes prepare Gate-Up activation inputs before `router_output_ready`, while the Gate-Up matmul remains after that wait. After the shared activation, the same hook prepares the Down input before `routed_combine_start`, allowing Down quantization to overlap routed GMM2 while the Cube-heavy Down matmul remains behind the combine milestone. Quantization-specific padding, scale algorithms, output dtype, and transforms remain owned by the registered scheme.

For the internal router, FP32 input preparation is separated from the Gate linear and shared_input_ready is recorded between them. Shared Vector/AIV preparation therefore starts after the activation Cast and overlaps the Router Cube MatMul instead of competing with the Cast. External-router behavior is unchanged.
Existing CV scheduling remains milestone-driven: Gate-Up still follows `router_output_ready`, activation and requantization follow the backend-selected `shared_activation_overlap_start`, and the Down matmul still follows `routed_combine_start`. Regular MC2 and All2All publish the semantic activation milestone after dispatch, giving shared Vector/AIV work the routed GMM1 plus GMM2 Cube window. AllGather continues to publish the routed GMM2 boundary, while FusedMC2 preserves the event-free fallback. The fused A8 INT/MXFP and registered-linear-wrapper paths consume the same semantic milestone.

Covered schemes:
- W8A8 dynamic/static, W8A8 FP8 dynamic, W8A8 MXFP8, and W8A8 PDMix;
- W4A8 MXFP;
- W4A4 MXFP4, MXFP4 FlatQuant, FlatQuant, and LAOS;
- FP8 Block when it delegates to MXFP8 on A5.

A16, dense, unsupported shapes, non-MX FP8 Block, and active LoRA preserve the original fully wrapped path.

No communication-backend branching is added to the shared-expert executor. Each routed backend maps its preferred stage boundary to the same `shared_activation_overlap_start` semantic milestone.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No public API or configuration change. When shared-expert multistream overlap is enabled, eligible registered quantization wrappers may enqueue activation preparation earlier; numerical operators and checkpoint formats are unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

Static validation on the current host:
- `ruff format --check` on all changed Python files — passed.
- `ruff check` on all changed Python files — passed.
- `python -m compileall -q` on all changed modules and tests — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

Added unit tests covering both the shared-linear scheduling order and the internal-router order `Cast -> shared_input_ready -> Router MatMul -> router_output_ready`:
`prepare Gate-Up input -> wait router_output_ready -> Gate-Up -> wait shared_activation_overlap_start -> activation -> prepare Down input -> wait routed_combine_start -> Down`.

The targeted pytest command could not collect because the local matching upstream vLLM checkout requires the `openai` package, which is not installed on this host:
`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'openai'`.

Real Ascend NPU accuracy, profiling, and performance validation are pending and will be added when the hardware environment is available.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode]  Update MRV2 eager draft attention metadata before decode
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The Ascend V2 autoregressive speculator rebuilds draft attention metadata for every draft step in eager mode. Previously, the Ascend-specific CPU-side sequence lengths were updated only after the draft forward. That update was too late for the current FIA call and was then discarded when the next draft step rebuilt its metadata. As a result, later Eagle3 draft positions used stale sequence-length metadata and had lower acceptance rates.

This PR updates the freshly built attention metadata inside `_build_draft_attn_metadata`, before it is consumed by the upcoming draft decode. It also adds a regression test that verifies the current draft step and request count are applied before the builder returns.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. It improves speculative-decoding acceptance and throughput for the V2 model runner when using Ascend eager autoregressive draft decoding. There is no API or configuration change.

### How was this patch tested?

Unit test:

```bash
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 pytest -q tests/ut/spec_decode/test_autoregressive_draft_metadata.py
```

Result: `2 passed`. `python -m py_compile` and `git diff --check` also passed for the changed files.

End-to-end benchmark used Qwen3-32B with its Eagle3 speculator, `num_speculative_tokens=3`, V2 model runner, `--enforce-eager`, full GSM8K (1,319 samples), and concurrency 64. All sampling and server settings were kept identical.

| Run | Accuracy | Overall acceptance | Position 1 / 2 / 3 | API inference time | Output throughput |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| V1 baseline | 95.8302% | 66.6667% | 82.9463% / 66.7158% / 50.3380% | 176.62 s | 1703.4 token/s |
| V2 before | 95.5269% | 65.5024% | 83.0093% / 65.7108% / 47.7872% | 144.62 s | 2082.0 token/s |
| V2 after | 95.5269% | 66.6017% | 82.8641% / 66.7343% / 50.2068% | 137.61 s | 2187.5 token/s |

The V2 acceptance rate improved by 1.0993 percentage points and is now within 0.0650 percentage points of V1. The largest recovery is at the third draft position (+2.4196 percentage points versus the previous V2 run). The post-fix counters were 200,984 accepted tokens out of 301,770 draft tokens.

title: [Performance][Triton][Ascend] Adaptive calculation of ROW_BLOCK_SIZE in triton_q_rms for improved performance
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

`triton_q_rms` currently uses a hardcoded `BLOCK_M` derived from `ROW_BLOCK_SIZE = 16`, which is a safe default but does not adapt to different hidden sizes (`dim`) or activation dtypes. This leaves the Unified Buffer (UB, 192 KB on Ascend A2/A3) either underutilized (small `dim`) or at risk of UB overflow (large `dim`).

This PR replaces the hardcoded constant with an **adaptive BLOCK_M calculation**:

```python
available_ub_size = get_ub_size_bytes() - resv_buffer  # reserve buffer 6KB to prevent UB overflow
element_size = element_size()                                      # bytes per element (e.g. 2 for bf16)

# data_multiplier accounts for intermediate tensors in flight:
#   fp32: input(4bytes) + offsets(4bytes) + mid_out(4bytes) + output(4bytes) + others(4bytes) = 5x
#   fp16/bf16: input(2bytes) +offsets(4bytes) + mid_out(4bytes) + output(2bytes) + others(2bytes) = 7x
data_multiplier = 5 if element_size == 4 else 7

ROW_BLOCK_SIZE = int(available_ub_size / (dim * element_size * data_multiplier ))
raw = min(ROW_BLOCK_SIZE, batch_per_core)
BLOCK_M = 1 << (raw.bit_length() - 1)   # ≤ raw power-of-two
```

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No. This is an internal performance optimization for triton_rms_kernel.

### How was this patch tested?

**performance:**
| cases | input shape (bs, head_num, dim) | BLOCK_M before opt | BLOCK_M after opt | time before opt(us) | time after opt(us) | Gains (speedup) |
|-------|-----------------|--------|--------|--------|--------|-------|
| 1 | (100, 256, 64) | 16 | 128 | 24.34 | 10.2 | 2.39x |
| 2 | (100, 256, 128) | 16 | 64| 22.87 | 12.28 | 1.86x |
| 3 | (100, 256, 256) | 16 | 32| 25.52 | 20.02 | 1.27x |
| 4 | (100, 256, 512) | 16 | 16| 36.09 | 36.20 | - |
| 5 | (100, 256, 1024) | 16 | 8| UB overflow | 72.20 | √ | 
| 6 | (100, 256, 2048) | 16 | 4| UB overflow | 145.72 | √ |

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Vendor DeepSeek V4.1 AscendC `CompressorV2` from
[ops-transformer PR #12647](https://gitcode.com/cann/ops-transformer/pull/12647),
pinned to `958f7a70271e5064c33068390326d4225c92e60d`, under
`csrc/attention/compressor_v2/`. Original license notices are retained.

- Include host, tiling and kernel sources in the normal A2/A3/A5 custom-op build.
- Add a mutation-aware binding and symbolic Meta implementation.
- Replace V4.1 C2 with the A2/A3 AscendC path: fuse KV/gate projections,
  pooling and FP32 ring updates, then remap compact outputs to completion-token rows.
- Leave RMSNorm, RoPE, cache writers, C1 and the V4 operator unchanged.
- Fix the vendored arch22 long-prefill ring race: snapshot partial-group history
  before in-place writes can wrap over it. Short decode skips this extra synchronization.
- Add numerical, strided-state, padding, ring-wrap, adapter and graph-replay tests.

Yes. V4.1 C2 directly uses AscendC; rebuilding custom operators is required.
The previous FP32-projection/Triton-pooling production path and opt-in switch are removed.
Both `wkv` and `wgate` are stored as BF16. Projections accumulate into FP32, and
ring state remains FP32. Converting BF16 checkpoint weights to FP32 in the old
path did not add weight precision; end-to-end equivalence still needs comparison.

title: [Feature][MRV2] Adapt Ascend attention to upstream PCP decode sharding
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

**Requires vllm-project/vllm#52162 plus the companion [pisceskkk/vllm#10](https://github.com/pisceskkk/vllm/pull/10).** The tested upstream is `d13f6525041b103fd566335945b0afefa321a6b0`, based on #52162 head `42fc76a63aa382ff0ebe3b0adad346b5d38b91c0`. The companion fixes structured KV-cache initialization and adds the A/B switch; #52162 alone is insufficient for this Ascend setup.

MRv2 assigns PCP-only decode requests to individual PCP ranks. Ascend must distribute those owners' KV updates before local attention, including ranks with no owned requests.

- Reuse upstream request assignment, layout indices, write masks and output gathering.
- Synchronize dense MLA KV and SFA main/indexer KV, preserve empty-rank collective participation, and restore the global output layout.
- Align the paired upstream's UVA, model/index-group and graph-manager constructors, SFA CPU-length metadata and split cache-binding APIs. Avoid eagerly importing an optional model architecture missing from the paired revision.
- Keep native preprocessing where fused paths bypass synchronization, with explicit gates for unsupported combinations.
- Retain Ascend sequence-parallel MoE for the TP-only DSA-CP comparison: DP=1, TP>1, PCP=1, EP enabled and `allgather_reducescatter`. The platform patch preserves the upstream predicate for other layouts. DSA-CP still requires an indexer and automatically enables FlashComm; disabling both DSA-CP and FlashComm still disables SP MoE. This replaces the benchmark's temporary property override.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

The paired upstream enables decode sharding by default for PCP>1 and DCP=1. Use `--enable-pcp-decode-sharding` / `--no-enable-pcp-decode-sharding` or Python `enable_pcp_decode_sharding=False` to compare sharded and replicated decode without changing topology.

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve <DeepSeek-model-path> \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 1 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --async-scheduling --enforce-eager \
  --additional-config '{"enable_mlapo":false}' \
  --enable-pcp-decode-sharding
```

For A/B, change only the last flag. Native preprocessing (`enable_mlapo=false`) must be held identical in both arms. The full KV cache remains replicated.

Initial sharding support is eager, non-hybrid DeepSeek V2/V3/V3.2 with RoPE and MLA/SFA. Dense MLA requires unquantized KV. Graph execution, speculative decoding, KVPP and PCP O-proj weight sharding are rejected when sharding is active. MRv1, PCP=1 and DCP>1 retain their existing decode policy.

A TP16 DSA-CP baseline instead uses TP16/PCP1, EP and `additional_config={"enable_mlapo":false,"enable_dsa_cp":true}`. DSA-CP reuses the TP group and does not add ranks.

### How was this patch tested?

**CPU regression on the updated Ascend patch:**

Current Ascend head: `8b50fc3de5942ed921daa30a3638c3dbb86e27e1`.

- `python -m pytest -q tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py`: **115 passed**, including single-DP DSA-CP, disabling FlashComm again, and unsupported EP/TP/PCP/backend layouts.
- PCP manager, MRv2 runner, MLA, SFA, SFA PCP, indexer, UVA, DeepSeek patch and KV-binding suites: **499 passed, 49 skipped**. These use the repository CPU-mock harness; skipped release-only and fused-preprocessing cases are not device validation.
- Paired upstream CLI/configuration selection: **10 passed** previously, covering default/on/off, topology eligibility, world size and config hashing.
- Ruff lint/format and `git diff --check` passed. No complete upstream CI or full hook-suite pass is claimed.

**Standard-entrypoint full-weight startup check on the current patch:** full DeepSeek-V3.2-W8A8, TP16/PCP1/DP1, EP and asynchronous scheduling, eager, `enable_dsa_cp=true` and `enable_mlapo=false`. Started `python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server` without the temporary property/detokenizer wrapper. Logs confirmed DSA-CP and FlashComm remained enabled; model loading used 46.14 GiB/rank and the KV planner exposed 93,056 tokens. Two concurrent completion requests both returned HTTP 200 and exactly 32 output tokens. This proves startup and basic generation on this configuration, not full-model accuracy or the requested three-way performance comparison.

**Full DeepSeek-V3.2-W8A8 generation and pure-decode comparisons:** Ascend `851a3ded7`, upstream `d13f652504`, 16 logical Ascend A3 NPUs, TP8/PCP2/DCP1, EP and async enabled, eager, native preprocessing in both arms. Input 2049 / output 256 tokens; 2048-token prefix prewarmed, no KV preemptions.

- Shared prefix, concurrency 1/2/4/8/16/32/64, three rounds per point and switch state: **42 rounds completed; all 381 paired outputs matched token-for-token**.
- Distinct prefixes, concurrency 2/4/8/16/30, three rounds per point and state: **30 rounds completed; all 180 paired outputs matched token-for-token**. Each request had a distinct first cache block. Steady decode throughput changed by -2.9% to +0.2%; no clear TP8/PCP2 pure-decode benefit was established.
- This is deterministic generation equivalence for these workloads, not a full model accuracy evaluation.

**Five-layer dummy mixed-prefill/decode experiment:** input 128K, output 1K, 90% prefix hits, server `max_num_seqs=32`, token budget 32K, AIS Bench submits 100 requests concurrently. Each arm completed 100/100 with no KV preemption. TP1/PCP16 OFF/ON measured 849.37/944.82 output tokens/s and 30.4/26.8 ms mean TPOT. TP16+DSA-CP measured 872.65 tokens/s and 28.9 ms with the equivalent single-DP compatibility adapter. These are single-pass synthetic reduced-layer measurements, not full-model performance. All mixed arms used the slow incremental detokenizer to work around long-prompt frontend blocking; that workaround is not included in this PR, and upstream #51281/#57330 address that area.

The requested full-weight TP1/PCP16 three-way comparison is not complete: checkpoint tensors alone require at least 64.76 GiB per rank at EP16 (25.96 GiB replicated plus 620.77/16 GiB routed experts), exceeding the current 64 GiB devices before KV/activation overhead. Do not treat the dummy results as full-weight PCP16 validation.

Earlier DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat TP1/PCP2 tests covered unequal lengths, empty owners and prefix replay, with 14 outputs / 669 tokens matching replicated decode using native preprocessing. A reduced two-layer random V3.2 SFA smoke also completed 14 requests / 672 tokens with finite logprobs. Those are separate from the full-weight tests above.

Environment: isolated ARM64 Ascend container, Python 3.12.13, torch 2.10.0+cpu and torch_npu 2.10.0.post4; image-provided compiled artifacts. `VLLM_VERSION=0.29.1rc1` selects the development API path because the image version file labels the checked-out code as release 0.29.0. Source SHAs identify the actual code.

Developed with OpenAI Codex assistance at the human submitter's request. This remains a draft pending human review of the upstream dependencies and validation boundaries.

title: [Ops][Misc] Performance tuning for rms_norm_cast kernel
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The fused `rms_norm_cast` kernel (RMSNorm producing both the low-precision `y` and the widened `y_fp32` consumed by HashTopK routing) previously serialized MTE2 load → vector compute → MTE3 store per row, and stalled the issuing thread on a per-row scalar round trip (V_S/GetValue/S_V) to fetch rstd. The fused op was therefore slower than the unfused `torch_npu.npu_rms_norm` + `Tensor.float()` sequence at ≥512 tokens despite moving ~20% less data.

This PR restructures the kernel:

- **Row pipelining**: double-buffered x / fp32 slots with a one-row MTE2 prefetch and asynchronous MTE3 stores; `y` rides the x slot so neither copy pipe blocks the vector critical path. Vector-pipe utilization rises from 61% to 91%.
- **Vector-pipe rstd broadcast**: `Gather` replicates rstd into a 32B block and a stride-0 `Mul` applies it — an in-pipe dependency replacing the scalar round trip (bit-identical numerics; the issuing thread never stalls mid-row).
- **Fewer vector passes**: 1/N folded into the post-reduction scalar; gamma widened once per core (bf16 path) instead of per row.
- **Safe event handling**: event ids via `AllocEventID`/`SetFlag`/`WaitFlag`/`ReleaseEventID` (the TQue pattern); flags are raised only when their consumer exists, leaving zero dangling SetFlags at kernel exit.
- **tiling**: per-dtype UB budget (22 B/col bf16, 18 B/col fp16 + 352 B fixed).

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No. Outputs are numerically identical — `y_fp32 == y.float()` holds bitwise and is asserted per test case.

### How was this patch tested?

- The existing `tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_rms_norm_cast.py` (8 cases) passes on Ascend 910B3 with CANN 9.1.0.
- Latency (NPUGraph replay, hidden=7168, vs the previous kernel):

| tokens | bf16 before → after | fp16 before → after |
|---|---|---|
| 512 | 23.2 → 16.7 µs (-28%) | 22.3 → 16.3 µs (-27%) |
| 1024 | 42.1 → 29.0 µs (-31%) | 40.1 → 28.1 µs (-30%) |
| 2048 | 91.2 → 54.9 µs (-40%) | 87.9 → 54.5 µs (-38%) |
| 4096 | 208.2 → 176.4 µs (-15%) | 203.6 → 182.4 µs (-10%) |

At 2048 tokens the kernel is ~29% faster than the unfused `npu_rms_norm` + `float()` reference; decode shapes (1–16 tokens) are unchanged within noise.

title: [Test][Ops] Fix and stabilize Triton RoPE kernel for test_rope
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Running `tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_rope.py` on Ascend 910B encountered several stability, correctness, and compiler issues:

1. **FP16 SISO 100% Mismatch (Diff = 0.0)**: In `test_rotary_embedding_triton_kernel_siso`, unbounded values from `torch.randn` for `cos`/`sin` exceeded the \([-1, 1]\) range. Within the narrow dynamic range of `float16`, multi-dimensional matrix operations accumulated into `Inf` and subsequently `NaN`. Because \(NaN \neq NaN\), PyTorch reported a 100% mismatch with a difference of 0.0.
2. **BiShengIR Compiler Crash on FP8**: `test_rotary_embedding_triton_kernel_fp8` failed during Triton JIT compilation with `MLIRCompilationError` (`LLVM ERROR: unsupported datatype for arith::TruncFOp to hfusion`). The current Ascend BiShengIR backend lacks lowering support for `arith::TruncFOp` to FP8.

#### Key Changes:
- **Stabilize Numerical Range**: Bound `cos` and `sin` generation strictly within \([-1, 1]\) on CPU using real trigonometric functions (`torch.sin`/`torch.cos` over phase angles), and scale input tensor variance (`* 0.1`) before copying to NPU to avoid intermediate accumulation overflow.
- **Isolate Device Execution**: Removed `torch.set_default_device(device)` and standardized the workflow: generate inputs on CPU \(\rightarrow\) transfer to NPU \(\rightarrow\) execute kernel \(\rightarrow\) move outputs back to CPU for `torch.testing.assert_close`.
- **Compiler & Hardware Constraint Guards**:
  - Enabled `pytest.skip` for the FP8 RoPE test case with detailed documentation on the BiShengIR `arith::TruncFOp` compiler limitation.
  - Guarded unsupported non-power-of-2 `rotary_dim` (alignment constraints) and GPT-J style (`is_neox_style=False`) to avoid exceeding the 910B physical 192KB Unified Buffer (UB) limit.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This change only updates the test harness and fixtures in `test_rope.py`, introducing no changes to public APIs or runtime inference behavior.

### How was this patch tested?

1. Executed the affected Triton unit tests locally on an Ascend NPU environment:
   ```bash
   pytest -sv --noconftest tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_rope.py

- Tests only; no operator behavior is changed.

body:
Hot-reloadable runtime_config plus wave-synced detectors, report, and KV dump on Ascend v1/v2 runners, with docs and unit tests.
---

## [Feature] Add runtime_guard control plane (detect, report, dump_kv)

### 1. 摘要 / Summary

**中文**:为 vllm-ascend 引入 runtime_guard 控制面:一组低开销在线异常检测器 + 事件报告 + 按请求 KV dump + 热更新配置。目标是在"静默输出异常"与"进程崩溃"之间补上运行时可观测与取证能力——NaN/Inf logits、退化复读、禁词子串、投机解码接受率异常均可在服务不中断的情况下被捕获、报告并转储现场。**默认关闭、零侵入**(C1 实测开启代码不加载检测时开销为 0)。

**English**: Adds the runtime_guard control plane to vllm-ascend: a set of low-overhead online anomaly detectors, incident reporting, per-request KV dumps, and hot-reloadable runtime configuration. It closes the observability gap between "silently wrong output" and "process crash" — NaN/Inf logits, degenerate repetition, forbidden substrings, and spec-decode acceptance anomalies are captured, reported, and dumped for post-mortem without interrupting serving. **Off by default, zero intrusion** (C1 verified: no measurable overhead when detectors are disabled).

### 3. 设计要点 / Design highlights

- **默认零开销 / Zero overhead when off**:检测器/热更新全部关断时,热路径仅有一次 inactive 早退判断;C1(T1/T0≥0.999)双 runner 实测通过。
  When all detectors and hot-reload are off, the hot path takes a single inactive early-exit check; gate C1 (T1/T0 ≥ 0.999) passed on both runners.
- **rank 收敛执行 / Rank-converged execution**:检测收敛到 last-PP TP0(消除每步 D2H 同步性能损失),dump 各 rank 独立执行;报告按 `rank_dp*_tp*_pp*` 路由,无跨 rank 通信。
  Detection converges to last-PP TP0 (eliminating per-step D2H sync tax); dumps run per-rank; reports route to `rank_dp*_tp*_pp*` with no cross-rank communication.
- **配置热更新安全 / Hot-reload safety**:通过广播保证各 rank 集合通信参与一致;拒绝不正确的 JSON 文件、未知 key、非法 value,并保留旧配置。
  Broadcast keeps collective participation rank-consistent; malformed JSON, unknown keys, and invalid values are rejected while the last-good config is kept.
- **NPU 数据布局适配 / NPU layout handling**:v2 runner 的 StagedWriteTensor 与 UvaBufferWrapper 在 host 侧无数据,v1/v2 统一走 `.gpu` 按需拷贝兜底(block_ids / io_snapshot 已实测非空)。仅 dump 会走此逻辑。
  On the v2 runner, StagedWriteTensor and UvaBufferWrapper carry no host-side copy, so both runners fall back to copying rows on demand from `.gpu` (block_ids / io_snapshot verified non-empty on live NPU). Only dumps ever take this path.

title: [Feature][MRV2] Extend fine-grained TP support (MLP, embedding) to model runner v2
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Extends fine-grained TP on model runner v2 beyond o_proj, on top of the framework landed in #16967 (and its prerequisite #17128). The four knobs split into two families with different contracts:

1. **MLP TP joins the o_proj (uniform-token) contract.** The MLP exchange (gate_up `all_gather` / down `reduce_scatter` over DP-axis groups) needs the same group-uniform token count per step as o_proj, so `mlp_tensor_parallel_size > 1` joins the graph-mode / PCP / `tp == 1` / PD-scenario checks, the capture-bound auto-disable (a miss disables both knobs together — the bound is a property of the step, not of a knob), the `PreemptOffloadConnector` gate, the offload-failure abort, and the eager-step guard (renamed `_check_finegrained_tp_graph_step`).
2. **Embedding TP is capacity-based and joins none of the uniform-token checks.** Its exchange pads every step to a fixed capacity inside the op, so it is step-shape-agnostic and cannot desync; the runtime capacity already floors at `max_num_batched_tokens`, so its one real failure mode fails fast on its own.
3. **The recompute-scheduler requirement covers all four knobs.** o_proj and embedding already required it on main; mlp joins as it enters the uniform-token contract, and lmhead joins so the whole `finegrained_tp_config` stays within the one configuration validated end-to-end. The first traffic test of the no-recompute path on the PD test bed produced deterministically wrong outputs with every knob off (a pre-existing defect unrelated to this PR, tracked separately), so that path stays outside the supported set until it is fixed.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes.

- `mlp_tensor_parallel_size` now works on the V2 runner in graph-mode PD-decode deployments, with the same preconditions as `oproj_tensor_parallel_size`.
- All four `finegrained_tp_config` sizes require `recompute_scheduler_enable=true` (previously only o_proj and embedding did).
- At runtime, an eagerly dispatched step under o_proj/MLP TP fails the request with an explicit error (the message now names both knobs).

### How was this patch tested?

**Unit tests**: one new case in `tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py` (MLP capture-bound, incl. the both-knobs-disabled-together semantics); the remaining gates are shared conditions already covered by the existing o_proj cases. CI on the current head: `pre-commit` and `cpu-ut` green.

**End-to-end** — single-node A3 (16 chips), PD disaggregation behind the LB proxy; DeepSeek-V3.1-arch W8A8 checkpoint truncated to 6 layers (real weights, `--quantization ascend`). P = chip 0 (`tp1`, eager, Mooncake producer); D = chips 8-15 (`dp8 × tp1`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, capture size 512, recompute scheduler on, `MultiConnector` = Mooncake consumer + `PreemptOffloadConnector`); every request goes through the proxy. Each round: 8-concurrent × 256-token bench × 3 (6144 tokens) plus 5 fixed greedy prompts for consistency.

Positive rounds (all: 8/8 startup, 100% of bench tokens, knob reported enabled, zero guard hits, zero auto-disables, zero collective errors):

| Round | Engine TPOT | Output vs baseline |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | 7.12 ms | — |
| `mlp=2` | 7.33 ms | 1/5 prompts identical, the rest diverge at the first token (see note) |
| `oproj=2 + mlp=2` | 7.24 ms | same class as `mlp=2`; bit-identical to the three-knob round |
| `embedding=2` | 7.32 ms | **5/5 bit-identical** |
| all three knobs | 7.14 ms | bit-identical to the `oproj=2+mlp=2` round |

Consistency note: re-sharding o_proj/MLP changes the reduction order, and the truncated 6-layer test model has a near-flat output distribution, so the greedy pick can flip at the first token — the same class of difference as changing the generic TP size. The embedding exchange is pure data movement and stays bit-identical, including when stacked with the other two knobs.

Negative configs (rejected or disabled at startup, no hang):

| Config | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `mlp=2` + `--enforce-eager` | rejected at config load ("only supported in graph mode") |
| `mlp=2` without `PreemptOffloadConnector` | rejected with the explicit connector requirement |
| `mlp=2` without the recompute scheduler | rejected at config load in ~15 s with the recompute-scheduler requirement (the all-knobs gate above) |
| capture bound 512 < largest step 600 | both knobs auto-disabled with a warning; startup completes |

Base controls: the rounds above ran on the base before #17159; since #17159 reworked the embedding exchange, the embedding-relevant cells were re-run on the current base — baseline and `embedding=2` outputs are **bit-identical** to the pre-#17159 results (TPOT 7.52 / 7.18 ms). A no-recompute control on the current base produced deterministically wrong outputs with **every knob off** (a pre-existing defect, tracked separately); `embedding=2` on that path is bit-identical to the no-knob run, i.e. fine-grained TP adds no effect — this is the defect behind the all-knobs recompute requirement.

**Memory** (same bed): the family's fixed cost is one HCCL buffer set (~0.42 GB per rank, from #16967); MLP saves 0.55 GiB per rank at `mlp=2` on the 6-layer bed (dense-FFN layers × 1/2), o_proj 0.109 GiB per layer per rank on a 1-byte checkpoint (#16967).

title: [Test][Ops] Fix MLA preprocess no-quant test cache layout
body:
## Why

`test_mla_preprocess_nq.py` passed 4-D NZ-shaped caches while selecting `cache_mode="krope_ctkv"`, which is an ND cache mode. Host tiling consequently read a block size of 32 and a RoPE head dimension of 16 instead of 128 and 64. The query output was also sized from the cache trailing axis rather than the logical KV rank, allowing an out-of-bounds device write that surfaced later as error 507015.

## What

- Keep the no-quant `wuk` tensor in ND format.
- Build the KV and RoPE caches with ND `[block_num, block_size, dim]` layouts.
- Allocate outputs using the corrected logical dimensions.
- Use NaN sentinels and an explicit stream synchronization to verify writes and surface asynchronous faults at the operator boundary.
- Remove the skip marker.

## Notes

- Verified repeatedly on the same Ascend NPU environment; both RoPE-enabled and RoPE-disabled cases pass:

```bash
pytest -sv tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_mla_preprocess_nq.py
```

- Tests only; no operator behaviour is changed.

title: [Test][Ops] Fix MLA preprocess QDown test cache layouts
body:
## Why

`test_mla_preprocess_qdown.py` constructed both cache modes with 4-D NZ-like tensors and sized query outputs from the physical cache trailing axes. For `krope_ctkv`, the host expects an ND cache; for `nzcache`, the physical C1 axis must be derived from the logical dimension without multiplying by the query head count.

The mismatched shapes made host tiling derive incorrect block and RoPE dimensions and allowed the kernel to write beyond the undersized query buffers. The asynchronous device fault then surfaced at a later synchronization point as error 507015.

## What

- Build `krope_ctkv` caches as ND `[block_num, block_size, dim]` tensors.
- Build `nzcache` caches as physical NZ `[block_num, dim // 16, block_size, 16]` tensors.
- Allocate query outputs from `kv_lora_rank` and `rope_dim` rather than physical cache axes.
- Initialize outputs with NaN sentinels, synchronize explicitly, assert each expected output is written, and remove the skip.

## Notes

- Verified repeatedly on the same Ascend NPU environment; all cache-mode and RoPE parameter combinations pass:

```bash
pytest -sv tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_mla_preprocess_qdown.py
```

- Tests only; no operator behaviour is changed.

title: [Feature] Add FLA RecurrentGDN Backend
body:
### Overview
This change introduces a switchable backend for the GDN decode recurrent operator. A new configuration item, `gdn_decode_backend1`, allows selection between `fla_npu` and native custom operators. The mechanism covers all three decode paths:

| Path | Location |
| :--- | :--- |
| 2.1 MTP spec decode | `AscendGatedDeltaNetAttention.forward` spec branch |
| 2.2 Mixed-batch non-spec decode | `split_non_spec` decode branch |
| 2.3 Prefill chunk / pure decode | non-spec branch |

### Performance
We conducted tests across 50 scenarios at the single-operator level, comparing the performance of operators in the fla package against the original recurrent operators. For recurrent_gated_delta_rule, the fla implementation reduced the average latency from 538us to 148us.

### How to use
Add extra addtional-config : `vllm serve xxx --additional-config '"gdn_decode_backend1": "fla_npu"`

Verified via the GitCode contents API for `Ascend/memfabric_hybrid`:
`script/` on `develop` contains 15 entries (`kernel/`, `run_pkg_maker/`,
`sign/`, `signtool/`, `README.md`, `build.sh`, `build_and_pack_run.sh`,
`ci-pre-commit-pr.sh`, `ci_devcontainer_check.sh`,

Note: the file is still present on `release/1.1`. I chose to drop the
