title: [BugFix][MoE] Guard fused MC2 dispatch against silent capacity truncation
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes silent output corruption in the fused MC2 MoE path (`enable_fused_mc2=1`) for long-context prefill.

**Root cause.** The `dispatch_ffn_combine` op sizes its internal per-rank token buffers from `max_output_size` and **silently discards work** once the per-rank post-dispatch token count reaches it:

```cpp
if (preCurrentmSum >= params.maxOutputSize) { currentM = 0; }
else if (preCurrentmSum + currentM > params.maxOutputSize)
    currentM = params.maxOutputSize - preCurrentmSum;
```

No error is raised — the affected tokens simply receive a corrupted MoE output, which surfaces as repeated/garbage tokens (issue #16941) and destroys the argmax margin.

`additional_config.mega_moe_max_tokens` is documented (`ascend_config.py`) as sizing **both** the op's `max_output_size` **and** the CANN MegaMoe symmetric buffer's `max_recv_token_num`, but only the op side was effectively guarded. The mean post-dispatch count per rank is `num_tokens * num_experts_per_tok`; measured load reaches **~4.9x that mean** on GLM-5.2 w4a8 / A3 / EP16, so the historical `65536` default does not cover long-context prefill chunks.

**Measured** (GLM-5.2-w4a8, A3, EP16, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` with 4-way context parallelism → 2048 tokens per rank per op call, topk 8):

| | per-rank post-dispatch load |
|---|---|
| median | 14,923 |
| p99 | 44,332 |
| max | 70,990 |
| single expert max | 31,711 (4.3x mean, **108% of the 65536 default**) |

Same service, same 67531-token request, greedy, 512 tokens:

| op capacity | peer buffer | truncated calls | clean requests |
|---|---|---|---|
| 65536 | 65536 | 9 / 58800 | 0 / 6 |
| **131072** | 65536 | 0 / 58800 | 6 / 6 |
| 131072 | 131072 | — | 6 / 6 |

Reproduced independently with `mega_moe_max_tokens=8192` on a 67531-token prompt: **273/288 op calls truncated and 28/288 produced NaN rows**, while the same request with `65536` answers correctly.

**Changes:**

- `_fused_mc2_required_capacity()` — rank-invariant lower bound derived **only from compile-time configuration** (the symmetric buffer is allocated by a collective handshake, so every EP rank must compute the same value):
  `max(token_dispatcher.max_num_tokens_per_rank, global_bs // ep_world_size, max_num_batched_tokens // tensor_parallel_size) * num_experts_per_tok * 8`. Cached, logged once.
- `_fused_mc2_capacity()` — `max(configured, required)` plus a one-time warning naming both buffers and the `--max-num-batched-tokens` alternative.
- Use it for **both** the op's `max_output_size` and the P / PD-mixed peer buffer (`max_recv_token_num`), instead of the raw configured value.
- `_verify_fused_mc2_no_truncation()` — raise instead of returning silently corrupted tokens. Skipped when truncation is provably impossible (`num_tokens * topk * ep_world_size < max_output_size`), so the decode path stays free of device syncs.
- Pass a **copy** of `topk_ids` as `expert_idx`: the op rewrites non-active entries in place (`ApplyXActiveMask` writes `expertPerRank * EP`), mutating the caller's routing tensor.

### Does this PR introduce *any* user-facing change?

Yes, two ways:

1. **Long-context prefill output changes** — previously silently corrupted under the fused MC2 path, now correct.
2. **Memory cost**: raising the capacity from `65536` to `131072` takes **21632 KV cache tokens** on this model (207744 → 186112, **−10.4%**), because the operator workspace and the peer buffer scale linearly with the value. Lowering `--max-num-batched-tokens` shrinks the requirement by the same factor if the KV cache is needed. A one-time warning states the value in use and how to silence it.

Previously valid configurations keep their exact behaviour when the computed requirement does not exceed the configured value.

### How was this patch tested?

- **Operator capacity A/B** (table above): identical request, capacity switched at runtime — `65536` → 9/58800 truncated, 0/6 clean; `131072` → 0/58800 truncated, 6/6 clean.
- **Minimal repro** with `mega_moe_max_tokens=8192` on a 67531-token prompt: 273/288 calls truncated + 28/288 NaN rows before; correct after.
- **Changing the op capacity alone** is sufficient for this workload, which confirms silent truncation is the root cause of the garbled long-context output. The peer buffer is raised as well so both stay consistent, as the vendor comment requires.

### Remaining (not addressed here, needs the operator side)

The fused MC2 path is **still not bit-reproducible**. Two identical greedy prefills of the same 67531-token prompt disagree on **17–36%** of positions at capacity `65536` and on **1–2%** at `131072` (top-1 agreement 0.64–0.83 per position bin), while `enable_fused_mc2=0` is bit-exact. The truncation fix roughly halves the drift but does not remove it.

### Related

- Issue #16941 — garbled / repeated tokens from silent truncation
- `vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py` — `mega_moe_max_tokens` documentation

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [BugFix][KV Pool] Fix layerwise cache group indexing under PP
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

With layerwise AscendStore and multiple KV cache groups, a nonzero PP stage can raise `IndexError` in `LayerBatchBuilder._build_transfer_arrays()` when indexing `_layer_cache_entry_offsets_np`. The group map has used stage-local layer IDs since #16412, but #16208 added the global PP offset when looking up save/load tasks. A missed lookup falls back to group 0 with a stage-local index that can exceed that group's layer count or select the wrong cache address.

Use stage-local IDs in the GVA branch of `_groups_for_layerwise_transfer()`, which now serves both save and load on main. Pool key and remote-address offsets remain unchanged. Extend the existing PP regression test through real save/load task and address construction for both PP stages, checking the local layer/task counts and expected tensor addresses.

Enable GLM-5.3-Flash non-layerwise KV pooling with its mixed NoPE MLA, compressed indexer, request-private circular tails and TP-sharded KDA state. Private tails must not participate in prefix hashing or pool transfer, and an empty RoPE view must not be registered at address zero.

Reworks #16854 on current main, with the original author credited through `Co-authored-by: Pz1116 <zpbzpb123123@gmail.com>`.

- Exclude non-prefix-cacheable groups while preserving group-indexed slots and existing key formats.
- Resume full-prefix hits at a complete page/state boundary so the request-private tail can be rebuilt.
- Preserve shared MLA keys, per-rank KDA payloads and all-rank hit checks.

Scope is GLM-specific KV pooling adaptation. Quantization loading, MTP implementation, native SFA operators, PD environment fixes and acceptance instrumentation are outside this PR.

Common hybrid KV-load failure recovery is explicitly out of scope. This PR does not patch the upstream scheduler or change baseline synchronous/asynchronous hybrid invalid-block reporting. The baseline hybrid load-failure limitation remains unresolved and will be handled separately; this PR does not claim safe failure recovery.

Enables GLM-5.3-Flash non-layerwise pooling with the hybrid cache manager enabled and `--mamba-cache-mode align`.

Memcache layerwise support is a separate dependent PR. Upstream Mooncake layerwise restrictions for recurrent Mamba/KDA state remain unchanged.

title: [Feature][Model] Support DeepSeek V4 Vision with DSA-CP
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds DeepSeek V4 Vision support to the legacy MRV1 DSA context-parallel path after the base Vision support landed in #15457.

The regular DSA metadata builder already creates bidirectional sliding-window indices for image spans. The DSA-CP builder did not carry those indices into its rank-local metadata, so Vision requests with `additional_config.enable_dsa_cp=true` lost the image-aware attention mask.

This change:

- builds the global Vision SWA indices from `mm_req_doc_ranges` in the legacy DSA-CP metadata builder;
- pads and slices them to the token range owned by each TP rank;
- forwards the rank-local indices to the DSA attention operator;
- fixes MRV1 DP graph padding so padded request slots reuse the last cumulative token offset instead of repeating the real scheduled-token vector. The old behavior can produce a source/destination shape mismatch while capturing a padded FULL_DECODE graph.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. DeepSeek V4 Vision can now be served with the legacy MRV1 DSA-CP path by setting `additional_config.enable_dsa_cp=true`.

### How was this patch tested?

- `python -m py_compile` on the four changed Python files.
- On an Ascend 800I A3 container:

  PYTHONPATH=/vllm-workspace/dsv4-vision-dsa-cp-pr:/vllm-workspace/vllm \
    pytest -q tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_v1.py \
      tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v1.py

title: [BugFix] Add off-stride graph capture size ceilings
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix off-stride default CUDAGraph capture sizes on Ascend. Fixes #16049 .

When `max_num_seqs` is not on the default capture-size grid, the largest decode batches could fall back to eager execution. This change preserves Ascend's reduced capture ceiling for memory savings while adding the exact ceiling to the capture-size list before upstream finalizes the graph configuration.

For example, `max_num_seqs=77` now produces a capture size of 77 and dispatches the largest decode batch to a FULL graph.

## Why this approach?

The exact ceiling is added while reusing upstream capture-size generation and filtering, so Ascend does not duplicate the upstream size-grid logic. Rounding the ceiling to 8/16, as in PR #16692, leaves the padded graph unreachable for FULL decode; duplicating the grid logic, as in PR #16623, increases long-term maintenance cost.

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No new configuration option is introduced. Off-stride default decode batches can now use CUDAGraphs instead of falling back to eager execution.

## How was this patch tested?

- `tests/ut/test_platform.py`
- A/B configuration and dispatcher check with `max_num_seqs=77`
- Baseline: capture sizes ended at 72 and batch 77 dispatched to `NONE`
- Fixed: capture sizes include 77 and batch 77 dispatched to `FULL`
- Result: `93 passed, 1 skipped`

title: [CPP][Spec Decode] Disable profiling chunk for draft models
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR prevents Chunked Pipeline Parallelism (CPP) profiling-chunk configuration from being applied to speculative draft models.

Draft models used by MTP, EAGLE, DSpark, and the 310P MTP path should not inherit the target model's profiling-chunk settings. Applying CPP to those draft models can create an unsupported scheduler configuration during speculative decoding. The target model keeps its CPP configuration; only the draft-model configuration is disabled.

The PR also separates CPP-enabled speculative-decoding E2E cases from the base MTP/DSpark tests so failures are isolated and both configurations retain independent coverage.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Speculative decoding with CPP no longer enables profiling chunk on the draft model, avoiding unsupported draft-model scheduling while preserving CPP on the target model.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added and updated unit coverage for MTP, EAGLE, DSpark, and the 310P speculative-decoding paths.
- Added a dedicated four-card Qwen3.5 PP + MTP + CPP E2E test.
- Added a dedicated eight-card DeepSeek V4 DSpark PP + CPP accuracy E2E test.
- Registered the new E2E files in the CI estimated-times configuration.
- GitHub Actions is running on the head branch.

title: [Refactor] delete VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASHCOMM1 env
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

FlashComm1 was still enabled by the `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASHCOMM1` environment variable, which was kept only as a compatibility path. This PR removes that path so FlashComm1 is enabled only through `additional_config.enable_flashcomm1` (`--additional-config '{"enable_flashcomm1": true}'`). `enable_dsa_cp` still auto-enables FlashComm1.

- `vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py` no longer reads `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASHCOMM1`.
- Docs, tutorial templates, translations, and the model-adapter skill are updated to the `additional_config` switch.
- Weekly and nightly e2e configs that set the env var are converted in place: `1` / `true` becomes `"enable_flashcomm1": true`, `0` becomes `false`, and commented-out env lines are deleted without turning the feature on.
- For PD configs, the flag is added only on the nodes that previously set the env var. Prefill-on / decode-off cases stay that way, including the GLM-5.2 Memcache PD case.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASHCOMM1` no longer enables FlashComm1. Use `--additional-config '{"enable_flashcomm1": true}'` instead.

### How was this patch tested?

- Updated the existing FlashComm1 unit tests in `tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py` so they no longer mock the removed env var.
- Migrated weekly and nightly e2e YAML configs to `additional_config.enable_flashcomm1` and checked that each node's previous on/off state is unchanged.
- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek V4 now uses Model Runner V2 by default, while two external-DP nightly cases still enable the legacy DSA-CP path on prefill nodes.

This PR migrates those prefill configurations to native PCP while preserving their device counts:

- DeepSeek-V4-Flash: DP4 x TP1 x PCP4, still 16 NPUs.
- DeepSeek-V4-Pro: DP4 x TP2 x PCP4, still 32 NPUs across two prefill nodes.
- Remove enable_dsa_cp from the prefill additional configuration.
- Explicitly set VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 for both nightly cases.
- Align MooncakeHybridConnector prefill.tp_size with the actual prefill TP size: 1 for Flash and 2 for Pro. Decode topology is unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This only updates nightly CI deployment configurations.

### How was this patch tested?

- conda run --no-capture-output -n vllm-ascend-dev ./format.sh ci

title: [Feature][SpecDecode] Enable ACL graph mode for GLM-Next MTP draft models
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it

GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`, draft model `glm5_next_mtp`) uses MTP speculative decoding with draft layers split across multiple physical KV-cache groups:

- primary MLA attention
- indexer KPool
- compressor tail

The generic GLM speculative-decoding path previously forced the draft model to run eagerly. In addition, the multi-KV-group runtime metadata was rebuilt using per-round tensor clones. Although correct in eager mode, these dynamically allocated tensors are incompatible with ACL graph replay, which requires the captured input addresses to remain stable.

This PR enables ACL graph mode for the specialized `AscendMultiKVCacheGroupMTPProposer` used by `glm5_next_mtp`. 

Other GLM speculative-decoding implementations remain forced to eager mode. Users can still explicitly keep the GLM-Next MTP draft eager by setting `"enforce_eager": true` in the speculative configuration.

The main changes are:

1. **GLM-Next MTP graph capability**

   The specialized multi-KV-group proposer declares support for GLM draft graph mode. The generic GLM forced-eager behavior remains unchanged for other GLM draft implementations.

2. **Graph-stable common metadata**

   Persistent per-`(KV-cache group, draft step)` slot-mapping buffers replace per-round clones. Capture and runtime drafting therefore reuse the same tensor addresses.

3. **Graph-stable KPool derived metadata**

   `AscendIndexerKPoolMetadataBuilder` keeps persistent buffers for:

   - compressed slot mappings
   - sequence lengths
   - cumulative query lengths
   - raw sequence lengths
   - positions

   The buffers are keyed by the persistent common slot-mapping address so that capture and replay bind the same storage.

4. **FULL graph padding support**

   Request-shaped KPool metadata buffers are sized using:

   ```python
   max(max_num_seqs, max_num_batched_tokens)
   ```

   This covers FULL draft graph padding, where the padded request dimension may exceed `max_num_seqs`. For example, four requests with MTP K=3 use a 16-token graph bucket.

5. **Cache-only builder graph entrypoints**

   `build_for_graph_capture` and `build_for_drafting` are implemented for the KPool and KPool-tail cache-only metadata builders.

6. **Multi-group graph-capture routing**

   Graph capture builds a separate metadata view for each physical KV-cache group and routes executable and cache-only groups through their appropriate metadata-builder entrypoints.

7. **FULL-mode sequence-length robustness**

   `seq_lens_cpu` may be intentionally invalidated during the first MTP draft transition to avoid a device-to-host synchronization. The FULL-mode updater now handles the field being `None`, consistently with the existing guards for `_seq_lens_cpu` and `num_computed_tokens_cpu`.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Yes.

When ACL graph mode is enabled for the target model, `glm5_next_mtp` drafting now uses ACL graph mode by default. Other GLM speculative draft implementations remain eager.

Users can explicitly disable draft graph mode with:

```json
{
  "method": "mtp",
  "num_speculative_tokens": 3,
  "enforce_eager": true
}
```

The first request using a previously uncaptured draft bucket may incur a one-time lazy graph-capture cost of approximately 10–15 seconds. Subsequent replays use the captured graph.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Unit tests

Extended:

- `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_multi_kv_cache_group_proposer.py`
- `tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_kv_cache.py`

The tests cover:

- persistent address semantics across metadata rebuilds
- independent buffers for different MTP draft steps
- KPool graph-capture and drafting entrypoints
- FULL-mode operation with absent CPU sequence lengths
- padded `num_reqs` exceeding `max_num_seqs`
- multi-group graph-capture metadata routing

The targeted unit-test suites pass with 40+ test cases.

#### End-to-end validation

Hardware and configuration:

- Atlas A3, 8 × Ascend 910
- tensor parallel size 8
- expert parallel enabled
- GLM-5.3-Flash W8A8
- MTP K=3
- target graph mode: `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`
- graph capture sizes up to 128

Results:

- draft buckets 4, 8, 16 and 32 passed
- request concurrency 1, 2, 4 and 8 passed
- all requests returned coherent output
- rejection-sampler acceptance remained 75%–100%
- greedy graph-mode output was bit-exact with the eager baseline across
  20 `(prompt, concurrency)` pairs
- repeated graph batches produced identical output, with no stale-metadata
  regression

Steady-state latency at concurrency 4 improved from 1.028 s to 0.863 s (approximately 1.19×).

At concurrency 8, graph mode also reduced latency. The measured mean was 1.984 s to 1.073 s, although the eager sample contained several approximately 5-second outliers; the corresponding median changed from approximately 1.25 s to 1.10 s.

### Notes

The remaining family-wide GLM forced-eager path is intentionally retained for GLM draft implementations that have not declared graph support.

title: [Feature][Sample] Add Triton apply_top_k_top_p fused op for sampling
body:
## What

A Triton implementation of top-k/top-p filtering for the sampler, opt-in via `VLLM_ASCEND_USE_TRITON_APPLY_TOPK_TOPP=1` (default off). Two entry points:

- `apply_top_k_top_p` — masked logits, bit-exact with `torch_npu.npu_top_k_top_p` (`torch.equal` on fp32/bf16/fp16)
- `fused_topk_topp_softmax` — same filtering with the final softmax folded into the kernel, returns fp32 probs directly; this is the branch the sampler uses when logprobs are not requested

Both take the per-request `[B]` k/p tensors from `_get_topk_topp_constraints()` as-is. The CANN op forces a `.item()` on that tensor (host sync on every decode step); this op doesn't.

## How it works

The host does the sort once (`torch.sort`, ascending, stable) and the kernel only works on the sorted row. Because the input is ascending, both the top-k mask (`s >= topk_value`) and the top-p mask (`cumsum > 1 - p`) are suffix-monotone, so the kept set collapses to a single scalar boundary `m = max(m_p, m_k)` per row. The kernel then only scatters the surviving suffix (~k elements) into a pre-filled output — the non-surviving positions are one contiguous block write instead of V random stores.

I used a scalar boundary rather than a cumsum-derived boolean vector as the scatter mask on purpose: triton-ascend 3.2.2 miscompiles that pattern (the store collapses to a few elements). The `v >= m` comparison mask sidesteps it.

![kernel flow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/15625122759/vllm-ascend/pr-assets/docs/pr17211/kernel_flow.png)

Two kernel paths: V ≤ 4096 loads the row in one block; larger vocabularies go tiled — pass 1 accumulates the softmax denominator, pass 2 walks tiles until the cumulative probability crosses `1 - p` (early exit; `tl.cumsum` runs only inside the crossing tile), pass 3 only touches the kept suffix. `m_p`/`m_k` can be looser than the exact CANN cutoffs; the final `v >= m` mask restores exactness, so the output stays bit-exact.

The sampler wiring prefers logprobs-preserving paths: when `raw_logprobs` is requested it falls back to the masked-logits variant + separate softmax/log_softmax.

## Enabling it

With `VLLM_ASCEND_USE_TRITON_APPLY_TOPK_TOPP=1` the sampler logs once at startup:

![switch log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/15625122759/vllm-ascend/pr-assets/docs/pr17211/enable_log.png)

## Performance

Test environment: single Ascend 910B3 (linux aarch64), CANN 9.0.0, torch 2.10.0 / torch_npu 2.10.0.post4, triton-ascend 3.2.2. Model: `Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8` (w8a8-quantized, vocab 151936). Serving benchmark command (identical for both runs):

```bash
vllm bench serve --model $MODEL_PATH --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 \
    --random-output-len 128 --num-prompts 300 --request-rate 10 \
    --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --temperature 0.6 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl
```

E2E serving benchmark, stock vs this PR (300/300 successful requests, identical total input/output tokens; 存量=stock, 改造后=this PR):

![serving bench](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/15625122759/vllm-ascend/pr-assets/docs/pr17211/serving_bench.png)

## Accuracy

![triton acc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/15625122759/vllm-ascend/pr-assets/docs/pr17211/acc_triton.png)
![stock acc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/15625122759/vllm-ascend/pr-assets/docs/pr17211/acc_stock.png)

## Tests

- `op/test_smoke.py` + `op/op_perf_test.sh`: 10-case matrix, fp32/bf16, single-pass + tiled paths, per-row k/p tensor and scalar inputs, k<0/k=0/k>V edge cases, determinism; bit-exact (`torch.equal`) vs `torch_npu.npu_top_k_top_p` + 20 randomized stress cases (N=1…1e5)
- `tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_apply_top_k_top_p.py`: 6 smoke cases incl. V=32000 tiled and per-row tensors
- ruff/mypy clean

Note on CI: `pre-commit` currently fails on `vllm_ascend/xlite/xlite.py:663` (`XModelConfig has no attribute index_full_mask`) — that's pre-existing on main since #16669; `tools/mypy.sh` type-checks the whole package so it fires on any PR. Nothing in this PR's files is flagged.

## Known limitations

- `tl.cumsum` lowers to an element-serial runtime call on triton-ascend 3.2.2 (~29.7us per 2048-wide tile vs ~0.2us for `tl.sum`, measured). The tiled kernel only runs it inside the single threshold-crossing tile, so the impact is small, but it would be nice to have a tree-scan lowering in the backend.
- The host-side `torch.sort` (~100-470us depending on B/V) stays. Callers that already hold sorted logits can use the `*_with_sorted` variants and skip it.

title: [BugFix][EPLB] Cover redundant physical experts in A2 ALLGATHER expert maps
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #14080.

With EPLB (`num_redundant_experts > 0`) on A2 (910B) + MRv1, the MoE **ALLGATHER** path crashes during decode CUDA-graph capture / first forward:

```
Index out of range in dimension 0: index value 263 exceeds bounds 256!
index_check.h:130 IndexCheckKernel<int>::ProcessScalar ... (idx < bound)
```

Two independent data points, same signature (bound == logical expert count, index == a redundant **physical** expert ID):

| Case | Logical experts | Redundant | Crash |
|---|---|---|---|
| #14080 (Qwen3-30B-A3B, EP=2) | 128 | 2 | `129 > 128` |
| User report (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8, EP=4/TP=4) | 256 | 16 | `263 > 256` |

**Root cause.** With EPLB, vLLM allocates *physical* experts (`num_experts = logical + redundant`, e.g. 256+16=272) and the router maps logical topk IDs to global physical IDs via `log2phy` (`routed_experts.py::_select_experts`). The A2 ALLGATHER dispatcher then builds its routing mask as:

```python
# token_dispatcher.py (pre-fix)
global_num_experts = len(expert_map) + global_redundant_expert_num   # 272 — correct
mask = expert_map[topk_ids] != -1                                    # OOB — expert_map has length 256
```

`layer.ascend_expert_map` was built in `init_eplb_config` over **logical** IDs only (`torch.full((n_experts,), -1)`), so physical IDs in `[256, 272)` trip the CANN `Index` op's embedded `IndexCheckKernel` (`idx < bound`), where the bound is the tensor's dim-0 (256). The crash fires from the first forward because the initial EPLB placement already puts redundant copies into the tail physical slots — no rebalance cycle is required.

The `expert_num` passed to `npu_moe_init_routing` was already the physical total; the mask map was the one overlooked site. (Forensic elimination of the other in-graph indexing ops — `npu_moe_init_routing`, `log2phy[topk_ids]`, MC2/MegaMoe paths — is in the full analysis below.)

**Why only A2.** A3 selects `FUSED_MC2` (MegaMoe consumes `topk_ids` + `moe_expert_num` = physical total, never indexes this map) and plain MC2 passes `moe_expert_num = len(expert_map) + redundant`. A2 has no `CANN_MEGAMOE` capability and the capacity/expert-density selector falls to ALLGATHER (the only consumer that indexes `expert_map` with physical topk IDs). A2 without EPLB has `log2phy is None` (IDs stay logical) — unaffected.

**The fix.** One invariant: `ascend_expert_map` is always a **global-physical → local-slot** map of length `num_experts` (logical + redundant). All consumers use the physical length directly or the new `phys_to_logical` bridge. `log2phy` output stays logical-length (router input unchanged).

Two adjacent latent bugs on the same path are fixed too — without them dynamic EPLB would die one cycle after the crash fix:

1. **Heat collection shape mismatch**: `npu_moe_init_routing` returns per-*global*-expert counts (`[num_experts]`) while `moe_load` is sized `num_local_experts` → `add_` shape error at the first EPLB cycle. Now gathered to per-slot counts via a new `local_phys_expert_ids` NPU buffer (size-guarded so MC2/FusedMC2 per-local counts pass through untouched).
2. **Stale layer maps after rebalance**: only the CPU bookkeeping copy was refreshed; `layer.ascend_expert_map` / `global_expert_map` kept pointing at pre-rebalance slots (silent misrouting). `update_ascend_eplb_maps` refreshes them, and the record file is written with logical IDs (it previously stored physical slot positions).

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `vllm_ascend/eplb/core/eplb_utils.py` | `init_eplb_config`: per-rank maps built full-length; returns `phys_to_logical` (flat placement, uniform for generated and file layouts); `generate_log2phy_map(..., phys_to_logical=None)` — physical-row grouping, output stays logical-length; `None` keeps the legacy behavior exactly. |
| `vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/routed_experts.py` | stores `phys_to_logical`; new `compute_local_phys_expert_ids`; `init_eplb` builds the NPU `local_phys_expert_ids` buffer; `update_ascend_eplb_maps` refreshes runtime maps; `forward_impl` gathers the global histogram into per-slot counts. |
| `vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/token_dispatcher.py` | AllGather: `global_num_experts = self.num_experts` (physical total from `moe_config`) — value-identical in every existing case, immune to the map-length invariant; MC2: `moe_expert_num = len(expert_map)` (physical length) — value-identical. |
| `vllm_ascend/eplb/core/eplb_worker.py`, `vllm_ascend/eplb/eplb_updator.py` | `phys_to_logical` published through `shared_dict` during `warm_up_eplb` and consumed in `pack_update_info`. |
| `vllm_ascend/eplb/adaptor/vllm_adaptor.py` | record file converts physical → logical IDs; `do_update_expert_map` refreshes layer runtime maps. |

The EPLB worker machinery (global2local/local2global, policies) is slot-value based and layout-agnostic — unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API/interface change. Behavior change is limited to A2 + MRv1 + EPLB with `num_redundant_experts > 0`, which previously crashed: dynamic and static EPLB now run. A3 (FUSED_MC2/MC2/ALLTOALL), A2 without EPLB, and MRv2 paths are value-identical pre/post patch.

### How was this patch tested?

- CPU UT (vllm 0.28.0, torch 2.13+cpu), `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on touched files:

  ```
  pytest tests/ut/ops/test_routed_experts.py tests/ut/eplb tests/ut/quantization tests/ut/_310p
  ```

  All pass; full-suite delta vs. the base commit is zero (the same 16 pre-existing CPU-environment failures occur on the base commit).
- New regression tests pinning the crash invariant:
  - `test_eplb_utils.py::test_allgather_mask_indexing_covers_physical_topk_ids` — `log2phy`-mapped IDs index the physical-length map in range, with the expected owned/not-owned mask (N=8, R=2, EP=2).
  - `test_eplb_utils.py::test_generate_log2phy_map_physical_layout_matches_logical_layout` / `..._with_tp_rotation` — physical-row mode ≡ legacy logical-row mode; output stays logical-length.
  - `test_routed_experts.py::test_compute_local_phys_expert_ids_orders_by_slot`, `test_update_ascend_eplb_maps_refreshes_runtime_maps`.
  - `test_vllm_adaptor.py::test_do_update_expert_map_refreshes_layer_runtime_maps`, `test_export_tensor_to_file_writes_logical_expert_ids`.
- A standalone CPU script verified `init_eplb_config` for the dynamic, static-file, and no-EPLB layouts against hand-computed ground truths, plus the `do_update_expert_map`/export flows.
- NPU e2e not run locally; **please re-enable `test_moe_tp_ep_eplb_full_decode_only` (Qwen3-30B-A3B, EP=2, `num_redundant_experts=2`, A2) in the CI flow** — it is the #14080 repro and the direct acceptance gate for this patch (graph capture completes, traffic serves, EPLB cycles run without `IndexCheck` / shape errors after the first rebalance). A3 FUSED_MC2 regression is covered by the existing eplb e2e set.

Full root-cause analysis (forensic elimination, data-flow diagram, per-path equivalence argument) is available on request — the branch contains a single commit.

title: [MRV2][BugFix][Kernel] Fix and optimize sampling mask packing on Ascend
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The sampling-mask kernel can overflow UB on Triton-Ascend when
`logits.stride(1) > 1`. For a batch-32, vocabulary-151936, stride-2
input, the original BLOCK_SIZE=8192 kernel fails compilation with:

`ub overflow, requires 12583424 bits while 1572864 bits available`

The implementation also has two Ascend-specific lowering issues:

- reducing the boolean keep mask does not produce the required finite-logit
  count;
- per-element variable shifts and the `[512, 8]` axis-1 reduction lower to
  scalar-heavy execution.

This PR adds an Ascend implementation for both the three-field bitmask API
and the four-field compact-ID plus bitmask API. Both interfaces launch the
same Ascend packing kernel. It:

- makes only strided vocabulary inputs contiguous, without modifying the
  caller's tensor;
- casts the keep mask to int32 before reduction;
- uses BLOCK_SIZE=4096 to remain within the NPU UB limit;
- transposes the packing layout from `[512, 8]` to `[8, 512]`, multiplies by
  compile-time bit weights, and reduces axis 0;
- routes both sampling-mask APIs through the same Ascend packing kernel;
- returns a zero-width `token_ids` tensor for the four-field API so its existing
  `tolists()` method uses the exact packed-mask fallback;
- logs a warning once per process when the four-field compact token-ID path is
  requested;
- adds operator documentation and registers the NPU regression test in the
  A2 single-card nightly matrix.

The four-field compatibility path preserves sampling results but temporarily
gives up the compact token-ID transfer optimization on Ascend. It avoids the
`tl.cumsum`-based dynamic scatter that hangs with Triton-Ascend 3.2.2.

The following msprof results use an Ascend 910, `npu:0`, 10 profiling
rounds, and `MemoryDetail,Occupancy,PipeUtilization,Roofline`. Values are
selected kernel task durations and exclude Python wrapper time and the
preceding contiguous copy.

| Case | Baseline | Optimized | Speedup | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `b1_v17_active1_colstride1` | 123.330 us | 5.640 us | 21.87x | 95.43% |
| `b8_v8191_active1_colstride1` | 244.573 us | 6.960 us | 35.14x | 97.15% |
| `b8_v8192_active1_colstride1` | 244.327 us | 6.680 us | 36.58x | 97.27% |
| `b8_v8193_active1_colstride1` | 365.349 us | 8.940 us | 40.87x | 97.55% |
| `b8_v8193_active0_colstride1` | 365.357 us | 8.780 us | 41.61x | 97.60% |
| `b32_v151936_active1_colstride2` | 4604.258 us | 84.758 us | 54.32x | 98.16% |
| `b128_v151936_active1_colstride1` | 18403.968 us | 327.093 us | 56.27x | 98.22% |

The original stride-2 BLOCK_SIZE=8192 implementation has no runtime
duration because it fails compilation with UB overflow. The table uses
the first compilable correctness-fixed implementation with the original
variable-shift packing as the performance baseline.

TTIR/NPU IR inspection confirms that the optimized packing lowers to
vector transpose, multiply, and reduction operations; the previous
tensor-wide scalar shift loop is absent.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?

Correctness revalidation environment:

- Ascend 910
- Python 3.12.13
- Torch 2.10.0
- torch-npu 2.10.0.post4
- Triton-Ascend 3.2.2
- CANN 9.1.0

The NPU regression test passed against both version-specific interfaces:

- pinned vLLM main `84030bbe3` four-field API: `4 passed`.

The performance data above was collected with Triton-Ascend 3.2.2.

The regression test verifies:

- finite support sizes 0, 1, 7, 511, 512, 513, 2048, 2053, and the full vocabulary;
- random sparse token positions and a vocabulary size not divisible by eight;
- active and inactive rows, including `num_sampled_tokens > 1`;
- NaN and positive/negative infinity exclusion;
- non-contiguous `logits` with `stride(1) == 2` and an unmodified caller view;
- exact packed masks, counts, and decoded token IDs;
- on the later four-field main API, a zero-width compact buffer, one compatibility
  warning per process, and exact token IDs through the packed-mask fallback.

The regression is registered as the A2 single-card nightly case
`sampling-mask`. The nightly matrix resolver was run locally and produced
the expected test path and `linux-aarch64-a2b3-1` runner.

Seven profiling cases covering small, tile-boundary, inactive, strided,
large-vocabulary, and large-batch inputs passed correctness checks. An
additional patterned vocabulary-size-17 case passed exact bit-order,
tail-byte, and count checks.

The following repository checks passed:

- `bash format.sh`
- `python -m compileall`
- `git diff --check`
- nightly matrix resolution for `a2.single_node.test_config`
- `SHELLCHECK_OPTS="--exclude=SC2046,SC2006,SC2086" pre-commit run
  --all-files --hook-stage manual --show-diff-on-failure`

title: [Feature][Attention] Add A5 FlashMLA BF16 and C8 model execution
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add the A5 FlashMLA BF16/C8 reader and its real dense-MLA model execution path. **Depends on #17198 (shared A5/C8 headers and FlashAttn prefill), #17297 (DCP exchange/combine helpers), and #17298 (output gate/masking).** Those implementations are deliberately not copied here; this PR is a separate review unit and is not independently mergeable before its dependencies. #17190 is an optional MLAPO preprocessing optimization, selected only when its operators are available.

The implementation includes:

- Native BF16/C8 paged reader, AICPU schedule producer, compressed-cache gather and BF16 prefill preparation, with PrivateUse1/Meta bindings and A5 build entries. C8 reuses the shared pipeline in #17198.
- Actual `AscendMLAImpl.forward` routing through BF16 decode, C8 quantized history, BF16 current chunks, DCP output merge, bounded expanded prefill and mixed decode/prefill. C8 query/KV scales come from the existing quantization contract. Optional MLAPO operator bodies are not part of this PR.
- Isolated Flash metadata helpers, graph-stable buffers populated from device lengths, and MRv1/MRv2 cache/spec/metadata/zeroing integration. FP8 latent and BF16 positional planes preserve manager page padding and neighboring storage.
- Kimi replicated-Q projection wiring and dense-MLA draft capture/replay integration. GQA and recurrent-state cache layouts retain their existing paths. No Conv1d, EPLB, KDA, PP scheduling or output-projection operator changes are included.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

The opt-in `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASH_MLA=1` enables the backend for dense MLA; default is `0`. The supported model contract is BF16 activations, latent width 512, positional width 64, one KV head, BF16 or calibrated FP8 E4M3 cache, and PCP1. Kernel pages are 128 tokens. Kimi TP8/DCP8 selects replicated Q before weight loading.

The normal projection/quantization C8 path remains usable without the optional MLAPO package. No end-to-end throughput or native accuracy result is claimed from CPU validation.

### How was this patch tested?

217 CPU cases passed across focused attention and worker tests:

```bash
python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/ut/attention \
  tests/ut/attention/test_flash_attention_metadata.py \
  tests/ut/attention/test_flash_mla_c8_prefill.py \
  tests/ut/attention/test_flash_mla_prefill_cpu.py \
  tests/ut/attention/test_flash_dcp_mlapo_cpu.py \
  tests/ut/attention/test_mlapo_input_quant_cpu.py \
  tests/ut/attention/test_mla_dcp_q_replicate.py \
  tests/ut/attention/test_kimi_dcp_q_replicate_default_cpu.py -q
python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/ut/worker \
  tests/ut/worker/test_flash_mla_cache_views_cpu.py \
  tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v2_device_metadata_cpu.py -q
```

CPU coverage executes production Python methods with emulated collectives/native operators, checks quantization and history/current orchestration, cache planes/offsets/zeroing boundaries, metadata ownership, mixed batches and ordinary projection when MLAPO is unavailable. It does not validate device kernel arithmetic.

Ruff lint/format and AST parsing passed for all 43 changed Python files; `bash -n csrc/build_aclnn.sh` and `git diff --check` passed. Native local include and binding closure was reviewed with the #17198 dependency. title: [KV Pool][BugFix] Synchronize MemCache initialization across DP workers
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

When MemCache workers initialize at different speeds, an early DP rank can proceed to NPU work while peers are still establishing their MemCache channels. Add a CPU process-group barrier after successful MemCache store initialization so workers in the same DP group finish that step before proceeding.

Read the option with the other connector settings in `AscendStoreConnector`, pass it through `KVPoolWorker`, and perform the synchronization in `MemcacheBackend._setup_store()`. Skip the barrier for DP size 1, metadata-only scheduler clients, and actual lazy initialization. Lazy initialization is request-driven and DP ranks may enter it independently; a collective there could block a rank waiting for idle peers. When a backend ignores a lazy initialization request and initializes eagerly, keep the startup barrier. Cover initialization ordering, configuration propagation, opt-out, invalid values, initialization failure, and lazy initialization without a barrier and eager fallback synchronization in unit tests.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. `kv_connector_extra_config.memcache_dp_init_barrier` is a boolean that defaults to `true` for the MemCache backend. Set it to `false` to disable the synchronization. With `MultiConnector`, configure it on the `AscendStoreConnector` child. For eager initialization, all ranks in a DP group must use the same value and reach initialization. Stores using lazy initialization skip the barrier even when the option is enabled.

### How was this patch tested?

Ran the following tests inside a newly created Linux container based on `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:nightly-releases-v0.27.1rc-a5-openeuler`, using the modified Ascend source and the vLLM revision recorded in `.github/vllm-main-verified.commit`:

```bash
python3 -m pytest \
  tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_backend.py \
  tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_ascend_store_connector.py \
  tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_pool_worker.py -q
```

Result: **232 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, with 14 PyTorch deprecation warnings. The image's original vLLM revision was incompatible with the current Ascend test setup; the test container used the pinned vLLM source below instead.

Changed-file Ruff lint/format checks, Markdownlint 0.45.0, and `git diff --cached --check` passed. GitHub CI passed the pre-commit hooks and Gitleaks scan on the previous revision. Its separate mypy step exposed six Python 3.10 incompatibilities in the new tests (`TestCase.enterContext`). The tests now use `ExitStack.enter_context` with `addCleanup(stack.close)` instead, and all 232 container unit tests pass again. The updated CI type-check result is pending.

These are mocked unit tests. End-to-end model serving and actual multi-rank MemCache synchronization have not been validated for this config-based patch.

title: [Performance][DSpark] Stack DeepSeek V4 context WKV projections
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR ports the DeepSeek V4 DSpark context WKV stacking optimization from upstream vLLM:

* Upstream PR: vllm-project/vllm#54674

In the current vLLM Ascend DSpark implementation, each draft layer independently applies its WKV projection to the same `context_states`.

This PR stacks the per-layer WKV projections into a single `MergedColumnParallelLinear` projection and splits the result back into per-layer KV states before the existing per-layer KV normalization, RoPE, and KV-cache insertion logic.

Conceptually, this changes the context WKV path from multiple small projections:

```text
X -> WKV_0
X -> WKV_1
X -> WKV_2
```

to one stacked projection:

```text
X -> [WKV_0 | WKV_1 | WKV_2]
```

The goal is to reduce projection launches and improve GEMM utilization on Ascend while preserving the existing DSpark KV-cache semantics.

Compared with the upstream NVIDIA implementation, vLLM Ascend already uses an independent `wkv` projection rather than a fused Q/KV projection, so this PR only ports the cross-layer WKV stacking optimization.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No.

This is an internal DSpark performance optimization and is intended to preserve model outputs and speculative decoding behavior.

### How was this patch tested?

Current status:

* [ ] Unit tests
* [ ] DeepSeek V4 DSpark model loading on Ascend
* [ ] Functional / correctness verification
* [ ] Performance benchmark on Ascend 910B

A unit test is included to verify that:

1. Per-layer WKV checkpoint parameters are duplicated into the corresponding shards of the stacked projection.
2. Context WKV projection is executed once and its output is split correctly for individual DSpark layers.

Performance and full Ascend verification results will be added to this PR before it is marked ready for review.

title: [Feature][Attention] MRV2 external FlashMLA on strided BBND cache with MLA DSpark
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This draft wires external FlashMLA metadata generation and attention execution into MRV2 target inference and MLA DSpark draft inference, while retaining the token-fused, non-contiguous BBND KV cache from #16456. Eager and FULL_DECODE_ONLY use the same operator path. This is a candidate for NPU integration testing, not a validated NPU implementation.

**Dependency: #16456 must land first.** Its source branch is in another fork, so this draft targets `main` and temporarily includes its cache changes. After that PR lands, rebase this PR to leave only the operator integration and rerun validation. MRV2 DSpark #16347 is already present and is not merged again.

This continues the public [historical handoff Draft](https://github.com/Henry-Avery/vllm-ascend/pull/2) on a newer main/cache baseline. Current main's DSpark post-load weight alignment and graph APIs are retained; historical load-time rotation is not reapplied.

Candidate commit: `2ec47279b60f674d4dcd43a7b8becd190434b8bd`.

Pinned inputs:

- Ascend main: `fde460648b159410eac68f4d32fec97587cc8f3d`.
- #16456: `4839002d74a5cac8965a5dfee11c627442bdaa79`.
- Combined baseline: `c8ca7b135f4cd989dd4367ac81919c7759be5514`.
- Paired vLLM: `84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c`.
- At publication, main has one later CI/bisect revert (`79eeed81c`); this candidate retains the pinned runtime baseline.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Opt in with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` and `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASH_MLA=1` (FlashMLA is off by default).

- Both stages import `flash_mla_with_kvcache_metadata` / `flash_mla_with_kvcache` from **`cann_ops_transformer.ops`**. The adapter does not call the in-tree `_C_ascend.flash_mla*` bindings or fall back to FIA when the external package is absent. Other Ascend operators may still use the in-tree extension.
- Both stages pass `max_seqlen_q=-1,max_seqlen_kv=-1`. The main operator uses `TND / PA_BBND / NTD`, actual TP-local Q heads in `{8,12,64,96}`, and QK/V dimensions 576/512.
- Preserve #16456 cache strides, storage offsets, page tables, slots, allocation, COW and zeroing. Write into original 512/64 component views without repacking persistent KV.
- Target and draft own separate schedules/buffers; device lengths and padding are refreshed outside graph capture/replay, with producer waits and consumer reuse fences. Keep V-up, gate, O-proj and non-MLA backends.
- Initial scope: A5, MRV2 dense MLA, BF16 KV, PCP/DCP=1, PP=1, no PD/KVPP. DCP helpers are preparatory only. TP4 requires both actual checkpoints' head geometry and memory capacity to fit; there is no replicated-head workaround.

The Chinese runbook is in `docs/flash_mla_mrv2.md`. The reference launcher is `examples/flash_mla_dspark.py`: target-only / DSpark, eager / graph, `--dry-run`, and `--preflight-only`. Preflight prints installed module/function paths and versions and probes the external Meta implementation; it does not certify NPU kernel dispatch or numerical correctness. No operator wheel is bundled.

Example (replace paths and the draft token count with checkpoint-specific values):

```bash
python examples/flash_mla_dspark.py \
  --target-model /path/to/target --draft-model /path/to/mla-draft \
  --num-speculative-tokens 5 --mode graph \
  --devices 0,1,2,3 --tp 4 --draft-tp 4 --dry-run
```

On the NPU host: inspect package/schema with `--preflight-only`, then test target eager, target + MLA draft eager, and the same inputs in graph mode. Checkpoints may require additional weight-quantization arguments; KV remains BF16.

### How was this patch tested?

Local host: macOS arm64, Python 3.12, CPU torch 2.8.0.

```bash
python -m unittest \
  tests.ut.attention.test_flash_mla_host_contract \
  tests.ut.spec_decode.test_flash_mla_dspark_host_contract \
  tests.ut.worker.test_flash_mla_integration_host_contract -v
```

- 40 CPU/mock tests passed. Coverage includes device length correction, context KV writes, padding/masks, target/draft ownership, stable buffers, executor fences, graph refresh/replay routing and single post-load alignment.
- An added test supplies in-tree FlashMLA bindings that fail if called: metadata and attention still use the external package; missing external entries raise rather than falling back.
- 4 #16456 lifecycle cases passed in an isolated CPU harness with actual worker methods/test bodies. Fix only the fixture's byte-count/BF16-element-count mismatch and per-subpage COW expectation; production allocator/COW/zeroing code is unchanged.
- Four launcher dry-run combinations and eight invalid-input cases passed; no NPU package was loaded and no service was started for these checks.
- Scoped lint/format, compile checks, whitespace checks and applicable pre-commit checks (including staged gitleaks) passed locally.

**Still unvalidated:** the installed external operator package on NPU, real scatter/RoPE/Triton execution, full vLLM import/build, checkpoint loading, numerical correctness, DSpark acceptance/rejection, graph capture/replay, collectives, four-card K3 service, and performance. CPU zeroer checks validate metadata only. A listening server or an importable package is not acceptance evidence.

title: [Performance][DSV4] Reuse filtered RoPE lookups
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR removes redundant DeepSeek V4 RoPE table indexing that remains on current main.

- adds an optional layer filter to `get_cos_and_sin_dsa` so draft attention queries only the RoPE config consumed by its layers
- resolves draft `*.swa_cache` layer names to their registered `*.attn` RoPE layer
- computes the ordinary RoPE cos/sin pair once before the DSpark context-KV layer loop and reuses it across all draft layers
- preserves existing target common/decode caching already present on current main

Current main has already absorbed part of the older optimization design, so this PR deliberately excludes that existing logic. It is independent of the block-table dirty-copy PR.

An earlier DSV4 DP16 decode profile showed that eliminating 26 redundant Index/IndexCheck pairs saved approximately 1.19 ms/step. On current main, only the draft config filtering and cross-layer context-KV reuse remain applicable, so a fresh profile is required before making a current-main performance claim.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API or output change. RoPE values are queried for the same positions and config; the result is reused by layers that share that config.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added unit coverage verifying layer-based config filtering and `swa_cache` to `attn` resolution.
- Repository pre-commit checks passed: Ruff check/format, codespell, typos, gitleaks, import and policy checks, and DCO sign-off.
- `python3 -m compileall` and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files.

NPU execution was not run locally. Required follow-up coverage on Ascend is: DSV4/DSpark eager correctness, affected attention backend smoke with real weights, graph-mode coverage, and a fresh Index/IndexCheck profile.

title: [BugFix][Engram] Skip HOST_UVA page migration during CPU binding
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #17286.

With Engram HOST_UVA offload, post-warmup CPU binding runs `migratepages` after the large host tables have already been registered and pinned. Migrating the whole worker can stall startup for many minutes, and DP replicas sharing a backing can request different NUMA destinations.

Keep CPU thread and IRQ affinity at the existing post-warmup/post-capture point, but skip process-wide page migration when `engram_config.cpu_offload` is enabled. Move the migration call out of the thread-binding methods so it can be skipped independently. Other configurations retain the existing migration behavior and ordering.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Engram HOST_UVA workloads can keep CPU binding enabled without the process-wide `migratepages` startup stall. No new configuration is required. Shared-table placement and selective page migration are outside this fix.

### How was this patch tested?

- The complete existing CPU-binding and V1 worker unit-test files passed (151 tests). Only existing CPU-binding expectations were updated for the migration call location and argument forwarding. No new test cases were added; mock-only tests cannot reproduce the pinned HOST_UVA page-migration stall, which was validated on hardware as described below.
- `bash format.sh ci` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Standalone validation, Ascend `2cd0042f1`: A3, CANN 9.1, 16 NPUs, TP2/DP8, shared Engram HOST_UVA, async scheduling, DSpark5 with eager draft, and FULL_DECODE_ONLY. All 16 workers completed post-capture affinity binding in 4-7 seconds; 1,257 measured requests succeeded. Two fixed 128-token probes matched the no-binding control exactly in tokens and logprobs. This ran under UID 1000, so IRQ writes were skipped due to permissions.
- Full P/D (1P1D) rerun on this PR head, external DP, Engram HOST_UVA with `{"cpu_offload": true, "dp_shared_memory": true}` and `enable_cpu_binding: true`, single-node TP4/DP4 prefill plus TP2/DP8 decode on 16 NPUs each, V1 runner, DSpark5, decode side on async scheduling with FULL_DECODE_ONLY. Every worker logged `CPU affinity applied without process-wide NUMA page migration.` and no `migratepages` process appeared on either node. Both halves reached ready: prefill in 353.5 s, decode in 475-513 s. Twelve measured `vllm bench serve` runs (128/4096 input, 256 output, concurrency 1/8/32, temperature 0) completed with mean ITL 37.4-50.2 ms and 66-643 output tok/s.
- Control on the PR merge base without this patch, same deployment: the decode half never reached ready. Up to 16 `migratepages` helpers appeared right after graph capture, EngineCore repeatedly reported `No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds`, and the helpers were still running more than 45 minutes later, with their target worker stuck in state `D` and `kill -9` having no effect.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [Feature][KV offload] Add fused lightning indexer manage and fused scatter copy sparse flash attention operators for sparse KV cache offloading.
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds two standalone AscendC custom operators for large-sequence sparse
KV cache offloading scenarios:

- `fused_lightning_indexer_manage`
- `fused_scatter_copy_sparse_flash_attention`

Together, the two operators cover the operator-level workflow from Lightning
Indexer TopK selection and sparse-cache management to missing-KV scatter copy
and sparse flash attention.

#### `fused_lightning_indexer_manage`

This operator performs the following operations in a single NPU invocation:

- Lightning Indexer TopK retrieval;
- initialization and steady-state eviction of the HBM sparse KV cache;
- TopK union management for multiple MTP query routes;
- cache-hit and cache-miss classification;
- generation of cache-miss source IDs and destination HBM slots.

A single batch may contain mixed request states:

- non-offload requests (`request_state = -3`);
- first-offload requests (`request_state = -2`);
- steady-state offload requests (`request_state = -1`).

Each request supports 1 to 14 query routes. The operator maintains the
persistent mapping from source token IDs to HBM logical slots through
`cache_slots_pool`.

The current implementation supports:

- FLOAT16 and BFLOAT16;
- 32 and 64 index heads;
- a fixed index head dimension of 128;
- a fixed TopK size of 2048;
- a cache block size of 128;
- source capacity up to `2^21`;
- Atlas A2 and Atlas A3 products.

`query_dequant_scale` and `index_key_dequant_scale` are reserved inputs in the
current implementation and are not consumed yet. Quantized Query and Index Key
dequantization will be supported in a follow-up change.

#### `fused_scatter_copy_sparse_flash_attention`

This operator combines missing-KV scatter copy and causal sparse flash
attention in a single public PyTorch custom-op call. It performs the following
operations:

- initialize the HBM sparse KV cache for first-fill requests;
- identify source-aware TopK cache misses during steady-state execution;
- scatter-copy missing KPE and CKV entries from DRAM to HBM;
- execute causal sparse flash attention over the requested TopK KV entries;
- support variable numbers of MTP query routes in the TND layout.

A single batch may contain:

- first-fill requests;
- steady-state requests containing cache hits and misses;
- requests with heterogeneous MTP query counts.

Each request supports 1 to 16 query routes, corresponding to MTP0 through
MTP15. The operator consumes the TopK slot and miss metadata produced by the
cache-management stage.

The current implementation supports:

- FLOAT16 and BFLOAT16;
- 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128 query heads;
- a fixed TopK size of 2048;
- a cache block size of 128;
- a 512-dimensional compressed KV representation;
- a 64-dimensional RoPE key representation;
- Atlas A2 and Atlas A3 products.

The operator uses two execution paths selected from device-side metadata:

- first-fill path: an internal helper fills the HBM sparse cache before the
  attention kernel accesses it;
- steady-state path: missing KV entries are copied while sparse attention is
  executed.

The first-fill helper and the main fused kernel are launched on the same NPU
stream. The helper becomes a device-side no-op for steady-state requests. Path
selection does not read CPU data and supports ACLGraph Capture and Replay.

#### Main changes

- add the two fused AscendC operator implementations;
- add the conditional first-fill scatter-copy helper;
- add operator definitions, tiling implementations and inference functions;
- add shape, dtype, device, contiguity and dynamic-input validation;
- add ACLNN interfaces and PyTorch custom-op registration;
- add Meta implementations;
- enable the operators for Atlas A2 and Atlas A3 products;
- add operator documentation and representative latency results;
- add standalone correctness and ACLGraph replay tests.

This PR only introduces the standalone operators and their operator-level
tests. Framework-side metadata construction, cache-manager integration and
model execution integration are not included and will be submitted separately.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes.

Two new PyTorch custom operators are exposed:

```python
torch.ops._C_ascend.npu_fused_lightning_indexer_manage(...)
torch.ops._C_ascend.npu_fused_scatter_copy_sparse_flash_attention(...)
```

No existing API, model execution path or default behavior is changed. The new
operators are not connected to the vLLM model execution path in this PR.

### How was this patch tested?

The operators were built and tested on an Ascend NPU environment.

Test environment:

- Device: Ascend 910_93
- CANN: 9.1.0
- npu-smi: 25.2.1
- OS: Linux
- Python: 3.12.13
- pytest: 8.3.2
- vLLM: `0.1.dev21135+g84030bbe3`

#### Lightning Indexer and cache-management tests

Test command:

```bash
pytest -sv \
  tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_fused_lightning_indexer_manage.py
```

Test result:

```text
collected 105 items
105 passed, 14 warnings in 27.91s
```

The tests use `torch_npu.npu_lightning_indexer` as the TopK reference
implementation and cover:

- FLOAT16/BFLOAT16 and 32/64 index heads;
- all query route counts from Q1 to Q14;
- non-offload, first-offload and steady-state requests;
- mixed request states and lifecycle transitions;
- cache initialization, eviction, hit/miss classification and miss union;
- repeated invocation and all-hit convergence;
- miss-occurrence boundaries around 2048 and 4096;
- long source IDs from `2^17` to near the `2^21` upper limit;
- representative invalid shape, dtype, contiguity and query-count inputs.

All 105 correctness cases passed, including the Q14 state matrix, mixed-state
batch cases and long-sequence cases.

#### Scatter-copy sparse flash attention tests

Test command:

```bash
pytest -sv \
  tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_fused_scatter_copy_sparse_flash_attention.py
```

The tests cover:

- FLOAT16/BFLOAT16 and 8/16/32/64/128 query heads;
- MTP0 and heterogeneous MTP2/MTP3/MTP8/MTP15 TND batches;
- steady-state fused scatter copy;
- first-fill requests and mixed-request batches;
- `attention_out` precision against a CPU reference;
- HBM KPE and CKV cache update correctness;
- ACLGraph Capture and Replay;
- switching from the captured steady-state path to the first-fill path through
  device-side metadata.

Representative latency results for both operators are included in their
respective README files. They are provided as reference data only and are not
used as test thresholds.

### End-to-end inference results

The operators were also evaluated end-to-end with GLM-5.2-w4a8 on Ascend 910C,
using TP16/EP16 and a 64K sequence length.

With the same batch size of 5, enabling KV cache offloading increases ITL only
from 73.56 ms to 78.42 ms, corresponding to a 6.6% degradation.

With KV cache offloading enabled, the batch size can be increased from 5 to 16.
In this configuration, ITL increases from 73.56 ms to 109.54 ms, while
throughput increases from 188 TPS to 406 TPS, corresponding to a 115%
throughput improvement.

The operator-level contributions are as follows:

* `fused_lightning_indexer_manage`: at batch size 5 without offloading, the
  total latency of the Lightning Indexer operators across all layers is
  2.89 ms. At batch size 5 with offloading, the total latency of the LIM
  operators across all layers is 6.83 ms, resulting in only a 3.94 ms
  increase in ITL.

* `fused_scatter_copy_sparse_flash_attention`: at batch size 16, with separate
  scatter-copy and sparse flash attention operators, the total scatter-copy
  latency across all layers is 11.75 ms and the total sparse flash attention
  latency is 18.81 ms. With the fused CopySFA operator, the total latency
  across all layers is 23.90 ms. Therefore, the fused operator reduces ITL by
  `11.75 + 18.81 - 23.90 = 6.66 ms`.

Compared with the first version of the fused operators, evaluated with 4
machines, 1P1D, 32 concurrent requests and a 29K sequence length, ITL is
reduced from 80 ms in the first version
([https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/14278](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/14278)) to 77.7 ms with the
current implementation, corresponding to a 2.3 ms ITL reduction. There is
still room for further optimization on the framework side.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [BugFix][Platform] Keep MiniMax-M3 GQA KV cache in BF16 on A5

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Split the MiniMax-M3 A5 mixed KV-cache policy out of #16904 so it can land independently of the pending CANN operators.

When MiniMax-M3 runs on Ascend A5 with FP8 KV cache, sparse-attention layers retain the configured FP8 policy while GQA layers are added to `kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers` and therefore use BF16. Existing user-provided skip layers are preserved and deduplicated.

The policy is limited to the two MiniMax-M3 architectures, FP8 KV-cache configurations, and hardware with FP8-attention capability. It has no dependency on `aclnnMsaIndexScore` or Generic Block Sparse Attention.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. MiniMax-M3 deployments on Ascend A5 that request FP8 KV cache will use BF16 KV cache for GQA layers. Other models, non-FP8 KV-cache configurations, and non-A5 devices are unchanged.

title: [MRV2][BugFix][Kernel] Fix and optimize sampling mask packing on Ascend
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This is a backport of #17193 for the v0.28.0 release branch.

The sampling-mask kernel can overflow UB on Triton-Ascend when
`logits.stride(1) > 1`. For a batch-32, vocabulary-151936, stride-2
input, the original BLOCK_SIZE=8192 kernel fails compilation with:

`ub overflow, requires 12583424 bits while 1572864 bits available`

The implementation also has two Ascend-specific lowering issues:

- reducing the boolean keep mask does not produce the required finite-logit
  count;
- per-element variable shifts and the `[512, 8]` axis-1 reduction lower to
  scalar-heavy execution.

This PR adds an Ascend implementation for the sampling-mask API. It:

- makes only strided vocabulary inputs contiguous, without modifying the
  caller's tensor;
- casts the keep mask to int32 before reduction;
- uses BLOCK_SIZE=4096 to remain within the NPU UB limit;
- transposes the packing layout from `[512, 8]` to `[8, 512]`, multiplies by
  compile-time bit weights, and reduces axis 0;
- replaces `SamplingMaskTensors.from_logits` with the Ascend implementation;
- adds operator documentation and registers the NPU regression test in the
  A2 single-card nightly matrix.

The following msprof results use an Ascend 910, `npu:0`, 10 profiling
rounds, and `MemoryDetail,Occupancy,PipeUtilization,Roofline`. Values are
selected kernel task durations and exclude Python wrapper time and the
preceding contiguous copy.

| Case | Baseline | Optimized | Speedup | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `b1_v17_active1_colstride1` | 123.330 us | 5.640 us | 21.87x | 95.43% |
| `b8_v8191_active1_colstride1` | 244.573 us | 6.960 us | 35.14x | 97.15% |
| `b8_v8192_active1_colstride1` | 244.327 us | 6.680 us | 36.58x | 97.27% |
| `b8_v8193_active1_colstride1` | 365.349 us | 8.940 us | 40.87x | 97.55% |
| `b8_v8193_active0_colstride1` | 365.357 us | 8.780 us | 41.61x | 97.60% |
| `b32_v151936_active1_colstride2` | 4604.258 us | 84.758 us | 54.32x | 98.16% |
| `b128_v151936_active1_colstride1` | 18403.968 us | 327.093 us | 56.27x | 98.22% |

The original stride-2 BLOCK_SIZE=8192 implementation has no runtime
duration because it fails compilation with UB overflow. The table uses
the first compilable correctness-fixed implementation with the original
variable-shift packing as the performance baseline.

TTIR/NPU IR inspection confirms that the optimized packing lowers to
vector transpose, multiply, and reduction operations; the previous
tensor-wide scalar shift loop is absent.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?

Correctness validation environment:

- Ascend 910
- Python 3.12.13
- Torch 2.10.0
- torch-npu 2.10.0.post4
- Triton-Ascend 3.2.2
- CANN 9.1.0

The NPU regression test passed against the vLLM v0.28.0 three-field
sampling-mask interface.

The regression test verifies:

- finite support sizes 0, 1, 7, 511, 512, 513, 2048, 2053, and the full vocabulary;
- random sparse token positions and a vocabulary size not divisible by eight;
- active and inactive rows, including `num_sampled_tokens > 1`;
- NaN and positive/negative infinity exclusion;
- non-contiguous `logits` with `stride(1) == 2` and an unmodified caller view;
- exact packed masks, counts, and decoded token IDs.

The regression is registered as the A2 single-card nightly case
`sampling-mask`.

The following repository checks passed:

- `bash format.sh`
- `python -m compileall`
- `git diff --check`
- `SHELLCHECK_OPTS="--exclude=SC2046,SC2006,SC2086" pre-commit run
  --all-files --hook-stage manual --show-diff-on-failure`

title: [BugFix] Fix SFA output projection TP for idle DP ranks
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix output-projection tensor parallelism (OTP) in the shared SFA path. When one DP rank has no requests, it must still contribute its projection weight shard to active ranks. Previously, the idle SFA path skipped those collectives; unequal decode graph buckets also produced incompatible exchange shapes.

- Keep idle SFA ranks in OTP collectives with empty local inputs.
- Exchange full DP inputs without sharding them twice, and use fixed-capacity communication buffers across graph capture/replay and uneven batches.
- Allow oversized profiling-only batches to participate with empty inputs while preserving their output shape.
- Preserve aliased SFA/Mamba cache pages and Conv-history offsets in PreemptOffloadConnector, which is required by the tested OTP deployment. This fixes GLM-5.3-Flash cache registration with the mandatory offload connector.

Refs #15665

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. SFA decode deployments using `oproj_tensor_parallel_size` can handle idle DP ranks and uneven batches, including GLM-5.3-Flash P/D serving. Existing configuration constraints remain in effect; no new option is added.

The shared SFA/OTP fix is also expected to apply to GLM-5.2 on the same execution path, but GLM-5.2 model-level validation is not claimed here.

### How was this patch tested?

- **296 unit tests passed** across the following commands, including regressions for idle ranks, uneven batches, stable collective buffers, profiling, and both shared-cache registration orders:

  ```bash
  python -m pytest -q tests/ut/ops/test_linear.py tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_v1.py tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2 tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_cache_config.py tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_kv_cache.py tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_kpool_model_backend.py
  python -m pytest -q tests/ut/kv_offload/test_preempt_offload_connector.py
  ```

- Real Ascend 910 NPU check: aliased-cache registration and selective Conv-history restore passed; unrelated state and padding were preserved.
- GLM-5.3-Flash W8A8 on 16 Ascend A3 NPUs: **P TP8+EP8 → D TP1+DP8+EP8+OTP8**, MRV1, MooncakeConnectorV2 transfer, and MultiConnector with PreemptOffloadConnector on D. D used `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` with capture sizes `[1,2,4,8,16]`, `max_num_seqs=16`, and `max_model_len=16384`. Five structured smoke requests passed, covering low concurrency, mixed-length concurrent requests, and resume after idle.
- Full **8-shot GSM8K: 1280/1319 (97.04%)**, temperature 0, 32 client workers, 10,240 generated-token cap, strict final `####` integer extraction. No HTTP or other client errors. Two length-limited incorrect answers are included in the score. The run had no preemptions; full-model preemption stress was not tested.
- Ruff check/format and `git diff --check` passed for the six changed files. No nightly case was added.

title: [Performance][Ops] Use fused rotary embedding for Gemma 4 global attention
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Gemma 4 global (full) attention RoPE currently falls back to native PyTorch on Ascend. vLLM's OOT registry dispatches by exact class name (`cls.__name__`), and `Gemma4RotaryEmbedding` (the `proportional` rope type) is not registered, so these layers never reach the Ascend fused rotary forward that sliding-attention layers already use.

This PR registers an adapter, `AscendGemma4RotaryEmbedding(Gemma4RotaryEmbedding, AscendRotaryEmbedding)`. Gemma4's constructor runs first and keeps its proportional frequencies (head-size exponents, zero-padded non-rotated pairs, `rotary_dim = head_size`), then the existing Ascend fused forward is reused unchanged. Non-rotated pairs have cos=1/sin=0 in the cache, so the full-head fused rotation is exact for them. Compatibility (310P) devices keep their current path.

Relation to #15332: that PR fuses split-QKV + RMSNorm + RoPE + V-norm for Gemma 4, but intentionally keeps the unfused chain on 950 (no A5 variant) and for KV-shared layers. Those paths still call `rotary_emb`, so this change is complementary.

Operator measurements on one Ascend 950PR, BF16, gemma-4-31B global-attention geometry (32 Q / 4 KV heads, head 512, `partial_rotary_factor=0.25`, 262144 positions), NPU graph replay with identical input clones in both paths:

| Tokens | Q+K native → fused (µs) | Query-only (KV-shared) native → fused (µs) |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | 33.2 → 13.8 (2.41×) | 20.4 → 13.8 (1.48×) |
| 4 | 35.9 → 14.1 (2.55×) | 22.1 → 13.4 (1.64×) |
| 32 | 47.6 → 13.8 (3.45×) | 30.3 → 16.2 (1.88×) |
| 256 | 87.9 → 33.0 (2.67×) | 61.6 → 29.5 (2.09×) |
| 1024 | 278.8 → 83.2 (3.35×) | 226.8 → 77.2 (2.94×) |

These are operator measurements, not end-to-end throughput; only global-attention layers (about one in six in gemma-4-31B) use this rope type.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Gemma 4 global-attention layers use the existing Ascend fused RoPE. The cos/sin cache is bit-identical to upstream. The fused kernel uses FP32 intermediate arithmetic, so outputs are not bitwise equal to the native BF16 fallback; against an FP32 reference with the same cache, query relative L2 error is ~0.083% fused vs ~0.119% native. No additional cache memory: the module-level cache recorders keep the first (sliding-layer) cache.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests (`tests/ut/ops/test_rotary_embedding.py`, `tests/ut/test_utils.py`): constructor/frequency cases for partial (512/128) and full (256/256) rotary, cache recording, unchanged-signature check, and registration of `Gemma4RotaryEmbedding`. 18 passed against vLLM `84030bbe` (the verified main commit) on CPU.
- NPU test (`tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_gemma4_rope.py`): 16 cases — BF16/FP16, 1/4/32/1024 tokens, Q+K and query-only, noncontiguous merged-QKV views, positions up to the cache end; checks the cache matches upstream exactly, outputs match an FP32 reference, and the 384 non-rotated dims pass through bit-exactly. All pass on 950PR.
- ruff check/format pass.

NPU runs used current-main `rotary_embedding.py`, `triton/rope.py`, `triton/triton_utils.py` and `envs.py` overlaid on an installed vllm-ascend 0.26.0rc1 / vLLM 0.26.0 stack (torch 2.10, torch-npu 2.10.0.post4, CANN 9.1.0); the full current-main engine was not run.

`tests/ut/test_utils.py` touches the same registration test as #17374 (Llama 3 RoPE); whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase.

Developed with Claude Code assistance; reviewed and submitted by the author.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Performance] Optimize DeepSeek-V4 VL embed_input_ids to remove per-step copies
body: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Profiling the DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp deployment (`dsv4-vision-exp`) showed ~4ms of copy operations inside `embed_input_ids` on every scheduler step. The cause was that the sentinel-replacement path re-executed avoidable copies per forward: 1. `torch.stack([...]).to(inputs_embeds.dtype)` — the four `image_*` parameters are float32 while embeddings are bf16, so every step re-stacked and re-cast the sentinel vectors. 2. `sentinel_mask & ~is_multimodal.to(input_ids.device)` — `is_multimodal` lives on CPU in this stack, so every step performed an H2D copy of the mask plus a device AND. This exclusion is unnecessary: positions flagged `is_multimodal` are always overwritten afterwards by `_merge_multimodal_embeddings`, so the table value written there is dead anyway. 3. `torch.where(...)` allocated a fresh full `seq_len x hidden` tensor per step on top of the `table[idx]` gather. Changes: - Cache the stacked sentinel table in the embedding dtype (`_get_sentinel_table`), built once per model instance and reused for the process lifetime. - Drop the redundant `& ~is_multimodal` exclusion and its per-step H2D copy (safe because `_merge_multimodal_embeddings` overwrites those positions afterwards). - Write the sentinel replacement in place via `torch.where(..., out=inputs_embeds)`, removing one full-sequence allocation per step.
