title: [https://nvbugs/6624972][fix] Preserve Nemotron-H hybrid_override_pattern with MLP layers
body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- Added and registered `NemotronHConfig` to preserve Nemotron-H patterns containing `-`, which Transformers 5.5.x cannot represent. The local config validates patterns, derives layer types and depth, and delegates representable patterns to the native config.
- The local config also handles checkpoints that contain only `layers_block_type`, legacy Mamba parameter names, and MTP pattern precedence. Verify that these compatibility paths preserve expected behavior for existing checkpoints.
- Imported TRT-LLM configs before tokenizer loading so registration is available during `AutoTokenizer` loading.
- Updated `NemotronHForCausalLM.__init__` to accept factory keyword arguments, including `use_cache`.
- Removed the Nemotron Nano NVFP4 integration waiver.

## QA Engineer Review

- Added Nemotron-H coverage for dense pattern loading, native config delegation, invalid patterns and block types, layer-type precedence, MTP behavior, cache defaults, tokenizer registration, and model-config loading.
- Added a CPU-only regression test for `_from_config(..., use_cache=False)`.
- Added `tests/unittest/_torch/test_custom_config_registration.py` to `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_cpu.yml`.
- Removed the Nemotron Nano NVFP4 waiver. The previously waived integration case is no longer excluded.
- Coverage verdict: **needs follow-up**. The supplied comments report a successful later CI run with automatic retries, but do not establish whether the unwaived integration case passed without retries.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/auto_deploy/models/custom/modeling_nemotron_h.py`: Verify that accepting factory keyword arguments does not alter model initialization.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/configs/__init__.py`: Verify that `NemotronHConfig` is exported and registered for `nemotron_h`.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/configs/nemotron_h.py`: Verify pattern preservation, validation errors, derived layer types and depth, missing-pattern reconstruction, MTP behavior, and cache settings.
- `tensorrt_llm/tokenizer/tokenizer.py`: Verify that TRT-LLM config registration occurs before tokenizer loading.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/test_custom_config_registration.py`: Covers config registration, Nemotron-H pattern handling, tokenizer loading, and model-config loading. The file is listed in `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_cpu.yml`.
- `tests/unittest/auto_deploy/singlegpu/models/test_modeling_nemotron_h.py`: Covers `_from_config(..., use_cache=False)` and preservation of the supplied config. No test-list entry is identified in the supplied evidence.
- `tests/integration/test_lists/waives.txt`: Removes the Nemotron Nano NVFP4 waiver, so verify that the integration case runs.
- `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_cpu.yml`: Adds the config-registration test file to the L0 CPU CI list.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

`transformers` 5.5.4's `NemotronHConfig` converts `hybrid_override_pattern` into `layers_block_type` with a mapping that only knows `M`, `E` and `*`. Every dense Nemotron-H checkpoint also uses `-` for MLP layers, so config construction raises `KeyError: '-'`. `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained` calls `AutoConfig.from_pretrained`, so this fails **before any model is built**.

Reproduced on `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2-NVFP4` (CPU only, no GPU required):

```
File ".../transformers/models/nemotron_h/configuration_nemotron_h.py", line 271, in _pattern_to_list
    return [pattern_mapping[char] for char in pattern]
KeyError: '-'
```

Widening that one mapping is **not** sufficient — each of these was checked against the installed 5.5.4:

- `NemotronHConfig.validate_layers_block_type` restricts entries to `{"mamba", "attention", "moe"}`.
- The base `validate_layer_type`, reached via `attribute_map = {"layer_types": "layers_block_type"}`, also rejects `"mlp"`.
- `hybrid_override_pattern` is a **read-only property** derived from `layers_block_type` through a reverse mapping with no `-`, so the MLP entries cannot be recovered even after the first two are relaxed.

TRT-LLM builds Nemotron-H by iterating `hybrid_override_pattern` (`modeling_nemotron_h.py`, `ModelConfig.get_num_attention_layers` / `get_num_mamba_layers`, and the mamba/attention masks in `config_utils.py`), so the literal checkpoint string has to survive config loading intact.

This PR adds a TRT-LLM-local `NemotronHConfig` that stores the pattern verbatim and registers it for `model_type="nemotron_h"`. Its `from_dict` delegates straight back to the native transformers class for **every** pattern transformers can express, so the only checkpoints whose behaviour changes are the ones that cannot be loaded at all today.

Upstream fixed this in transformers v5.6.2; `requirements.txt` pins `transformers==5.5.4`. Updating that pin is a substantially larger change than this compatibility shim.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/_torch/test_custom_config_registration.py` — four new CPU-only tests: the dense pattern survives `AutoConfig` with layer counts intact, representable patterns still resolve to the **native** transformers class, invalid pattern characters raise a clear `ValueError`, and `ModelLoader.load_hf_model_config` returns a usable config.
- `test_e2e.py::test_ptp_quickstart_advanced[Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2-nvfp4-NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2-NVFP4]` — the `nvbugs/6624972` waiver is removed so this B200 `pre_merge` case exercises the fix directly.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Please check this after reviewing the above items as appropriate for this PR.

title: [trtllm-agent][https://nvbugs/6812350][fix] Raise remote MPI worker exceptions from submit_sync
body:
## Description

`RemoteMpiCommSessionClient.submit_sync` could return an exception object where
its callers expect `List[T]`.

When a worker task fails, the server forwards the failure as the response
payload itself:

```python
# RemoteMpiCommSessionServer.mpi_future_callback
if future.exception() is not None:
    self.queue.put(future.exception())
    return
```

The client returned that payload verbatim, so the caller received a bare
exception instead of a list. `CachedModelLoader._download_hf_model_if_needed`
then iterates it:

```python
model_dir = next((d for d in model_dirs if d is not None), None)
```

which raises `TypeError: '<SomeError>' object is not iterable` — far from the
real cause, and hiding whatever the worker actually raised.

The other two sessions do not have this problem: `MpiPoolSession.submit_sync`
and `MpiCommSession.submit_sync` both return `[future.result() for ...]`, and
`future.result()` re-raises. This change makes the remote session consistent
with them.

## Test Coverage

No new test. The change is a two-line guard on an error path that requires a
live remote MPI session with a failing worker to exercise; it has not been run
against such a session. It is derived from the two call sites quoted above.

Behaviour on the success path is unchanged: `res` is a list there, so
`isinstance(res, BaseException)` is false and the function returns as before.

## PR Checklist

- [x] PR title follows the required format
- [x] Change limited to a single concern
- [ ] CI green

title: [None][fix] Python transceiver: run gen-side KV transfer consensus across helix CP ranks under attention-DP
body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review
Attention-DP generation-side transfer consensus now spans helix CP ranks and, when configured, PP ranks. This prevents a rank from proceeding before its peers receive KV data. Non-DP and attention-DP without CP retain their existing consensus paths. KV-size metric scaling is factored into a helper; attention-DP scales by CP size, while other paths use TP × CP.

`KVCacheManagerV2` no longer rejects attention-DP with helix CP. Its restrictions on block reuse and draft managers remain. The DeepSeek V3 Lite helix integration path switches to the Python transceiver with NIXL. The shared helix test also sets a bounded request timeout so a transfer deadlock can fail the test instead of occupying the GPU slot until the class-level timeout.

## QA Engineer Review
The new `test_transceiver_adp_helix_consensus.py` covers attention-DP consensus with CP and PP, completion and cancellation outcomes, non-DP behavior, and KV-size scaling. The added `test_kv_cache_manager_v2_accepts_attention_dp_with_helix_cp` case covers MHA and MLA manager construction. The H100 CI list includes that manager test. The changed integration test selectors’ CI or manual-QA listing is not established by the available evidence.

The test-list waiver removal re-enables the B300 DeepSeek V3 Lite `test_auto_dtype_with_helix` case. Test execution results are not established. Coverage verdict: needs follow-up.

## Per-File QA Perspective
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/disaggregation/transceiver.py`: Verify that attention-DP consensus waits for matching completion across CP and PP ranks, and that non-DP behavior remains unchanged. Check KV-size metrics for attention-DP and non-DP mappings.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/kv_cache/kv_cache_manager_v2.py`: Verify initialization accepts attention-DP with helix CP and still rejects block reuse and draft managers.
- `tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_transceiver_adp_helix_consensus.py`: Covers CP/PP consensus, completion and cancellation outcomes, non-DP behavior, and metric scaling. No corresponding CI or manual-QA test-list entry is established.
- `tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_cache_transceiver_single_process.py`: Adds MHA and MLA manager-construction coverage for attention-DP with helix CP. The H100 CI list includes this test.
- `tests/integration/defs/accuracy/test_disaggregated_serving.py`: Updates the helix integration path to use the Python transceiver with NIXL and bounds request timeout. Verify backend setup and timeout handling for both DeepSeek V3 Lite and the shared helix helper.
- `tests/integration/defs/disaggregated/test_configs/disagg_config_ctxtp2_gentp1cp2_deepseek_v3_lite_bf16_tllm_gen.yaml`: Changes both workers to NIXL with the Python runtime. Verify this configuration in the DeepSeek V3 Lite helix transfer path.
- `tests/integration/test_lists/waives.txt`: Removes the waiver for the B300 DeepSeek V3 Lite helix test. Verify that the re-enabled test runs and passes.
- `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_h100.yml`: Adds the attention-DP helix manager test to H100 CI. No changed integration helix selector is confirmed in this list.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Under attention-DP the Python KV cache transceiver (`KvCacheTransceiverV2`) skipped the gen-side transfer-completion consensus entirely when `pp_size == 1`, assuming every DP rank owns disjoint requests. With helix context parallelism the CP ranks of one DP group share the same requests, so a CP rank could start decoding a request whose KV blocks its partner rank had not received yet, and the helix all-to-all deadlocked (all gen ranks stuck in `cuda_event.synchronize()`, killed by the hang detector after 300 s).

`KVCacheManagerV2` rejected attention-DP + helix for exactly this reason (`disagg transfer-completion consensus is skipped under attention-DP`); that is what fails `TestDeepSeekV3Lite::test_auto_dtype_with_helix[...pp1dp2cp2...]` once the test is moved to the Python transceiver (see #19472). Switching the test to the V1 manager only turns the ValueError into the hang.

This PR mirrors the C++ transceiver, which builds its attention-DP sync group from all PP x CP ranks of the same DP index (`mGroupDataComm`):

- `transceiver.py::_init_sync_policy`: under attention-DP, gather over the CP group (then PP when present) and require `pp_size * cp_size` agreements. Non-DP and DP-without-CP paths are unchanged.
- `kv_cache_manager_v2.py`: lift the attention-DP + helix rejection.

Verified on 8xB300 with DeepSeek-V3-Lite disaggregated serving (ctx tp4 -> gen tp2 cp2 helix, attention-DP on, Python transceiver / NIXL, GSM8K ref 64.74 / threshold 61.54):

| Config | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| KV manager V1, overlap on | hang (300 s hang detector) | 64.14 |
| KV manager V2, overlap on | ValueError at startup (hang if rejection removed) | 63.38 |
| KV manager V2, overlap off | ValueError at startup | 64.33 |
| non-DP `pp1tp2cp2`, overlap on (regression check) | 64.94 | 64.94 |

## Test Coverage

- New `tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_transceiver_adp_helix_consensus.py`: sync policy and consensus under attention-DP with CP, CP x PP, and the unchanged DP-without-CP / non-DP paths.
- Existing transceiver unit tests (`test_transceiver_bounded_polling.py`, `test_sync_transfer_timing.py`, `test_transfer_ownership_regressions.py`, `test_kv_cache_transceiver_contract.py`): 149 passed against the patched package.
- Integration: `accuracy/test_disaggregated_serving.py::TestDeepSeekV3Lite::test_auto_dtype_with_helix[fifo_v2-cudagraph:with_padding-pp1dp2cp2-overlap_{on,off}]` on the Python transceiver (migrated in #19472).

- PR description clearly explains what and why. If using CodeRabbit's summary, please make sure it makes sense.

body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- Updates startup and warmup instrumentation in `model_engine.py`, `py_executor.py`, and `py_executor_creator.py`.
- Preserves host-side timing, nested-phase accounting, failure timing, and exception propagation.
- Adds timing for warmup phases, the pre-warmup rank barrier, executor initialization, allocation, teardown, and worker startup.
- Review severity counts are unavailable.

## QA Engineer Review

No test changes.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/model_engine.py`: Routes warmup timing through `_WarmupTimer`. Verify phase summaries, failure reporting, timer purposes, and shape timing.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/py_executor.py`: Instruments the pre-warmup rank barrier. Verify diagnostic output and confirm that the change adds no synchronization.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/py_executor_creator.py`: Instruments executor initialization, allocation, teardown, and worker startup. Verify timer propagation, event ordering, and cleanup behavior.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

TinyLlama ctxpp4/genpp4 can exhaust its 300-second readiness deadline while Blackwell workers are still initializing and warming up. Increase only this test's startup deadline to **900 seconds** and remove its B200/B300 waives for NVBug 6771023. The latest B300 cold-cache diagnostic reached cluster readiness in **639.988 seconds**, so neither the initially proposed 500 seconds nor 600 seconds covers that run. A 900-second budget provides about 260 seconds of headroom; this is not a worst-case bound.

Integrate and extend the diagnostics from [PR #19304](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/19304): phase/shape timings, percentages, slow-phase warnings, PID/rank identifiers, and profiling/final-executor warmup purpose and pass numbers. Add startup timing around MPI and worker readiness, model/executor initialization, resource allocation/teardown, existing rank barriers, HTTP startup, service registration and complete cluster readiness. Nested phases are excluded from outer totals; parent-process waits overlap worker execution and must not be summed across processes. Failed phases retain elapsed time and propagate exceptions.

These are host-side measurements using existing synchronization; no CUDA synchronization, barriers or collectives are added. Attention timing includes model forward, first-touch JIT and waiting rather than pure compiler time. Logs follow existing filtering; Python API users can enable them with `TLLM_LOG_LEVEL=INFO`. Worker-exit detection remains active.

This PR adjusts the timeout and adds diagnostics. It does not optimize startup; investigation of model initialization, compilation/cache reuse and autotuning will be a separate follow-up.

## Test Coverage

Target integration test: `disaggregated/test_disaggregated.py::test_disaggregated_ctxpp4_genpp4[TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0]` (8 GPUs).

| Platform / run | Tested readiness budget | Cluster launch-to-ready | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B300 / isolated JIT caches | 900 s | **639.988 s** | **1 passed**, full pytest **672.58 s** |
| B200 / isolated JIT caches | 500 s | **228.326 s** | PASS |
| B200 / cache reuse | 500 s | **93.144 s** | PASS |

B300 was tested on `dc36700308` with a per-invocation 900-second override. Commit `5fcc8be33c` makes that same timeout the test's source default; this final timeout/comment-only revision has not been separately GPU-rerun. B200 was tested on `9311771ce1`.

B300 cold-start breakdown (two rank-0 workers running concurrently):

| Stage | Measured wall time |
| --- | --- |
| Model initialization | approximately 294 s |
| Sampling module warmup | 84.5–84.6 s |
| Attention warmup | 149.7–149.9 s |
| Autotuner | 22.7–23.5 s |
| First warmup total, including the warmup stages above | 265.5–271.0 s |
| Second internal warmup pass | 0.8–1.2 s |

The second internal pass is part of the same startup, not a separate hot-start run. The startup/warmup log validator passed after correcting its expected PID count to cover both passes on all eight ranks; pytest passed independently, while the original wrapper exit code reflected that validator issue. A successful current-implementation B300 hot-start measurement is still outstanding: the preceding cache-reuse attempt failed on a 60-second NCCL initialization timeout.

**CPU regression tests:** 13 added cases; **32 passed, 22 deselected** (GPU cases excluded), covering:

- `_StartupTimer`: nested/repeated phase accounting, unattributed time, failed-phase timing, exception propagation and depth restoration.
- Warmup diagnostics: repeated phases, exception timing, empty/zero-duration summaries and slow-warning threshold boundaries.
- Executor creation: profiling and final allocation phase names/order, including both estimation and direct-allocation paths.

`unittest/test_startup.py` is explicitly listed in `l0_cpu.yml`; the other two test files are covered by the existing `unittest/_torch/executor` directory entry, with the new cases marked CPU-only. Pre-commit and the targeted readiness-argument check passed for the final change.

Cold runs isolate FlashInfer, Triton, Torch-extension and CUDA caches; OS page caches are not globally cleared, and weights remain on shared storage. These are individual measurements rather than a worst-case startup bound. The 900-second budget leaves approximately 260 seconds of headroom relative to the measured B300 readiness time.

title: [#19551][fix] Preserve disagg worker events after event failure
body:
## Description

`WatchEventQueue.drain()` destructively removes the queued watch events before `DisaggClusterManager.worker_event_loop` processes them.

Previously, the event loop handled the entire drained batch under a single exception handler. If processing one event raised an exception, the loop stopped processing the batch. Any events that had already been drained but appeared later in the same batch were therefore discarded and could not be retried on the next polling iteration.

This can leave the cluster manager with stale or missing worker state. For example:

```text
[DELETE unknown-worker, SET w1]
            |
            v
DELETE raises ValueError
            |
            v
SET w1 is never processed
            |
            v
drained queue is empty
```

### Fix

This change:

* isolates exception handling to each individual watch event so one failing event does not abort the rest of the drained batch;
* handles DELETE events for unknown workers as an idempotent no-op instead of allowing the lookup error to abort the batch;
* preserves the existing behavior for normal SET and known-worker DELETE events.

### Tests

Added two regression tests:

* `test_worker_event_loop_keeps_batch_after_unknown_delete`
* `test_worker_event_loop_isolates_on_event_failures`

The tests exercise the real `worker_event_loop` and `WatchEventQueue.drain()` path and verify that later events in the same drained batch are still processed.

The tests were also checked against the original implementation:

```text
Original HEAD:
  test_worker_event_loop_keeps_batch_after_unknown_delete -> FAIL
  test_worker_event_loop_isolates_on_event_failures       -> FAIL

HEAD + isolation-only change:
  test 1 -> FAIL
  test 2 -> PASS

HEAD + unknown-DELETE-only change:
  test 1 -> PASS
  test 2 -> FAIL

Current implementation:
  test 1 -> PASS
  test 2 -> PASS
```

This confirms that the regression tests cover both parts of the fix.

## Validation

### System

```text
TensorRT-LLM commit: 67a0328029
GPU: NVIDIA Tesla T4, 16 GB VRAM
Compute Capability: 7.5 (SM75)
Driver: 580.178.04
CUDA: 13.0
Python: 3.12.10
OS: Linux (OpenHPC)
```

The #19551 regression itself is CPU-only and does not exercise CUDA, NIXL, UCX, or model execution.

### Regression tests

Executed on the OpenHPC environment:

```bash
timeout 120 /tmp/repro-venv312/bin/python -u -m pytest \
  tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_disagg_cluster_manager_worker.py \
  -k "test_worker_event_loop" \
  -p no:cacheprovider -q
```

Result:

```text
2 passed, 13 deselected, 19 warnings in 2.48s
```

The two new regression tests both passed.

### Relevant non-etcd test suite

```bash
timeout 200 /tmp/repro-venv312/bin/python -u -m pytest \
  tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_disagg_cluster_manager_worker.py \
  -k "not etcd" \
  -p no:cacheprovider -q
```

Result:

```text
10 passed, 5 deselected, 19 warnings in 17.56s
```

### Additional etcd validation

An etcd test was also successfully executed in the unsandboxed OpenHPC environment:

```text
1 passed, 14 deselected, 19 warnings in 7.32s
```

The remaining etcd variants could not be reliably exercised in the sandbox because the environment prevents etcd/gRPC networking (`operation not permitted`). The same limitation was reproduced against an unmodified HEAD, so it is not attributable to this change.


Resolves #19551.
@karljang — requesting your review when you have a chance. Thanks!

## QA Engineer Review

title: [None][fix] preserve multimodal UUID in V2 KV events
body:
## Description

Buffered KV cache event protocol V2 currently derives multimodal tokens from content digests, but drops the frontend-provided multimodal UUID before events are serialized. This causes routing observers to see a different identity from the one attached to the request.

This change carries both the digest and optional multimodal UUID through the native and Python V2 token/radix/event paths. Digest equality and hashing remain unchanged for cache lookup and reuse, while serialized V2 events now add `uuid` when one was provided. UUID-less inputs keep the existing schema, legacy tuple forms remain accepted, and protocol V1 retains its existing UUID-as-hash behavior. The request binding, documentation, and regression coverage are updated accordingly.

Functional impact is limited to preserving multimodal identity in V2 buffered event payloads; no cache-key or cache-reuse semantics change. No performance regression is expected.

- All pre-commit hooks passed for changed files.
- Native V2 digest-pool and event tests: 8 passed.

title: [None][fix] Retire KV transfer ownership after late backend completion
body:
## Summary

Allow an ownership-enabled Python KV transfer that became `IN_DOUBT` to retire safely when its **exact retained backend operation** later proves DONE. Logical failure/cancellation stays unchanged, and admission quarantine remains closed.

Depends on #19377; merge it first. Both target `main` and were rebased onto `1a36f4fed`; review this PR's [isolated change](https://github.com/chienchunhung/TensorRT-LLM/compare/6f0b43a23dc86516c07beaf6f56ff75fb442168e...f372733fe8906c0f4c1225d8ac5278b8627e9c9a).

## Major changes

- [Same-handle settlement](https://github.com/chienchunhung/TensorRT-LLM/blob/f372733fe8906c0f4c1225d8ac5278b8627e9c9a/tensorrt_llm/_torch/disaggregation/native/transfer.py#L674): recheck retained request/status identity, require positive DONE, and retire the physical claim idempotently.
- [Ordered reporting and cleanup](https://github.com/chienchunhung/TensorRT-LLM/blob/f372733fe8906c0f4c1225d8ac5278b8627e9c9a/tensorrt_llm/_torch/disaggregation/native/transfer.py#L1125): retry `IN_DOUBT → FAILED_QUIESCED` evidence in worker order; prevent later failure reports overtaking it; release retained storage once.
- [Receiver settlement](https://github.com/chienchunhung/TensorRT-LLM/blob/f372733fe8906c0f4c1225d8ac5278b8627e9c9a/tensorrt_llm/_torch/disaggregation/native/transfer.py#L364): retain sibling/publication/local-completion gates and permanently reject invalid evidence. `FAILED_QUIESCED` is physical proof, not delivery success.

Existing opt-in bridge only: matching binaries/configuration, unique request IDs, one immutable selected ADP writer group, and no retry/reroute remain required. No new activation profile, deadline, abort, or restart policy; unproven operations remain retained.

## Verification

- **Unit-test delta:** [36 new cases / 15 test functions](https://github.com/chienchunhung/TensorRT-LLM/blob/f372733fe8906c0f4c1225d8ac5278b8627e9c9a/tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_transfer_late_settlement.py) cover exact-handle identity, duplicate/concurrent settlement, report ordering/retries, sibling retention and shutdown; **12 cases** check unchanged failure/cancellation outcomes.
- **Native Linux CI, pre-rebase head `5760bc13b`:** all **36/36 new cases passed on each x86 and ARM stage** ([results #61069](https://nv/trt-llm-cicd/job/main/job/L0_MergeRequest_PR/61069/)).
- **Current head `f372733fe8`:** [full CI #61879](https://nv/trt-llm-cicd/job/main/job/L0_MergeRequest_PR/61879/) is running.
- **Changed-line unit-test coverage:** not yet measured in native CI; measure this PR's isolated delta against #19377, not the combined stack.

These CPU unit tests do not establish real NIXL/CUDA or multi-rank qualification.

Rebase is patch-equivalent. Isolated size, excluding #19377: **216 production + 527 test lines changed**.

## Description

When a request's prompt exceeds `max_seq_len`, the 400 response exposed internal deduction arithmetic and was unactionable:

```
`default_max_tokens` (-2785) must be greater than 0, ...
`default_max_tokens` (-2785) = max_seq_len (69632) - `splited_prompt_len` (72417)
```

This PR replaces it with OpenAI's wording, which agent frameworks already pattern-match to trigger context compaction:

```
This model's maximum context length is 69632 tokens. However, your messages resulted in 69666 tokens. Please reduce the length of the messages.
```

and attaches the machine-readable code `context_length_exceeded` to the error payload (`ErrorResponse.code` now allows a string; it stays the HTTP status for every other error). The HTTP status (400) and the reject-don't-truncate semantics are unchanged; the `max_tokens<=0` validation message is untouched.

The message is raised in `_deduce_max_tokens` and crosses the executor IPC boundary as a plain string (`RequestError`), so the server detects it by text in `create_error_response`, the single chokepoint through which the chat, completions, and responses endpoints render request errors.

KDA prefill can produce different outputs and recurrent state for identical inputs because TMA can overwrite shared Q/K while K1 Pass 2b is still reading them. title: [None][feat] support W4A16 GPTQ linear layers in the PyTorch backend
body:
# [None][feat] support W4A16 GPTQ linear layers in the PyTorch backend

The native PyTorch backend does not recognize Hugging Face GPTQ configuration or select a W4A16 GPTQ Linear method. This adds direct loading of dense 4-bit GPTQ checkpoints using the existing grouped INT4 FP16/BF16 GEMM, including zero-point conversion, fused QKV/gate-up loading, and tensor-parallel weight slicing.

Related to the W4A16 GPTQ item in #3701. Supports group sizes 64/128 and GPTQ v1/v2 with activation ordering disabled. The scope is dense Linear-based projections; embeddings and lm_head remain unquantized, and GPTQ support for fused MoE expert layers is outside this PR. Unsupported checkpoint layouts and partial updates fail explicitly. No new public configuration fields or CUDA kernels are introduced.

Validation on RTX 3090: 33 CPU and 36 GPU tests pass, including loader entry points, preservation of existing KV-cache quantization, rejection of partial weight loading, asymmetric zero points, fused projections, GQA replication, and CUDA Graph capture. GPU test inputs use fixed local generators. All 168 quantized matrices of Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-GPTQ-Int4 match independent dequantization; two greedy generation prompts match an independent HF FP16 reference token-for-token. CPU/A10 test registration and usage documentation are included.

Merged main at abc69b9c377218570f3a4bc4ef8e07b630450b78 and resolved the quantization-config test conflict by preserving the upstream NVFP4 tests alongside the GPTQ tests. Scoped formatting, lint, file checks, and static AST test-list validation pass. The merge preserves the original GPTQ production behavior and CI-registration changes; the documentation also records the loading-memory limitation below.

title: [None][fix] Refuse paged-context attention when no fused kernel exists
body:
## Description

`TrtllmAttentionMetadata` enables `use_paged_context_fmha` whenever chunked prefill, KV block reuse or speculative draft tokens are configured. All three require the context phase to attend to KV that is already in the cache, and only the fused context FMHA kernel can do that.

`AttentionOp::initialize()` ends with `mEnableContextFMHA = mIsGenerationMLA || mFmhaDispatcher->isSupported()`, so a configuration with no compiled kernel silently clears the flag and the context phase runs the unfused path. That path builds K and V from the current chunk alone: the cached prefix is dropped from attention and then overwritten by the chunk's write-back. Every request with a non-zero cached length returns a plausible wrong answer with no error and no warning that reaches the caller.

A kernel can be missing either because the kernel set has none for that combination, or because the build's `--cuda_architectures` does not name the SM of the device it is running on — `cuda_configuration.cmake` stamps `-DEXCLUDE_SM_<arch>` for every omitted architecture, which compiles the matching block of the trtllm-gen cubin table out. Both cases reach the same silent fallback.

This PR refuses instead: `get_attention_op` now rejects a non-MLA paged-context configuration whose initialization produced no context FMHA kernel. The check runs after `initialize()` (only the initialized op reflects the exact Q/KV/output precision, mask type and page size) and outside `initialize()` itself, which is `noexcept`. The error names both causes and the available remedies.

It also adds `thop.fused_context_fmha_kernel_exists(head_size, kv_cache_dtype, tokens_per_block, output_dtype)` to query what the running build contains for a dense causal paged-context probe (output dtype is explicit because the runtime chooses it independently of the KV cache dtype). The probe fixes the mask, layout and head ratio, so it is a diagnostic; the op-level refusal is the authoritative check. A new developer-guide section documents both.

## Test Coverage

`tests/unittest/_torch/attention/test_context_fmha_kernel_presence.py` (requires a GPU): the lookup rejects invalid dimensions and unsupported precisions, reports present for a configuration the SM100-family kernel table carries, reports absent for a head size it does not, and is page-size sensitive.

title: [None][fix] Preserve KV transfer outcomes independently of polling
body:
## Summary

Commit each native KV-transfer Attempt's logical outcome when the task/session changes state, rather than when it is first polled. A later cancellation, failure, or physical completion cannot rewrite an earlier Delivered/Failed/Cancelled result. Physical retirement and deadlines are unchanged.

## Major changes

- [`_LogicalOutcomes`](https://github.com/chienchunhung/TensorRT-LLM/blob/6f0b43a23dc86516c07beaf6f56ff75fb442168e/tensorrt_llm/_torch/disaggregation/native/transfer.py#L214): serialize completion against session failure/cancellation; preserve original cause and local/peer cancellation origin.
- [`TaskHandle.poll()`](https://github.com/chienchunhung/TensorRT-LLM/blob/6f0b43a23dc86516c07beaf6f56ff75fb442168e/tensorrt_llm/_torch/disaggregation/native/handle.py#L40): observe the committed outcome while keeping report progress separate.
- [Regression tests](https://github.com/chienchunhung/TensorRT-LLM/blob/6f0b43a23dc86516c07beaf6f56ff75fb442168e/tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_task_handle.py#L655): cover early/late/fresh observers, queued cancellation, sibling outcomes, original errors, and scatter/cancel ordering.

## Verification

**Regression-first history:** [commit 1 `9bb4b212cf`](https://github.com/chienchunhung/TensorRT-LLM/commit/9bb4b212cf102bad48f7c4729b688d06295dd505) adds only tests; production remains `main@1a36f4fed`. [Commit 2 `6f0b43a23d`](https://github.com/chienchunhung/TensorRT-LLM/commit/6f0b43a23dc86516c07beaf6f56ff75fb442168e) adds the fix.

| Reproducer | Required fixed behavior |
|---|---|
| [Late completion with early/late/fresh polling](https://github.com/chienchunhung/TensorRT-LLM/blob/9bb4b212cf102bad48f7c4729b688d06295dd505/tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_task_handle.py#L652) | Failure/cancellation remains unchanged for every observer; late completion cannot become Delivered. |
| [Queued sender abort after cancellation](https://github.com/chienchunhung/TensorRT-LLM/blob/9bb4b212cf102bad48f7c4729b688d06295dd505/tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_task_handle.py#L716) | Preserve Cancelled and its local/peer origin, rather than generic Failed. |
| [Repeated failures before first poll](https://github.com/chienchunhung/TensorRT-LLM/blob/9bb4b212cf102bad48f7c4729b688d06295dd505/tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_task_handle.py#L762) | Preserve the original failure cause rather than the later cleanup error. |

- **Before fix (RED):** native Linux execution of the test-only commit has not been captured. The reproducer commit is available, but native RED → GREEN proof is not yet complete.
- **After fix (GREEN), pre-rebase `8b20e0410`:** native x86 and ARM each passed **55/55 TaskHandle cases (27 → 55, +28)** and **76/76 combined TaskHandle/fetch/publish cases** ([CI #61068](https://nv/trt-llm-cicd/job/main/job/L0_MergeRequest_PR/61068/)).
- **Current head `6f0b43a23d`:** [full CI #61881](https://nv/trt-llm-cicd/job/main/job/L0_MergeRequest_PR/61881/) is running; the rebase is patch-equivalent.
- **Changed-line coverage:** not measured in native CI. CPU unit-test passes do not establish real NIXL/CUDA or multi-rank qualification.

Size: **208 production + 318 test lines changed**.

title: [None][feat] Mooncake store part 1: pool, CLI, and V2 scheduler preemption
body:
## Description

Splits out the part of the Mooncake store integration [MR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/19171) that does not depend on KV connector support in KVCacheManagerV2, so it can be reviewed and merged without waiting on that work [MR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/17974).

The store side is complete: the pool master and its lifecycle, segment donation from nodes that run no connector, the JSON config, block hashing and key namespacing, and the pinned host slots pages pass through where GPUDirect RDMA is unavailable. `trtllm-serve` provisions the pool during bringup, and `mooncake_master` / `mooncake_donor` cover the parts of a pool that cannot belong to a server.

The connector that moves KV pages in and out of the pool needs the KV cache layout description, and follows separately [here](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/19171).

When Mooncake is in use, native host offloading with KVCMv2 is turned off.

Also adds preemption to the V2 scheduler, which is what a full pool falls back to when there is no cache tier below GPU to suspend into: suspended pages stay HELD and unevictable there, so suspension frees nothing. A victim gives its pages up and re-prefills. Alongside it, a deadlock detector fails loudly when consecutive scheduling passes can neither schedule nor reclaim anything, instead of spinning at full speed while looking healthy.

title: [TRTLLM-16282][feat] Add sparse KV cache configuration and tier-aware locking
body: ## Description Sparse attention history needs to remain pinned in host memory while writable and dense pages stay on the GPU. This PR implements **steps 1–2** of the offload/demotion roadmap below, establishing the storage and locking rules needed for later offload. The sparse flag defaults to false, preserving existing dense configuration behavior. 1. **Configure sparse storage.** Add opt-in `BufferConfig.is_sparse` in C++ and nanobind, require level-1 `HOST_MEM`, and reject sparse SSM buffers and mixed sparsity within an attention layer. Include sparsity in lifecycle identity and GPU pool grouping while preserving compatible sparse-buffer coalescing. 2. **Define tier-aware locks.** Keep writable and dense pages locked on GPU and allow sparse history to remain locked in level-1 host memory. Preserve the intended tier through resume, prefetch, shared-prefix rebasing, and OOM rollback. Copy partial reused prefixes from their actual source tier into private GPU pages, deduplicate batched migration, prevent ordinary migration of locked pages, and preserve event ordering and tier-correct slot accounting. The C++ subsystem guide and Python type declarations are updated alongside these changes. The declarations also describe planned device page-table and sparse-fetch APIs whose runtime implementations remain follow-up work. **The step numbers describe implementation order; the planned runtime path is 4 → 3 → 5.** Blue steps 1–2 are included in this PR. Orange steps 3–5 will come in separate PR: - **4 — Advance the history watermark:** `setHistoryLength()` identifies newly completed sparse-history pages and triggers demotion. Input-token, partial, and dense pages continue ordinary GPU management. - **3 — Batched demotion:** `KvCache::demoteSparsePages()` will deduplicate pages, reserve host slots, wait for prior use, copy full coalesced pages GPU → CPU, and publish host indices and completion events. - **5 — Register GPU cache ownership:** transfer retained GPU pages to the sparse cache and expose clean buffer entries keyed by host slot and buffer index, with per-pool tracking, eviction, and dirty-row hooks. In that planned flow, **the host page becomes authoritative and remains locked**, while `SparsePageHandoff` retains the original GPU allocation until ownership transfer or cleanup. Clean GPU cache entries need no writeback; every entry referring to a host slot must be invalidated before that slot is reused. Full Batch device-table publication, `fetch_sparse_pages`, H2D refill, and attention integration are future consumers outside this offload/demotion plan. ## Test Coverage - `KvCacheManagerV2ConfigTest`: dense defaults, host-tier requirements, rejected configurations, sparse/dense separation, and compatible pool coalescing. - `KvCacheManagerV2PageLockTest`: nine regressions covering shared host prefixes, dense GPU locks, partial-prefix copying, disk restoration, writable pages, rollback, mixed lifecycles, commit rebasing, and scratch-slot accounting. - Existing cold-page and migration-statistics tests updated for generalized migration. - Python `TestSparseBufferConfig`: binding defaults/copy behavior and configuration validation. Validation performed while preparing the commits and draft: repository pre-commit and DCO hooks passed for the tier-aware locking commit, `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed, and the pre-push hooks (including the confidentiality scan) passed. GPU/runtime tests were not rerun while preparing this draft. ## PR Checklist - [x] Description explains the implemented behavior and remaining draft scope. - [x] Regression tests cover the new configuration and locking paths. - [x] All three commits include DCO sign-off. - [ ] Review the remaining repository submission requirements and CI results before marking ready.

title: [None][refactor] BREAKING: Remove the Python backend of KVCacheManagerV2
body:
## Summary

KVCacheManagerV2 shipped two implementations of the same subsystem behind
`TLLM_KV_CACHE_MANAGER_V2_BACKEND`. The C++ port is the default, is what CI exercises, and
is the only backend newer features support, so the Python implementation was carrying
duplicate block-key hashing, eviction and stats logic that had to stay bit-identical to
C++, plus a mypyc + `rawref` build pipeline that existed only to make it fast enough to
matter.

`tensorrt_llm/runtime/kv_cache_manager_v2/` is now a re-export shim over the nanobind
module plus the backend-agnostic `_introspection` dispatcher: **36 tracked files down to 4**,
net **−13k lines**.

## Commits

1. **Remove the Python backend** — the deletion, consumer migration and build cleanup.
2. **Lock SSM life cycles into KVCM2 page-movement statistics** — new C++ coverage for
   behaviour that only the deleted Python tests guarded.

## New bindings

Only one consumer needed native support. The KV-aware router's V2 hashing is expressed with
the existing `sequence_to_blockchain_keys` (every caller chains from a reuse-scope root, and
its first yielded pair *is* that root), so `v2_sha256_block_hasher` is gone and **no hashing
binding was added**. Equivalence was verified against a reference implementation of the old
per-chunk chaining across 3 block sizes x 2 algorithms x salted/unsalted -- byte-identical --
and against golden digests captured from the Python hasher before deleting it.

The native disaggregated bounce buffer did need something: `PooledPhysMemAllocator` and
`VirtMem` wrap the existing `cudaVirtMem.{h,cpp}`. They register on the **`_introspection`
submodule**, not the package surface, because they carry no stability promise -- the package
namespace is the stable surface. Three members total (`device_id`, `address`, `destroy`); the
package's exported API shrinks from 74 to 72 symbols.

## BREAKING

- `TLLM_KV_CACHE_MANAGER_V2_BACKEND=python` no longer exists.
- `build_wheel.py --mypyc` and `TRTLLM_ENABLE_MYPYC` are gone, along with `setup_mypyc.py`,
  the `rawref` C extension and the `setup.py` packaging surgery they required.
- **Streaming KV events (`kv_cache_config.kv_events_config`) are dropped.** The sink is
  duck-typed Python and the C++ radix tree calls its sink natively, so there is no live
  path. `validate_streaming_support` now rejects the config and points at the buffered path
  via `event_buffer_max_size`. The interface is kept as a stub and its tests are skipped
  rather than deleted, so a native sink can restore it later.

## Test coverage

Deleting the Python implementation orphaned `test_kv_cache_stats_life_cycles.py`, which
drove the Python page-movement recorders through a duck-typed stand-in. That behaviour —
SSM/recurrent life cycles appearing in iteration stats, with global cache-hit counters
staying attention-only — was fixed in **both** backends by #17447, but only ever tested in
Python, and no C++ test builds an SSM life cycle at all.

The second commit closes that with a hybrid attention + SSM fixture (the first in the C++
suite) and three cases: offload/onboard per life cycle, the attention-only alloc-counter
guard, and host drops. **Each was confirmed to fail when the life-cycle filters are restored
in `KvCache::_recordMigratedSlots` / `_recordDroppedPages`** — a regression lock that cannot
detect the regression is worthless.

Host-drop coverage is new for attention too; nothing asserted it against a live manager
before.

## Verification

- `kvCacheManagerV2StatsTest`: 13/13 (10 pre-existing + 3 new)
- `tests/unittest/kv_cache_manager_v2_tests/`: 255 passed, 20 skipped
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/`: 788 passed
- `executor/test_stats_serializer.py`, `disaggregated/test_router.py`: green
- Repo-wide grep for any deleted submodule: clean

All run on a B200. Note the local dev box is an H100 while `cpp/build` was configured
`CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=100-real`, which aborts on kernel launch — an artefact of the build
config, not a code defect, and it reproduces identically on unmodified `main`.

changed by this PR.

Existing tests cover zero-KV mask construction and the eager sanitization helper,
but they do not send a mask containing `True` values through the cross-rank
exchange.

The existing end-to-end Helix tests also give every rank a non-zero KV slice, so
the zero-local-KV neutralization path is not exercised.

The new test poisons masked rows with NaN, drives `_helix_post_process` across two

control verifies that the NaN poison remains observable when sanitization is
disabled, so the positive tests have a meaningful failure signal.

same-device check, a mask allocated on another GPU can pass validation and its
pointer can be dereferenced from the wrong device.

- an empty mask;
- a mask length that does not divide the all-to-all entry count;

| NCCL | 17 | eager | compiled sanitize + transpose/store path |
| FIFO v2 | 17 | eager | sender-side shared-memory sanitization |
| FIFO v2 | 96 | CUDA Graph | production capture/replay path |
| FIFO v2 | 17 | mask withheld | negative control; output must contain NaN |

- per-rank zero-KV masks;
- NaN-poisoned masked rows;
- a float64 reference combine;
- output finiteness and numerical checks;
- deadline-bounded MPI `Ibarrier` calls around CUDA Graph capture.

## Summary

Rework how CBTS Layer C decides which test a coverage row belongs to. The current design hands the current nodeid to subprocesses through a marker file they poll and a stop file that suppresses writes; both are best-effort, and neither can tell anyone when attribution has gone wrong. This PR replaces them with a `AF_UNIX` context channel with acknowledgements, keys tracker activation to imports rather than to a guess about the process, and records a **taint** whenever the channel cannot vouch for a record, so a suspect row is visible in the database instead of silently wrong.

## Issues

- **Attribution was best-effort.** Subprocesses learned the current test by polling a marker file at a fixed interval. A worker starting a test before its next poll recorded the previous test's nodeid, and nothing recorded that this had happened. 
- **Process identity was inferred.** `sitecustomize.py` guessed what a process was by inspecting command lines, so a new launch shape silently landed in the wrong branch — including a pytest process with no plugin loaded, whose whole run then landed under the empty context and was dropped by the merge.
- **Shutdown raced the artifact.** A stop sentinel plus a fixed sleep was the only thing between a still-writing worker and the results tar.

## What changes

**Context channel (`cbts_channel.py`, new).** The pytest process binds an `AF_UNIX` socket and broadcasts the current test to its subprocesses. Newline-terminated frames: `C <seq> <nodeid>` announces, `X <seq>` ends the session, `A <seq>` acknowledges, `I <uid>` identifies a subscriber. Registration and the first context are delivered under one lock and read on the subscribing thread, so a process is on the right context before `subscribe()` returns. `announce()` waits for acknowledgements before the test body runs, which is what keeps a reused pool worker from spending the start of a test answering to the one before it. At session end the producer announces `X` and waits for every subscriber to save and disconnect, so the output directory is quiet before the tar reads it — the sentinel file and its sleep are gone.

MPI pool workers are spawned from an environment captured before `pytest_configure` bound the socket, so the patched `MPIPoolExecutor` (`cbts_pool.py`, split out of the plugin so a non-pytest process can install it) forwards the address through mpi4py's own `env` payload, applied during the worker's sync handshake.

**Cooperative process roles.** `CBTS_PROCESS_ROLE` is set by whoever launches a process — `outer_pytest` by `L0_Test.groovy`, `inner_pytest` by `test_unittests.py` — and popped by `sitecustomize.py`, so a role describes exactly one process and the workers it spawns come up unlabelled, which is what they are. Only the processes nobody on our side launches (pip's build tooling, raylet's workers) are still recognised from their launch target, and there the target is read from the interpreter's own options rather than pattern-matched against a command line.

**Import-keyed activation.** A meta-path finder wraps the resolved loader so a hook fires the moment `exec_module` returns: `mpi4py.futures` finishing installs the pool patch before any executor exists, and `tensorrt_llm` finishing subscribes to the channel and *then* enables `PY_START`, in that order, so recording never starts against a stale context. A bounded timer still activates a
process that never imports the framework.

**Taint.** Where the channel cannot vouch for a record, the affected rows are kept and marked. Two kinds, because a single failure spoils two different things:

| `kind` | Claim | You cannot trust |
|---|---|---|
| `attribution` | rows recorded under this test may belong to another one | what is **there** |
| `incomplete` | rows recorded under this test are right, but some are missing | what is **absent** |

When a subscriber stops keeping up during test A and test B starts, B's work keeps landing on A: A is `attribution`-tainted and B — with every test after it — is `incomplete`. The producer names both because it announces every test itself. A process that never managed to subscribe records the one failure the producer structurally cannot see (it has no socket, no identity, no row anywhere); it taints its spawn context for attribution and the whole stage for incompleteness, since it never heard an announcement and cannot name the tests missing its coverage. That over-reports when such a process really did serve one test — the cheap error, taken over the silent one.

Taints live in the recording process's own leaf database, so they need no extra artifact and no extra collection path. `compact_db.py` gains a `taint` table, a `taint_rows` view, and a `tainted` column on `test_case_meta` (stage-scoped when the taint names the empty context); the reducer merges them like every other relation. `touch_db.incomplete_capture_tests()` adds `tainted != 0`, so a tainted test joins the never-skipped set alongside a failed outcome and a missing worker save.

## Test coverage

- `tests/unittest/scripts/test_cbts_channel.py` (new) — announce/ack ordering, join-under-lock, ejecting a hung subscriber, drain at session end, and the taint set each failure produces.
- `tests/unittest/scripts/test_cbts_bootstrap.py` (new) — role handling across launch shapes (`python -m pytest`, `python -X … -m pytest`, console script), opt-out targets, and that the plugin registers regardless of invocation.
- `tests/unittest/scripts/test_compact_db.py` — taint round-trip, taint scope (per-test vs stage-scoped), and merge idempotency with taints present.

## Docs

`coverage_utils/README.md`, `coverage_utils/COLLECTION.md` and `coverage_selection/SELECTION.md` are brought in line with the code.

- **`CuteDslFc12FusedMoE` is not reachable.** The op it drives, `torch.ops.trtllm.cute_dsl_nvfp4_fc12_fused_rubin`, is registered nowhere on `main`. ## Description

SM90 SageAttention now runs the refreshed warp-specialized kernel, shipped as a pre-built cubin. It scales Q and K in the groups its BMM1 fragment hands each thread, so it supports one recipe:

- INT8 Q/K, e4m3 PV
- block sizes (q, k, v) = (2, 16, 1)
- head_dim 128, separate Q/K/V, padding mask, no KV cache

Kernel generation (cpp/kernels/fmha_v2):

- SageAttention comes from pre-built cubins. SAGE_CUBIN_TRAITS holds the metadata rows the runtime needs, and get_kernel_code() rejects sage specs.
- Enumerate only the SM90 separate-Q/K/V spec. Drops the SM89 cubins, the contiguous-block SM90 cubin, and the bin/fmha.exe sage test.

Quantizer (common/sagePartition.h, common/sageQuant.*):

- A scale grouping is a CuTe layout, so one quantizer serves both the contiguous (SM100) and per-thread (SM90) groupings.
- The two consumers derive a scale buffer's head stride differently and are not passed it, so each partition declares its own convention.
- Adds the V-staging / K-mean phase split, and optional K-smoothing that stays off.

Runtime (common/attentionOp.*, kernels/fmhaDispatcher.cpp):

- Select the scale partition and the FMHA input data type per SM.
- SM90 SageAttention is selected as E4M3: the fmha_v2 kernel table is keyed on input and output data type alone and cannot encode int8 Q/K with an e4m3 V. The quantizer still writes INT8 Q and K.
- Reject SageAttention on unsupported architectures and block sizes, and report unsupported block sizes where they are configured.


## Test Coverage

Tests:

- test_attention_trtllm_sage_hopper covers the SM90 recipe.
- test_sage_attention_self_attention is gated to SM100, the only architecture implementing its contiguous-block recipe.

title: [None][fix] Size the FlashInfer page-index buffer for VSWA on V1 KV cache
body:
## Description

`FlashInferAttentionMetadata._post_init_with_buffers` read
`kv_cache_manager.blocks_in_primary_pool` directly to seed `max_num_blocks`,
which sizes the flat `_paged_kv_indices` buffer and the per-pool VSWA buffers.
That scalar is not part of the KV cache manager interface:

* `KVCacheManagerV2` always exposes it as a property.
* The V1 `KVCacheManager` only assigns it when it ends up with a single pool.
  The VSWA sizing path (`calculate_max_num_blocks_for_vswa()`) fills the
  `blocks_per_window` dict instead and leaves the scalar unset, as the standing
  `FIXME` next to it in `pyexecutor/resource_manager.py` already notes ("only
  covers the single window case and not VSWA scheme").

Any VSWA model routed to a V1 manager therefore dies in metadata construction
with:

```
AttributeError: 'KVCacheManager' object has no attribute 'blocks_in_primary_pool'
```

Disaggregated serving is one such route: `llm_utils.py` keeps a model's V2
preference only for the NIXL + Python-transceiver combination and otherwise
falls back to V1, so a VSWA model that runs fine aggregated crashes as soon as a
cache transceiver is configured.

The fix routes the read through a small `_get_blocks_in_primary_pool()` helper:

* use `blocks_in_primary_pool` when the manager exposes it (V2, single-pool V1);
* otherwise take the largest primary count from `blocks_per_window`. That is an
  upper bound across the pools, so the buffer stays large enough for every
  pool, and it feeds the same `max_num_blocks` seed that the per-layer buffer
  sizes are folded into;
* raise a named `AttributeError` describing both missing attributes when
  neither is available, instead of an anonymous attribute read.

This matches the `getattr`-guarded V2-only lookups a few lines further down in
the same function ("V1 managers lack the per-pool infrastructure"). The
`FIXME` in `resource_manager.py` is left in place; its other point
(single-window-only semantics of the scalar) still stands.

## Test Coverage

Unit test (CPU-only, stub managers):

`tests/unittest/_torch/attention/test_flashinfer_attention.py::TestFlashInferAttention::test_blocks_in_primary_pool_falls_back_to_blocks_per_window`

* a V2-shaped manager returns the scalar even when a `blocks_per_window` table
  is also present;
* a V1 VSWA-shaped manager (no scalar, three windows) returns the largest
  per-window primary count;
* a manager with neither attribute, or an empty `blocks_per_window`, raises an
  `AttributeError` that names the manager type and the missing attributes.

The failure this fixes was first hit in disaggregated serving of a VSWA model
whose class prefers the V2 KV cache manager but was demoted to V1: engine setup
aborted during metadata construction with the `AttributeError` above. This
change removes that crash by sizing the buffer from the per-window table when
the scalar is absent; the guard itself is covered by the unit test above.

title: [None][feat] add VisualGen VSA and SOL sparse attention on PrimTS block-sparse FMHA
body:
## Description

VisualGen sparse attention on the PrimTS block-sparse FMHA merged in #18815. VisualGen ships two block-sparse algorithms for DiT video models; this PR gives both a TRTLLM backend (Triton predictor + generic block-sparse FMHA) next to the existing CuTeDSL kernels, selected by `AttentionConfig.backend` under one configuration per algorithm:

- **VSA** (`VideoSparseAttentionConfig`): coarse/fine Video Sparse Attention for the FastVideo VSA checkpoints. Metadata, route prediction and post-processing are shared by the TRTLLM and CuTeDSL backends (`attention_backend/sparse/vsa`); the TRTLLM backend runs the top-k prediction as Triton kernels and the fine stage through the block-sparse FMHA, with dense fallback, packed or separate QKV, TP, Ulysses and CUDA Graph support.
- **SOL** (`SolAttentionConfig`: `tau`, `thresh_type`, `disabled_until_timestep`, `dense_layers`): the TRTLLM backend runs the SOL predictor as a functional Triton operator (block pooling, key statistics, `diag`/`exact` thresholds, exact-block selection) and executes the exact blocks plus proxy K/V summaries through the block-sparse FMHA (proxy-compensated attention from flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4872). The fused CuTeDSL Sol-Attn kernel of #18329 stays as the CUTEDSL backend of the same config.
- Shared pieces: one timestep-to-phase reduction (`attention/backends/sparse/timestep_phase.py`) used by SkipSoftmax, both SOL backends and a single `sparse_attn_phase` CUDA Graph key; the VisualGen TRTLLM wrapper passes separate Q/K/V and block-sparse routes into the core for sparse calls, fuses QKV for the dense-layer and dense-phase calls of a route-predicting backend (the TRTLLM kernel serves dense self-attention from fused QKV only), and shares one FMHA plan cache per model component through the new optional `fmha_state` constructor argument of `TrtllmAttention`. These two are the only core attention changes.
- The sparse TRTLLM backends reject cross-attention, context parallelism and attention quantization; dense layers and dense timestep phases return no routes and run the dense kernel.

Behavior notes: per-token timesteps reduce to their largest live value, so a Wan 2.2 5B I2V conditioning frame at timestep zero no longer disables a configured dense prefix; SkipSoftmax dense and sparse CUDA graphs are keyed per phase on every model with a cutoff, including LTX-2. Docs: `docs/source/features/visualgen-sparse-attention.md` (per-algorithm guide) and the `SOL-Attn` column in `docs/source/models/visual-generation.md`.

## Performance and accuracy of the TRTLLM backends

One B200, `Wan2.1-VSA-T2V-14B-720P`, 720x1280, seed 42, guidance 5.0, prompt "A cat sitting on a sunny windowsill watching birds outside.", CUDA Graph on, torch.compile off. Long = 81 frames (75,600 tokens per stream), Short = 9 frames (10,800 tokens). Deployment settings follow the documentation: SOL `tau=1.0`, `diag`, `disabled_until_timestep=0.6`, `dense_layers=[0, 2, 3, 4]`, which on this checkpoint's UniPC schedule (flow shift 3.0) runs 34 of 50 steps dense and 16 sparse; VSA has no dense prefix or dense-layer option and follows the checkpoint recipe, sparsity 0.9 at 81 frames and 0.875 at 9 frames. LPIPS is AlexNet on the raw frames, scaled to [-1, 1], mean over frames (the normalization of `scripts/visualgen_eval/visual_gen_lpips_score_eval.py`); scoring the same clips as H.264 MP4 agrees within 0.005 except on near-identical pairs, where the codec adds 0.01 to 0.015.

End to end, 50 denoising steps (the timed request after warmup and one settle request):

| Workload | Algorithm | Backend | 50-step denoise s | Speedup vs dense | Speedup vs CuTeDSL |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Long | dense | TRTLLM | 584.4 | 1.00x | – |
| Long | dense | CuTeDSL | 599.7 | 0.97x | – |
| Long | SOL | CuTeDSL | 560.2 | 1.04x | – |
| Long | SOL | TRTLLM | 518.6 | 1.13x | 1.08x |
| Long | VSA | CuTeDSL | 371.0 | 1.58x | – |
| Long | VSA | TRTLLM | 325.6 | 1.79x | 1.14x |
| Short | dense | TRTLLM | 40.0 | 1.00x | – |
| Short | SOL | CuTeDSL | 39.8 | 1.00x | – |
| Short | SOL | TRTLLM | 38.6 | 1.04x | 1.03x |
| Short | VSA | CuTeDSL | 41.1 | 0.97x | – |
| Short | VSA | TRTLLM | 38.7 | 1.03x | 1.06x |

Sparse phase alone (the dense prefix disabled so every timed step is sparse; ms per self-attention call, mean over 40 layers and 24 Long / 48 Short timed steps, CUDA events inside the captured graph). This is the kernel-level comparison the end-to-end numbers are built from:

| Workload | Algorithm | Backend | Attention ms/call | Speedup vs dense | Speedup vs CuTeDSL | Transformer step ms | Step speedup vs dense | Step speedup vs CuTeDSL |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Long | dense | TRTLLM | 183.71 | 1.00x | – | 11,709 | 1.00x | – |
| Long | SOL | CuTeDSL | 127.70 | 1.44x | – | 9,218 | 1.27x | – |

On Long the TRTLLM backends spend 2.7 ms (SOL) and 5.8 ms (VSA) per call in the Triton predictors, against 7.2 ms of in-kernel preprocessing for SOL CuTeDSL and 15.8 ms for the VSA CuTeDSL predictor; the rest of the gap is the block-sparse FMHA itself (57.6 vs 120.5 ms for SOL, 36.0 vs 52.0 ms for VSA). The end-to-end SOL speedup is smaller than the per-call one because the documented example runs 34 of 50 steps and 4 of 40 layers dense.

LPIPS under the deployment settings (mean over frames; lower is closer). The dense TRTLLM pipeline is bit-exact run to run and between eager and CUDA Graph, so every non-zero value is kernel numerics amplified by the sampler; two exact dense kernels (TRTLLM vs CuTeDSL) already differ by 0.30 after 50 steps, which is the floor for any cross-kernel pair:

|---|---:|---:|
| dense TRTLLM vs dense CuTeDSL (exact-kernel floor) | 0.303 | 0.152 |
| SOL TRTLLM vs dense TRTLLM (its own dense kernel) | 0.010 | 0.030 |
| SOL CuTeDSL vs dense CuTeDSL (its own dense kernel) | 0.008 | 0.026 |
| SOL TRTLLM vs SOL CuTeDSL (prefixes run different dense kernels) | 0.304 | 0.153 |
| VSA TRTLLM vs VSA CuTeDSL | 0.154 | 0.419 |
| VSA TRTLLM vs dense TRTLLM / VSA CuTeDSL vs dense TRTLLM | 0.836 / 0.844 | 0.522 / 0.473 |

With the dense prefix, each SOL backend reproduces the sample of its own dense kernel (PSNR 38 dB on Long), and the two SOL backends differ from each other by exactly the dense-kernel floor. VSA converges to a different, clean sample than dense at 0.9 sparsity; both VSA backends agree on that sample within the floor on Long, and the Short VSA pair (0.42) is the most sensitive case (same scene, different framing, at a 9-frame workload the VSA checkpoint was not trained for). With the SOL prefix disabled entirely, SOL likewise converges to its own sample (LPIPS 0.79 vs dense for both backends, 0.10 between them). Kernel-level closeness is asserted by the parity tests in `sparse_attention/{sol,vsa}/test_*_parity.py`.

title: [None][feat] Report per-request speculative-decoding acceptance on the response
body:
## Background

TensorRT-LLM already computes per-request speculative-decoding acceptance on the PyTorch backend, then discards the attribution at the HTTP boundary. The exact `(accepted, drafted)` totals reach the serve layer and go only to the server-side perf-metrics JSONL; the per-position vectors are consumed into the Prometheus counters, where `collector.py` sums them across every request. There is no surface from which an HTTP client can obtain per-request acceptance:

| Surface | Why it does not work |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /metrics` | Per *iteration*, not per request — one iteration touches many requests via in-flight batching, so `specDecodingStats` is a batch rollup. Also drained on read into a `deque(maxlen=1000)` that evicts silently. |
| `GET /prometheus/metrics` | Cumulative over server lifetime, summed across all requests. ~32 fixed time series regardless of request count. |
| Response headers | `build_metrics_headers()` emits only timing and step breakdowns; no spec field. Server-Timing is a flat `name;dur=` list, so it structurally cannot carry a histogram. |
| `trtllm.perf_metrics` SSE event | Built by JSON-serializing that same headers dict, so it inherits the same limitation. |
| `perf_metrics_output_dir` JSONL | Has the data, but it is a file on the server's filesystem. |

Benchmarking tools consequently cannot report acceptance length per request. This is a known gap — `tests/integration/defs/perf/test_perf_sanity.py` carries CI exemptions noting that `aiperf does not propagate TRT-LLM's non-standard avg_decoded_tokens_per_iter field`.

## Summary

Two commits, reviewable independently.

**1. `[fix]` per-position arrays truncating at 16 positions.** `MAX_SPEC_DECODE_POSITIONS = 16` was bounding two unrelated things: per-request buffer size (an accuracy concern) and Prometheus `token_position` label cardinality (an operational one). The second was *emergent, not stated* — `MetricsCollector` iterates `range(len(per_pos_drafted))` with no clamp of its own, so the cardinality bound held only because the arrays happened to be length 16.

That means `max_draft_len > 16`, reachable with EAGLE3 dynamic-tree and Medusa, silently drops every position past 16, and the existing `trtllm_spec_decode_{drafted,accepted}_tokens_total` counters under-report with no indication anything was lost.

The two concerns are separated: the arrays grow on demand in the accumulator, and an explicit `MAX_SPEC_DECODE_POSITION_LABELS` clamp moves to `MetricsCollector` where cardinality actually matters. `MAX_SPEC_DECODE_POSITIONS` is retained as the initial allocation size, so the common case never reallocates. **This commit stands alone as a bug fix** and is a prerequisite for the emitted payload below being trustworthy.

**2. `[feat]` emit acceptance per choice.** Added as `speculative_decoding` on each response choice, beside the existing `avg_decoded_tokens_per_iter` — which already establishes a per-request spec-decode field in the response body.

```json
{
  "index": 0,
  "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "..."},
  "finish_reason": "stop",
  "avg_decoded_tokens_per_iter": 2.5,
  "speculative_decoding": {
    "acceptance_rate": 0.5,
    "total_accepted_draft_tokens": 30,
    "total_draft_tokens": 60,
    "num_spec_steps": 20,
    "acceptance_histogram": [8, 0, 6, 6],
    "num_spec_tokens": 3
  }
}
```

**No new instrumentation.** Every value is already an attribute on `GenerationResultBase`, which is exactly what the four OpenAI postprocess handlers already receive — so this is a serializer, not a probe.

`per_pos_accepted` is prefix-cumulative and therefore a survival function, so the acceptance histogram is its negative first difference. Totals come from `spec_dec_totals`, which the executor accumulates exactly, rather than from summing the (previously capped) vectors.

Mean acceptance length is deliberately **not** a field: it would duplicate `avg_decoded_tokens_per_iter` on the same choice and the two could drift. Consumers derive it as `1 + total_accepted_draft_tokens / num_spec_steps`.

## Enablement

Server-side only, via a new `per_request_spec_decode_stats` `TorchLlmArgs` field (`status="prototype"`), set through the YAML passed to `--extra_llm_api_options`. Off by default.

This deliberately differs from `return_perf_metrics`, which additionally requires a per-request `X-TRTLLM-return-metrics` header. Benchmarking clients discover this payload by *shape* rather than being told which engine they are talking to, so requiring a vendor-specific request header would mean a client must already know it is talking to TensorRT-LLM in order to find out. The cost stays opt-in because an operator who does not set the field pays nothing.

Kept independent of `return_perf_metrics`, which also mounts the Prometheus endpoint — coupling them would mean asking for acceptance numbers silently starts a metrics server.

## Correctness

Three identities hold on every emitted payload, and a consumer may rely on them:

```
sum(acceptance_histogram)        == num_spec_steps
sum(j * acceptance_histogram[j]) == total_accepted_draft_tokens
total_accepted_draft_tokens      <= total_draft_tokens
```

Verified end to end against a live `trtllm-serve` run (20/20 requests, 0% errors) with a benchmarking client consuming the field. Summed across the run, the pooled histogram reconciles exactly:

| Check | Computed | Reported |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sum(pooled_histogram)` | 1624+207+64+42+35 = **1972** | total steps = 1972 |
| `sum(j x histogram[j])` | 207+128+126+140 = **601** | total accepted = 601 |
| `601/7813` | 7.6923076923% | overall acceptance rate = 7.6923076923076925 |
| `1 + 601/1972` | 1.304766734279919 | token-weighted acceptance length = 1.304766734279919 |

The derived quantities match to the full float. `num_spec_tokens: 4` was read correctly from `speculative_config`, and the histogram was sized `max_draft_len + 1`.

## Known limits

- **PyTorch backend only.** The C++/TRT path populates spec metrics via `updateNumTokensPerIteration` and has no per-position vectors, so the field is simply absent there.
- **Not wired for `/v1/responses`**, whose schema has no `choices` array to attach to.
- **`num_spec_tokens` is `null` under `draft_len_schedule`**, where the per-step bound varies by batch size — the honest answer rather than a guess.
- **Tree drafting**: `total_draft_tokens` counts paths, not tree nodes, mirroring the `getMaxDraftPathLen` clamp in `updateNumTokensPerIteration`. The histogram is tree-agnostic by construction — it records output lengths per step and encodes no parent/child structure.
- Disaggregated serving is untested.

## Test coverage

- `tests/unittest/executor/test_spec_decode_stats_payload.py` (new) — histogram derivation, the three identities, padding to the configured budget, adaptive drafting, deep drafting past the initial capacity, and every omission path. Registered in `l0_a10.yml`.
- `tests/unittest/executor/test_spec_dec_stats_pairing.py` — cases for growth past the initial capacity and for the common case not reallocating.
- `tests/unittest/metrics/test_collector.py` — label cardinality stays capped when the arrays run deep.
- `TorchLlmArgs` change reflected in the API-stability reference and the golden manifest.

## API stability

Additive with a default, so `api-compatible`. Touches `tests/unittest/api_stability/references/llm.yaml` and `tensorrt_llm/usage/llm_args_golden_manifest.json`; please confirm the manifest matches a fresh run of `scripts/generate_llm_args_golden_manifest.py` in CI.

title: [https://nvbugs/6813351][fix] Revert "optimize qwen3.5 perf by removing gather and scatter op (#17365)"

## Description

Reverts #17365 (commit fbac78bd2af, "[None][perf] optimize qwen3.5 perf by removing gather and scatter op") for https://nvbugs/6813351.

#17365 added an indexed-pool fast path to the FlashInfer GDN prefill adapter (`tensorrt_llm/_torch/modules/fla/flashinfer_chunk.py`) that passes the SSM state pool and slot indices straight to `flashinfer.chunk_gated_delta_rule` on SM100/SM103. This PR removes that fast path so the adapter always gathers the indexed state into FlashInfer's packed layout, runs the kernel, and scatters the final state back, as before #17365.

Two later changes touched the same code and are kept intact:
- #19108 (preallocated GDN prefill state workspace): the `state_workspace` argument, its validation and the docstring text stay; with the fast path gone the workspace path is now used for every call.
- #19376 (FlashInfer GDN prefill on SM120/121): the `is_flashinfer_gdn_prefill_supported_arch` predicate and its tests stay.

title: [None][feat] Add the Blackwell (SM100/SM103) MXFP8 fused FC12 MoE kernel to CuteDslFusedMoE on feat/rl_rc
body:
## Description

Adds the Blackwell (SM100/SM103) port of the Rubin MXFP8 fused FC1+SwiGLU+MXFP8-requant+FC2+finalize MoE kernel to `CuteDslFusedMoE`, so the `CUTEDSL` backend serves W8A8 MXFP8 on GB200/GB300 the way it already does on Rubin. Port of the corresponding tekit commits onto `feat/rl_rc`.

- **Kernel** (`cute_dsl_kernels/blackwell/moe/`): vendored from the dynamic-kernel-generator `mxf8-opt/blackwell-port` branch (+ a small compat shim). Same `__call__` ABI and adapter contract as the Rubin kernel; the Rubin-only 128-datapath SFA descriptor is replaced by standard SM100 block-scaled MMA with a shared-memory SFA repack. Tiles: 1CTA 128x128 / 128x256, 2CTA 256x128 / 256x256 (FC2 on 128-wide sub-tiles with a two-stage accumulator).
- **Op** `trtllm::cute_dsl_mxfp8_fused_fc12_moe_inplace_blackwell` (`Sm100Mxfp8FusedFc12MoeRunner`): mirrors the Rubin op. Tactic = `(mma_tiler, mma_inst_shape, cluster_shape_mn, scheduler, stream_weights, fc1_prefetch_ktiles, fc2_prefetch_ktiles, sparse_gather)`; the last four are GB300-measured policies (L2 evict_first weight streaming, TMA-warp L2 weight prefetch, padded-group skipping in the A gather) the autotuner picks per token bucket.
- **Backend**: `CuteDslFusedMoE.can_implement` accepts MXFP8 on SM100/SM103 behind the new `IS_CUTLASS_DSL_FUSED_FC12_BLACKWELL_AVAILABLE` probe (`cutlass.memory`, `cutlass.tensor_utils`, `cutlass.utils.blackwell_helpers`, `cutlass.utils.blockscaled_layout`; no `rubin_helpers` needed). `run_moe_mxfp8_impl` dispatches by SM.
- **rl_rc-specific**: the Rubin op on this branch fuses `zero_output` and raw BF16 input quantization into its workspace reset. The Blackwell kernel has neither, so its op accepts the same arguments and performs them as separate launches (memset + `mxfp8_quantize`); `_fuses_mxfp8_input_quant` is gated to SM107 so the module keeps the native quantizer on Blackwell. No locality-domain variant (`is_locality_domain_enabled` is SM107-only).
- **Docs**: `MOE_DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md` backend table, capability matrix, tests table and a "Blackwell fused FC12" section.

GB300 graph-replay medians vs the unpoliced kernel (kernel-level, from the DKG branch): TEP8 8/21/32 tokens 15.6/34.1/47.4 -> 16.1/26.2/42.4 us; DEP16 32 tokens 62.8 -> 59.5 us; DEP4 16k tokens 2514 -> 1913 us.

## Test Coverage

Run on GB300 (SM103) inside `tensorrt-llm:pytorch-rubin-py3-sbsa-ubuntu24.04-trt11.3.0.85-0.8dev-202608311114-10540` with a wheel built from this branch (`-a 103-real -D NVRTC_DYNAMIC_LINKING=ON`):

| `tests/unittest/_torch/thop/parallel/test_cute_dsl_moe.py::test_mxfp8_fused_fc12_moe_blackwell` (every tactic on the small shapes; 4 shapes x 2 routing tiles) | 8 passed |
| `tests/unittest/_torch/moe/test_moe_backend.py::test_cutedsl_mxfp8_fused_fc12_accuracy_ab` (fused vs per-expert MXFP8 reference vs fp32 oracle, identical inputs) | 3 passed; fused-vs-oracle 2.65-2.68% RMS vs 2.68-2.70% for the reference, cosine 0.99964 (same as Rubin) |
| `tests/unittest/_torch/moe/test_moe_backend.py -k "mxfp8 and cutedsl"` | 6 passed |
| `tests/unittest/_torch/moe/test_mxfp8_moe_partial_refit.py -k CUTEDSL` (now also runs on SM100/SM103) | 9 passed |
| `tests/unittest/_torch/moe/test_moe_module.py::test_configurable_moe_single_gpu` CUTEDSL+MXFP8 (CI matrix; plus the new 512-expert top-10 4096x3072 local shape, 7 routing methods) | 9 + 14 passed |

title: [#18616][fix] Continue a reasoning end tag the model began, do not restart it
body:
## Description

`ThinkingBudgetLogitsProcessor._forced_token` had two budget checks that disagreed. The first discounts the end tokens the model already emitted; the fallback below it counted those same tokens as reasoning content and forced `reasoning_end_token_ids[0]` again. In the band `budget - partial_end_len <= content < budget` the first branch correctly declined and the fallback fired anyway, restarting the end sequence at index 0.

With a two-token `</think>` the stream came out `</` `</` `think>`, so the reasoning parser never matched a clean end tag and reasoning text leaked into `message.content`. Same class of failure as #16785, which fixed the stale-token-view path and left the arithmetic alone.

The fix is one check that always discounts the partial end sequence and resumes at `reasoning_end_token_ids[partial_end_len]`. That value is 0 when no end sequence is in flight, so the old fallback behavior is unchanged.

Only multi-token end sequences are affected. On the Qwen2.5 tokenizer `</mm:think>` encodes to 5 ids and `<channel|>` to 4.

## Test Coverage

`tests/unittest/llmapi/test_sampling_params.py::test_thinking_budget_logits_processor_does_not_restart_partial_end_sequence`, added here. Greedy decode from `[1, 5, 6, 2]` with budget 3 gives `[1, 5, 6, 2, 2, 3, 7]` on main and `[1, 5, 6, 2, 3, 7, 7]` with this change. The file's other nine thinking-budget cases pass before and after.

Fixes #18616.

## PR Checklist

## Description

Adds two E2E training tests to the existing `DGX_B200-4_GPUs-Verl-Post-Merge-1` Jenkins stage, layered directly on top of #14037.

#14037 bumps the verl pin to `d324b01` and replaces the three file-level verl wrappers with 19 per-case wrappers. The verl pin is unchanged in this PR.

Until this PR, the verl post-merge stage only ran rollout unit tests; no end-to-end training test exercised the trainer ↔ rollout boundary owned by TRT-LLM.

This PR adds:

- **`test_e2e_convergence_qwen25_05b_grpo_trtllm`**
  - Runs 30-step GRPO on Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct + GSM8K + TRT-LLM rollout.
  - Asserts:
    - `max(critic/rewards/mean) > 0.01` to verify a learning signal.
    - `max(actor/ppo_kl) < 0.1` to verify the trainer policy stays close to the rollout policy.
  - This catches weight-sync, dtype, and NaN-gradient regressions at the TRT-LLM rollout boundary.

- **`test_e2e_smoke_qwen25_7b_megatron_trtllm`**
  - Runs a 3-step Megatron actor + TRT-LLM rollout smoke test on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.

    - Megatron actor: TP=2, PP=1
    - TRT-LLM rollout: TP=2
    - Script: `examples/grpo_trainer/run_qwen3_8b_megatron.sh`
  - Pass condition: subprocess exits with code `0`.
  - Exercises the most feature-loaded combination currently shipped by verl: Megatron + TP/PP + TRT-LLM.

This PR is **stacked on #14037**.

GitHub will show both commits in the diff until #14037 merges. After #14037 is merged, the diff will automatically recompute to only the eight files added or modified in this PR.

body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- Adds lazy registries for model chat hooks and reasoning-parser structured-output hooks.
- Moves Kimi K3 and `gpt_oss` behavior into registered extensions.
