title: [None][fix] Cosmos3: bump cosmos_guardrail to 0.3.1 and fetch only the guardrail files it loads
body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- Updates Cosmos3 guardrail installation to `cosmos_guardrail==0.3.1` and uses `opencv-python-headless`.
- Restricts checkpoint downloads to `blocklist/*` and `face_blur_filter/*` at revision `cf03c03`.
- Materializes `blocklist/nltk_data` symlinks as regular files.
- Preserves the original `GatedRepoError` as the cause of the user-facing `ValueError`.
- Review severity counts are unavailable from the supplied findings.

## QA Engineer Review

- Adds CPU-only tests for cache handling, masked downloads, offline misses, gated-repository errors, NLTK materialization, idempotency, and preservation of unrelated cache entries.
- Registers the tests in `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_cpu.yml`.
- Coverage is sufficient for the changed paths. The supplied context reports 329 unit tests passing.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `examples/visual_gen/models/cosmos3/README.md`: Verify the updated guardrail and headless OpenCV installation instructions.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/visual_gen/models/cosmos3/guardrails.py`: Verify download filtering, revision pinning, error conversion, and NLTK symlink materialization.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/visual_gen/models/cosmos3/pipeline_cosmos3.py`: Verify the missing-dependency message matches the updated installation requirements.
- `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_cpu.yml`: Confirms the Cosmos3 guardrail tests are included in CPU CI.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_cosmos3_guardrails.py`: Covers cache behavior, download filtering, error handling, and NLTK data handling. The test is listed in `test-db/l0_cpu.yml`.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Four changes to how Cosmos3 obtains its guardrail (verified on GPU nodes), plus CPU-only unit tests for the two new code paths.

### Bump `cosmos_guardrail` `0.3.0` → `0.3.1`

The version users are told to install (README + the `ImportError` hint in `pipeline_cosmos3.py`) moves to the `0.3.1` hotfix. Diffed the two wheels: bugfix-only, no API change, `Requires-Dist` identical — nothing in the TRT-LLM dependency set shifts. Everything the pipeline touches (`CosmosSafetyChecker`, `check_text_safety`, `check_video_safety`, `.text_guardrail`, `.video_guardrail`) is byte-identical. Fixes in 0.3.1: `allow_patterns` for `blocklist` / `video_content_safety_filter` were missing a trailing `/*` and matched nothing; blobs dir whitelisted in `nltk.data.path` for nltk ≥ 3.10; one spurious warning removed.

### Make the documented guardrail install actually importable

`cosmos_guardrail` imports `cv2` at module load and depends on the full `opencv-python` build. The README (and the matching `ImportError` hint in `pipeline_cosmos3.py`) told users to uninstall that build — correct, it is not allowed in TensorRT-LLM environments — but put nothing back, so `import cosmos_guardrail` failed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'cv2'` and the pipeline refused to start. TensorRT-LLM itself carries no opencv by design; the example is the right place to install one. The instruction now adds `opencv-python-headless` after the uninstall, in that order so the headless build owns a complete `cv2/` directory.

Four changes to how Cosmos3 obtains its guardrail (verified on GPU nodes), plus CPU-only unit tests for the two new code paths.

### Fetch only the guardrail files that are actually loaded

`download_guardrail_checkpoint()` called `snapshot_download()` with no `allow_patterns`, pulling the whole `nvidia/Cosmos-1.0-Guardrail` repo — **17 GB** measured in the HF cache — of which `CosmosSafetyChecker` instantiates **135 MB**:

| subtree | size | loaded in 0.3.x |
|---|---|---|
| `aegis/` (LlamaGuard-7b + Aegis adapter) | 13 GB | no — no reference left in the package; Qwen3Guard replaced it |
| `video_content_safety_filter/` (SigLIP-so400m) | 3.3 GB | no — `VideoContentSafetyFilter` is commented out upstream |
| `face_blur_filter/Resnet50_Final.pth` | 110 MB | yes — `RetinaFaceFilter` |
| `blocklist/` | 26 MB | yes — `Blocklist` |

The fetch is now masked to `["blocklist/*", "face_blur_filter/*"]`. The mask is deliberately coupled to what the package loads (commented in `guardrails.py`): the library's own `snapshot_download` passes no revision, so anything our pinned pre-fetch misses would come off unpinned `main` rather than `GUARDRAIL_REVISION`. Widen it if a future `cosmos_guardrail` loads more.

Not changed: the checkpoint revision pin (`cf03c03`) is already the tip of that repo's `main`.

### Make the blocklist readable on nltk ≥ 3.10.3

The HF cache exposes every file in a snapshot as a symlink into `blobs/`, and `cosmos_guardrail`'s `Blocklist` points `nltk.data.path` at `<snapshot>/blocklist/nltk_data`. nltk 3.10.3 (2026-08-12) added `pathsec`, which opens data files with `O_NOFOLLOW` and raises `PermissionError` on a symlinked final component — with no opt-out (its docstring assumes "corpora/data files are never symlinks"). 0.3.1's own nltk fix whitelists `blobs/` in `nltk.data.path`, which satisfies the path-validation layer but not the open-time check. So on a **freshly populated cache**, `check_text_safety()` raises; caches populated by older huggingface_hub hold regular files and keep working, which is why existing installs don't see it.

`download_guardrail_checkpoint()` now copies each blob over its symlink under `blocklist/nltk_data` (temp file in the same directory + `os.replace`, so a crash leaves the symlink intact). That is the layout huggingface_hub produces with `HF_HUB_DISABLE_SYMLINKS=1`, limited to the ~25 MB nltk reads. The library's later `snapshot_download` leaves the copies alone — `_hf_hub_download_to_cache_dir` returns early on `os.path.exists(pointer_path)` without checking link-ness. Runs on both the cache-hit and download branches.

## Test Coverage

On 1×B200 with a native build of this branch, against an **empty** `HF_HOME` (the byte count is only meaningful on a cold cache):

```
mask     : ['blocklist/*', 'face_blur_filter/*']
--- after the masked download ---       TOTAL 135.3 MB
--- after CosmosSafetyChecker() ---     TOTAL 135.3 MB
library pulled an extra 0.0 MB from this repo
loaded models: ['Blocklist', 'Qwen3Guard', 'RetinaFaceFilter']
check_text_safety(benign) -> True
check_video_safety(blank) -> (4, 64, 64, 3)
```

The zero-growth line is the load-bearing one: constructing the checker after the masked download fetches nothing further, so the mask is complete, not merely smaller.

Unit tests — `test_cosmos3_pipeline.py`, `test_cosmos3_edge.py`, `test_cosmos3_distilled.py`, `test_cosmos3_transformer.py`, `test_offloading.py`: **329 passed, 0 failed** (54 deselected as integration). Note these cover the wiring only — `conftest.py::disable_cosmos3_guardrails` turns guardrails off suite-wide and the guardrail-path tests use fakes — which is why the real 0.3.1 package was exercised by hand above.

**nltk materialization** — 1×A10, nltk 3.10.3, `HF_HUB_DISABLE_SYMLINKS` unset, empty `HF_HOME`, both the download and cache-hit branches:

```
Materialized 75 nltk_data symlinks
nltk_data: 75 files, 0 symlinks, 0 leftover tmp, 0 hardlinked
face_blur_filter symlinks left untouched: 1
after CosmosSafetyChecker(): 75 files, 0 symlinks, 0 inodes changed
Blocklist.is_safe(benign)  -> True
Blocklist.is_safe(plurals) -> False 'Prompt blocked by censorship: … two **** carrying **** …'
[fresh] PASS   [prewarmed] PASS
```

The plurals line is the load-bearing one: "zombies"/"rifles" are not in the word lists, "zombie"/"rifle" are, so the block can only come from the `word_tokenize` + `WordNetLemmatizer` pass reading the materialized `nltk_data` — the exact path that raised before.

**Unit tests** — `tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_cosmos3_guardrails.py`, `cpu_only`, registered in `l0_cpu.yml`. No network, no checkpoint: `snapshot_download` is replaced by a recorder and the symlink handling runs against a synthetic HF-cache-shaped tree under `tmp_path`. Covers: both `snapshot_download` calls carry `repo_id`/`revision`/`allow_patterns` (dropping the mask on either path restores the 17 GB fetch); cache hit = exactly one `local_files_only` call; `GatedRepoError` → `ValueError`; materialization handles relative and absolute symlinks, produces regular files with `st_nlink == 1`, leaves `blocklist/custom/` and `face_blur_filter/` symlinks and the blobs untouched, leaves no temp files, is idempotent, skips symlinked directories, and is a no-op when `nltk_data` is absent. 10 tests.

## PR Checklist

Please review the following before submitting your PR:

## Dev Engineer Review

- Keeps the SM120 `lm_head` in `W4A16_NVFP4` and uses Marlin dense NVFP4.
- Preserves SM100/103 quantization behavior.

- Test-list changes use valid paths and remain scoped to the intended suites.
- No API or exported entity changes are reported.
- Reported benchmarks show improved ITL and throughput. TTFT remains unchanged.

## QA Engineer Review

- Verdict: sufficient.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

- Enable XQA decode multi-block for FP8 KV cache on SM120.
   - Fix XQA V-cache paging at `head_dim=256`. The page cursor advanced once per `xIter` instead of
    once per V tile which is incorrect for `headElems==256` and `cacheVTileSeqLen==32`.
   - Fix an output race in XQA multi-block mode. The merge was gated by `isLastCta` but the output
    write was not, so every CTA wrote `output[idxReq]` and the last writer won.
- Add `head_dim=256` to SM120 fmha_v2 kernels that cover `chunked_prefill=True` with FP8 KV cache.
- Keep lm_head at `W4A16_NVFP4` on SM120. Promotion to W4A4 is now conditional on
  SM100/103 and SM120 uses Marlin dense NVFP4 rather than falling back to bf16.

## Performance

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | 1x RTX PRO 6K Blackwell 600 W | 
| Dataset | sglang `bench_serving`, `random`, `--random-range-ratio 1.0`, ISL=8000, OSL=1000 |
| Requests | warmup = BS, timed = 5 × BS |
| Server | `max_num_tokens: 8192`, chunked prefill off, `max_seq_len: 9000`, CUTEDSL MoE, piecewise graphs |

title: [None][perf] DFlash draft latency for Qwen3.5-4B
body:
## Description

- Reduce DFlash draft latency primarily in draft attention kernel and host overhead.
- Tested with `RedHatAI/Qwen3.5-4B-FP8-dynamic` target and `z-lab/Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash` draft.
- One LLM-API change: Add `FA4` option to `DFlashDecodingConfig.attention_backend`.
- Validate piecewise graphs for `RedHatAI/Qwen3.5-4B-FP8-dynamic`.

### Changes

| change | Output tok/s  | Speedup | 
|---|---| ---| 
| Baseline w/o DFlash | 1211.4  | -  |
| Baseline with DFlash |  1345.4 |  11.1% |
| **Update draft K/V outside the flash-attn kernel** — scatter the block's K/V into the pooled cache with an indexed copy instead of letting `Append_KV` do it per draft layer. | 2176.8 | 62% |
| **Add FA4 draft attention backend**, selectable for SM90 alongside the existing TRTLLM backend which targets  SM100/103. | 2301.1 | 5.7% |
| **Promote all Mamba layers in one kernel** — stack per-layer V2 pool views so the accepted recurrent state is promoted by a single kernel instead of one per layer. | 2321.2 | 0.87% |
|  **Remove host syncs** from the pre-draft bookkeeping region — stage acceptance/context-length updates into pinned memory and scatter asynchronously to device buffers.  | 2418.9 | 4.2% |
|  Use `inplace_slice_copy` for captured hidden states so `torch.compile` functionalization stops cloning the full buffer per captured layer.  | no change eager | enables piecewise |

| Benchmark setup | |
|---|---|
| GPU | 1x H100 NVL |
| Target model | `RedHatAI/Qwen3.5-4B-FP8-dynamic` |
| Draft model | `z-lab/Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash` |
| Batch size | 10 |
| Dataset | Speed-bench throughput low-entropy, custom ISL/OSL distribution |
| ISL distribution | min 2178 / p25 3500 / p50 4096 / p75 4776 / max 11309 |
| OSL distribution | min 268 / p25 397 / p50 544 / p75 653 / max 771 |
| Draft length (K) | 4 |
| Acceptance length | verified 3.65 (out of 5) before and after each change |
| Harness | `sglang.bench_serving`, end-to-end, 100 bench prompts after 50 warmup prompts |

Existing `TestQwen3_6_35B_A3B::test_nvfp4_dflash` covers TRTLLM and Vanilla backends on B200.

title: [TRTLLM-16283][feat] Prepare DeepSeek V4 attention for sparse KV offload
body: ## Description DeepSeek V4 ratio-4 sparse attention currently assumes compressed KV is GPU-resident. This PR adds the attention-side integration for keeping completed compressed-KV history on the host and fetching each layer's selected history pages back to the GPU. It prepares the KVCM fetch inputs and consumes the returned GPU page table through the existing sparse MLA/FMHA path. The initial target is single-token ratio-4 decode with BF16 or per-tensor FP8 main KV. The feature is default-off, and enabling `enable_kv_cache_offload` still raises `NotImplementedError` until the KVCM runtime and end-to-end validation are complete. ## Workflow and PR scope The diagram shows the full intended workflow: **blue = this PR**, **gray = existing execution**, and **orange = pending KVCM runtime work**. | Stage in the diagram | Added by this PR (blue) | |---|---| | Declare ratio-4 compressed KV sparse | Add the opt-in configuration and separate sparse main `COMPRESS` buffers from resident indexer/SWA caches. | | Prepare each batch | Wait for prior cache work, upload mixed-tier page tables in request order with `copy_base_page_indices_to_device()`, record history counts, and build the resident GPU write table in persistent metadata. | | Decode: select and request history pages | After the indexer/compressor streams join, convert top-k token indices to unique history-page ordinals and call `fetch_sparse_pages()` for this layer's `COMPRESS` buffer. Repeat for each ratio-4 sparse layer. | | Decode: consume fetched KV | Merge fetched history with the resident tail into a separate read table, validate required pages and bounds, mask padded rows, and convert the original top-k tokens to GPU indices for sparse MLA/FMHA. | | After all model layers and sampling | Order cache work after model readers/writers, then use the existing `resize()` history update to make newly completed pages eligible for offload. The next batch waits for that cache work before refreshing its tables. | Fresh prefill uses the resident write table and existing attention path without a history fetch. The existing compressor, indexer, and sparse MLA/FMHA kernels remain the compute path shown in gray. The timing and data distinctions are: - History becomes eligible for offload **after the whole model step**; selected history is refetched **per sparse layer** during decode. - Page selection deduplicates transfers. KVCM sparse API declarations and runtime implementation are separate work. This PR also rejects unsupported batch layouts and history policies. ## Test Coverage - The complete rerun passed 149 tests on H100 in 72.76 seconds, with no failures or skips. It covers every newly added or modified test function, plus configuration regressions and the golden manifest check. - Coverage includes metadata preparation, page selection/merge, per-layer fetch/address consumption, history boundaries and stream ordering, required-page coverage, FP8 scheduler preparation, CUDA graph replay/padding, and rejection paths. - Earlier B200 validation passed 120 offload tests in 34.85 seconds. - Commit hooks, lint/formatting, Python compilation, and diff whitespace checks passed. title: [#19495][fix] Align LTX-2 scale factors with tensor axes
body:
## Description

Fixes #19495.

`SpatioTemporalScaleFactors` was declared in `(time, width, height)` order, while LTX-2 latent tensors and `get_pixel_coords` consume scale factors in `(time, height, width)` order. The symmetric default hid the mismatch.

This change aligns the tuple with tensor-axis order, uses named fields in `from_pixel_shape`, and adds an asymmetric regression covering latent conversion, round-trip upscaling, and patchifier coordinates. The default symmetric path is unchanged; there is no performance impact.

## Upstream Provenance

This is a focused backport of the same correction already present in [Lightricks/LTX-2@7df34df](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-2/commit/7df34dfa83e48a21ea2db4cf8df77bab7e7328e8). TensorRT-LLM currently pins the older LTX-2 commit `28c3c73`; a full vendor refresh would include many unrelated changes, so this PR carries only the upstream axis-order fix and its regression test.

## Test Coverage

- Exact current `main` reproduces latent dimensions `(5, 2, 8)` and a failed round trip for asymmetric factors.
- The changed production modules pass 4/4 direct assertions: asymmetric conversion, round trip, coordinate mapping, and symmetric control.
- `remove-crlf`, `codespell`, `ruff`, and `ruff-format` pre-commit hooks pass on both changed files.
- Full repository pytest was not run locally because the Windows environment does not contain the TensorRT-LLM native runtime DLLs.

## PR Checklist

- [x] I reviewed the description and test coverage above.
- [x] The change follows the TensorRT-LLM coding guidelines to the best of my knowledge.
- [x] A regression test covers the new asymmetric code path.
- [x] No dependencies, ownership, documentation, or architecture diagram changes are required.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

- Corrects `SpatioTemporalScaleFactors` to use `(time, height, width)` order.

- Updates `video_vae.py` initialization without changing scale-factor values.
- Symmetric defaults remain unchanged. No performance impact or unrelated scope change is indicated.

## QA Engineer Review

## Description

Pure relocation closing four tasks of Epic TRTLLM-14558 — T14 (TRTLLM-14844), T15 (TRTLLM-14845), T20 (TRTLLM-14850), T22 (TRTLLM-14852) — landed together because they split the same two source directories; 6 commits, **277 files changed, +945 / −609**. **No runtime behaviour, no numerics, no public API and no configuration change.**

### What moves where

| source root (tracked files at base) | destination |
|---|---|
| `tensorrt_llm/_torch/cute_dsl_kernels/` (137) | split by domain into `_torch/attention/kernels/`, `_torch/moe/kernels/`, `_torch/visual_gen/kernels/` and a new neutral `_torch/kernels/` |

The 277 files are 209 renames + 47 modifications + 13 creates + 8 deletes. 217 files leave the roots above: 209 git-detected renames plus 8 byte-empty `__init__.py` re-created at their new levels.

The 13 creates are 12 `__init__.py` markers plus one new module, `tests/microbenchmarks/cute_dsl_kernels/_offline_loader.py`; the 8 deletes are the byte-empty `__init__.py` they supersede. The `blackwell/` and `rubin/` architecture levels are preserved inside each destination, and two SM107 unit tests that landed upstream mid-flight (#18761, #18765) travel with the move.

### Commits

| # | ticket and purpose | scope | surface |
|---|---|---|---|

### Ownership

42 files change effective CODEOWNERS owner, all in commit 3, and no file loses an owner: kernels-devs→torch-attention-devs 17, →moe-devs 12, →torch-visual-gen-devs 8, runtime-devs→kernels-devs 3, moe-devs→torch-attention-devs 1, trt-llm-devs→torch-visual-gen-devs 1. The top-k slice is empty, its exact-file rules being repointed rather than deleted.

GitHub reads CODEOWNERS from the base branch, so reviewers must be requested by hand: `@NVIDIA/trt-llm-kernels-devs`, `@NVIDIA/trt-llm-torch-attention-devs`, `@NVIDIA/trt-llm-moe-devs`, `@NVIDIA/trt-llm-torch-visual-gen-devs`, `@NVIDIA/trt-llm-topk-devs`, `@NVIDIA/trt-llm-runtime-devs`, the KV-Cache, Models and CBTS owners, `@NVIDIA/trt-llm-infra-devs` and `@NVIDIA/trt-llm-oss-compliance`.

### Verification

Re-verified at this head after the rebase: absolute-import resolution replayed commit by commit (1620 baseline modules, 0 new unresolved against `main`), the seven vacated source roots at 0 tracked files, 209 git-detected renames, the CODEOWNERS owner diff (42 changes, 0 files newly unowned), test-list path existence for `waives.txt` and the l0 test-db (0 new dangling against `main`), a residue scan for every old path token, and `pre-commit` (all hooks pass, including `Validate test list entries exist in source files`). title: [https://nvbugs/5385167][fix] Potential fix for response queue size
body:
[MLPerf] Potential fix for response queue clear

## Description

Response queue was not being cleared after completion of response. This PR is a possible fix for it. Needs more understanding on what changed around `is_llm_response` or whether this is logically correct. 

When post-processing workers are enabled, the result is of type 'Output' and when we do not have post-processing workers, the result type is `llm_request.LlmResponse`. The PR fixes it so an assertion fails when the type constraints are not satisfied. 

The effect of this bug is that when running with post-processing workers, the result queue doesn't get cleared leading to spikes in execution, likely due to resizing of the queue. A symptom of this was error messages at server shutdown indicating that requests couldn't be cancelled. 


## Without fix:
Terminating the server after running 640 requests produces the following output on main. The requests are still maintained in the data structure causing the destructor to go over them and attempt to abort them.

```
[09/02/2025-02:36:34] [TRT-LLM] [W] Request of client_id 639 is finished, cannot abort it.
[09/02/2025-02:36:34] [TRT-LLM] [W] Request of client_id 640 is finished, cannot abort it.
[09/02/2025-02:36:34] [TRT-LLM] [W] Request of client_id 641 is finished, cannot abort it.
[09/02/2025-02:36:34] [TRT-LLM] [W] Request of client_id 642 is finished, cannot abort it.
[09/02/2025-02:36:34] [TRT-LLM] [I] Thread proxy_dispatch_result_thread stopped.
[09/02/2025-02:36:34] [TRT-LLM] [I] Thread proxy_dispatch_kv_cache_events_thread stopped.
[09/02/2025-02:36:34] [TRT-LLM] [I] Thread proxy_dispatch_stats_thread stopped.
[09/02/2025-02:36:34] [TRT-LLM] [I] Thread await_response_thread stopped.
[09/02/2025-02:36:34] [TRT-LLM] [I] Thread dispatch_stats_thread stopped.
[09/02/2025-02:36:34] [TRT-LLM] [I] Thread dispatch_kv_cache_events_thread stopped.
INFO:     Application shutdown complete.
INFO:     Finished server process [19628]
```

## With fix:

title: [None][feat] Load static FP8 Cosmos3 Nano/Super checkpoints without re-quantizing them
body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- Added static ModelOpt FP8 loading for single-GPU Cosmos3 Nano and Super checkpoints.
- Preserved separate Q/K/V and gate/up projections for static FP8 checkpoint fidelity.
- Added shared QKV input quantization and split GatedMLP support.
- Added `silu_and_mul_2in` and `swiglu_2in` with FP8 output support and B200 tuning.
- Preserved fused topology for BF16, dynamic FP8, and other models.
- Added BF16 activation execution for the denoising steps the checkpoint's `diffusion_step_policy` nominates.
- Added destination-dtype validation for static scale loading.
- Rejected unsupported multi-GPU static FP8 configurations and unsupported split GatedMLP options.
- Added documentation and checkpoint-fidelity coverage for Cosmos3 Nano/Super FP8.
- CI failed without individual test results. Re-trigger CI before final approval.

## QA Engineer Review

### Test changes

Added tests for:

- `test_swiglu_2in.py`: two-input SwiGLU behavior, quantization, compilation, CUDA graphs, validation, and B200 tuning.
- `test_gated_mlp_split.py`: split and fused topology, checkpoint loading, quantization, compilation, CUDA graphs, scale validation, BF16, and unsupported configurations.
- `test_attention_qkv_share.py`: shared quantization, validation, numerical equivalence, bypass paths, and rank handling.
- `test_cosmos3_fp8.py`: static and dynamic FP8 resolution, module layouts, topology selection, scale validation, and exact checkpoint loading.
- `test_quant_static_guard.py`: high-precision destination handling and incompatible FP8 destination rejection.
- `test_cosmos3_step_precision.py` and `test_cosmos3_step_precision_component.py`: step-window selection, precision dispatch, activation quantization behavior, reset and validation, and FP8 component accuracy.
- `test_visual_gen_cosmos3.py`: static FP8 T2I generation, topology validation, and LPIPS regression.

### Test-list coverage

`tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_b200.yml` includes entries for the SwiGLU, split GatedMLP, shared-QKV, Cosmos3 FP8, step-precision component, and Cosmos3 Nano FP8 LPIPS tests.

`tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_cpu.yml` includes `test_cosmos3_step_precision.py`.

The static quantization guard test has no reported test-list entry.

**Verdict: needs follow-up** because CI provides no individual test results and complete coverage cannot be confirmed until CI is re-triggered.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

The pre-quantized (ModelOpt-calibrated) Cosmos3 Nano and Super FP8 checkpoints
already loaded, but they did not load *faithfully*.

Static FP8 calibrates one scale per projection. The Cosmos3 topology fused the
generation tower's Q/K/V into one `Linear` and both towers' gate/up into
another. A per-tensor FP8 `Linear` holds exactly one weight scale, so the loader
kept `max(scales)` and re-quantized the other members of each group onto it:

> `qWi' = FP8-round((si * qWi) / max(s))` instead of keeping `si * qWi`

That is a second rounding on top of ModelOpt's. It affected **141 of 252 fused
shards in Nano and 252 of 448 in Super (~56% in both)**, and on affected shards
the added error was **7-18x the numerical floor** measured without the extra
conversion. The checkpoints were fine; the fusion was discarding their
calibration.

This PR keeps those projections separate under static FP8, so every tensor and
scale loads exactly as calibrated. One predicate,
`transformer_cosmos3.uses_static_fp8()`, gates all of it. **BF16 Cosmos3,
dynamically quantized Cosmos3, and every other model keep the fused topology
unchanged.**

vLLM-Omni's Cosmos3 implementation also keeps these projections separate; the
single-scale fusion was specific to this topology.

### It is also faster

Unfusing was expected to cost a little. It does not — the split topology is
**2.13% faster** end to end (Nano, default T2V, one B200: 104.62 s vs 106.90 s,
variants interleaved at the load level, 4 measured runs each after a discarded
warmup, ranges non-overlapping).

The win is not in the GEMMs (CUPTI puts split QKV at 1.03x fused and gate/up at
1.00x). Fusing QKV hands downstream code `qkv.split()` **views** that keep the
fused row stride, so per-head QK RMSNorm, RoPE and the und/gen K/V concatenation
all read strided. Split projections are contiguous `Linear` outputs. A
kernel-level profile diff attributes the delta to exactly those ops.

### What changed

**Shared infrastructure** (opt-in, inert for every existing caller):

* `swiglu.py` / `torch_custom_ops.py` — a new two-input SwiGLU,
  `trtllm::silu_and_mul_2in`, computing `SiLU(G) * U` from two separate tensors
  and quantizing the result directly for the FP8 `down_proj`. Bit-exact against
  the shipped fused kernel on every tested BF16/FP16 shape, with `swiglu_limit`,
  with `swiglu_alpha`/`swiglu_beta`, and when emitting FP8. It is **0.79x** the
  shipped fused activation on the FP8 path Cosmos3 takes (1,047 -> 824 us Nano,
  2,211 -> 1,725 us Super), DRAM utilization 68% -> 86-87% (B200). Full
  `custom_op` contract: `register_fake`, `opcheck`,
  `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)`, CUDA-graph capture.

  Its launch parameters live in a table beside the op, keyed on SM version and
  read through `get_sm_version()` — the convention for per-architecture tuning
  of custom ops. The `sm_100` row is from a B200 sweep; an `sm_103` sweep landed
  within 0.4% of the same configuration, so it shares that row rather than
  carrying a copy. Untuned SM versions take the same row as a fallback: they are
  not rejected and no performance claim is made for them. A test pins every row
  (and the fallback) as a launchable configuration, and another pins the
  `sm_103`/`sm_100` equality so the documented measurement cannot silently
  diverge.

  `torch.cat([gate, up])` was rejected — it adds a full intermediate-sized GPU
  copy — as was writing both GEMMs into column slices of one `[M, 2I]` buffer,
  which is *silently* mis-written because `cublas_gemm_caller` hardcodes
  `ldc = n` (`cublasScaledMM.cpp`) while `cublas_scaled_mm_out` still validates
  the output stride.

* `gated_mlp.py` — opt-in `GatedMLP(split_gate_up=...)`. Quantizes the shared
  activation **once** and hands both projections the FP8 tensor
  (`FP8QDQLinearMethod.apply` passes a pre-quantized input straight through).
  Rejects LoRA and `force_dynamic_quantization` explicitly rather than by
  accident.

* `visual_gen/modules/attention.py` — opt-in
  `Attention(share_qkv_input_quant=...)`, the FP8 analog of the existing NVFP4
  dedup, with the same single-quantization property for Q/K/V.

Both carry a `post_load_weights()` validating the invariant the sharing rests
on — that the group's projections carry the *same* calibrated `input_scale`.
Checked at load, never in `forward()`: reading a scale tensor on the hot path
would sync the device and break fullgraph compilation. The invariant was
verified exhaustively across the shipped checkpoints — 108 groups in Nano, 192
in Super, **zero** with differing input scales — but a checkpoint that violated
it would otherwise produce silently wrong output.

**Cosmos3 wiring** (`transformer_cosmos3.py`): `uses_static_fp8()` drives all
four sites — GEN cross-attention (`SEPARATE_QKV` + shared quant), UND causal
attention (shared quant; already separate), and both towers' gate/up.
`post_load_weights()` gained a second pass over `GatedMLP`/`Attention`, because
`named_modules()` yields parents before children and the invariants must be
checked after the projections finalize.

Since Cosmos3-Edge (#16773) landed, both decoder layers build their MLP through
`_build_cosmos3_mlp()`, so `split_gate_up=uses_static_fp8(model_config)` is
passed there rather than at the two call sites. That is load-bearing: dropping
it leaves static FP8 on the fused topology, which still loads and still renders
plausible output while re-quantizing 56% of shards — the exact defect this
change removes. `test_topology_follows_quantization` and
`test_static_fp8_checkpoint_realizes_expected_module_layout`, which pins the
exact per-tower Linear counts, both fail if it regresses.

Edge's Nemotron-dense recipe (`recipe.gated_mlp` false) builds `MLP` instead,
which has no gate/up pair to split and is unaffected. A statically quantized
Edge checkpoint would need its own handling; none exists today.

**The loader needed no change.** `DynamicLinearWeightLoader` dispatches on each
module's own `weight_mode`, and the existing key remap already emits
per-projection checkpoint names, so a split (`VANILLA`) module matches its
checkpoint tensor directly while `params_map` continues to serve the fused BF16
path untouched.

### Supported surface, and what is refused

Nano and Super; T2V, T2I, I2V and V2V; **one GPU**; static per-tensor
`QuantAlgo.FP8` checkpoints only.

Static FP8 **raises `NotImplementedError`** for `tp_size`, `ulysses_size`,
`cfg_size`, `cp_size` or `parallel_vae_size` above 1, rather than running
untested. The guard is deliberate: putting cross-attention on `SEPARATE_QKV`
changes how the parallel wrappers treat it — with Attention2D engaged, Ulysses
is disabled rather than failing, announced only by a `logger.debug` — and a
quiet fallback is worse than a refusal. Existing distributed Cosmos3 tests use
synthetic BF16 weights and do not validate FP8 sharding, per-rank scales, or the
NVLink/NCCL collective paths.

Also out of scope, and documented as such in the example README:

* **Audio (T2AV/TI2AV) runs, and is not refused.** Both checkpoints ship the
  audio tower (`sound_gen: true`), so audio is quantized and generated like any
  other task; the single-GPU guard covers only the parallel axes. It is simply
  less exercised than the four video/image tasks and carries no quality claim.
* **No quality measurement of our own.** There is no accuracy or
  generative-quality benchmark for these checkpoints here. This PR claims
  functional support and checkpoint fidelity — *not* that FP8 and BF16 are
  visually equivalent. Step precision is enabled by default on the strength of
  the recipe authors' reports and two independent implementations, not on a
  measurement taken in this repository; the component tests establish that it
  reduces activation-quantization error at the component level, which is a
  narrower claim than image quality.
* **Official Hub IDs exist and are verified.** `nvidia/Cosmos3-Nano` and
  `nvidia/Cosmos3-Super` publish the FP8 checkpoints on their `fp8` branch,
  loadable directly via `VisualGenArgs(model=..., revision="fp8")`. Verified
  against both: the full checkpoint-fidelity suite passes (15/15 — bitwise
  weight/scale equality, split topology counts), the Super quantized-module
  set is identical to the build this PR was developed against, and both carry
  the `diffusion_step_policy` — a full Nano pipeline load engages it end to end
  (252 generation linears step-gated, 252 reasoner linears pinned to 16-bit,
  towers diverging mid-schedule exactly as the policy states).

One interaction is documented but left unguarded: `SEPARATE_QKV`
cross-attention also falls back from CUTEDSL VSA to VANILLA, which would drop
sparse attention under FP8 with no diagnostic. No shipped Cosmos3 config enables
VSA, so the combination is unreachable today.

## Test Coverage

New, 78 unit tests:

* `tests/unittest/_torch/modules/test_swiglu_2in.py` (32) — `torch.library.opcheck`,
  `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)`, CUDA-graph capture, rank-N inputs,
  non-contiguous rejection, and bit-exactness against the shipped kernel for
  BF16 / FP16 / `swiglu_limit` / `swiglu_alpha`+`swiglu_beta` / FP8 output.
* `tests/unittest/_torch/modules/test_gated_mlp_split.py` (19) — split topology,
  single-quantization by storage identity (`data_ptr`, not dtype — three
  independent quantizations would also yield FP8 everywhere), scale-mismatch
  rejection, LoRA and dynamic-quantization refusals.
* `tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_attention_qkv_share.py` (12) — the same
  for Q/K/V, including the cross-attention case where k/v come from a different
  tensor and sharing must *not* engage.
* `tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_cosmos3_fp8.py` (15) — checkpoint-gated.
  `test_previously_fused_groups_now_load_exactly` compares FP8 weights bitwise
  against the raw checkpoint tensors, and first asserts the group's weight
  scales genuinely differ — otherwise fusion would have been lossless and
  exactness would hold trivially under either topology, leaving the test unable
  to discriminate. `test_topology_follows_quantization` and
  `test_dynamic_quantization_stays_fused` pin all four directions so the BF16
  and dynamic paths cannot drift silently.

Regression: the existing `test_fused_activation_quant.py` and
`test_cosmos3_transformer.py` suites stay green.

**Step precision** (new, see below):

* `tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_cosmos3_step_precision.py` (24, CPU) —
  the step policy (which steps are selected, that selection is a pure function
  of the step index so CFG branches cannot disagree, the one-step warmup
  carve-out), dispatch between the two paths, the dequantization arithmetic,
  and the refusal to accept an already-quantized activation.
* `tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_cosmos3_step_precision_component.py`
  (7, GPU) — a real quantized `GatedMLP` driven through
  the checkpoint's declared policy, comparing feature-on against feature-off **in the same
  job**: that the shared-activation optimization stands down on edge steps and
  stays engaged on middle ones, that the two paths produce different output at
  all, and that the 16-bit step lands **closer to the unquantized reference**
  than the quantized step. No stored artifact — the comparisons are exact
  arithmetic or an A/B against the module's other path.

**No LPIPS golden.** An earlier revision of this PR added one; it has been
removed. It rendered T2I at 4 steps, which the step-precision default puts
entirely on the 16-bit path, so the committed image no longer matched the path
under test. Re-cutting was not worth it: it was a per-checkpoint reference cut
on B300 (sm_103) but scheduled only on B200 (sm_100), and a stored *quantized*
golden does not survive that boundary — kernel selection, split-k and reduction
order and autotuner choices all change with the architecture. The checkpoints
are not staged in CI, so it skipped there in any case. What it protected is
covered by the bitwise weight/scale comparison and the topology-count assertions
in `test_cosmos3_fp8.py`, which are deterministic and architecture-independent.

CI (`l0_b200.yml`, `l0_cpu.yml`): the checkpoint-free suites run **pre-merge**
beside the other `visual_gen` unit suites. The FP8 checkpoints are not staged in
the CI `llm-models/` tree, so `test_cosmos3_fp8.py` **skips** there — a skip
reports green, so it should not be read as evidence that the FP8 path is
exercised in CI today. It is exercised locally: 15/15 against both the Nano and
Super checkpoints, including the published `Cosmos3-Super-Text2Image` FP8 build.

## Denoising-step activation precision

A ModelOpt checkpoint carries one activation scale per projection, calibrated as
a max over the whole sampling trajectory. That single scale fits the first and
last denoising steps worst, and the recipe's authors attribute frame-to-frame
flicker in video output to it. Those steps now run the resident FP8 weights
through a 16-bit GEMM instead — the weight is dequantized with its own
`weight_scale` and `input_scale` goes unused — while the middle steps keep the
checkpoint's fully quantized path.

No extra weights are read: same weights, same scales, no second checkpoint and
no persistent dequantized copy.

**The recipe comes from the checkpoint.** The producer publishes it under
`quantization_config.runtime.diffusion_step_policy` — which steps take the
16-bit path, and what the understanding tower does — and ships it only with the
builds whose calibration needs it. Of the six published FP8 builds, `nano`,
`super` and `super-i2v` carry a policy; the image build and both distilled
4-step builds deliberately do not, because the flicker this targets is not
observed there. A checkpoint without a policy therefore runs fully quantized,
and this PR exposes no configuration of its own: there is nothing left for a
knob to decide, and enabling the feature for a checkpoint that did not ask for
it would be wrong for half the fleet. It also means distilled schedules need no
special-casing.

Policy shapes we do not implement are refused rather than partially honoured:
unknown or missing fields, `schema_version` other than 1, and any other `type`,
`index_space`, `default_mode` or `overlap` value. Silently ignoring a field the
producer set is indistinguishable from the feature not working. `overlap` is
validated and not acted on — it selects which mode wins where the two windows
meet, which the predicate already yields; vLLM-Omni treats it the same way.

vLLM-Omni (vllm-project/vllm-omni#6560) and SGLang (sgl-project/sglang#36380)
landed the same mitigation independently, with the same one-step warmup
carve-out. This matches their semantics.

The reasoner is not step-gated. The policy states its precision outright,
because the understanding tower runs once per request — on whichever
transformer call builds its KV cache — so deriving it from a step index matches
the published 3-and-3 policy only because step 0 falls inside the first window,
and would stop matching for a policy with `first_steps: 0`. vLLM-Omni resolves
it the same way.

Unlike either implementation, this topology quantizes shared activations
**above** the `Linear`: gate/up and q/k/v each quantize once and hand the same
tensor to their projections, and `swiglu_2in` emits FP8 straight into
`down_proj`. All three must stand down while a 16-bit step is selected, or the
step still runs on FP8 activations and the feature is silently absent. A
quantization method advertises that by publishing `high_precision`; the sharing
sites consult it, and `apply_fp8_w8a16_linear` raises rather than accept an
already-quantized activation.

Coverage note: the component tests install the wrapper themselves, so they
cannot see the transformer reading the wrong config key or handing the
unconditional path to the wrong tower. Transformer-level wiring tests cover
both, and both mutations were confirmed to fail them.

## A loader fix this path depends on

#17699 added a guard refusing static-quant recipes against unquantized
checkpoints. It resolves the algorithm by module *name*, falling back to the
global recipe for any module without its own `quant_config` — which includes
modules that cannot be quantized at all. `Embedding` reaches the quantized
linear loader because it subclasses `LMHead` -> `Linear`, yet its `__init__`
never exposes `quant_config`, so it always keeps a high-precision buffer, and
ModelOpt does not list it in `ignore` because only `Linear` targets were ever
candidates. Every static-FP8 VisualGen checkpoint therefore failed to load on
`language_model.embed_tokens`.

The guard now consults the destination buffer, which is the condition its own
docstring describes. A module built for FP8 holds a float8 buffer and still
raises; where the destination is unknown the check proceeds, keeping the
fail-closed behaviour. Both directions are pinned in
`test_quant_static_guard.py`. Static FP8 is the only pre-quantized recipe in the
tree, so this was latent until this PR.

## PR Checklist

Please review the following before submitting your PR:
- PR description clearly explains what and why. If using CodeRabbit's summary, please make sure it makes sense.
- PR Follows [TRT-LLM CODING GUIDELINES](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of your knowledge.
- Test cases are provided for new code paths (see [test instructions](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/tree/main/tests#1-how-does-the-ci-work))
- If PR introduces API changes, an appropriate PR label is added - either `api-compatible` or `api-breaking`. For `api-breaking`, include `BREAKING` in the PR title.
- Any new dependencies have been scanned for license and vulnerabilities
- [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) updated if ownership changes
- Documentation updated as needed
- Update [tava architecture diagram](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/tava_architecture_diagram.md) if there is a significant design change in PR.
- The reviewers assigned automatically/manually are appropriate for the PR.

title: [#17714][feat] NcclEP: make algorithm/layout selectable so HIGH_THROUGHPUT+FLAT works on EFA
body:
## Description

Closes #17714.

The `NcclEP` MoE backend hardcodes `Algorithm.LOW_LATENCY` (`nccl_ep_utils.py`) and forces `Layout.RANK_MAJOR` at three layers (the `NcclEpContext` ctor default, `get_nccl_ep_context`, and `communication/nccl_ep.py::_get_context`). On AWS EFA the safe algorithm/layout tuple is fabric-dependent: the device-initiated `LOW_LATENCY` path takes a CUDA illegal memory access at first dispatch, while `HIGH_THROUGHPUT`+`FLAT` runs correctly (details and the both-ways substrate caveat in #17714).

This PR adds `TRTLLM_NCCL_EP_ALGO` (`LOW_LATENCY` | `HIGH_THROUGHPUT`, default `LOW_LATENCY` — behavior unchanged for existing users) and plumbs it through all three layout decision points; under HT the layout defaults to `FLAT` (the HT kernel asserts on `RANK_MAJOR`).

The HT/FLAT path also carries three buffer-contract differences the LL default never exercises, all gated on the same probe:

- 2D `[max_recv, hidden]` recv buffers (the HT kernel asserts `ndim==2`; LL keeps its 3D rank-major shape)
- int64 `recv_topk_idx` per the shipped v0.1 `nccl_ep.h` HT ABI, narrowed back to int32 at the dispatch return boundary because `torch.ops.trtllm.fused_moe` requires int32 routing ids (expert ids and the `-1` unrouted sentinel both fit; under LL the cast is a no-op)
- dispatch `layout_info=None` under HT (per `nccl_ep.h`: counters arrive via `ncclEpUpdateHandle`; `src_rank_counters` is an LL-rank-major-only field)

**Framing (honest):** this is an opt-in **correctness/enablement** change, not a performance win — at our measured shape native `nccl_ep` HT is ~3.7× slower than a CPU-proxy reference. The point is that users on fabrics where the hardcoded tuple faults currently have no way to select the tuple that works.

**Measured** on 2× p5en (16× H200) over AWS EFA, NCCL 2.30.4 + `nccl_ep` 0.1.0: 16/16 ranks × 3 rounds dispatch+combine correctness-checked PASS, plus a real `trtllm-serve` (Qwen3-30B-A3B, EP8) producing coherent, arithmetically-correct output. Default (`TRTLLM_NCCL_EP_ALGO` unset) leaves every code path byte-equivalent to today's behavior.

## Test Coverage

- Default-path inertness: with `TRTLLM_NCCL_EP_ALGO` unset, `NcclEpContext` resolves `LOW_LATENCY`+`RANK_MAJOR` exactly as before (existing NcclEP tests cover this path).
- HT/FLAT enablement was validated on live EFA hardware (16-rank correctness harness + real serve, above); the tuple is not exercisable in single-GPU CI. Happy to add a unit test asserting the env-gate → (algorithm, layout, buffer-shape, dtype) resolution logic without requiring multi-node fabric if reviewers want it.

## PR Checklist

- [x] PR description clearly explains what and why.
- [x] PR follows TRT-LLM coding guidelines to the best of my knowledge.
- [ ] ~~Test cases are provided for new code paths — resolved as deferred-on-request: default path covered by existing NcclEP tests, HT/FLAT tuple not exercisable in single-GPU CI; env-gate resolution unit test offered in Test Coverage, will add if reviewers want it.~~
- [x] No API change (env-var opt-in only; default behavior unchanged) — no `api-compatible`/`api-breaking` label needed.
- [x] No new dependencies.
- [x] No ownership/docs/architecture-diagram change.
- [x] Please check this after reviewing the above items as appropriate for this PR.

- Preserved `LOW_LATENCY` as the default.
- Selected `RANK_MAJOR` for `LOW_LATENCY` and `FLAT` for `HIGH_THROUGHPUT`.
- Cached the algorithm per context and included it in context cache keys.
- Rejected explicit non-`FLAT` layouts for `HIGH_THROUGHPUT`.
- Added high-throughput buffer handling, including 2D receive buffers.
- Narrowed routing indices to `int32` at the dispatch return boundary.

title: [None][feat] Add opt-in disaggregated transfer diagnostics
body:
## Why

Add opt-in, request-level evidence for admission/backpressure and KV-transfer ownership debugging following [#18150](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/18150). This PR observes existing behavior; it does not change admission, ownership, timeout policy, or transport messages.

## What changed

- Record admission/rollback, transfer-window decisions, KV pressure, readiness, queueing, submission/completion, settlement, timeout/cancellation, KV release, and decode readiness. Bypassed Gate 2 is observed only as a counterfactual.
- Consolidate request/rank metadata and timeout events in [shared helpers](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/d43a87d7078ee6ac93ff52e0734d5bcda0e0bf32/tensorrt_llm/_torch/disaggregation/diagnostics.py). Share one descriptor-local payload measurement with the existing [native performance logger](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/d43a87d7078ee6ac93ff52e0734d5bcda0e0bf32/tensorrt_llm/_torch/disaggregation/native/transfer.py); its enablement and timing semantics remain unchanged. RequestPerfMetrics continues owning aggregate request metrics.
- Use a bounded, asynchronous sink and an offline [analyzer](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/d43a87d7078ee6ac93ff52e0734d5bcda0e0bf32/scripts/disagg_transfer_diagnostics.py). Runtime/scheduler capabilities distinguish unsupported events from missing evidence; writer-cohort metadata handles attention-DP broadcasts.
- Correlate explicit disaggregated IDs across workers only within a shared run UUID. Fallback IDs remain process-local, and sessionless wire observations report unknown identity scope. Durations never cross process/clock domains.

## Usage and overhead

Diagnostics are **disabled by default**. Enable with `TRTLLM_DISAGG_TRANSFER_DIAGNOSTICS=1`. For cross-worker correlation, set `TRTLLM_DISAGG_TRANSFER_DIAGNOSTICS_RUN_ID` to the same fresh UUID on all CTX/GEN workers.

Disabled mode avoids diagnostic clock reads, request scans, UUID generation, serialization, queueing, and I/O; cheap flag checks and minimal bookkeeping remain. No measured zero-overhead claim is made. Enabled diagnostics are for targeted debugging, not authoritative throughput measurement, and do not enable the existing aggregate performance collectors.

The sink is bounded and best-effort. Queue/write losses are reported when possible; blocked/broken stdout or process exit can lose the final tail, and partial writes can produce malformed records. The analyzer reports incomplete/unknown evidence rather than inventing correlations.

## Validation

- Rebased onto main `1a36f4fed9`; current head: [`d43a87d707`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/commit/d43a87d7078ee6ac93ff52e0734d5bcda0e0bf32). Integration hooks/tests follow the current coordinator and native Chunk/CacheExtent/PeerFetch APIs.
- Added coordinator, lifecycle, payload-reuse, fallback-ID, and cleanup regression coverage, including disabled/enabled/failing diagnostics and independent performance-logger flags. A fresh end-to-end self-review found no remaining actionable issues.
- **106 analyzer tests passed.** **36 isolated sink/helper tests passed** using the actual diagnostic module without importing the unavailable application runtime; this is not a runtime-suite pass.
- Applicable pre-commit checks, Python compilation, test-list validation, pinned-memory policy, and whitespace checks passed. Runtime pytest collection is blocked locally by missing PyTorch; runtime/GPU integration and performance validation remain for CI.
- [Full CI requested](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/18913#issuecomment-5784837718) with `/bot run --disable-fail-fast`. [Jenkins launcher #75116](https://nv/trt-llm-cicd/job/helpers/job/PR_Github/75116/) has started for `d43a87d707`, with [full-CI pipeline #61869](https://nv/trt-llm-cicd/job/main/job/L0_MergeRequest_PR/61869/) dispatched; test results are pending. The PR currently lacks `ci: full pre-merge approved`, so gated multi-GPU coverage requires maintainer approval.

Earlier CI results validate older heads only.

title: [None][feat] Add opt-in per-request cached KV token logging
body:
## Description

Iteration logs expose only the sum of cached KV tokens, making it difficult to inspect individual cached-prefix lengths in a disaggregated GEN batch. Set `TLLM_LOG_CACHED_KV_TOKENS_PER_REQ=1` before starting workers to add `cached_kv_tokens_per_req` to the existing `states` log. The flag is read once during model-engine initialization and defaults to off.

The list follows model-input sequence order and excludes CUDA graph padding requests. Filtering follows the context, extend, first-draft, and generation groups used by input preparation, including beam expansion. This handles padding inside the packed MTP batch and preserves all real beam entries. The normal input, steady-generation, and encoder-decoder fast paths all update the diagnostic. Attention-DP dummy rows remain part of the scheduled-input accounting.

The existing `cached_kv_tokens` total retains its original semantics. The companion `cached_kv_tokens_cuda_graph_padding` field reports the excluded contribution, so:

```text
cached_kv_tokens = sum(cached_kv_tokens_per_req) + cached_kv_tokens_cuda_graph_padding
```

For example, `[100, 200]` with a padding contribution of `7` corresponds to a total of `307`. With beam width 1, each retained entry corresponds to one scheduled request; multiple beams produce per-sequence entries. These are cached-prefix token counts, not physical KV-cache occupancy.

Disabled mode does not traverse requests, copy counts, or format the extra fields. Enabled mode adds CPU filtering and logging without new CUDA synchronization.

## Test Coverage

- Added 8 regression tests in `TestCachedKvTokenLogging`: encoder-decoder padding, MTP padding before real rows, multiple beams, promoted context order, attention-DP dummy preservation, padding-only batches, and stale-value cleanup on steady/empty batches. The tests also check snapshot independence and total reconciliation.
- Locally executed those 8 tests against the actual helper in an isolated CPU source harness, plus 18 cases exercising the actual flag initialization and all three logging call sites with the environment unset/0/1. Full TensorRT-LLM test-module imports and GPU inference were not run locally.
- Python syntax compilation, `git diff --check`, repository pre-commit checks, and DCO validation.

title: [None][fix] Bound DSpark scratch positions across graph replays
body:
## Description

The embedded DSpark worker shares a reserved slot among CUDA graph padding and attention-DP idle requests. Its decode position currently accumulates across generation steps for the lifetime of the worker. Eventually, RoPE gathers can index past their fixed table even though the dummy rows are subsequently masked.

Reset the scratch slot's previous position to zero inside `_advance_generation_state()` using tensor operations, so the reset executes on every CUDA graph replay without host synchronization. Real-request position bootstrap and advancement retain their existing behavior. This adds one tensor comparison/selection to the generation path; full-serving performance has not been measured for this upstream adaptation.

## Test Coverage

Added `test_dspark_generation_state.py` under the existing `hw_agnostic` directory, already included by the CPU and H100 CI lists:

- CPU: initialized and uninitialized scratch positions at/beyond the RoPE boundary, duplicate scratch rows with different accepted-token counts, repeated advancement, real-request bootstrap, and recycled real-slot state.
- CUDA: capture/replay with changing real/scratch mappings and accepted-token counts for batches 16, 32, 48, 64, 96, and 128, followed by 1,000 all-padding replays.

Validation performed locally on macOS with PyTorch 2.8.0:
- Invoked the two CPU regression cases using the actual `_advance_generation_state` method extracted from upstream source via AST, isolating it from unavailable TensorRT-LLM runtime dependencies. Both fail with out-of-bounds indexing on unpatched main and pass with the fix.
- Ruff 0.9.4 lint and formatting checks pass for both changed files.
- `git diff --check` passes.

The full upstream pytest suite, pre-commit suite, and CUDA replay tests have not been run in this environment. GPU CI validation is pending.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Reviewed the applicable checklist items: focused internal fix, regression coverage provided, no public API or dependency changes, and no ownership or architecture changes.

## Summary

The `OpenAIDisaggServer` (disaggregated proxy) does not implement the `/v1/models` endpoint, causing incompatibility with standard OpenAI API clients such as the OpenAI Python SDK, LangChain, and other tools that rely on this endpoint for model discovery.

**Current behavior:**
```
curl http://localhost:8100/v1/models
# Returns: {"detail":"Not Found"}
```

**After this change:**
```
curl http://localhost:8100/v1/models
# Returns: {"object":"list","data":[{"id":"model-name","object":"model","created":...,"owned_by":"tensorrt_llm"}]}
```

- Import `ModelCard` and `ModelList` from `openai_protocol`
- Register `/v1/models` GET route in `register_routes()`
- Add `get_models()` handler that extracts the model name from the server configuration and returns an OpenAI API-compatible `ModelList` response

This mirrors the existing `/v1/models` implementation in `OpenAIServer`, adapted for the disaggregated proxy which reads the model path from `DisaggServerConfig.server_configs`.

- No new dependencies

Closes #12097

title: [None][feat] make KVCacheManagerV2 pool rebalancing parameters configurable
body:
## Summary
- Expose the previously hardcoded KVCacheManagerV2 pool-rebalancing tuning knobs as user-configurable fields on `KvCacheConfig`, gated behind the existing `enable_kv_pool_rebalance` flag:
  - `kv_pool_rebalance_min_sampled_kv_caches` (default 2000)
  - `kv_pool_rebalance_cooldown_secs` (default 120.0)
  - `kv_pool_rebalance_target_ratio_update_interval` (default 100)
  - `kv_pool_rebalance_ratio_threshold` (default 1.25)
  - `kv_pool_rebalance_moving_average_decay` (default 0.9999)
  - `kv_pool_rebalance_check_interval` (default 10)
- Threaded through both the C++ `KVCacheManagerConfig` (with nanobind bindings) and the mirrored pure-Python `KVCacheManagerConfig` used by the production PyTorch backend.
- Regenerated `tensorrt_llm/usage/llm_args_golden_manifest.json`.
- Addressed CodeRabbit review feedback:
  - `kv_pool_rebalance_cooldown_secs`/`kv_pool_rebalance_ratio_threshold` now reject non-finite (`inf`/`nan`) values at all three layers: the public Pydantic model (`allow_inf_nan=False`), the pure-Python `KVCacheManagerConfig.__post_init__`, and the native `KVCacheManagerConfig::validate()`.
  - `PyExecutor.__init__` now raises `ValueError` for `kv_pool_rebalance_check_interval <= 0` instead of allowing a later `ZeroDivisionError` in `_can_pause_for_rebalance()`.
  - Added `TestPoolRebalance` coverage for non-default `rebalance_min_sampled_kv_caches`, `rebalance_cooldown_secs`, and `rebalance_ratio_threshold`, asserting their gating behavior on both the sample-count, cooldown, and deviation decision points.
  - Added a pure-Python-backend-only regression test (`test_invalid_rebalance_settings_raise_on_python_backend`, skipped under the default C++ backend) covering all eight invalid `rebalance_*` combinations rejected by `KVCacheManagerConfig.__post_init__`.
- Follow-up fixes from self-review (anticipating reviewer feedback):
  - Moved the `kv_pool_rebalance_check_interval` validation in `PyExecutor.__init__` to the very first statement (before any CUDA/device access), and added a direct unit test (`TestKvPoolRebalanceCheckIntervalValidation` in `test_kv_pool_rebalance.py`) that calls `PyExecutor.__init__` unbound to confirm the `ValueError` actually fires — the existing rebalance tests all construct a `MagicMock(spec=PyExecutor)` and never exercise the real constructor, so this path had no coverage.
  - Fixed a stale `enable_kv_pool_rebalance` docstring that still described the sample-count/cooldown gates as fixed V2 internals ("2000-sample / 120s cooldown") rather than pointing at the new `kv_pool_rebalance_min_sampled_kv_caches`/`kv_pool_rebalance_cooldown_secs` fields this PR adds.
  - Known gap, left as-is: `rebalance_target_ratio_update_interval` and `rebalance_moving_average_decay` only have invalid-value-rejection coverage (via `test_invalid_rebalance_settings_raise_on_python_backend`), not a test asserting a custom value changes `tryUpdateTargetRatios()`'s cadence/decay. Exercising that end-to-end needs new introspection getters (for the target-ratio-update counter and the moving averages) that don't exist today; given the pure-Python backend is slated for deprecation, adding new test-only API surface there isn't worth it right now.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/unittest/kv_cache_manager_v2_tests/test_kv_cache_manager_v2.py::TestPoolRebalance` (pure-Python backend, `TLLM_KV_CACHE_MANAGER_V2_BACKEND=python`, fast mode): all 6 cases pass, including the 3 new non-default-config gating tests.
- [x] `pytest tests/unittest/kv_cache_manager_v2_tests/test_kv_cache_manager_v2.py` (pure-Python backend, fast mode): 146 tests, 109 passed. 24 pre-existing errors are unrelated to this change — they come from a stale compiled nanobind extension in the dev sandbox missing upstream's `reuse_match_backoff`/`CachedCudaEvent` symbols (confirmed via the `TypeError` messages), not from anything touched here. The C++-backend path (default) needs a full rebuild to verify in this sandbox; CI will do that.

Deferring to CI, which builds the package and will run this.
- [x] Manual sanity check: instantiated the pure-Python `KVCacheManagerConfig` with the new fields, confirmed defaults, and confirmed validation rejects `rebalance_ratio_threshold<=1`, negative `rebalance_min_sampled_kv_caches`/`rebalance_cooldown_secs`, non-positive `rebalance_target_ratio_update_interval`, `rebalance_moving_average_decay` outside `(0, 1)`, and non-finite `rebalance_cooldown_secs`/`rebalance_ratio_threshold`.

- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_py_executor_creator_flashinfer_spec_gate.py`: CPU-only tests cover FlashInfer admission and rejection rules. No test-list entry is reported.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/speculative/hw_agnostic/test_dflash_config_budget.py`: CPU-only tests cover budget validation, sizing, warnings, and configuration wiring. No test-list entry is reported.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/speculative/hw_agnostic/test_dflash_ctx_arena_sizing.py`: CPU-only tests cover KV-cache served-length handling and position-embedding caps. No test-list entry is reported.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

DFlash's pooled-context K/V buffers are allocated lazily during warmup, after the KV-cache pool has committed, so sizing mistakes fail late and opaquely: an oversized `max_batch_size` dies as a bare CUDA OOM, and a violated token budget (`max_batch_size * (1 + max_draft_len) > max_num_tokens`) corrupts memory at engine init. This PR has two commits:

**Commit 1 — config-time budget validation and sizing/position fixes:**
- `validate_dflash_ctx_buffer_budget` (called from `TorchLlmArgs.validate_speculative_config` for DFlash) turns both failure modes into config-time errors: it enforces the token-budget rule and estimates the pooled-context buffer footprint against the memory left after the KV pool commits. The budget subtracts an estimate of the per-rank weight footprint (checkpoint shard bytes across TP x PP ranks) before applying `(1 - free_gpu_memory_fraction)`; budgeting against the device total blesses batch sizes that then OOM in warmup. Refusals name the largest fitting `max_batch_size`.
- Buffer capacity is `min(max_seq_len, max_position_embeddings)` — the same clamp the lazy allocation applies. Sizing off `max_position_embeddings` alone made 1M-position drafters refuse batch sizes their serve shape fits with room to spare (~21x over-budget at a 49152 serve length).
- The context arena reads the served length from `attn_metadata.kv_cache_manager.max_seq_len`, which every backend carries, instead of a `max_seq_len` attribute only some metadata classes declare. On FlashInfer the attribute read came back empty and the arena was sized for the drafter's advertised 1048576 positions (a 165 GiB allocation, OOM in the first warmup forward) instead of the served 49152.
- RoPE drafter prefill context is written at slot-local positions: on a prefix-cache hit the target-forward positions start at the reused-token count, which would offset every stored key from the numbering the draft queries use.

**Commit 2 — FlashInfer one-engine speculation gate as a qualification boundary:**
The FLASHINFER one-engine speculation check refused every one-engine mode that does not share the target KV cache, with a message claiming a capability gap. That predicate is too broad (it refuses modes that need no separate draft KV cache manager at all — the suffix automaton, and DFlash's VANILLA/FA4 draft backends with worker-owned private buffers) and inaccurately stated for DFlash, where the refusal is a qualification decision: the combination boots and generates at a small batch size but has not been qualified at serving scale. `_flashinfer_one_engine_spec_supported` refuses DFlash regardless of draft backend or cache ownership, admits one-engine modes that need no separate draft manager, and states the qualification grounds plus the remedy (TRTLLM target attention).

## Test Coverage

All CPU-only:
- `tests/unittest/_torch/speculative/hw_agnostic/test_dflash_config_budget.py` (new): the buffer-bytes formula (VANILLA and TRTLLM paged layouts), budget derivation and weight-shard estimate, the config-time refusals with fitting-value messaging, the trained-width warning, and the `TorchLlmArgs` wiring including the weight-subtraction path.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/speculative/hw_agnostic/test_dflash_ctx_arena_sizing.py` (new): the arena sizing decision on metadata with and without the `max_seq_len` attribute, agreement between backends, and the position table remaining a ceiling.

title: [None][fix] Gate disaggregated KV block reuse admission on verified write coverage
body:
## Description

In disaggregated serving, the generation worker admits the KV block range it
received from the context worker into the block-reuse (radix) tree once the
transfer reports SUCCESS. A SUCCESS result alone is not proof that the
destination pages were actually written: a write that is skipped, partial, or
misrouted while a SUCCESS result frame is still delivered would put
never-written pages into the reuse tree under the prompt's token hashes, and
any later request sharing that prefix would silently reuse the poisoned
blocks (cross-request contamination). The failure is silent because the
original request itself is unaffected — only future reuse hits are wrong.

This change makes reuse admission fail-closed on verified write coverage:

- **Sender attestation** (`native/transfer.py`, `Sender._deliver_kv_to_agent`):
  the `transfer_size` carried in each KV result frame now attests only bytes
  from a submission that actually completed (`write_meta.sizes.sum()`), and is
  0 otherwise — never intent. Previously it was populated only when perf
  logging was on.
- **Receiver accounting** (`native/transfer.py`, `KVRecvTask` / `RxSession`):
  each receive task records the expected byte total of its published
  destinations (`expected_write_bytes`) and accumulates the writers' attested
  bytes; `write_verified` requires strict equality (over-coverage means
  duplicated/misrouted writes and is as disqualifying as missing coverage).
  `RxSession.kv_write_verified()` is the per-rank admission predicate.
- **Plumbing** (`base/transfer.py`, `native/fetch.py`, `transceiver.py`): the
  transceiver computes the local destination byte total
  (`_chunk_num_bytes(extent.local)`) and passes it through
  `PeerFetch.fetch(..., expected_write_bytes=...)` into `RxSession.receive`.
- **Cross-rank consensus** (`transceiver.py`): per-rank reuse trees stay
  consistent only if every rank admits the same tokens, so the verified
  verdict is intersected across ranks in the existing batched outcome
  allgather (one extra id list, no extra collective).
- **Fail-closed commit gate** (`transceiver.py`,
  `commit_blocks_for_reuse`): the received range is committed to the reuse
  tree only when the request carries a positive verified verdict
  (`py_kv_transfer_verified`); a missing verdict is treated as unverified.
  Skipping the commit never affects the request itself — generation proceeds
  normally, the blocks just stay out of the reuse tree — so the gate can only
  trade a reuse hit for correctness.

## Test Coverage

New: `tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_verified_reuse_admission.py`
(cpu-only, mock-based):

- `KVRecvTask.write_verified`: exact coverage verifies; short, over, and
  unknown-expected coverage do not; empty transfer (fully cached prefix)
  verifies trivially; untransferred task never verifies.
- `RxSession` accounting: expected bytes plumb into the task; multi-writer
  SUCCESS results accumulate attested bytes; a SUCCESS result with zero
  attested bytes (the false-success case) leaves the session unverified even
  though the transfer looks complete; partial coverage and FAILED-result
  bytes do not verify; an empty session is never verified.
- Commit gate: verified request commits to the reuse adapter; unverified or
  missing verdict does not.
- Cross-rank consensus: a request is verified only when every rank verified
  its shard; the no-sync path uses the local verdict; the quiesced-only call
  shape used by the context path is unchanged.
- Sender attestation: a completed submission attests the actual byte total in
  the result frame; a failed submission attests zero.

Updated: `tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_transfer_ownership_regressions.py`
for the widened consensus outcome list and the new `receive` parameter.

title: [nvbugs/6758245] Avoid metrics queue polling when iteration stats are disabled
body:
## Rubin issue
NVBug 6758245 reports that Kimi K3 NVFP4 serving on Rubin regresses when `enable_iter_perf_stats=false`: output performance and interactivity degrade versus the enabled configuration. The failure is in the disabled `/metrics` path, not in metric computation.

## Root cause / invariant
With iteration stats disabled, no background stats buffer is created. The `/metrics` handler nevertheless fell through to the legacy `get_stats_async(2)` queue poll, causing a timeout/poll on every request. With stats enabled, the collector-owned buffer path was used. The invariant is that disabled stats must return an empty metrics payload without touching the stats queue, while VisualGen, enabled buffered metrics, and legacy missing-flag behavior remain unchanged.

## Change
- Short-circuit disabled iteration stats in `OpenAIServer.get_iteration_stats`.
- Add repeated direct-call and registered FastAPI `/metrics` regression coverage.

## Evidence
The Rubin reproduction recorded the false arm entering `legacy_queue_poll` with `get_stats_async(2)` and the true arm using `buffer_return`; after the guard, the false arm is `disabled_short_circuit`.

## Validation
- Commit `4ccb3fdf8c5facc9dbf4a77e40cde19d71dc4141` reviewed and transplanted as `c5854eab343ba78a70ab81c01e1ae13866d85b4a`.

## Description

LLM.encode() accepts model-specific tensors via `**model_kwargs`, but the encoder runner rejected them whenever encoder CUDA graphs were enabled, so models needing an extra input had to give up graph capture.

This PR replaces that rejection with a declaration. Each tensor `kwarg` is declared in `EncodeCudaGraphConfig.extra_model_inputs`; the runner gives it a static buffer, captures every bucket with a zero-filled stand-in so the graph sees the full `forward()` signature, and copies the caller's tensor into the buffer on each replay (zero-filling the padding tail).

A spec has exactly one symbolic dimension, which is what lets it cover every bucket:

- "`num_tokens`" — scales with the packed token count (e.g. `token_type_ids`)
- "`batch_size`" — one row per request (e.g. per-request features)

Other dimensions are fixed integers. Before `forward()`, a declared `kwarg` must be a tensor matching its spec; an undeclared tensor raises (almost always a forgotten spec, and falling back silently would hide the lost speedup), while an undeclared non-tensor runs that call eagerly instead of being frozen into the graph at its capture-time value. Tensors may be on host or device.

## Example

```python
from tensorrt_llm import LLM
from tensorrt_llm.llmapi import EncodeCudaGraphConfig, EncodeExtraInputSpec

cuda_graph_config = EncodeCudaGraphConfig(
    batch_sizes=[1, 2, 4],
    num_tokens=[64, 128],
    seq_lens=[32, 64],
    enable_padding=True,
    extra_model_inputs=[
        EncodeExtraInputSpec(name="token_type_ids", shape=("num_tokens",), dtype="int32"),
        EncodeExtraInputSpec(name="per_request_feature", shape=("batch_size", 20), dtype="float32"),
    ],
)

llm = LLM(model=MODEL, encode_only=True, cuda_graph_config=cuda_graph_config)

outputs = llm.encode(
    prompts,
    token_type_ids=token_type_ids,     # (total_tokens,) int32
    per_request_feature=per_request_feats,  # (len(prompts), 20) float32
)
```

### Not supported

`extra_model_inputs` is rejected for feature-mode and encoder-decoder encoder graphs.

## Test Coverage

title: [https://nvbugs/6665906][fix] Restore Mistral Large 3 multimodal inference
body:
## Description

The verified NVBug 6665906 startup failure is caused by `checkpoint_format="mistral_large_3"` selecting `MistralNativeInputProcessor` while `Mistral3VLM` advertises multimodal encoder item scheduling. The native processor did not implement the required scheduling hooks, so engine construction failed before inference.

Static analysis also identifies a follow-on required by this model geometry: Mistral-Large-3 uses a 1664 / 16 = 104 Pixtral attention head. TRTLLM-GEN does not support head size 104, so SM100 must route that exact shape to FMHA v2. FMHA v2 must generate both the head-dimension-104 kernel and its packed-QKV padding-mask variant. This follow-on has not yet been observed in a GB200 run because the verified startup failure occurs first.

This change:

- shares the Pixtral encoder item-scheduling contract between the Hugging Face and mistral-native input processors
- adds head size 104 beside the existing head size 72 SM100 fallback to FMHA v2
- generates the SM100 head-dimension-104 kernel and keeps the packed-QKV padding-mask allowlist synchronized
- adds CPU generator and processor-contract coverage and removes the NVBug waiver

Adding 104 to the padding-mask allowlist also enables the same Pixtral-Large fused shape on the existing SM80/86/89/90/120 FMHA v2 families. This is intentional coverage of the same model geometry, not a separate behavior change.

The NVBug 6572838 change is not sufficient here because it disables the multimodal encoder for text-only tests; this MMMU case requires the vision encoder.

title: [TRTLLMINF-336][infra] Publish the BOLTed build under a distinct name
body:
## Description

The canonical-overwrite scheme cannot be made race-free. The canonical SBSA tarball is
downloadable the moment `Build-SBSA` finishes, and `Build-Docker-Images` runs in parallel
with the SBSA branch, so `get_wheel_from_package.py` fetches it hours before `BoltProfileGen`
could replace it. The image then contains the unoptimized wheel permanently, even when BOLT
later succeeds, and nothing about the run says so. `Dockerfile.bolt` does not close that gap
either -- it copies profiles into the image, it does not optimize the installed binaries.

This publishes the optimized build as `bolted-<tarball>` instead, a second object next to an
untouched canonical one. The artifact is its own publication signal: it appears atomically
and only on success, so a consumer that names it either gets optimized bytes or gets nothing
to fetch. Consumers that require optimization name it explicitly and fail when it is absent
(wired up separately); consumers that do not care keep reading the canonical object, which
now never changes under them.

Two things fall out:

- The input is unambiguous. Canonical is the un-BOLTed build by construction, on a fresh
  `artifactPath` and on a re-run alike, so the `unbolted-<tarball>` snapshot and the probe
  that preferred it exist only to prevent a double-BOLT that can no longer happen. Both go away.
- The SBSA test stages, which are sequenced after `BOLT-Profile-Gen`, now prefer
  `bolted-<tarball>` when it is there, so post-merge still exercises the very build the run
  promotes. They fall back to canonical loudly -- that is all that exists on x86, on pre-merge,
  and when the producer did not publish.

`Build.groovy`'s pre-merge path keeps naming its BOLTed tarball canonical: it runs before the
upload, so that object is written once, already optimized, and no consumer can have fetched
an earlier version of it.

**Renames the job parameter** `boltPublishCanonical` -> `boltPublishBolted`. Because the
`parameters{}` block replaces the job's parameter list on every run, an undeclared parameter
is dropped even when the parent sends it -- so the first post-merge run after this lands
publishes nothing. Harmless (publication is still off), but worth knowing.

Still default OFF; the rollout is flipped on in #19209.

## Test Coverage

No automated tests -- this is CI infrastructure, and the publish path is dead code until the
toggle in #19209 lands, so this PR is a no-op on `main`.

What to look for on a `/bot run`: the SBSA test stages log
`[BOLT] no bolted-<tarball> ... (HTTP 404); testing the canonical un-BOLTed build`
and download exactly as before. The `BoltProfileGen` stage logs
`PUBLISH_BOLTED_TARBALL=false: not publishing a BOLTed tarball.`

The publish path itself is first exercised by #19209.

Renames the job parameter boltPublishCanonical -> boltPublishBolted. Still default OFF; the rollout is flipped on in a follow-up change.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- Publishes optimized artifacts as `bolted-<tarball>` without overwriting the canonical artifact after merge.
- Publishes only when `boltPublishBolted`, profile application, and promotion are enabled.
- SBSA stages prefer the bolted artifact and fall back to the canonical artifact.
- `jenkins/Build.groovy` still creates and uploads `unbolted-<tarball>` during pre-merge consumption. This conflicts with the stated removal of the unbolted snapshot and requires confirmation.
- Review findings and test results were not supplied.

## QA Engineer Review

No test changes.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- **`jenkins/BoltProfileGen.groovy`**: Verify separate bolted publication, canonical artifact preservation, missing-output handling, publication conditions, and the renamed parameter default.
- **`jenkins/Build.groovy`**: Verify the pre-merge path and confirm whether `unbolted-<tarball>` must remain. Current logic preserves and uploads this artifact.
- **`jenkins/L0_Test.groovy`**: Verify bolted-artifact probing, retries, HTTP-status handling, fallback behavior, and artifact selection in both test paths.
