title: [https://nvbugs/6777522][test] Guard VisualGen ffmpeg apt install with timeout and retry
body:
## Description
`_visual_gen_deps` installed ffmpeg with an unbounded `apt-get update`/`apt-get install`, so a stalled or mid-sync mirror hung the entire pytest session until the 3600s timeout (https://nvbugs/6777522). Because the hang happens inside a test, CI's retry mechanism is skipped, so a transient mirror blip can consume a whole post-merge stage. The trigger seen in the field was the unrelated NVIDIA CUDA apt repo serving mid-sync metadata right after a CUDA release ("File has unexpected size … Mirror sync in progress?"), which failed the blanket `apt-get update`.
The install is now a bounded, retried helper (`install_ffmpeg_via_apt` in `conftest.py`) that runs `dpkg --configure -a` → `apt-get update` → `apt-get install ffmpeg`, with a 240s per-attempt timeout and up to 3 attempts (15s backoff), so a stalled mirror fails fast instead of hanging:
- Bound both apt calls' per-connection timeout (`Acquire::http(s)::Timeout=30`) so a stall fails fast on either the index fetch or the `.deb` download; retries are owned by the loop (apt's internal retry left at its default of 0).
- `apt-get update` is required — the CI image ships without apt lists (`docker/common/install_ci.sh` ends with `rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*`), so `install` can't fetch ffmpeg without it. Its exit code is tolerated (`|| true`) so an unrelated repo that is unreachable or mid-sync (notably the NVIDIA CUDA repo) can't fail the whole step; `install` never refetches that repo, so the ffmpeg install from Ubuntu is the real gate.
- `export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive` + `dpkg --configure -a < /dev/null` run first so that if a prior attempt was SIGKILLed mid-unpack, the retry repairs the interrupted dpkg state without blocking on a debconf prompt.
Behavior is unchanged when ffmpeg is already present — the `shutil.which` guard short-circuits.

## Test Coverage
- `examples/visual_gen/test_media_deps_install.py` (`l0_cpu` stage, no GPU): runs the real `install_ffmpeg_via_apt()` — no mocking — and asserts the `ffmpeg` CLI is then on `PATH`, i.e. verifies the bounded/retried install genuinely works. Confirmed on a node that a fresh install (ffmpeg removed → reinstalled, as root) succeeds.
- End-to-end coverage via existing VisualGen example tests that request `_visual_gen_deps` (e.g. `test_visual_gen_wan.py::test_visual_gen_quickstart` / `::test_visual_gen_api_walkthrough` on H100 pre-merge, and `test_visual_gen_qwen_image.py::test_qwen_image_example`).
Timing measured on a cluster node (Ubuntu 24.04): `apt-get update` ~4s and `apt-get install ffmpeg` ~29s, so the 240s per-attempt timeout is ~7x a healthy install and the 3-attempt sequence stays well under the 3600s stage budget.

title: [#19435][fix] Keep the insufficient-KV vote rank-safe under attention-DP
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/19436/files) against `main`.

## Summary

- `_sync_gen_only_benchmark_has_insufficient_kv()` returned before
  `_allgather_model_parallel_status()` whenever this rank's
  `_benchmark_fill_phase_active` flag was clear. That flag is rank-local dynamic state,
  so a post-fill rank could skip the gather while a still-filling peer was already inside
  it, leaving the two ranks on different collectives of the same communicator.
- The flag is now voted instead of read: only the rank-uniform
  `benchmark_req_queues_size` / `is_warmup` conditions short-circuit, the flag travels in
  the status tuple, and the fail-fast decision is taken from the gathered result. Normal
  serving (`TLLM_BENCHMARK_REQ_QUEUES_SIZE` unset) still returns before any collective.
- **The terminal vote is counted only from ranks that are still filling** (rev2, see
  below). A rank that has cleared its own fill phase has no fill left to declare
  unfittable, so its `terminal_no_fit` must not fail-fast a peer whose fill is healthy.
- Regression coverage is added to the existing `TestFailFastDuringBenchmarkFill` class,
  reusing its executor stub, so the tests drive `_prepare_and_schedule_batch()` rather
  than a copy of the decision logic.

## Root cause

`py_executor.py:3686-3688` gated the model-parallel gather on rank-local state:

```python
if (self.benchmark_req_queues_size <= 0 or self.is_warmup
        or not self._benchmark_fill_phase_active):
    return False
```

`_benchmark_fill_phase_active` is seeded from the static benchmark-disagg config but is
cleared per rank when the *global* fill gate opens (`_check_benchmark_disagg_gate`,
`py_executor.py:3995`). A rank that has cleared it then returns before the gather its
peers are entering. The fill gate gathers a pickled object (`MPIDist.tp_allgather`) while
`_can_queue()` gathers a raw `MPI.INT64_T` (`tp_allgather_int64`), so MPI matches them by
order and datatype instead of failing — the same failure class already documented from a
live run at `py_executor.py:4676-4679`.

This was the only site in the tree that gated a collective on rank-local state before
entering it. The rank-safe sibling states the required discipline at
`py_executor.py:3903-3905`: *"Keep going to the shared allgather even when this rank is
not done so model-parallel ranks cannot diverge in collective order."*

### rev2: the terminal vote is also rank-local

Voting the flag fixed the *collective-order* divergence but left a second, opposite
divergence: rev1 still read `status[2]` from every rank.

```python
any_rank_terminal_no_fit = any(status[2] for status in all_rank_status)   # rev1
any_rank_terminal_no_fit = any(
    status[2] for status in all_rank_status if status[0])                 # rev2
```

`local_terminal_no_fit` means *"my fill cannot fit"*. It is only meaningful on a rank
that is itself still filling. A post-fill rank's stale `True` could therefore fail-fast a
peer whose own fill was perfectly healthy — one rank still kills the other, just from the
post-fill side. `all_ranks_fetched` is unchanged: every rank must still have fetched the
full queue before the gate can open.

## Scope

- Included: the benchmark-disagg fill-gate fail-fast path in
  `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/py_executor.py` and its tests.
- Not included: the scheduler, KV transfer, model forward, and the `_can_queue` gather.
  No public API or configuration change.

## Validation

### Unit

| Test | Baseline | Patch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tests/unittest/_torch/disaggregation/test_benchmark_disagg.py` (CPU, torch 2.13.0+cu130) | 72 passed | **81 passed** |
| `test_post_fill_peer_terminal_vote_does_not_kill_a_filling_rank` under rev1 code | **FAILED** — the post-fill rank's terminal vote fail-fasts the healthy filling rank | — |
| same test under rev2 code | — | **passed** |

The A/B row is the point of the new test: it is red on the exact revision the review
question was asked about and green after the gate.

### 3-GPU end-to-end (`TLLM_BENCHMARK_REQ_QUEUES_SIZE=64`)

Three distinct L20s: CTX (`tp_size=1`) on one, GEN (`tp_size=2` + `enable_attention_dp`)
on two others, NIXL `KvCacheTransceiverV2` (`cache_transceiver_config.backend: NIXL`),
router `schedule_style:
context_first`, `NGram` speculation (`max_draft_len=4`) on the GEN worker only. rev2
applied to the installed wheel and verified in-process.

| Observation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Rank-safe gather at the gate | returns on both ranks; no collective-order divergence |
| Fill gate | **opens** — `Benchmark disagg fill complete: 32 active requests ready, gate opening.` |
| Requests submitted by the client | 64 (`POST /v1/completions` ×64 at the router) |
| Requests served to completion | 32 of 64 (mean TTFT 4.74 s, mean E2EL 6.44 s, 4096 output tokens = 32 × 128) |
| Where the run then stops | GEN's executor loop wedges **downstream of the gate**, in `SamplerEvent.synchronize()` (`sampler/sampler_features.py:570`) — see Limitations |

### Why earlier runs never reached the gate

`benchmark_serving.py:322-347` sends **one** warm-up prompt before the burst
(`no_test_input=False`, the default). With `TLLM_BENCHMARK_REQ_QUEUES_SIZE=64` the GEN
worker holds that single request until 64 have been fetched, and the client blocks on the
warm-up response before ever submitting the burst — a client-side deadlock that looks
exactly like "the fill gate never opens" (`num_fetch_requests=1 < 64`, one
`POST /v1/completions` in the router log). Passing `--no-test-input` is what makes the
gate observable at all; with it, the same configuration opens the gate and serves
requests.

## Limitations

- **The original #17095 signature was not reproduced.** The gate opens and requests are
  served, but the run then wedges *after* the gate, in the sampler's D2H event wait:
  `py-spy` on both GEN ranks shows `_executor_loop` → `_update_requests` →
  `sampler.update_requests` → `SamplerEvent.synchronize()` → `cuda_event.synchronize()`,
  with the CTX rank idle in `queue.get()`. 32 of 64 requests are served, then the GPU
  event never completes. This change is therefore **not** claimed to fix that deadlock;
  it removes a rank-divergence at the fill-gate vote and is validated as such.
- The wedge is not caused by `TRTLLM_GPU_KEEPALIVE`: it reproduces identically with the
  keepalive disabled (`TRTLLM_GPU_KEEPALIVE=0`, no keepalive activity in the worker log).
- DSpark is Blackwell-only (`dspark_attention_custom_op.py:70-71`), so the reporter's
  backend cannot run on this hardware; the E2E used `NGram` on the GEN worker.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/disaggregation/` as a whole cannot be collected in this
  environment: `test_backend_contract.py` and `test_disagg_coordinator_admission.py`
  import symbols (`Attempt`, `transfer_window_bypass_eligible`) that the installed wheel
  does not export. That is repo-vs-wheel drift, unrelated to this change, and both files
  fail identically before and after it.

title: [#17900][perf] Fuse NVFP4 tail after NCCL fallback
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/17901/files) against `main`.

## Description

Closes #17900.

On topologies without P2P support, the AllReduce fallback completes the collective with NCCL. This PR fuses the remaining residual add, RMSNorm, and NVFP4 quantization into the existing local `residualRmsNormFp4Quant` kernel on supported Blackwell configurations.

The fused tail is gated to SM 10.x/12.x, contiguous matching FP16/BF16 inputs, a contiguous scalar FP32 scale, no bias, and a hidden dimension divisible by the NVFP4 scale-factor vector width. Unsupported shapes, layouts, and operations retain the separated local tail.

Both local tails consume raw device pointers. The shared fallback used by `allreduce` and `allreduce_pg` now rejects `residual`, `norm_weight`, `scale`, or `bias` on a device different from `input`, before selecting or launching either local tail. Sending a mismatched tensor to the separated path would leave the invalid-pointer risk in place. The architecture predicate is shared with the kernel launcher, NVFP4 layout limits are named constants, and the new local variables follow the repository naming convention.

## Validation

For follow-up commits `a4afba4` (bias device check + coverage) and `7e78fdb` (op namespace fix):

- Added the missing `bias` device check at the shared `fallbackRunSubsequentOps` boundary, so all four auxiliary tensors are rejected before either local tail runs.
- Extended the regression cases to cover `bias` on CPU and on a second GPU: 32 parametrized cases in total (four auxiliary tensors, CPU/cross-GPU mismatches, FP16/BF16, and both NVFP4 output variants). Each case also checks that the CUDA context remains usable after rejection.
- Fixed the new helper to call `torch.ops.trtllm.allreduce`. The thop is registered in the `trtllm` namespace, so every case raised `AttributeError` before reaching a device check and the new coverage never executed.
- Formatted the changed regions with the repository's pinned clang-format (16) and yapf (0.40.2); `git diff --check` is clean.

Measured on a rented 4x RTX 5060 Ti node (SM 12.0, no P2P), driver 580.126.09, CUDA 13.0 and torch 2.12.0+cu130, built from source with `--cuda_architectures=120-real`:

- `pytest tests/unittest/_torch/multi_gpu/test_allreduce.py -k nccl_nvfp4_auxiliary_device` (1 rank): **32 passed** — the compiled checks reject `residual`, `norm_weight`, `scale` and `bias` on CPU and on `cuda:1`.
- `-k "allreduce_fusion_patterns and hidden:128 and seqlen:16"` (2 ranks): **7 passed**, including `RESIDUAL_RMS_NORM_QUANT_NVFP4` and `RESIDUAL_RMS_NORM_OUT_QUANT_NVFP4`, so the fused NVFP4 tail still runs on SM 12.0.
- A wider `allreduce_fusion_patterns` selection: 35 passed, 7 failed with CUDA OOM because a co-tenant vLLM worker held ~13.8 GiB on every GPU of that node; those failures are environmental and were not re-run.
- Model E2E was not run on this node. The build needed two local, unrelated workarounds that are not part of this PR: `ENABLE_UCX=0` plus a pinned `CUDA_nvrtc_LIBRARY` for the partial CUDA install, and the paired-FP8 PTX guard in the MoE all-to-all translation unit mentioned below.

Previously recorded validation before this follow-up:

- SM120 source build with CUDA 13.0: passed.
- Existing multi-GPU pytest selection on a no-P2P node: 6 passed, 42 deselected; 2 ranks, hidden sizes 128/7168, sequence lengths 16/256/8192.
- Directed four-rank `RESIDUAL_RMS_NORM_OUT_QUANT_NVFP4` test: all ranks passed; residual maximum error 0, RMSNorm maximum error 0.00390.
- Nemotron NVFP4 TP4/EP1 E2E: 25/25 non-empty OpenAI-compatible responses.
- At FP16 shape `[64, 8192]` on four RTX 5060 Ti GPUs, the measured local tail improved from 0.103 ms to 0.039 ms. This is a historical component measurement, not a new end-to-end performance result.

The historical full SM120 checkout needed an unrelated paired-FP8 PTX compatibility workaround in a MoE all-to-all translation unit. That workaround is not included in this PR.

- [x] Regression tests are included.
- [x] DCO sign-off is included.
- [ ] GPU regressions, full build, and model E2E on the latest follow-up commit.

## Description

Disaggregated serving used hostname both as the advertised endpoint and as the local AF_INET listener address. A hostname that is valid for peers can therefore fail local IPv4 binding.

title: [None][feat] auto-detect reasoning and tool parsers across the Qwen series
body:
## What

Make `--reasoning_parser auto` and `--tool_parser auto` pick the right parser across the Qwen series, so serving a Qwen checkpoint does not require first looking up which parser it needs.

### Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8

- add a Qwen3.5 reasoning parser that handles both thinking and non-thinking chat-template prompts
- auto-select the Qwen3.5 reasoning parser for Qwen3.5, Qwen3.8, and Qwen4 experimental model types
- auto-select the existing Qwen3 Coder XML tool parser for Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6, and Qwen3.8 model types
- leave the Qwen3 and Qwen3-Coder parser implementations unchanged
- update Qwen3.8 deployment examples to use automatic parser selection

### Rest of the Qwen family

Running both resolvers over every Qwen checkpoint under `LLM_MODELS_ROOT` and comparing the answer against each checkpoint's chat template turned up four cases where `auto` answered wrongly or refused to start:

- **The chat template was only read from `tokenizer_config.json`.** Checkpoints re-saved by a newer `transformers` write the template to `chat_template.jinja` and leave that key `null`, so every `nvidia-Qwen3-*` FP8/NVFP4 checkpoint and the Qwen3-Next PTQ ones silently resolved to no reasoning parser at all. A new `tensorrt_llm/llmapi/hf_chat_template.py` reads the template from `chat_template.jinja`, `tokenizer_config.json`, or `chat_template.json` — the three layouts that actually occur in the store.
- **`--reasoning_parser auto` aborted on Instruct checkpoints.** Detection correctly answers "this model emits no reasoning block", and the CLI then rejected the flag with `BadParameter`. Auto-detection now separates an unrecognized model type (still an error) from a recognized one that needs no parser (logged, serves normally).
- **Qwen3-VL, Qwen2-VL and Qwen2.5-VL were in neither mapping**, so `auto` failed on both flags. They are mapped now, and reasoning stays template-driven so the Thinking and Instruct variants of a type resolve differently.
- **Qwen3-Coder is a `qwen3_moe` checkpoint**, indistinguishable from plain Qwen3 by `model_type`, so `auto` selected the Hermes JSON tool parser for a model trained to emit `<function=...><parameter=...>` XML. A template that asks for the XML shape now promotes the checkpoint to `qwen3_coder`; the mapping table stays authoritative otherwise.

Forced-thinking detection also moved from "`<think>` appears anywhere in the template" to "`<think>` appears in the generation prompt". Instruct templates mention the tag in order to re-render reasoning kept in the conversation history, and one checkpoint in the store (`qwen3-next-80b-instruct-nvfp4-ptq-fp8kv`) was read as a thinking model because of it.

Not covered: `qwen3_omni_moe` is left out because that architecture is not in the PyTorch backend's model registry, and no full Qwen3-Coder checkpoint is available locally, so that path is exercised by a unit test rather than against a real template.

## Validation

- clean TensorRT-LLM native Release build on 4x GB300 with CUDA 13.4, SM103, and NVRTC dynamic linking
- editable-install isolation audit passed before image export
- `trtllm-serve --help` passed
- exported `.sqsh` isolation audit passed

- both resolvers re-run over all Qwen checkpoints under `LLM_MODELS_ROOT`: every difference from the previous behaviour turns an unresolved or wrong answer into the one the checkpoint's chat template implies, and no case regressed
- pre-commit checks passed for all modified files

title: [None][fix] Pad INT8-woq MoE intermediate to 64 for tensor-parallel sharding
body:
#15550 has merged, so this now stands alone on main: the padding fix, non-aligned-shape test coverage, and two C++ changes addressing CodeRabbit findings from that review.

## Problem

`INT8WoqPerChannelFusedMoEMethod` does not pad its per-partition intermediate dimension after tensor-parallel sharding, so any model whose `moe_intermediate_size / tp_size` is not a multiple of 64 fails to load at TP > 1. The INT8 mixed-GEMM preprocessor (`preprocess_weights_for_mixed_gemm`) requires 64-aligned rows (`rows_per_tile = 128 * 8 // BITS_PER_ELT_A`, `BITS_PER_ELT_A = 16` for W8A16). The FP8, NVFP4, MXFP4 and WFP4A16 fused-MoE methods all round the sharded intermediate up and `F.pad`; INT8-woq was the only one that did not.

This limitation is already noted in-tree: should_skip_cutlass in tests/unittest/_torch/moe/moe_test_utils.py records that W8A16 "fails in preprocess_weights_for_mixed_gemm (num_rows % rows_per_tile != 0)" and skips the affected TP configurations rather than exercising them.

## Reproduction

`nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B` has `moe_intermediate_size = 1856 = 64 × 29`. Since 29 is prime, `1856 / tp` is a multiple of 64 only for `tp ∈ {1, 29}`; every power-of-2 TP leaves a non-aligned shard (`1856/8 = 232`, not ÷64). The native W8A16 checkpoint at `--tensor_parallel_size {2,4,8}` fails during weight load:

```
File ".../fused_moe/quantization.py", in load_expert_w3_w1_weight
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (464) must match the size of tensor b (232) at non-singleton dimension 1
```

TP = 1 loads (1856 is already 64-aligned) but the checkpoint does not fit a single 32 GB card, so TP > 1 is required in practice.

This is not specific to one checkpoint. Across the current Nemotron 3 MoE lineup, Nano, Lightning, Elastic, TwoTower and Cascade-2 all have `moe_intermediate_size = 1856`  and are misaligned at every TP ≥ 2, and Super (2688 = 64 × 42) is misaligned at TP ≥ 4. Ultra (5120 = 64 × 80) is aligned at every TP ≤ 8 and pays no padding cost, which also shows the change is a no-op wherever alignment already holds.

## Fix

Round the per-partition intermediate up to a multiple of 64 in `create_weights`, and `F.pad` each shard up to it in both weight loaders and the fc31 scales. Zero-padding is numerically inert (`Relu2(0) = 0` for squared-ReLU, `silu(0)·0 = 0` for gated), meaning it is lossless.

## Test Coverage

Adds a W8A16 CUTLASS parameter set with `intermediate_size = 200` (a multiple of neither 16 nor 64, rounding up to 256), covering both the non-gated (squared-ReLU) and gated (SwiGLU) layouts; the gated case additionally exercises padding of the `w3` gate projection before concatenation. Every `intermediate_size` in `MOE_MODEL_CONFIGS` is already a multiple of 64, so this path previously had no coverage. Without the fix all eight cases fail with AssertionError in preprocess_weights_for_mixed_gemm (num_rows % B_ROWS_PER_MMA == 0 in tensorrt_llm/quantization/functional.py); with the fix all eight pass against the dequantized reference on A100 for float16 and bfloat16.

Note that the new parameter set bypasses the 128-alignment gate in `get_quick_skip_reason()` for this case only, since that gate is precisely what the padding makes unnecessary for W8A16; all other skip reasons are honoured. Happy to instead relax that gate for W8A16 generally if maintainers prefer.

The generator also raises `ValueError`  unless both activation families are present, so an upstream rewording of the skip message cannot silently drop one of them.

## Validation

Consumer Blackwell (sm_120), TP = 8: native W8A16 checkpoint loads and serves; GSM8K 5-shot strict-match **0.8385 ± 0.0101** vs BF16 **0.8393 ± 0.0101** (Δ 0.0008, within stderr). Also loads and serves coherently at TP = 2 and TP = 4. All 40 existing W8A16 cases in `test_moe_backend.py` pass on A100 (gated and non-gated, float16 and bfloat16, CUTLASS). The branch merges cleanly against current `main`.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- Weight shards receive zero padding. FC1 scales receive unit-scale padding.
- Shape validation now runs after activation and layout resolution.
- Gated and non-gated activation paths use the correct intermediate-dimension rules.
- No public API or configuration changes were found.
- The implementation is consistent with the stated padding requirement.

## QA Engineer Review

title: [None][feat] Add W4A16 per-channel weight-only support for Cutlass fused MoE
body:
Description

Adds INT4 weight-only per-channel (W4A16) support to the Cutlass fused MoE path. Before this change, any non-INT8 per-channel quantization was refused outright in moeOp.cpp with TORCH_CHECK(false, "Unsupported weight only quantization"), even though the layers beneath it already handled INT4.

Changes

  • Generalise the per-channel flag from use_int8_woq_per_channel to use_woq_per_channel across the Python bindings and moeOp.cpp, so INT4 reaches the runner.
  • Extend the non-gated inter-size handling added in #15550 to INT4. Under the dim-swapped per-channel layout the sub-byte packing sits on fc1's inter dim, so mInnerDimMultiplier must multiply the fc1 side. The previous form is equivalent at INT8, where the multiplier is 1, but rejects every valid INT4 shape. Applied in both runMoe and runMoeMinLantency.
  • Add W4A16WoqPerChannelFusedMoEMethod: packed weight creation, per-output-channel scales, TP-aware loaders, and a 64-row alignment diagnostic that names the offending tensor and TP size instead of surfacing a bare AssertionError from inside preprocess_weights_for_mixed_gemm.
  • View both expert weight tensors as torch.quint4x2 at the quantized op call site. Without this, isInt8Quant() matched and CutlassMoeFCRunner was instantiated at uint8_t, producing incorrect output rather than an error.
  • Fix the meta kernel, which reported half the hidden size for packed INT4 and so disagreed with the real kernel under torch.compile.
  • Take the default unpadded_hidden_size after the per-channel layout swap in both runMoe and runMoeMinLantency. It was previously read from fc2_expert_weights.sizes()[1], which is inter_size under that layout.

Validation

Hardware: NVIDIA GB10, sm_121, single GPU. W4A16 takes the SM80 interleaved layout path.

Unit. W4A16 added to the parametrized MoE backend tests, comparing the Cutlass kernel against a dequantized reference at the existing 0.99 / 0.96 tolerances. 31 W4A16 cases pass across fp16 and bf16, sequence lengths 1 and 8, and six expert configurations up to 60 experts at hidden 2048. Running the W4A16 and W8A16 selections together gives 88 passed, 0 failed, so the shared per-channel path is not regressed. Non-gated W4A16 is covered end to end: QuantAlgo.W4A16 is in the element-wise (Relu2) sweep with a non-gated reference, giving 20 cases matching the W8A16 arm. QuantAlgo.W4A16 was also added to test_moe_module.py's QUANT_ALGOS, so the CUTLASS single-GPU module tests exercise it. Running the W4A16 and W8A16 selections together now gives 125 passed, 0 failed.

Model level. Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B, routed experts quantized offline to symmetric per-output-channel INT4 with everything else left BF16.

  | BF16 | W4A16 | delta -- | -- | -- | -- model weights | 58.82 GB | 17.81 GB | −69.7% output throughput | 199.8 tok/s | 414.7 tok/s | +107.6% mean TPOT | 156.4 ms | 74.5 ms | −52.4% mean TTFT | 1261.2 ms | 674.0 ms | −46.6% GSM8K strict-match, 5-shot | 0.8378 ±0.0102 | 0.8203 ±0.0106 | −0.0175

Benchmark: 500 prompts, 512 input and 512 output tokens, concurrency 32, 500/500 completed with zero failures. The GSM8K difference is 1.2 sigma on the standard error of the difference and is not statistically significant at n=1319.

The model-level measurements were taken on 1.3.0rc17; the branch is rebased onto main and the unit tests rerun there, built against the devel:1.3.0rc24 image (PyTorch 2.12).

Checkpoint format

Routed experts only (*.mixer.experts.N.{up_proj,down_proj}.weight); every other tensor stays BF16 and is listed in exclude_modules. Weights are quantized symmetrically per output channel with scale = absmax / 7, then packed two INT4 per byte along dim 0, the output dim, even logical index in the low nibble. Scales are written alongside as {key}.weight_scale at full unpacked width. hf_quant_config.json carries quant_algo: W4A16.

Related work

#16198 is open against the same two files (quantization.py and moeOp.cpp) and adds 64-row padding for INT8-woq under tensor parallelism. Since that one will land sooner, this PR will need a rebase. That padding approach is also the natural fix for the TP limitation below, as a follow-up.

Known limitations

  • should_skip_cutlass groups W4A16 with the 128-alignment quantizations although the real constraint is 64 rows. This is conservative rather than wrong. The multi-GPU module tests now run W4A16 on H100 and B200, but test_configurable_moe_multi_gpu uses DEP/TEP, which both set moe_tp_size = 1, so they cover expert parallelism; MoE tensor parallelism above one rank remains unexercised and is left to the 64-row padding follow-up. See Related work.
  • The inter-size check is shared with INT8, but the change is a no-op there: with mInnerDimMultiplier == 1 the new form is algebraically identical to the previous one in both the gated and non-gated branches. Only INT4, where the multiplier is 2, changes behaviour.
  • Validated on sm_121 only.
## Dev Engineer Review - Added plain per-channel `W4A16` support to the CUTLASS fused MoE path. - Added packed INT4 weights, per-channel scales, TP-aware loading, alignment checks, and `torch.quint4x2` operator inputs. - Generalized the kernel flag from `use_int8_woq_per_channel` to `use_woq_per_channel`. - Corrected packed INT4 dimension handling and `unpadded_hidden_size` derivation. - Added gated and non-gated reference support. - Added validation for unsupported activation, scale, alignment, and fused-checkpoint configurations. - Updated INT8 handling without changing its inter-size calculation because `mInnerDimMultiplier` remains 1. - Review points: - The renamed public arguments can affect external callers. Update downstream integrations if they use the old name. - Tensor parallelism greater than 1 remains conservatively skipped. - Validation covers `sm_121`; other architectures require additional validation. - Reported validation passed 125 selected W4A16/W8A16 tests with 159 skipped and 0 failed tests. ## QA Engineer Review - Added `test_cutlass_w4a16_weight_shapes_gated_and_nongated`. - Added `test_cutlass_w4a16_unaligned_rows_raise_diagnostic`. - Added `test_cutlass_w4a16_aligned_rows_accepted`. - Extended backend and module test matrices with `QuantAlgo.W4A16`. - Added W4A16 quantization utilities and reference accuracy checks. - Added W4A16 backend entries to: - `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_b200.yml` - `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_h100.yml` - The backend test functions are represented in the integration test lists. - Module-level W4A16 coverage is not identified in the listed test-db entries. - Reported test-list validation and pre-commit checks passed. - **Verdict: needs follow-up** for explicit CI test-list coverage of the module-level tests and broader architecture coverage.

title: [#15178][fix] Fix unified-memory Mamba KV estimation
body:
## Description

Refs #15178.

On integrated GPUs, the estimation dry run can start from a `mem_get_info()` budget that is already depressed by mmap-backed weights sharing the same physical memory pool.

When hybrid Mamba models use an affine `CacheCost`, `_get_token_num_for_estimation()` subtracts the recurrent-state intercept from that reduced budget and can clamp the provisional token cap to zero. That is enough to trip `assert max_blocks_per_seq > 0` in the attention-window path even though the later affine sizing still succeeds.

This change keeps the final affine sizing unchanged. It only relaxes the provisional estimation cap on integrated GPUs by dropping the affine intercept from the dry-run budget calculation.

The regression test covers the zero-clamp case by mocking an affine `CacheCost`, a small `mem_get_info()` budget, and an integrated device.

## Test Coverage

Validated in the matching TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc18 CUDA 13 / PyTorch 2.10 runtime with:

- `python -m pytest tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_kv_cache_estimation.py -k integrated_gpu_estimation_ignores_affine_intercept -q`

…ared length, not max_input_len

To see a list of available CI bot commands, please comment `/bot help`.

Fixes #19514. Follow-up to #18609 / #19450.

### Problem

For encoder-decoder models, `_get_cross_kv_cache_layout()` (`tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/_util.py`) sizes the cross-attention KV pool from `llm_args.max_input_len` (default 1024), which overwrites the engine sequence length unconditionally; the config-derived encoder limit is then applied with `min()` and can only shrink it further. Whisper declares its encoder length as `max_source_positions` (1500), which was not in the lookup list, so every `openai/whisper-large-v3` request with default arguments failed in `prepare_cross_metadata`:

```
The max KV cache length of input sequences (1500) exceeds the KV cache manager's maximum supported length (1024).
```

### Change

- Add `max_source_positions` to the encoder-length lookup.
- When the model declares an encoder length, use it as the cross pool length (the pool holds the encoder output; that limit is authoritative).
- Fall back to `max_input_len` only when the model declares no encoder length, so models without any of those config attributes keep today's behaviour.

One function, `+14 −6`.

### Verification

RTX 5070 Ti (sm_120), `nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/release:1.3.0rc25` with the #19450 guard, `openai/whisper-large-v3`, LLM API directly:

| config | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| defaults (`max_input_len` 1024, block reuse on) | `1500 exceeds 1024` | transcribes, 30 s clip in 3.5 s |
| `max_input_len=1500` (workaround) | transcribes | transcribes |

Verified against the 1.3.0rc25 release rather than a `main` build; the function is byte-identical between the two. Run matrix and logs are in my comments on #19450 and in #19514.

## Description

CBTS previously classified Markdown files as noop. For a docs-only change, the legacy Jenkins filter first selected CPU-Build_Docs, but the later CBTS filter rebuilt the job set from an empty affected-stages list and discarded that docs job.

- all documentation claims select CPU-Build_Docs

title: [#19337][fix] Correct VBWS width tracking and terminal-step finalization
body:
## Description

Variable-Beam-Width Search (VBWS) returns empty output sequences when generation terminates on a widening step in the PyTorch backend with the default overlap scheduler.

For

```python
SamplingParams(
    n=100,
    best_of=100,
    use_beam_search=True,
    beam_width_array=[16, 32, 100],
    max_tokens=3,
    temperature=0.0,
)
```

the expected per-step transitions are `1 -> 16`, `16 -> 32`, `32 -> 100`. The observed ones are `1 -> 16`, `16 -> 16`, `16 -> 32`, and the response holds 100 output slots of which only 16 carry generated tokens; the other 84 have empty `token_ids`.

There are two independent defects, and both have to be corrected to get the requested beams back.

1. `LlmRequest.get_beam_width_by_iter()` indexes `beam_width_array` with `decoding_iter`. The Python sampling loop advances `py_decoding_iter`, and `_handle_responses` copies it into `decoding_iter` only after the step has been sampled, so under the overlap scheduler the schedule is read one step behind where it is consumed. A widening array repeats a width instead of advancing.
2. `_prepare_beam_history_cba()` slices the finalized snapshot with `_get_beam_width_in(request)`, the width that *entered* the step. The snapshot already holds the beams the step *produced*, so on a widening terminal step the extra beams are dropped and their output slots stay padded.

The change is two lines plus the comments that explain them:

- index the schedule with `py_decoding_iter`;
- finalize with `_get_beam_width_out(request)`, the same accessor the sampler sized the step with.

`get_beam_width_by_iter()` keeps mirroring the C++ clamping formula. The only C++ consumer of that formula is the micro-batch scheduler, which runs before the sampler advances `py_decoding_iter`, so the two counters are equal at every point where C++ reads the width; `test_vbws_cpp_formula_matches_past_array_end` still pins the agreement, now with both counters held in sync.

Scope of the behaviour change:

- Change 1 only reaches requests that set `beam_width_array`; with no array the override delegates to the base implementation, which returns `sampling_config.beam_width` for both `for_next_iteration` values.
- Change 2 also reaches fixed-width beam search, in the one case where a step changes the width without an array: the context step, which enters with a single row and leaves `beam_width` beams. Finalizing it with the input width kept beam 0 and padded the rest, so `max_tokens=1` at `beam_width=4` returned one sequence and three empty ones. That is the same defect with the same root cause, and it is fixed too; `test_beam_search_finish_on_first_step_returns_every_beam` covers it. Every other fixed-width step enters and leaves the same width, so the two accessors agree and nothing changes.

Not addressed here: the micro-batch scheduler budgets `getBeamWidthByIter()` tokens per request while generation rows are laid out at the static `py_beam_width`, so for VBWS the budget is narrower than the rows the forward emits regardless of which counter is read. That predates this change and is orthogonal to the empty-output defect.

Fixes #19337

## Test Coverage

New and updated tests, all in `tests/unittest/_torch/sampler/test_beam_search.py`:

- `test_beam_search_vbws_widening_terminal_step[overlap|no_overlap]` (new, end to end on the dummy-model engine): `beam_width_array=[2, 3, 4]` with `max_tokens=3`, so the run ends exactly on the `3 -> 4` widening step. Asserts the width each step produces and that all four beams hold three tokens. The existing `test_beam_search_vbws_e2e` decodes past the end of the array, so its last step holds the final width and cannot reach this case; it also runs only with the overlap scheduler disabled, where the two counters stay in sync.
- `test_vbws_width_follows_python_iter_when_response_handling_lags` (new, unit): pins the schedule against `py_decoding_iter` while `decoding_iter` trails, which is the overlap state between `_update_requests` and `_handle_responses`.
- `test_cba_finalize_collects_beams_a_widening_step_produced` (new, unit): CBA finalization of a step that widened from 3 beams to 4, with an empty pool, so every output beam must come from the live ones.
- `test_beam_search_finish_on_first_step_returns_every_beam` (new, end to end): fixed-width beam search with `max_tokens=1`, so the run ends on the context step and every beam has to survive finalization.
- `_set_vbws_iteration()` (new helper) and the four schedule-walking tests that used it: they set `decoding_iter` only, which no longer drives the Python override. The helper holds both counters at the same iteration, the state every non-overlap step is in.

Measured on the reporter's environment, where each defect is isolated:

| applied | `[overlap]` | `[no_overlap]` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| neither (current `main`) | fail: produced widths `[2, 2, 3]`, expected `[2, 3, 4]` | fail: `beam 3 holds 0 tokens` |
| finalization only | fail: produced widths `[2, 2, 3]` | pass |
| width tracking only | fail: `beam 3 holds 0 tokens, expected 3: []` | fail: `beam 3 holds 0 tokens` |
| both | pass | pass |

`test_cba_finalize_collects_beams_a_widening_step_produced` fails without the finalization change with the fourth output row still padded (3 of 12 elements differ) and passes with it. `test_beam_search_finish_on_first_step_returns_every_beam` fails without it with `beam 1 holds 0 tokens, expected 1: []` -- the beams it returns are `[[6], [], [], []]` -- and passes with it, returning `[[6], [5], [4], [3]]`.

```bash
pytest tests/unittest/_torch/sampler/test_beam_search.py \
    -k "vbws or cba or finish_on_first_step"    # 32 passed
pytest tests/unittest/_torch/sampler/test_beam_search.py
# 305 passed, 12 skipped, 1 failed -- the failure is
# test_beam_search_disagg_first_token_is_end_id, which needs the NIXL
# transfer agent and is unrelated to this change
scripts/run_mypy.sh                             # no issues found in 17 source files
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

Independently reproduced on a public checkpoint (Qwen3-0.6B, bfloat16, single GPU) using the exact parameters from the issue -- `beam_width_array=[16, 32, 100]`, `max_tokens=3`, `n=best_of=100`, `temperature=0.0`, `ignore_eos=True` -- with only the two source files toggled:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| output length histogram | `{0: 84, 3: 16}` | `{3: 100}` |
| non-empty outputs | 16 | 100 |
| distinct beams | 17 | 100 |

The three highest-ranked beams are token-for-token identical before and after, so the change recovers the 84 dropped beams without reordering anything. The histogram before the fix matches the one in the issue, which also shows the defect is independent of the model, its vocabulary, and the prompts used.

These runs were on a v1.3.0rc26 build, the version the issue was reported against. `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/sampler/beam_search.py` is identical between v1.3.0rc26 and current `main`, and so are the changed lines of `llm_request.py`, so the same patch applies to `main` unchanged; CI on `main` remains the authority.

- PR description clearly explains what and why.
- PR follows the TRT-LLM coding guidelines.

- No new dependencies.
- No CODEOWNERS change.
- No documentation change: this restores the documented VBWS behaviour.
- No tava architecture diagram change: no design change.

title: [None][doc] GVR V2: Self-Sampling and Multi-Thresholding for Faster Exact Top-K
body:
<!--

SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

## Description

**GVR V2: Self-Sampling and Multi-Thresholding for Faster Exact Top-K**  
*A Unified Selection Core for Prefill and Decode in TensorRT LLM*

Sparse-attention Top-K must find exact winners while controlling full-row reads, candidate work, and integration state. This article explains how GVR V2 uses current-row self-sampling and dense multi-threshold verification to narrow exact refinement, and how removing the temporal Top-K prior lets prefill and decode share the streaming selection core.

Four main sections cover:

1. **Motivation and design foundations:** temporal-hint variability and prior-state maintenance, followed by the connection to Floyd–Rivest SELECT. Later V1 already uses multi-thresholding; V2 changes calibration and removes the prior lifecycle. Figure 2 defines overlap after temporal-hint index mapping: +1 for V3.2 and unchanged compressed-bin indices for V4 Pro. Its blue points are current selections predicted by the mapped hint; this distinguishes prediction accuracy from same-token retention. Classical randomized comparison bounds are distinguished from V2's deterministic sampling and GPU latency objective.
2. **Self-sampling and multi-thresholding:** an algorithm overview and exactness invariant precede candidate amplification and GPU implementation. Figure 5 uses a simplified tail-count staircase and explicit K/E/D population segments, with qualitative explanations instead of arbitrary numerical ratios. The article explains 8/16-score sample windows, vector loads, sector utilization, sample coverage, register pressure, histogram anchors, and execution families. Detailed addressing, HIC/TSH rules, counter ownership, and prefetch placement are documented in the companion.
3. **Performance and roofline analysis:** direct comparisons of GVR V2, GVR V1 (temporal hint), and TensorRT LLM radix CUDA. Paired heatmaps show V2 speedups over radix CUDA and GVR V1 across the length–batch grid. Three-implementation latency plots and Pareto curves include average/peak reachable rates. The text distinguishes ideal-traffic efficiency from measured DRAM utilization and the repeated-score-row benchmark from heterogeneous serving concurrency.
4. **TensorRT LLM integration and takeaways:** removed prior state, phase-specific row metadata, shared streaming selection, graph readiness, historical serving results with separate attribution, and a `trtllm-bench throughput` enablement example.

The performance reference is PR #19076's measured public revision. All three implementations cover the same 9,746 B200 FP32 cases, including 21 Flash layers, 30 Pro layers, and all 61 V3.2 layers. GVR V2 delivers geometric-mean gains of **5.05× over radix CUDA and 1.46× over GVR V1**. Individual minima and win rates remain visible. GVR V1 denotes the temporal-hint implementation from [PR #16877](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/16877), the newer V1 implementation in the measured dataset. The comparison spans benchmark runs and does not isolate calibration alone.

The radix heatmap aggregates 275 shape cells across all eleven batch sizes and reaches **20.18×** on V4 Pro at 4,099 scores and batch size 1,024. Cell values are geometric means across layers, distinct from individual-case extrema. The color scale covers all observed values without clipping. The GVR V1 heatmap covers the same 275 shapes with a separate 1–3× scale; its averages range from 1.05× to 2.87×. Orange corners mark 15 shapes containing individual-layer regressions, preserving the distinction between a 1.05× Pro shape average and the 0.689× individual minimum. The discussion explains that informative temporal hints can still improve local admission, while their variability motivates V2’s robustness goal.

Eleven SVGs show the comparison, temporal variability, algorithm evolution, selection/recovery, candidate work, GPU sampling, radix and V1 speedup distributions, latency, roofline behavior, and shared integration. Public timing exports, provenance, summaries, and plotting code contain only the retained implementations. Existing retained timing observations are unchanged; the single V1 reference, V2, and radix use complete common coverage.

title: [None][perf] Overlap TRTLLM-Gen FMHA JIT warmup compilation with engine warmup (opt-in)
body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- Added opt-in asynchronous TRTLLM-Gen FMHA JIT warmup with `TRTLLM_GEN_FMHA_ASYNC_WARMUP=1`.
- Overlapped compilation with engine autotuning, CUDA-graph capture, and memory profiling.
- Serialized export-library access and drained background work before CUDA-graph capture and kernel destruction.
- Added per-device and per-`TllmGenFmhaKernel` warmup registry state.
- Added foreground verification and inline fallback for worker, compilation, and completion failures.
- Deduplicated identical per-layer warmup sweeps.
- Added multi-CTA buffer validation and JIT cache-miss diagnostics.
- Deleted copy construction and copy assignment for `TllmGenFmhaKernel`.
- Preserved default synchronous behavior.
- Limited code changes to `fmhaKernels.h`.
- Internal B200 testing reported warmup reduction from 163 seconds to approximately 26–30 seconds.
- Internal testing reported unchanged spec-decode acceptance and steady-state performance, with no first-traffic compilation misses.

## QA Engineer Review

No test changes.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

At engine startup, TRTLLM-Gen FMHA generation kernels are NVRTC-compiled synchronously inside the first warmup forward — ~5–11s per kernel variant depending on host CPU, 80–160s total on MLA fp8-KV configs (DeepSeek-family), ~2min for sparse gen kernels. This sits directly on the engine cold-start critical path.

This PR overlaps that compilation with the rest of engine warmup:

- **Opt-in via `TRTLLM_GEN_FMHA_ASYNC_WARMUP=1`**: the warmup grid compiles on a single background thread while autotuning, CUDA-graph capture, and memory profiling proceed. Default off; flag-off behavior is unchanged apart from deduplicating identical per-layer warmup sweeps (every layer of a warmup forward requests the same grid — only the first compiles anything).
- **Serialization**: all calls into the FMHA export lib go through a global interface mutex. The lib's `kernelCache` is an unsynchronized global LRU (cache *hits* mutate it too), and kernel selection mutates shared state through the `FmhaAutoTuner` occupancy probe (attribute set→query on a shared dummy kernel), so concurrent foreground/background access is not safe without it.
- **CUDA-graph safety**: the background queue is drained before graph capture, and `run()` drains if invoked on a capturing stream.
- **No post-ready misses**: a foreground verify pass re-walks each registered sweep before the engine reports ready; any gap (background failure, worker-thread start failure, compile exception) degrades to inline compilation.

Context: discussed with @PerkzZheng in the NVIDIA↔Baseten channel; he asked us to share the change so the code owners can integrate and validate. Measured on B200 deployments (Kimi-K2.x-class MLA fp8-KV, eagle3 one-model spec decode): critical-path warmup 163s → ~26–30s, spec-decode acceptance and steady-state throughput unchanged, no first-traffic compile misses. The win scales with host CPU slowness (compile time dominates) and with the recently widened `kDefaultWarmupSeqLenQCandidates`, which grows the warmup grid this PR takes off the critical path.

One file changed: `cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/trtllmGenKernels/fmha/fmhaKernels.h` (wrapper-level only; no changes inside the export lib).

## Test Coverage

- Flag off (default): existing FMHA integration/unit tests cover this path — behavior is identical apart from the sweep dedupe, which the foreground verify pass also re-validates.
- Flag on: exercised on internal B200 deployments (TP4 MLA fp8-KV + eagle3 one-model spec decode, and GLM-class sparse-attention configs): A/B vs flag-off shows identical spec-decode acceptance and steady-state performance; burst traffic immediately after readiness shows no compile-triggered latency spikes.
- Happy to add a gtest for the warmup registry/drain state machine if the code owners want one — guidance welcome on where it should live.

title: [None][perf] Optimize GVR prefill windows and BF16 refinement
body:
<!-- Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved. -->

## Description

Improve FP32 self-sampling prefill by bypassing selection for short rows, constructing a fallback bracket from the first K values of the current window, and reusing the register kernel for supported bounded windows. The measured gains are concentrated in prefill. The latest two-round cold decode confirmation gives parent/current geometric means of **0.999847× FP32 / 0.999947× BF16**, with floors of **0.967177× / 0.964407×**; per-case absence of regressions is not established. The BF16 Main refinement change retains a local **1.054613×** cold speedup at `v4_pro_1024k_L46`, BS=1024, without establishing an overall decode gain.

Depends on [#19285](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/19285), based on commit `c7f34372c7fe1c899e35b96fa8a4f98975e104a4`. This upstream PR targets `main` and temporarily includes the parent commits because the parent branch is in the author fork. Rebase onto `main` after #19285 lands. Incremental comparison from that parent commit: [five-file incremental diff](https://github.com/longcheng-nv/TensorRT-LLM/compare/c7f34372c7fe1c899e35b96fa8a4f98975e104a4...7470e04631afb348324f072747a5032f5cfcb9e6).

The incremental change updates three existing production files and two existing test files, with no new production module:

- In the FP32 streaming prefill kernel, rows with at most K valid values emit local identity indices and `-1` padding without entering the selection body. Construct the fallback bracket lazily when needed.
- Add a prefill specialization to the existing register template. Its current route is restricted to SM100, K=512/1024/2048, and trusted window bounds up to 4096; K=2048 additionally supports bounds up to 8192. Prefill remains FP32-only. Keep window-local output indices and cover partial row slabs during warmup using small representative allocations.
- Pass `scores.shape[1]` to both readiness and execution in the existing TopK consumer. This conservative logical-width bound needs no device-to-host read. A wide packed tensor can still use streaming Main even when its actual windows are short; omitting the low-level bound also retains Main. Explicit bounds must remain valid for every row across graph replays.
- For BF16 decode, narrow the ordered-key domain to 16 bits only in streaming Main's valid, fully staged degenerate-refinement branch (`degen A`). Histogram and emission use the high 16 bits of the existing ordered FP32 key. Other refinement paths and FP32 decode behavior retain the existing templates.

## Performance

Measured on NVIDIA B200 (SM100, 148 SMs), comparing the frozen parent commit above with PR head `7470e04631afb348324f072747a5032f5cfcb9e6`. Speedup is **reference GPU time / candidate GPU time**; floor is the minimum case speedup. Each case contributes equally to the geometric mean. GPU durations are taken from Nsight Systems traces, summing the kernels belonging to each public call; preparation, conversion, validation, and compilation are outside timing. All timing repetitions are retained, with no NCU durations, fastest-repetition selection, or A/A-based correction. The latest cold confirmation and the earlier cold/warm campaign below retain their own protocols and statistics.

### Decode: latest cold confirmation (2026-09-22)

Two complete rounds cover all **9,746 cases per dtype** (886 captured inputs × 11 batch sizes), using the hardware-event trace backend and 512 MiB cache eviction before each target. The 82 processes contain **623,744 timed calls and 155,936 full-output checks, all passing**. Each source contributes eight timed calls per case/dtype/round. The combined results pool all 16 calls per source, compute each case's ratio of arithmetic-mean GPU durations, and then take the geometric mean across cases. These are descriptive two-round results, without a per-case confidence or equivalence guarantee. This confirmation and the earlier full-grid campaign used different physical B200 GPUs and are not pooled.

| Scope | Reference / candidate | Geometric mean | Floor | Maximum |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Round 1 | Parent FP32 / this PR FP32 | 1.000004× | 0.940230× | 1.048128× |
| Round 1 | Parent BF16 / this PR BF16 | 1.000105× | 0.939920× | 1.056734× |
| Round 2 | Parent FP32 / this PR FP32 | 0.999688× | 0.949037× | 1.048848× |
| Round 2 | Parent BF16 / this PR BF16 | 0.999786× | 0.937831× | 1.069405× |
| Combined | Parent FP32 / this PR FP32 | **0.999847×** | **0.967177×** | **1.034364×** |
| Combined | Parent BF16 / this PR BF16 | **0.999947×** | **0.964407×** | **1.054613×** |

The combined FP32 floor is `v4_flash_8k_L06`, BS=4: **3.536 → 3.656 µs** (+120 ns). The BF16 floor is `v4_pro_8k_L32`, BS=1: **3.414 → 3.540 µs** (+126 ns). Both configurations remain below 1.0× in both rounds, even though some earlier worst cases reverse direction. The BF16 maximum is `v4_pro_1024k_L46`, BS=1024: **180.668250 → 171.312375 µs**.

Cold mechanism controls provide the following evidence:

- The exact same callable exhibits repeatable label/order differences even with fixed eviction RNG state. Three different kinds of single preceding kernel change this effect; a host-delay control does not have the same effect. Hardware-event and software tracing also change the effect's magnitude or direction. This establishes a contribution from execution/measurement conditions, without identifying a unique physical cause or demonstrating a profiler bug.
- A six-process comparison with equal GPU work balances observed launch-ordinal weights within each process. For BF16 Reg at `v4_flash_4k_L38`, BS=16, the control remains **0.993231×**, with all six process ratios below 1; the balanced condition is **0.996131×**. The paired effect is **1.002920×**, with descriptive 95% interval **[0.987983, 1.018083]**. It does not establish that balancing removes the residual. These selected-case intervals are exploratory, not multiple-comparison or equivalence guarantees.
- Fresh compilation of that BF16 Reg specialization yields identical **31,232-byte machine text**, **1,952 encoded SASS instructions including control words**, normalized PTX, launch constraints, and corresponding resources. Raw PTX/cubin containers differ by namespace. These are newly exported artifacts, not recovered cubins or code addresses from the timed processes; matching instructions do not prove identical physical execution time.

Exact-callable and mixed-source controls also have sub-1.0× floors. In the combined grid, exact-callable A/A uses eight calls per side; source and mixed-source comparisons use 16. Mixed-source controls have the same source composition on each side, rather than being the same callable. No control floor is used to correct a source-comparison floor or set an acceptance threshold. **The remaining floors are retained and are not fully explained; neither near-1.0× geometric means nor matching code establish zero decode regression for every case.**

### Decode: earlier complete-grid campaign (retained)

The earlier decode and prefill measurements below retain all 12 repetitions per case/arm/cache mode and use arithmetic-mean GPU kernel times. Cold runs use 512 MiB eviction; warm runs use a preparatory invocation of the same arm. The latest confirmation above adds no new warm measurements.

The 886 captured inputs are evaluated at all 11 batch sizes from 1 through 1024. Both dtype variants pass selected-value equivalence against `torch.topk` on their respective inputs, allowing interchangeable tied indices. BF16 input conversion is performed before timing. The complete grid contains 935,616 timed operator calls and 116,952 full output checks.

| Reference / candidate | Cache | Geometric mean | Floor | Maximum |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Parent BF16 / this PR BF16 | Cold | 0.999963× | 0.950050× | 1.053441× |
| Parent FP32 / this PR FP32 | Cold | 1.000154× | 0.960843× | 1.043657× |
| Parent FP32 / this PR BF16 | Cold | 1.269721× | 0.811228× | 2.876181× |
| Parent BF16 / this PR BF16 | Warm | 0.999970× | 0.982484× | 3.186501× * |
| Parent FP32 / this PR FP32 | Warm | 1.000520× | 0.973239× | 1.021867× |
| Parent FP32 / this PR BF16 | Warm | 1.241764× | 0.740861× | 4.024118× |

The same-dtype BF16 geometric means are approximately 1.0×, so this change does not establish an overall decode speedup. The FP32/BF16 cross-dtype rows include the BF16 behavior already provided by #19285 and are not the incremental gain of this PR. Their geometric means, 1.269721× cold and 1.241764× warm, remain below the original 2× FP32-to-BF16 target. Several case ratios remain below 1.0×.

* The raw BF16 warm maximum, 3.186501× at `v4_pro_512k_L52`, BS=1024, is dominated by one parent repetition at 2037.004 µs. The other 11 parent repetitions are 74.111–75.615 µs, and all 12 candidate repetitions are 73.983–75.487 µs. The long-tail cause is not established. This maximum is retained in the unfiltered table and is not evidence of a steady-state algorithmic gain.

All 50 FP32 decode compilation specializations covering this grid match the parent in actual machine-code `.text`, encoded SASS including control bits, PTX instructions, launch constraints, and resources; all 9,746 host dispatch/runtime-argument records also match. Raw PTX/cubin containers differ because the harness namespaces differ. Matching compiled code does not guarantee identical measured latency, as the FP32 floor values show.

### Prefill: fixed synthetic window panel

These are **FP32 synthetic prefill windows derived from a decode capture**, not real prefill captures or the 9,746 decode cases. The 24 predetermined trials cover rows 128–4096, window envelopes 2048/4096/8192, and K=512/1024/2048. Each comparison uses the same bound policy in both arms. All 1,152 timed outputs pass exactness checks. The four groups remain separate:

| Window/bound policy | Trials | Cache | Geometric mean | Floor | Maximum |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| All rows short; no bound | 4 | Cold | 3.082499× | 2.628435× | 3.588550× |
| All rows short; no bound | 4 | Warm | 3.834724× | 2.937063× | 5.046735× |
| 50% short rows; no bound | 6 | Cold | 1.528959× | 1.320341× | 1.865871× |
| 50% short rows; no bound | 6 | Warm | 1.622664× | 1.374516× | 2.026699× |
| 50% short rows; actual window bound | 6 | Cold | 2.132079× | 1.406228× | 2.867362× |
| 50% short rows; actual window bound | 6 | Warm | 2.477460× | 1.531659× | 3.063377× |
| 50% short rows; logical column bound | 8 | Cold | 1.786926× | 1.278316× | 2.338309× |
| 50% short rows; logical column bound | 8 | Warm | 1.963659× | 1.333141× | 2.482561× |

The no-bound groups remain on streaming Main; the actual-window-bound group exercises supported register windows. The logical-column-bound group models the consumer's bound policy and includes its fallback decisions, but it is measured through the isolated operator harness rather than an end-to-end serving workload. Its results do not imply that every packed prefill tensor selects Reg. Other GPU architectures and end-to-end model performance are unvalidated by this panel.

## Validation

- Latest cold decode study (2026-09-22): **122 accepted processes, 893,504 timed calls, 160,400 untimed primers, and 160,752 full-output checks, all checks passing**. This includes the two-round full grid above and separate RNG/order/backend, preceding-work, tail, and equal-work scheduling cohorts. Cohorts retain separate statistics; these totals are an execution inventory. The BF16 Reg compile-only comparison adds no performance samples.
- Final GVR test suite on B200: **183 passed, 1 skipped**; the skipped test specifically requires SM103. Includes prefill short/empty/offset/tied windows, warmup, graph replay, and existing decode controls.
- BF16 refinement: **30 directed fixtures pass exactness** on the final uninstrumented source. A separate diagnostic copy confirms changed-branch execution across **12 selected reader/geometry templates and 16 template/storage combinations**, covering index rereads, packed values, local staging, and split local/global staging. Observed paths are 25 degen-A fixtures, three existing dense whole-bin fixtures, and two incomplete-staging degen-B fixtures. This establishes the selected reader-path coverage, not exhaustive numerical or constexpr coverage.
- FP32 preservation: 50/50 actual compilation comparisons and complete 9,746-case dispatch coverage pass, including Main, Reg/RegImg, RegClus, and Clus.
- Consumer/CPU checks: 25 focused consumer tests and 332 composition/routing checks pass; applicable pre-commit checks pass for all five changed files.

GPU tests and benchmarks load the frozen host/device sources in an isolated harness. The full test-file run uses the final test file without harness-specific edits, with package bootstrap that bypasses repository conftest/plugins; it does not establish installed-package or full-model integration coverage. The diagnostic copy is used only to record BF16 branch execution, not to supply performance results.

**Controlled decode follow-up (2026-09-21):** Eighteen accepted B200 sessions cover the original 16 diagnostic cases, five additional cases selected from the actual BF16 Main-route tails, and a separate paired-only study of three case/dtype targets. They contain **93,312 timed operator calls and 4,860 full output checks**. Each cohort retains its own protocol and statistics. Two sessions with observed external GPU contexts were retained, excluded as whole sessions, and rerun with their original schedules; no individual timing was removed.

- **Local BF16 Main benefit:** At v4_pro_1024k_L46, BS=1024, parent/current is **1.053105× cold** (descriptive 95% session interval [1.051872, 1.054340]) and **1.058791× warm** ([1.057359, 1.060224]). The key16-only variant reproduces the gain, the prefill-only variant is approximately 1.0×, and both A/A controls are within the prespecified [0.99, 1.01] practical band on this configuration. This does not establish a grid-wide decode improvement.
- **Compiled-code attribution:** Twenty BF16 artifacts cover five configurations and four source variants. Prefill-only versus parent and full PR versus key16-only are executable-equivalent on all five configurations. The two Reg configurations and one Complement configuration match across all four variants; the two Main configurations change only across the key16 factor, with unchanged register/shared-memory resources and launch constraints. This is selected BF16 coverage, in addition to the 50-specialization FP32 preservation check above.
- **Timing differences are not all source effects:** The six-arm study still contains sub-1.0× ratios. On v4_flash_1024k_L30, BS=2, FP32 warm, parent/current is 0.984575× while parent/the exact same callable under another label is 0.984652×. A separate two-arm study rotates module/block order and reverses equal-length label-to-source assignments. Its average parent/current ratios are near 1.0× on all three targets, but the same-callable A/A control also reverses direction with session orientation. This supports a sequence/measurement-history contribution; the specific hardware or timing mechanism is unresolved.
- **No blanket equivalence claim:** The persistent FP32 target v4_flash_4k_L30, BS=16, has paired-only cold parent/current 1.003530× with interval [0.983849, 1.023605], so per-case 1% equivalence is not established there. Some warm intervals also remain outside the practical band. All repetitions and sub-1.0× results are retained; the intervals use six session blocks, not independent per-call samples, and are exploratory without a multiple-comparison guarantee.

The 2026-09-21 follow-up measurements used one B200 on a different node from the earlier full-grid campaign, with the same image and toolchain. Those selected-case diagnostics do not replace the complete-grid geometric means, floors, maxima, or the prefill table above, and do not establish zero regression for every configuration.

title: [None][fix] Keep drafting alive when dynamic draft length hits its floor
body:
## Description

One-engine speculative decoding carries cross-iteration drafter state: the draft KV cache, MTP's hidden-state and token pools, and the per-request context buffers DFlash keeps. All of it is only refreshed while the draft forward runs.

A `draft_len_schedule` resolves to `0` above its largest batch-size key, and `max_concurrency` is translated into exactly such a schedule, so at high concurrency every one-engine worker took its `skip_drafting` path. Positions kept being allocated for the drafter while nothing wrote them, and once the batch shrank and speculation resumed, the drafter attended to rows that were never initialized. Nothing failed loudly — the acceptance rate silently collapsed for the remainder of every affected request. This behavior was never documented.

This PR floors the draft lengths resolved from a schedule at `DecodingBaseConfig.min_runtime_draft_len` (1 for one-engine algorithms) so drafting keeps refreshing that state.

### Design notes

**The floor is applied where the draft length is read, not in the config.** Both read sites change together — `get_draft_len_for_batch_size` (runtime) and `_compute_dynamic_draft_len_mapping` (CUDA-graph capture) — because graphs are looked up by an exact `(batch_size, draft_len)` match, so a floor applied to only one of them would silently drop exactly the high-concurrency batches to eager execution. The user's `draft_len_schedule` is left exactly as written.

**`min_runtime_draft_len` is a two-valued property on the config.** It answers one question: the smallest draft length that keeps this algorithm's cross-iteration state coherent. It lives on the config rather than the worker because the graph mapping is computed before any worker exists.

**Explicit `0` values in a schedule are floored rather than rejected**, so existing configs keep loading. The new `min_draft_len` argument defaults to `0`, so the two-model drafter path — where an explicit `0` tier is a legitimate off-switch with its own per-request protection — is unchanged.

**`skip_drafting` and the per-worker `runtime_draft_len == 0` branches are kept.** They remain reachable through the acceptance-rate gate, which disables speculation permanently and never re-enables, so no state can go stale behind it.

**Vanilla MTP opts out of dynamic draft length entirely.** It builds one MTP module per draft token, each owning its own KV-cache layer, and only runs `mtp_layers[:runtime_draft_len]`, so *any* draft length below the module count strands the trailing modules — a floor of 1 cannot fix it. It now keeps its static draft length, with a warning at load time naming whichever knob was ignored (the module count is only known once the checkpoint has resolved).

**One rejection-sampling fix is included because the floor creates the exposure.** `write_padding_onehot_draft_probs` previously one-hot'd stale `draft_probs` rows only for gen requests entering with exactly zero draft tokens. With a floor those requests arrive holding a shorter draft instead of an empty one, so the stale suffix `[start, draft_len)` is one-hot'd instead of the whole row. This also covers upward transitions between two non-zero draft lengths, which were already uncovered.

### User-visible behavior change

`max_concurrency` now means "reduce speculation to the shortest sustainable draft length above this batch size" rather than "turn speculation off". `acceptance_rate_window_size` together with `acceptance_rate_threshold` remains the way to disable speculation for good. Nothing in-tree depends on the previous hard-off behavior for one-engine modes (no docs page, no config in `examples/configs/database/`, no deployment guide; the AUTO heuristic uses NGram, which is unaffected).

For reference, this is consistent with how other frameworks handle the same trade-off: vLLM V1's Dynamic SD and SGLang's adaptive speculative decoding both allow a draft length of 0 and both keep the drafter running at 0 to preserve its KV cache. vLLM V0, which skipped the drafter instead, had to disable speculation permanently per request as a result.

## Test Coverage

New, hardware-agnostic (`tests/unittest/_torch/speculative/hw_agnostic/test_min_runtime_draft_len.py`, in a directory already registered in `l0_h100.yml`):

- scheduled draft lengths are unchanged; the implicit tier above the largest key is floored
- an explicit `0` tier is floored without rewriting the caller's schedule
- the floor defaults to `0`, preserving the two-model path's semantics
- `min_runtime_draft_len` is 1 only for one-engine modes
- vanilla MTP opts out of dynamic draft length while MTP-Eagle and the other one-engine modes do not
- **the CUDA-graph mapping and the runtime resolution agree for every graph batch size across four schedule shapes, and no graph is captured with drafting disabled**

Updated: `test_dynamic_spec_decode.py` — the mocked resolver gains the new argument, and its draft-length cycle becomes `4-4-2-2-1-1-2-2` (the `2 -> 0 -> 2` phase becomes `2 -> 1 -> 2`, matching the new semantics).

Behavior shift to be aware of in existing integration tests: the dynamic-draft-length tests whose `max_batch_size` exceeds their largest schedule key (e.g. `{50: 4, 200: 3, 350: 2}` with `max_batch_size=500`) now run at draft length 1 instead of 0 in that band. They assert accuracy, which is invariant to acceptance-rate changes, so they should be unaffected.

## Open items before this leaves draft

- [ ] Full unit/integration run. The change was verified by proving the two resolution sites agree across schedule shapes, but the suite has not been executed against a build of this branch.
- [ ] Measure throughput at a batch just above the cutoff (floor 0 vs 1). This is the main cost of the PR and is currently modeled, not measured.
- [ ] Confirm the DeepSeek-V3-Lite checkpoint reports `num_nextn_predict_layers == 1`. If it is greater, the vanilla-MTP opt-out silently disables the schedule in `test_mtp_dynamic_draft_len`, `test_mtp_sa_dynamic_draft_len` and `test_mtp_eagle_dynamic_draft_len` — they would still pass, since they assert accuracy only.
- [ ] An acceptance-rate/length regression test across a `K -> floor -> K` transition with a mid-run prefill. No existing test can observe this bug class: the dynamic-draft-length tests do reach the implicit tier but assert accuracy, which speculation preserves by construction.

## Deliberately out of scope

Each of these is pre-existing and unrelated to the floor:

- DSpark combined with the acceptance-rate gate: DSpark has no `runtime_draft_len == 0` path and uses a static `max_draft_len`, but the gate zeroes `runtime_draft_len` without checking `support_dynamic_draft_len()`.
- Attention-DP: `runtime_draft_len` is resolved from the rank-local batch size with no cross-rank consensus, so ranks can run different numbers of draft forwards.
- The one-model (`bisect_left`, implicit tier above the largest key) and two-model (`bisect_right`, clamped) lookups interpret the same `draft_len_schedule` differently.

## Follow-up

Keep-warm — running the drafter during the off band so speculation can be switched fully off again — is the natural sequel, per algorithm. Recommended order on measured cost: MTP (N=1) first, then DFlash, then Eagle3 bundled with a KV-only draft-KV write, since a full-forward warm on a multi-head-attention draft head reads a large fraction of the target's KV traffic at long context.

## PR Checklist

- [x] PR description clearly explains what and why.
- [x] PR follows [TRT-LLM CODING GUIDELINES](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of my knowledge.
- [x] Test cases are provided for new code paths.
- [ ] API label: the `max_concurrency` / `draft_len_schedule` semantic change above needs a maintainer call on `api-compatible` vs `api-breaking`. No field is added, removed or retyped, so `api_stability` references and the `llm_args` golden manifest are unaffected, but the meaning of an accepted value changes.
- [x] No new dependencies.
- [x] No ownership changes.
- [x] Field descriptions updated; no separate docs page describes this behavior.

title: [#17908][fix] Make BlockRadixTree.clear() terminate on a childless RootBlock
body:
# [#17908][fix] Make `BlockRadixTree.clear()` terminate on a childless `RootBlock`

> Closes https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/issues/17908

## Background

`BlockRadixTree.clear()` (in `tensorrt_llm/runtime/kv_cache_manager_v2/_block_radix_tree.py`)
shrinks `self.next` **only as a side effect** of the inner loop: `detach_next()` prunes a
`RootBlock` when its *last child* is detached. A `RootBlock` that is already childless has
no child to detach, so the outer `while self.next:` loop re-selects the same root forever
and `clear()` never returns. The trailing `assert not self.next` is unreachable in that state.

A childless root is not exotic: `RootBlock.__init__` ends with `prev.next[self.key] = self`,
so `add_or_get_existing()` publishes an empty root **by construction** before its caller
attaches a block; any interruption between those two steps leaves the tree permanently
unclearable. The only production caller is `KVCacheManager.shutdown()`, which therefore
hangs whenever the tree holds a childless root.

```python
tree = BlockRadixTree(object(), 32)
tree.add_or_get_existing(ReuseScope(lora_id=0, salt=None))
tree.clear()   # never returns (pins one core at 100%, no GPU activity)
```

## Summary

Root-edge bookkeeping is centralised into a single new helper,
`detach_root_block(root)`, that removes a `RootBlock` from its tree's top-level `next`
registry:

- `detach_next()` now calls it when the last child of a `RootBlock` is detached
  (eager prune path — unchanged behaviour, same bookkeeping).
- `clear()` now calls it directly for a root that never gained a child, so **every**
  iteration of the loop makes explicit progress (detach a childless root, or remove one
  subtree) and the loop provably terminates.

Changes:

- `tensorrt_llm/runtime/kv_cache_manager_v2/_block_radix_tree.py`
  - add `detach_root_block()`;
  - route `detach_next()`'s root pruning through it;
  - make `BlockRadixTree.clear()` detach childless roots explicitly.
- `tests/unittest/kv_cache_manager_v2_tests/test_block_radix_tree.py` (new)
  - 6 CPU-only regression tests (`pytest.mark.cpu_only`): empty tree, childless-root
    regression, single chain removal (incl. orphan checks), mixed childless + populated
    roots, multi-branch subtrees, idempotence and post-clear reuse of the same reuse scope.

## Impacts

- `clear()` terminates for every reachable tree state; `KVCacheManager.shutdown()` can no
  longer hang behind a childless root.
- Removal order for populated trees is unchanged (still post-order, leaves first, via the
  existing `remove_subtree` path), so page-cleanup semantics of `Block.__del__` and
  event-manager notifications are untouched.
- No API change; internal only. The fix is pure Python and was validated with CPU-only
  tests in the `kv_cache_manager_v2` fast mode
  (`TLLM_KV_CACHE_MANAGER_V2_BACKEND=python`).

## Verification

Reproduced the hang on `main` (`777a2c7`) with the snippet above (process does not return;
killed by `timeout`). After the fix the snippet returns immediately and the new test file
passes; pre-fix, the same tests hang at the first childless-root case.

```bash
# fast mode (see kv_cache_manager_v2/AGENTS.md)
PYTHONPATH="$REPO_ROOT/tensorrt_llm/runtime/" \
  python "$REPO_ROOT/tests/unittest/kv_cache_manager_v2_tests/test_block_radix_tree.py" -v
```

Existing related tests still pass: `test_kv_cache_salting.py` (3 tests).


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Dev Engineer Review

- `BlockRadixTree.clear()` now removes childless roots and always makes progress.
- `detach_root_block()` centralizes root cleanup for explicit clearing and eager pruning.
- The change preserves populated-tree removal order and does not change public APIs.

## QA Engineer Review

- Modified `tests/unittest/kv_cache_manager_v2_tests/test_block_radix_tree.py`.
- Added six CPU-only tests for empty, childless, populated, mixed, branched, idempotent, and reusable tree states.
- The tests verify root removal, orphaned blocks, termination, and reuse after clearing.
- The suite is listed in `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_cpu.yml` and other applicable test lists.
- Coverage verdict: **sufficient**.

## Per-File QA Perspective
