title: [None][feat] Add request lifecycle events to the disagg KV transfer perf log
body:
## Why

Disaggregated requests today are observable only in pieces: `PerfTimer` CSV rows cover the ctx worker pipeline, `RequestPerfMetrics.kv_cache_transfer_start/end` cover the gen receive window, `DisServingRequestStats` and Prometheus expose per-iteration aggregates, and `get_status_dump` gives a hang-time snapshot. None of them answers "where did request N wait between GEN ingress and decode readiness, and which gate held it": scheduler KV admission, the transfer-window budget, KV rollback, timeout start/observe, cancellation and session settlement are not recorded anywhere.

#18913 proposed a parallel diagnostics stack (new sink, new env vars, ~30 nested emit blocks, a 1.4k-line analyzer) for this. Roughly a third of its events duplicate `PerfTimer` and the request metrics, and the instrumentation cost in `transfer.py` is significant. This PR takes the minimal route instead: add only the missing boundaries, on top of the logging infrastructure that already exists.

## What

- `PerfLogManager.event(name, request, **fields)`: one JSONL line per lifecycle boundary, written to `{TRTLLM_KVCACHE_TIME_OUTPUT_PATH}/lifecycle_rank{rank}_pid{pid}.jsonl`. Same directory and same gate as the existing CSVs; no new environment variable. Timestamps use the rank-aligned steady clock that `kv_cache_transfer_start/end` already use, so the events line up with the request metrics and `PerfTimer` rows without a second clock domain. Disabled path is one attribute check per call site; `event()` swallows its own errors.
- Eleven single-line call sites for the boundaries nothing else covers: `gen_ingress`, `gen_kv_admission` (scheduler V2 `prepare_disagg_gen_init`), `gen_transfer_window` (admitted/deferred with active and budget blocks), `gen_kv_rollback`, `ctx_send_ready`, `timeout_started` / `timeout_observed` (both sides), `cancel_requested`, `settled` (ctx and gen; completed/failed/cancelled), `ctx_kv_released`, `gen_decode_ready`. The event list is documented in `LIFECYCLE_EVENTS` in `perf_logger.py`.
- `scripts/disagg_lifecycle_timeline.py`: joins the JSONL files by disaggregated request id, prints each request's ordered timeline with gaps, and a p50/p90/max table of every observed transition. Cross-process gaps are flagged.
- `tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_disagg_lifecycle_events.py` (CPU-only): disabled path writes nothing, record shape and identity, error isolation, unchanged CSV gating, and the timeline script end to end.

`transfer.py` and `PerfTimer` are untouched; `ctx_transfer_queued`/`worker_dequeued`/`backend_*` from #18913 are already available as `queue_latency_ms` / `transfer_latency_ms` in the existing CSV.

## Behavior change

None for existing users. `TRTLLM_KVCACHE_TIME_OUTPUT_PATH` keeps producing the same `{instance}_{rank}.csv` and `*_gen_transfer_summary.csv`; the directory additionally gains one `lifecycle_*.jsonl` per process.

## Test

- `tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_disagg_lifecycle_events.py`: 8 passed (chuangz-desktop dev container, installed package overlay).
- `pre-commit run --files <changed>`: all hooks pass.
- Not yet exercised end to end on a multi-GPU disagg run; CI pending.

## Relationship to #18913

Alternative, smaller implementation of the executor-level part of #18913, reusing `PerfLogManager` instead of a new diagnostics module. Happy to fold in additional boundaries from that PR as single `event()` calls if they turn out to be needed.

body:

Valid ticket formats:
  - JIRA ticket: [TRTLLM-1234] or [FOOBAR-123] for other FOOBAR project

NOTE: "@coderabbitai title" will be replaced by the title generated by CodeRabbit AI, that includes the "[type]" and title.
For more info, see /.coderabbit.yaml.

-->

## Description

Switches the C++ build from C++17 to C++20 repo-wide. The forcing function is torch 2.14 on public PyPI: its `ATen/ATen.h` has a hard `#error C++20 or later`. The NGC container's `2.14.0a0` branched earlier and does not carry that `#error`, so this is groundwork rather than a fix for something broken today.

Beyond flipping the standard, four things needed adapting:

- **xgrammar** (`3rdparty/patches/xgrammar_cxx20.patch`) — `structural_tag.h` builds a recursive `std::variant` whose `SequenceFormat` / `OrFormat` constructors are defined in-class, instantiating `std::vector<Format>` while later alternatives are still incomplete. Always UB; C++17 tolerated it, clang under C++20 does not. Moved out of line, matching what upstream xgrammar already does.
- **`std::tuple` CTAD in nvcc-compiled sources** — with a clang host under C++20, EDG cannot disambiguate any `std::tuple` CTAD (verified in isolation: clang/C++17 ok, clang/C++20 fails, gcc/C++20 ok). Replaced with `std::make_tuple` in `Poly.h` and `mixtureOfExpertsTest.cu`.
- **`CXX_SCAN_FOR_MODULES OFF`** globally — CMake started emitting C++20 module dependency scans the build images have no `clang-scan-deps` for.
- **fmha_v2 anonymous enums → `static constexpr int`** — arithmetic between anonymous enums is deprecated in C++20 (P1120), which this PR turns into 12572 warnings. Patch by @yihwang-nv; folded in here rather than deferred because the warnings are introduced by this change.

Also removes the leftover C++17 pins across the repo, so outside `3rdparty/` there are now none.

### Note for reviewers

This **overrides #19065** (@100milliongold): `IsSimpleAlphaBeta` in `moe_gemm_tma_ws_launcher.inl` keeps the double-`is_constructible_v` form agreed in this PR's review over the `!is_aggregate_v` guard that landed on main. `is_constructible_v` alone does not account for P0960 parenthesised aggregate initialisation; the two-constructor check describes that branch directly instead of relying on aggregate-ness as a proxy.

The last commit, `[None][chore] Temporarily honor --post-merge in the multi-GPU gating`, is **temporary and must be dropped before merge**.

## Test Coverage

No new tests: this is a build-standard change with no runtime behaviour change.

- CI pipeline #61229 on `c877b86`: `Build-x86_64`, `Build-SBSA` and both single-GPU test jobs all passed. Remaining failures were a PLC agent connectivity abort and the multi-GPU approval-label gate, neither related to this PR.
- Full clang wheel build reproduced on a cluster node (6998 targets), with each failure attributed by a compiler × standard matrix; the only C++20-introduced one is fixed here, the rest are pre-existing clang-only issues.
- xgrammar and 3rdparty patch-command fixes verified directly against GNU patch across pristine / fully-patched / partially-patched / conflicting source trees.

Not covered: runtime behaviour, `MULTI_DEVICE=0`, and the `xqa` / `train_ops` CUDA standard changes (those targets are not reachable from the default build).

title: [https://nvbugs/6705034][fix] Route zero-token causal-conv input to the channel-major kernel
body:
## Description

A zero-token `x` reaches `causal_conv1d_fwd` with the strides its no-op transpose left behind (an empty tensor is always reported contiguous, so the caller's `.contiguous()` does not restride it). The stride-based layout classification therefore saw it as channel-last, and because 0-byte CUDA allocations can alias each other, the channel-last in-place guard rejected the call with:

```
RuntimeError: causal_conv1d_fwd: the channel-last path cannot run in-place; `out` must not overlap x
```

This broke `unittest/_torch/modules/kimi_kda/test_kda_prefill_op.py::test_kda_mixer_empty_prefill` on DGX_B200 (https://nvbugs/6705034), waived in #18549.

The channel-last kernel also cannot run an empty input anyway (zero token chunks would give an empty launch grid), so this change routes `seqlen == 0` to the channel-major kernel, which handles empty input (conv-state write-back only) the way it always has before the channel-last path was introduced in #18081.

## Test Coverage

- Unwaives `unittest/_torch/modules/kimi_kda/test_kda_prefill_op.py::test_kda_mixer_empty_prefill` (DGX_B200), which exercises exactly this zero-token path.

The C++ side is untouched. All changes are in the CuTe DSL kernels, the custom op layer, the CuTe DSL MoE module, the locality-domain policy, tests and the MoE developer guide (11 files, +2386 / -119).

## Commits

1. **Port the decode optimizations**: sparse gather for small token counts, cached FC2 weight loads, and a fused workspace reset kernel with programmatic dependent launch.
2. **Stream weights as a fused FC12 tactic**: L2 evict-first weight loads become an autotuner tactic alongside the tile size, and the decode token buckets are always profiled (`tune_max_num_tokens` anchors the buckets to the module's saturation token count).
3. **Fold the dense output memset into the workspace reset**, removing a launch; regression tests.
4. **Scale the sparse-gather selection by the rank's expert share**, so TEP and DEP layouts estimate local routes correctly.
5. **Run the MXFP8 fused FC12 MoE across two locality domains where it wins**: a separate autotuned op that runs the kernel on two compute partitions, each holding half of every expert's inner channels; used per token count only when the autotuner finds it at least 1% faster. Off by default (`enable_locality_domains`).
6. **Widen the locality-domain admission rule** to the measured neutral point (2048 rows / ~4096 estimated local routes).
7. **Fuse the MXFP8 input quantization into the workspace reset**: BF16 activations are quantized to E4M3 + UE8M0 inside the reset launch when the full-GPU op runs, bit-exact with `mxfp8_quantize`.
8. **[test] Drive the CuTe DSL locality-domain module tests through `run_moe`**: `test_moe_module_locality_domain_correctness_rubin` and the BF16 lifecycle test on this branch call `forward_chunk`, which no MoE impl defines here, so they raised `AttributeError` before this PR. They now apply routing, quantize on the no-communication path and call `run_moe` with the no-comm plan, mirroring `run_backend_moe`. Independent of the port; drop if preferred.

9. **[chore] Apply pre-commit formatting** to the ported files (isort/yapf/ruff output; `l` parameter of `_is_tactic_feasible` renamed to `num_groups`).
10. **Run one parent reset for both MXFP8 locality-domain shards**: the split op now launches one reset on the caller's stream before the fork that clears both partitions' workspaces, clears the output (`zero_output`) and quantizes raw input once; the shards launch GEMM-only (`skip_reset`), the concurrent tuning runner gains a `prologue_fn`, and the module hands raw activations to the split like to the full-GPU op. Same-wheel module-level A/B, worst rank, us (off = locality disabled / on = enabled): TEP8 tok 8/16/32/64/128/256: 22.2/28.7/34.2/45.9/58.2/66.4 -> 20.7/25.7/28.7/37.7/49.7/55.4; DEP4 tok/rank 8/16/32: 52.1/74.5/100.6 -> 43.5/60.3/81.1; DEP16 tok/rank 4/16/32: 26.0/37.8/43.0 -> 24.4/34.7/40.2; 1-4 tokens within noise.

## Adaptations from the tekit MR

- Module layout: `_torch/moe/fused_moe/` and `tests/unittest/_torch/moe/`.
- Gating uses `IS_CUTLASS_DSL_RUBIN_AVAILABLE` (no internal-build flag on this branch).
- The SwiGLU clamp comes from `_mxfp8_fused_fc12_swiglu_limit()`.
- `CuteDslFusedMoE` derives from `MoEImplBase` here, so `tune_max_num_tokens` is computed in its constructor the same way `CutlassFusedMoE` does.

## Verification (Rubin SM107, wheel built from this branch)

- `test_fc12_input_quant.py`: 39 passed (quantize-in-reset bit-exact vs `mxfp8_quantize`).
- `test_moe_backend.py -k cutedsl_mxfp8_fused_fc12`: 3 passed. Fused vs fp32 oracle 2.65-2.68% RMS, reference MXFP8 module vs oracle 2.67-2.71%, fused vs reference 1.72-1.79%, cosine >= 0.9996 (the fused kernel adds no error beyond the reference's requantization floor).
- `test_locality_domain_planner.py`: 55 passed, 7 skipped.
- `test_cute_dsl_moe.py -k "fused_fc12 or input_quant or locality"`: 64 passed, 2 failed. The two failures are `test_moe_module_locality_domain_correctness_rubin` NVFP4 cases and are pre-existing on `feat/rl_rc`: `run_moe_nvfp4` passes `expert_counts` / `expert_capacity` to `cute_dsl_nvfp4_grouped_gemm_finalize_inplace_rubin`, whose registered schema has no such arguments. Not touched by this PR.

## Performance (same wheel, `feat/rl_rc` python vs this branch, Rubin, HBM 4752 MHz)

Module-level `quantize_input` + `run_moe` per call, CUDA-graph replays, 4 module copies rotated so weights are cold in L2, Qwen3.5-397B geometry (512 experts, top-k 10, hidden 4096, intermediate 1024), power-law routing (alpha 0.8), worst rank per token count. Microseconds.

| layout | tokens/rank | base | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TEP8 (64 local experts) | 1 | 19.96 | 14.88 | -25% |
| | 4 | 23.24 | 17.99 | -23% |
| | 16 | 32.22 | 28.72 | -11% |
| | 64 | 53.47 | 45.85 | -14% |
| | 256 | 73.63 | 66.44 | -10% |
| DEP4 (128 local experts) | 1 | 26.44 | 21.22 | -20% |
| | 8 | 58.04 | 52.12 | -10% |
| | 32 | 107.57 | 100.60 | -6% |
| DEP16 (32 local experts) | 1 | 23.94 | 18.07 | -25% |
| | 8 | 40.01 | 31.92 | -20% |
| | 32 | 51.14 | 43.01 | -16% |

Every measured row is faster; the saving is 4-8 us per call (fewer launches and no separate memset / quantization), 20-27% at 1-4 tokens and ~10% at 128-256 tokens. With the parent reset (commit 10) enabling locality domains adds a further 10-19% from 8 tokens/rank up on all three layouts and is within noise at 1-4 tokens (the selector keeps the full-GPU op there); before that commit the split's extra launches made the flag neutral.

## Test coverage

- New: `tests/unittest/_torch/thop/parallel/test_fc12_input_quant.py`.
- Extended: `test_cute_dsl_moe.py` (fused FC12 op, reset/memset fold, sparse-gather rule, locality-domain split and admission, input-quant fusion rules), `test_moe_backend.py` (fused FC12 accuracy A/B incl. 16-token bf16-input case), `test_locality_domain_planner.py`.

title: [None][fix] Restore tensor sharing strategy on errors
body:
## Description

`SharedTensorContainer.dump_to_dict()` temporarily switches PyTorch's process-wide sharing strategy to `file_system`. If CPU storage serialization raises, the previous strategy was not restored, leaving later IPC operations with mutated global state. Concurrent callers could also observe or overwrite that process-wide state.

Restore the original strategy in a `finally` block, serialize the switch/reduce/restore window with a module-level lock, and cover both failure recovery and concurrent callers with regression tests.

## Test Coverage

- Exact current `main` Linux probe reproduces the leak: `file_descriptor` becomes `file_system`.
- The failure-path test asserts serialization runs under `file_system` before the injected error, then confirms restoration to `file_descriptor`.
- The concurrency test blocks the first reducer with an event and verifies that a second reducer cannot enter until the first call releases the strategy lock; the equivalent direct-source Linux probe passes.
- `isort`, `remove-crlf`, `yapf`, `codespell`, `ruff-legacy`, and `git diff --check` pass on the changed files.

title: [TRTLLM-16416][test] Add machine profile catalogue for QA test selection
body:
The QA LLM functional cluster pipeline hands the same flat test list to every architecture it allocates. A test that cannot run on the allocated machine is still dispatched to it, occupies the allocation, and only then skips, because pytest evaluates skipif conditions at run time on the node. The cost is queue time.

Deciding feasibility before Slurm allocates needs a description of the machine that is about to be allocated. No such description exists: every hardware fact in the repo comes from a run-time probe, and there is not even a GPU-name-to-SM table.

Add tests/qa_selection/, the data layer for that decision:

- MachineProfile, a frozen dataclass carrying only the facts the suite's skip decorators consult -- sm, device_name, device_memory_mib, gpu_count, max_gpu_per_node, cpu_arch, mpi_world_size. gpu_count is allocation state, so with_gpu_count() returns a sized copy rather than mutating the entry.
- MachineCatalog, a read-only Mapping that validates on load: unknown keys, missing keys, wrong types and non-positive numerics are all rejected, naming the offending profile and field. An unknown machine name raises, listing the known names, so a machine we cannot describe fails loudly instead of selecting wrongly.
- profiles.json, covering H100, B200, B300, GB200, GB300 and VR200. Values are read from the in-production catalogue in trt_jenkins (src/com/nvidia/dlswqa/LLMCluster.groovy, MAKO_PROFILES and CLUSTER_CONFIGS) rather than hand-entered, and are maintained by hand from there.

Memory fields are named *_mib because the unit is the failure mode: the value is what nvidia-smi reports, which is framebuffer minus ECC and carveout, and is always under the marketed board capacity. Every value was bounded against vendor capacity as an upper bound, never an equality.

nvlink and nvls are deliberately absent. Neither decides anything in this scope, and neither is a property of a machine type -- NVLS is a capability check across every visible device, and NVLink activity depends on how many GPUs the job received, so a profile keyed by machine name cannot express either correctly.

Placed at tests/qa_selection/ rather than under tests/integration/defs/: defs/__init__.py imports torch, so importing anything beneath it costs 1321 modules and ~1.9s, while this package imports in 0.01s with only the standard library. That matters because the plugin in a later commit is loaded via -p, which imports the package before any conftest. This mirrors tests/test_common/, whose __init__.py is empty for the same reason.

No behaviour change: nothing imports this package yet, no collection changes, no CLI options added.

title: [None][feat] Python-controlled NIXL bounce transfer (bounce v2)
body:
## Description

A Python/C++ hybrid re-partition of the NIXL bounce-buffer KV-cache transfer for disaggregated serving: the control plane (credit scheduling, chunk planning, wire protocol, request lifecycle) lives in Python where it can iterate quickly, while a minimal C++ mechanism layer keeps every per-tick/per-chunk-critical operation (batched gather/scatter kernel, CUDA-event and NIXL-status polling, RDMA posting, fabric-VMM arena) off the GIL. Opt-in via `TRTLLM_BOUNCE_V2_ENABLE`; the default path is untouched.

### Architecture

- **Pure-logic core** (`tensorrt_llm/_torch/disaggregation/bounce_v2/`): buddy allocator, credit scheduler (round-robin fairness, drain anti-starvation, eager budget, lease+quarantine), numpy chunk planner (32B-aligned packing, scatter-run coalescing), binary wire codec v3 (C++-compatible 44-byte header, batched ACK). Standalone-importable, stdlib+numpy only.
- **C++ mechanism layer** (`cpp/.../nixl_utils/bounce_v2/`): batched copy kernel, fabric arena, a ~50µs CompletionPoller whose `drain()` hands Python all terminal completions as one array per GIL acquisition, and a BatchedCopyPool doing run-splitting and plan staging in C++. `NixlTransferAgent` gains below-the-splitter primitives (`postXferRequest`/`registerRegionImpl`) with locked wrappers for the Python-bound surface.
- **Python transport** (`reactor.py`/`engine.py`): one reactor thread runs sender and receiver roles over pyzmq with ~1ms batch ticks; eager gather overlaps the WANT→GRANT round trip; WANT chunk sizes are hard-validated before entering the scheduler; every failure path resolves `wait()` with a reason string; a watchdog covers reactor death.
- **Integration**: sender-side branch in the native Python transceiver; handshakes ride the existing rank-info exchange via a new optional field (omitted when unset, so older peers keep decoding).

### Test coverage (all green on RTX A6000 over real NIXL/UCX)

- 130 CPU-only pure-logic tests (ported from the C++ bounce suites, incl. region-conservation invariants and golden wire bytes)
- 19 GPU mechanism-binding tests (roundtrips, BUSY backpressure, poller shutdown with in-flight work)
- 35 GPU transport/integration tests (WANT-validation DoS resistance, multi-chunk streaming with region recycling, peer re-registration, concurrent + bidirectional transfers, failure-reason assertions)
- Single-process cache-transceiver e2e through the production `TransferWorker` wiring for both transceiver protocols, plus a disabled-default case
- Existing transceiver regression subset unaffected with the feature disabled

### Notes for reviewers

- Design doc (EN/ZH) available; the partition criterion is invocation frequency: per-request logic in Python, per-chunk/per-tick in C++.
- Follow-ups tracked outside this PR: GB200 GIL-probe gate and ≥50GB/s perf validation (`bounce_v2/probe.py` ships here), config migration from the env gate to `CacheTransceiverConfig`, v1 `native/bounce` deprecation.

title: [None][test] Disable ctx overlap scheduler for deepseek-v4-pro con8 disagg config
body:
## Description

Sets `worker_config.ctx.disable_overlap_scheduler: true` for
`gb300_deepseek-v4-pro-fp4_8k1k_con8_ctx1_dep4_gen4_tep8_eplb0_mtp3_ccb-NIXL`.

#18346 removed the unconditional `ctx_config["disable_overlap_scheduler"] = True` from
the `ctx_only` path on the rationale that "the overlap scheduler works fine for a
context-only run". That holds at high concurrency, but not for this config. Measured on
oci-aga GB300, 3 arms x 2 reps, base `21dc97fbc8` (pre-#18457) with #18457 applied as the
third arm:

| ctx `disable_overlap_scheduler` | #18457 | iterations | req/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| `true` (this PR) | – | 22 | **7.82 / 7.75** |
| `false` (today, pre-#18457) | – | 34 | 6.00 / 5.99 |
| `false` (today, main) | applied | 33 | 6.20 / 6.25 |

**+25% over current main** for the `ctx_only` case. #18457 is merged and active in the
`false` arm above (verified: KVCM V2 gate passes, `IndexMapper capacity` 3 -> 5), so this
is not something the merged fix already covers.

### Why the overlap scheduler cannot win here

perf-sanity drives `--max-concurrency 8` at `request_rate=inf`, i.e. a closed loop:
nothing arrives except as an echo of a completion. With per-iteration/per-rank counters
added to `py_executor.py` (forwarded, router in/assigned/scheduled, plus each rank's
pre-router active-list size and how many of those are `GENERATION_TO_COMPLETE`), the
steady state is:

- `A(N) = F(N)` — no real backlog; everything resident is a retiring request
- `R(N) = F(N-1)` — deferred teardown: the request is still `GENERATION_TO_COMPLETE` at
  `N+1` and only retires there, so its response leaves one iteration late
- `A(N) = R(N-2)` — permit release, new POST, next fetch

so `F(N) = F(N-3)`: a 3-iteration permit round-trip, against 2 with overlap disabled
(confirmed by E2E latency in iteration units, 2.00 vs 2.78). Sustained cadence is then
fixed by Little's Law on the fetch grid:

```
in-flight = cadence x period
    8     =  4.00   x   2     overlap off   (measured 4.000)
    8     =  2.67   x   3     overlap on    (measured 2.696 / 2.727)
   12     =  4.00   x   3     what overlap-on would need to match
```

7456-token prompts against `max_num_tokens: 8192` allow 1 ctx request per rank per
iteration, so the cap is 4/iteration at `dep4`; both overlap-on arms average 2.67 of 4,
i.e. the scheduler is never the binding constraint — concurrency is. Matching
overlap-off at `dep4` would need 12 concurrent requests and the config specifies 8. No
scheduler or balancing change closes that; #18457 removes the phantom admission charge
(measured: summed charge 86 -> 3, exactly the overlap-off value) but not the extra
iteration of residency, which is why it buys 1 iteration of 34.

### Scope

This config generates four CI tests, and the ctx worker's config is shared by all of
them, so all four baselines shift once after merge:

| test | measured here |
|---|---|
| `aggr_upload-ctx_only-...` | yes, +25% |
| `disagg_upload-e2e-...` | no |
| `disagg_upload-gen_only-...` | no |
| `disagg_upload-e2e-time_breakdown-...` | no |

Only `ctx_only` was measured. The three disagg modes are expected to be neutral-to-better
(the same deferred-teardown residency applies to their ctx worker) but that is a
prediction, not a measurement — happy to measure them before merge if reviewers prefer.

A per-config yaml value is used rather than restoring the `ctx_only` override because the
override would re-disable overlap for all 24 `ctx_only` configs including the
high-concurrency ones, where overlap plus #18457 beats overlap-off by ~2%. Six
`gb300_nemotron-ultra-v3-fp4_*` configs already set ctx `disable_overlap_scheduler: true`,
so this needs no new grammar.

### Follow-ups, not addressed here

- The threshold is `concurrency < 3 x ctx_dp`, so five other `ctx_only` configs are
  predicted affected — the three `con1` cases most strongly (a 3/2 period ratio on a
  single-user latency measurement). They are left alone pending measurement.
- The underlying product issue stays open on nvbug 6778910. The lever is residency, not
  accounting: emitting the response before the following `_fetch_new_requests` would make
  `R(N) = F(N)` and drop the period to 2. Overlap-on iterations are already cheaper than
  overlap-off (457 vs 502 ms), so fixing residency should land this config ~10% *above*
  the overlap-off number this PR restores, rather than merely matching it.

## Test Coverage

Config-only change; no product code touched. The emitted value was verified through the
`ctx_only` build path, which copies `worker_config.ctx` wholesale
(`ctx_config = dict(worker_config.get("ctx", {}))`, `test_perf_sanity.py:3511`) into
`ServerConfig.disable_overlap_scheduler` (`:1530`) and reports it to the perf DB as
`b_disable_overlap_scheduler` (`:1690`), so the shift is attributable in the baseline
history:

```
ctx.disable_overlap_scheduler = True    # this PR
gen.disable_overlap_scheduler = False   # unchanged
```

The `gen:` block of this yaml carries its own `disable_overlap_scheduler` at line 76 and
is deliberately left at `false`; only the `ctx:` occurrence at line 106 is changed.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Single-line config change, verified to land in the `ctx:` block only
- [x] Measured, 2 reps per arm, counters bit-identical across reps
- [x] Perf baselines for the four affected tests to be refreshed after merge

title: [None][fix] Pass NVML CC settings by reference in release/1.2.1
body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

`confidential_compute_enabled()` in `tensorrt_llm/_utils.py` calls `pynvml.nvmlSystemGetConfComputeSettings(cc_settings)`, passing the `c_nvmlSystemConfComputeSettings_v1_t` struct by value. The underlying NVML C API declares this function as taking a pointer (`nvmlSystemGetConfComputeSettings(nvmlSystemConfComputeSettings_v1_t *)`), so the pointer/by-value mismatch can crash the worker during initialization on Hopper-and-newer GPUs, before the HTTP server becomes ready.

The equivalent call was already corrected on `main` via https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/16850 (`byref(cc_settings)`), but that PR also did a larger, unrelated refactor (new cached `get_cc_and_nvle_status()`, split CC/NVLE booleans). This change backports only the pointer fix to `release/1.2.1`, leaving this branch's existing `confidential_compute_enabled()` function and its CC/NVLE classification logic (the three-way `or` across `ccFeature`/`multiGpuMode`) untouched.

## Approach

- Add `from ctypes import byref` and wrap the settings struct in `byref(cc_settings)` when calling `pynvml.nvmlSystemGetConfComputeSettings`, matching the fix already on `main`.
- Add regression tests (`tests/unittest/utils/test_confidential_compute.py`) covering all branches of the CC/NVLE classification (`ccFeature` enabled, `PROTECTED_PCIE`, `NVLE`, and combined), and register the file in `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_a10.yml` under the existing "CPU-only test, no dedicated job" precedent comment (this branch predates the `l0_cpu.yml`/`cpu_only` marker convention introduced by #16850 on `main`).

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/utils/test_confidential_compute.py` — 4 new parametrized cases.

**Validation performed:** This sandbox is macOS/arm64 with no GPU, no Docker, and no `torch`/`tensorrt`/`mpi4py` available (the `tensorrt` package has no macOS wheel, so the full `tensorrt_llm` package cannot be imported here). To still exercise the real patched source, the third-party/heavy imports unrelated to this fix (`torch`, `tensorrt`, `nvtx`, `mpi4py`, `tensorrt_llm.bindings`, `tensorrt_llm.logger`) were stubbed in `sys.modules`, and `tensorrt_llm/_utils.py` was loaded from disk via `importlib` so the actual patched line executes. Ran:

```
python3 -m pytest --noconftest tests/unittest/utils/test_confidential_compute.py
```

All 4 cases pass against the fixed code. Reverting only the `byref` change (via `git stash` on `tensorrt_llm/_utils.py`) and re-running the identical command makes all 4 cases fail (the swallowed `AttributeError` from passing the struct by value causes `confidential_compute_enabled()` to silently return `False`), confirming the test reproduces the reported defect. Restored the fix afterward. Also ran `pre-commit run` on all changed/new files (isort, yapf, ruff, ruff-format, codespell, autoflake) — all passed.

**Not run:** this repo's own CI, which is triggered via a `/bot run` PR comment on NVIDIA's internal Blossom CI and isn't reachable from this environment; a live-hardware reproduction of the original segfault on real NVML/driver hardware. `main`'s own CI history shows unrelated PR-title-lint failures on unrelated pushes to this base, so a full green run isn't guaranteed to be blocked on this change specifically.

## Scope: 18 of 30 candidate files

Twelve were dropped after verification. The notable ones:

- **`compilation/patterns/residual_add_norm.py` and `compilation/utils.py` — `main` already has the fix.** `compilation/patterns/__init__.py:24` defines `_make_pattern_example_inputs` with the same Torch 2.13+ `_trace_args_for_initial_trace` rationale, and derives arity from `signature(search_fn)` rather than hardcoding dummies. Strictly better than the Rubin version; nothing to port.
- **Three of four candidate config fields were dropped**, each verified unbacked:
  - `uses_spcompress` would raise `TypeError` — `SkipSoftmaxParams` is a frozen dataclass whose only fields are `algorithm` and `scheduler`, on `main` *and* on the Rubin branch.
  - `use_lamport_sync` has no reader anywhere on either branch.
  - `enable_ugpu` has no consumer on either branch.

title: [None][feat] Helix speculative verify groups: fp8 + fp4 MLA and DSpark
body:
## Summary

Adds Helix support for **speculative verify groups** end to end — the per-token
kernel contract, the runtime that produces it, every attention backend that
consumes it, and the DSpark speculative-decoding path that selects it.

A verify group of `1 + draft_len` tokens can straddle a ledger-page boundary, so
KV ownership *within one group* splits across two CP ranks. The existing
per-sequence `helix_is_inactive_rank` gate cannot express that — it is
all-or-nothing for the whole group.

Merge-back of MRs !10550 (dspark + helix), !10593 (fp8 adaptation),
!10634 (helix + fp4 KV) and !10652 (fp4+helix accuracy fix).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Stacked on #19070** (FP4 MLA attention backend). GitHub cannot express a
> cross-fork stack, so this targets `main` and its diff currently *includes*
> #19070's commit. Review only the five `mb-helix` commits on top; merge #19070
> first and this collapses to just those.
>
> Scope split: **#19070 = the FP4 MLA backend. This PR = all Helix work**
> (fp8 + fp4 + DSpark), including the Helix-conditional changes to the fp4 files.

Supersedes the closed #18166, which implemented the same per-token primitive
against pre-relocation paths and covered only the bf16/fp16 CuTe DSL decode
path. The C++ here is character-identical to it.

## Commits

| Commit | Scope |
|---|---|
| `a3b6ac18` | C++ kernels: `helix_local_slots`, fifo-v2 sanitize |
| `c5f13ffa` | core runtime + FP4 MLA consumer |
| `c6705027` | CuTe DSL MLA decode — fp16 |
| `48dee57d` | CuTe DSL MLA decode — fp8 |
| `8c6bb9b8` | DSpark speculative decoding under Helix CP (Kimi K3) |

## What's here

**Kernel side (C++)** — `helix_local_slots`, a per-token rank-local KV write
slot plumbed through `mlaKernels.{cu,h}` and `thop/dsv3RopeOp.cpp`. `-1` means
another rank owns the token's global position. Non-null supersedes the
per-sequence gate *and* supplies the KV write index; null leaves every existing
path unchanged. The zero-KV sanitize moves into the fifo-v2 all-to-all sender,
where the entry is already streaming through shared memory.

**Runtime** — `TrtllmAttentionMetadata` gains `helix_local_slots` /
`helix_kv_bounds`, derived on device in `recompute_helix_spec_buffers` following
the round-robin page ledger (page `b` -> rank `b % cp_size`). `model_engine`
packs the group's global positions host-side and reports a per-sequence *count*
of owned new tokens, since with a split group ownership is a count, not a
boolean. Under the overlap scheduler the host packs from a stale base, so the
accepted-count correction already applied to `position_ids` is applied before
the recompute and mirrored back for capture symmetry.

**All three attention consumers**
- **FP4 MLA** — validation plus the `USE_HELIX`/`USE_HELIX_LOCAL_SLOTS`
  specializations in the Triton append kernel, and the mask in both CuteDSL
  MuFu16 variants, which now also emit the softmax row stats the combine needs.
- **CuTe DSL MLA decode, fp16 and fp8** — per-token `kv_bounds` replaces the
  implicit causal bound `K - (S_q - 1) + q_tok` in both masked-phase branches,
  the masked span widens by one, `fold_sq` padding rows are clamped so their
  discarded results still read in range, and tokens with no local KV emit the
  `(-inf, 0)` softmax identity so the cross-rank combine stays exact.

**DSpark** — the K3 helix speculative allowlist admits standalone DSpark linear
chains and raises loudly on anything else. The draft model runs on the CP-free
repurposed mapping (the helix ledger governs only the target KV), and the
KV-cache cost model follows: draft slopes are scaled by `cp_size` because a
draft token is priced against a rank-local target token, while intercepts are
per-request rank-local bytes and stay unscaled.

## Bug fixed along the way

`MLA` now derives its zero-KV mask from the per-token bounds when they are
valid. A rank holding only a group's tail page has **zero** visible KV for the
group's leading tokens while its per-sequence `kv_len` is nonzero — the
per-sequence mask missed exactly those rows, so their decode rows were fully
masked and the combine could multiply an uninitialized partial by a zero
correction.

`FallbackFmha` rejects verify groups outright: the fused thop path's spec-dec
mask and per-sequence gate both assume the new KV entries are the trailing slots
of one rank's `kv_len`. Being last in the library list, this makes dispatch
raise rather than run silently wrong.

## Deliberately excluded

- **fp8 tensor-valued softmax/output scales.** An unrelated ABI change that sits
  beside the fp8 helix work on the source branch. main's `cutlass.Float32`
  scalars and the `softmax_scale_log2` precompute are kept; the `kv_bounds`
  masking is independent of both.
- **The SM107 arch widening**, which is interleaved with the helix hunks in both
  decode kernels and carries `{$nv-internal-release}` markers. It belongs to the
  kernels PR (#19184); arch gates here are byte-identical to base.

## Test status

Static verification only: the helix C++ is byte-identical to the source branch,
kernel/runner argument order lines up across fp8 and fp16, every file parses,
lint/format hooks pass, and each helix symbol has both a producer and a consumer.

**Not yet built or run.** `test_helix_postprocess.py` and `test_mla_helix.py`
need a GPU run, and the fp8/fp16 CuteDSL masking is untested kernel logic — that
is the gate before this leaves draft.

## Summary

Text-only follow-up to the SM107 (Rubin) bring-up. Docs, developer guides, code comments and error strings still said "SM100/SM103" for paths whose actual gates (`is_sm_100f` = `100 <= sm < 110`, `isSM100Family()`, trtllm-gen `ARCHS 100 103 107 100f`, `_MLA_*_SUPPORTED_SM_VERSIONS`) already accept SM107. Every changed line was traced to its gate and, for TRTLLM-Gen MoE, to the exported cubin table.

Main edits:
- **One code fix (review finding):** `TrtllmTrtllmGenW4a8Nvfp4Fp8Impl.can_implement` now rejects SM107 (`SM_UNSUPPORTED`). The batchedGemm export ships E2m1-weight x E4m3-activation kernels only as `sm_100a`/`sm_103a` cubins (no `sm_100f`/`sm_107a`), so the family-wide `is_sm_100f` gate let SM107 through to a "No kernel found" at runner construction. Unit test added in `test_moe_impl.py`.
- `MOE_DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md`: TRTLLMGen / DeepGemm / MegaMoE-DeepGemm cells and backend table add SM107. Cutlass and DenseGEMM cells unchanged (their Python gates exclude SM107).
- `docs/source/features/quantization.md`: `Rubin(sm107)` row (Y everywhere except NVFP4 KV cache, which is forced to FP8 on SM107).
- `supported-models.md` footnotes, DeepSeek-V3/V4 READMEs, `sparse-attention.md` Sparse MLA row, NVFP4 cold-page docs: add SM107.
- Comments/strings in `fp8Quantize.cpp`, `mxfp8Gemm.cpp`, `allReduceFusionKernels.cu`, `cutlass_heuristic.cpp`, `gemm_configs.h`, `attnResFwd.h`, and a few Python files whose predicates already admit SM107.

Left as SM100/SM103 on purpose: everything gated `(100, 103)` in code (Cutlass MoE quant table, DenseGEMM, CuTe DSL NVFP4 dense runners, PrimTS, FlashInfer trtllm-gen FMHA/DFlash, NVFP4 KV cache, FP8 LoRA grouped GEMM) and paths backed by external kernels not verifiable in-tree (MiniMax-M3 MSA, TriAttention).

Reviewer note: MegaMoE-DeepGemm and TRTLLM-Gen BF16 cells follow TRT-LLM's `is_sm_100f` gate; SM107 coverage of the underlying DeepGEMM / FlashInfer kernels was not verified in-tree. `llm_args.py` is touched only in a field description string.

- New `test_w4a8_nvfp4_fp8_leaf_is_pinned_to_its_arch_specific_cubins` (SM100/103 eligible, SM107 rejected) in `tests/unittest/_torch/moe/test_moe_impl.py`; everything else is text-only.

title: [None][fix] Keep the family suffix for 10x architectures in DeepEP
body:
## Description

`cpp/tensorrt_llm/deep_ep/CMakeLists.txt` classifies each entry of `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` and re-emits it for DeepEP. The comment directly above the branch states the requirement:

```cmake
# The FP4-related conversion instructions in DeepEP require SM100a, SM110a,
# or SM120a.
if(${CUDA_ARCH_MAJOR} EQUAL 10 AND ${CUDA_ARCH_MINOR} EQUAL 0)
```

The first branch requires `CUDA_ARCH_MINOR EQUAL 0`, so it only matches `100`. The `elseif` also requires `CUDA_ARCH_MINOR EQUAL 0`, so it only matches `110`, `120`, and later `x00` architectures. Every other member of the 10x family therefore falls through to the final `else` branch and is emitted with no suffix at all.

The regex does not capture the suffix either — `[af]?` sits outside the capture groups — so an incoming `103a-real` or `107f-real` loses its suffix on the way through.

Observed with an unmodified checkout of `main` (a76e0b2b):

| `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` entry | emitted for DeepEP | |
|---|---|---|
| `90a-real`  | `90-real`   | |
| `100f-real` | `100f-real` | matches the comment |
| `103a-real` | `103-real`  | suffix dropped |
| `107f-real` | `107-real`  | suffix dropped |
| `110f-real` | `110a-real` | matches the comment |
| `120f-real` | `120a-real` | matches the comment |

`103` and `107` are the two 10x architectures currently reachable through `cuda_configuration.cmake`, and both end up with a bare target while their siblings do not.

This PR drops the `CUDA_ARCH_MINOR EQUAL 0` condition from the first branch so that the whole 10x major is routed to the existing `100` handling. That matches the stated intent in #17336 that `100f` kernels are meant to cover the whole `10x` family:

> we want `100f` kernels to cover the whole `10x` architectures to reduce build time and binary size

Only `103` and `107` change. `90`, `100`, `110` and `120` are unaffected.

Note on older CMake: when `CMAKE_VERSION < 3.31` the existing fallback emits `100a` and `103a` because family targets cannot be expressed there. That limitation is unchanged by this PR; `107` simply follows the same path `100` already takes instead of getting a bare target.

## Test Coverage

The branch logic was extracted verbatim into a standalone script and executed with `cmake -P` against both the current and the proposed condition, over the architecture strings `cuda_configuration.cmake` can produce. The table above is that output; with the change, `103a-real` and `107f-real` produce the same result as `100f-real`, and every other input is byte-identical to current behavior.

A full `build_wheel.py` configure with `-a "90-real;100-real;103-real;107-real"` was also run on the unmodified tree to capture the current `deep_ep DEEP_EP_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES:` line, which is what surfaced the bare `107-real` entry.

I do not have Rubin hardware, so this PR makes no claim about runtime performance on SM107. It only restores the suffix that the surrounding comment requires.

## PR Checklist

- [x] The PR title follows the required format.
- [x] The change is limited to a single file and a single condition.
- [x] The commit is signed off (DCO).
- [ ] Requires a maintainer to confirm the intended handling for `103`, which currently also receives a bare target.

Related: #19069 (closed — that approach was wrong, and the reason is written up there), #17336 (original SM107 recognition).

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

`cpp/tensorrt_llm/deep_ep/CMakeLists.txt` now routes all CUDA major-version `10` architectures through SM100-family handling. This fixes suffix handling for architectures such as `103a-real` and `107f-real`. Architectures `90`, `110`, and `120` retain their existing paths. The change affects DeepEP and NVSHMEM CUDA architecture configuration only. No API, runtime, or performance changes are introduced.

body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

`flash_attn4.py` sets `FA_DISABLE_2CTA=1` by default before importing Flash Attention. An explicit `FA_DISABLE_2CTA=0` preserves the option to re-enable 2CTA. Review finding counts are unavailable.

## QA Engineer Review

No test changes.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/visual_gen/attention_backend/flash_attn4.py`: Verify the default 2CTA disablement and preservation of explicit environment values. Verify FA4 correctness and long-sequence performance.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!--
Please write the PR title by following this template:

**[JIRA ticket/NVBugs ID/GitHub issue/None][type] Summary**

Valid ticket formats:
  - JIRA ticket: [TRTLLM-1234] or [FOOBAR-123] for other FOOBAR project
  - NVBugs ID: [https://nvbugs/1234567]

Valid types (lowercase): [fix], [feat], [doc], [infra], [chore], etc.

Examples:

**[JIRA ticket/NVBugs ID/GitHub issue/None] @coderabbitai title**

NOTE: "@coderabbitai title" will be replaced by the title generated by CodeRabbit AI, that includes the "[type]" and title.
For more info, see /.coderabbit.yaml.

-->

## Description

<!--
Please explain the issue and the solution in short.
-->
FA4's 2CTA forward path is enabled by default and regresses performance on long attention sequences, up to +35% on Wan2.2-T2V. The regression scales with sequence length and is present across all VisualGen models tested (Wan2.2-T2V, Qwen-Image, LTX-2, FLUX.2). No test showed 2CTA-enabled outperforming 2CTA-disabled.

Fix: `flash_attn4.py` now defaults `FA_DISABLE_2CTA=1` before the FA4 import (the upstream `flash-attn-4` package reads this env var once, at import time). `FA_DISABLE_2CTA=0` remains available as an explicit opt-back-in.

An alternative is upgrading to [`flash-attn-4==4.0.0b31`](https://pypi.org/project/flash-attn-4/4.0.0b31/), which includes an [upstream register-allocation fix](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2869) that eliminates register spills in the affected 2CTA kernel, allowing default CTA selection without this workaround.

However, b31 requires `quack-kernels>=0.5.3`. Combined with this repository's CUTLASS DSL 4.8 pin, the evaluated upgrade path uses [`quack-kernels==0.6.5`](https://pypi.org/project/quack-kernels/0.6.5/). That version removes `quack.activation.sub_packed_f32x2`, which the packaged MiniMax-M3 `fmha_sm100` softmax implementation still calls. The package upgrade therefore also needs an MSA compatibility fix or dependency update, plus validation of MiniMax-M3, VisualGen, distributed attention, and DFlash.

This PR retains the smaller workaround supported by the measured workloads. The dependency upgrade can follow separately once the complete package combination is validated. Disabling 2CTA may sacrifice performance on workloads outside the tested set where 2CTA is beneficial.

Full findings, methodology, and before/after validation can be found [here](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.ostoner_coreai_1/TensorRT-LLM-2/TensorRT-LLM/examples/visual_gen/fa4_2cta_benchmark/FA4_2CTA_SUMMARY.html). 

## Test Coverage

<!--
Please list clearly what are the relevant test(s) that can safeguard the changes in the PR. This helps us to ensure we have sufficient test coverage for the PR.
-->
This changes which FA4 kernel runs, so existing correctness tests should verify numerical agreement within tolerance, alongside performance tests to check for regressions. Both are included in l0_b200.yml:
- `tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_attention_fa4.py`
- `tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_attention_perf.py`

Also validated manually end-to-end (Wan2.2-T2V, 480×832×165): patched default now runs at 7.91s/step vs. 10.58–10.62s/step before the fix.

title: [None][doc] Make the PR title examples pass the PR title check
body:
### Problem

Every entry under "Good PR Titles Examples" in `CONTRIBUTING.md` is rejected by the check that gates PRs.

`Check PR Title Format` in `.github/workflows/pr-check.yml` requires:

```
^(\[(None|[A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+|#[0-9]+|https:\/\/nvbugs\/[0-9]+)\]) *(\[[a-z0-9]+\]) (([^ ].*)?[^ ])$
```

that is `[ticket][type] Summary`. The documented examples use a Conventional Commits prefix instead. Run against that regex:

| documented example | result |
| --- | --- |
| `feat: Add support for starcoder-v2 FP8 base + FP16/BF16 LoRA` | rejected |
| `BREAKING CHANGE: Set default max batch size to 2048` | rejected |
| `chore: Remove version from plugins .so` | rejected |
| `None: Stringized enums for better error msgs` | rejected |
| `fix https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/issues/700: a Memory leak issue in C++ runtime` | rejected |
| `[TRTLLM-5516] perf: replicate dummy request for cuda graph padding` | rejected |
| `[nvbug/5334370] fix: Fix one model EAGLE3` | rejected |

Seven for seven. The four examples the workflow prints in its own failure message all pass, so the check and the guide disagree and the check is the one that decides.

I hit this from the outside: I titled five PRs after the fifth row above, because linking the issue by URL is what the file shows. The GitHub-issue form is probably the costliest one to get wrong, since a URL looks plausible where `[#1234]` is what passes.

### Change

`CONTRIBUTING.md` only. The section now states the required shape, lists the four ticket kinds the regex accepts, names the lowercase type, and gives examples that pass.

BREAKING CHANGE stays. It moves into the summary, which is where the check leaves room for it.

### Verification

Every example in the new section was run against the regex from the workflow:

```
[TRTLLM-1234][feat] Add support for starcoder-v2 FP8 base + FP16/BF16 LoRA   pass
[https://nvbugs/1234567][fix] Fix one model EAGLE3                           pass
[#1234][fix] Fix a memory leak in the C++ runtime                            pass
[#1234][doc] Update documentation                                            pass
[None][chore] Remove version from plugins .so                                pass
[None][feat] BREAKING CHANGE: Set default max batch size to 2048             pass
```

### What I did not do

I did not touch the regex. Whether the guide or the check is the one that should move is yours to decide; I assumed the check, since it is what runs on every PR and the workflow already documents this format in its failure output. If the intent is the other way round and Conventional Commits titles should be accepted, then this PR is the wrong half of the fix and I am happy to close it.

### What the replacement removes

Called out so it is not a surprise in the diff. The old paragraph carried two things that did not survive:

- the link to [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/). The title format the check enforces is not Conventional Commits, so the reference pointed at the wrong spec.
- the sentence "if the PR is not related to any bug and task, consider using `chore` or None as the placeholder". The ticket table covers that case directly: `[None]` is the no-ticket entry, and `chore` is a type, not a ticket. Keeping both spellings of the same advice is what made the old text ambiguous.

Neither is a behaviour change; both are text the new section states more precisely.

### Review round (brnguyen2)

- The type list read as a closed set of eight. The regex is `(\[[a-z0-9]+\])`, so any lowercase word passes, and the workflow's own failure message (`pr-check.yml:48`) ends its list with "etc.". Added `[ci]` and "for example", per the suggestion. Counting the 1162 most recent commit titles on `main` I see `ci` 23 times, and also `unwaive`, `baseline`, `tests` and `docs` once or twice each, which is the open set showing through.
- Both `[!IMPORTANT]` lines now sit inside blockquotes so GitHub renders them as callouts. The review flagged the one next to my change; the same break exists further down in a section I had not touched, and I fixed that one too rather than leave the file half-corrected. Say the word and I will drop it back out.

title: [https://nvbugs/6708299][fix] Support group_size=32 for W4A16_NVFP4 and validate NVFP4 group sizes
body:
## Description

ModelOpt's Qwen3.5-27B `nvfp4_mlp_weight_only` checkpoint declares 32-element scale groups. The loader assumed 16 and allocated twice as many scales, failing with 5,570,560 versus 2,785,280 elements (NVBug 6708299).

Support 16/32-element groups in dense W4A16_NVFP4 Linear allocation, checkpoint loading, ROW-TP sharding, and Triton dequantization. W4A4 and Marlin remain 16-only. The shared width resolver now lives in `quantization/utils/fp4_utils.py`: omitted/None widths resolve to 16, while explicit unsupported values, including 128, are consistently rejected by ModelOpt parsing and Linear construction. The implicit AWQ/GPTQ default remains compatible without silently accepting an explicitly declared 128.

Review follow-up:
- Restrict the MoE guard to NVFP4/NVFP4_ARC/W4A16_NVFP4. Preserve W4A8_NVFP4_FP8's backend-fixed 32-element allocation, fixing the four B200 failures from CI run 60308.
- Reject 32-element W4A16 expert entries during ModelOpt parsing and Qwen normalization before backend selection/promotion. The reported 27B checkpoint is dense and has no MoE experts; this PR does not add 32-element W4A16 MoE support. Rename the supported-width constant to explicitly identify dense Linear support.
- Send 32-element Qwen LM heads through the existing load-time bf16 dequantization fallback, avoiding full LM-head dequantization on every decode step. Native 16-element quantized LM-head paths remain enabled.
- Keep direct quant_config access and repair the older Marlin test fixtures to match real Linear modules.
- Mark hardware-independent cases cpu_only. The CPU list already covers the MoE, modules, and modeling directories; the linear file is already listed for H100/GB10 GPU coverage. Remove explicit H100 entries for the two Qwen tests now covered by CPU CI.

## Test Coverage

Validated from an isolated checkout/container on one B200, using PyTorch 2.14.0a0 (DLFW 26.08) with compatible 1.3.0rc26 native binaries:

- **109 passed** across `test_hf_quant_config.py`, `test_w4a16_nvfp4_linear.py`, `test_nvfp4_moe_block_width.py`, and `test_modeling_qwen3_5_vl.py` (`-k "not test_all"`). Includes actual 16/32-group GPU dequantization, ROW-TP scale sharding, and Qwen construction/weight-loading smoke coverage.
- **54 passed** with CUDA hidden and `-m cpu_only`, confirming the CPU markers and registration work without a visible GPU.

title: [None][perf] Avoid prefix probes when the KV cache v2 context chunk budget is insufficient
body:
## Description

With chunked prefill and prefix-aware scheduling enabled, the KV cache v2 scheduler probes pending context requests even when the remaining token budget guarantees that their admission will be skipped. Long prefixes and many pending requests can make these unnecessary probes expensive.

Check the existing chunk-budget eligibility predicate before the per-request prefix probe, and share that predicate with chunked admission. Continue scanning so encoder requests can still schedule. Preserve unlimited-budget behavior, the minimum chunk-unit requirement for FCFS, and positive sub-unit budgets for FORCE_CHUNK. Nonchunked admission is unchanged.

An internal benchmark measured approximately 12% higher token throughput with this change on the evaluated workload.

## Test Coverage

Add nine synthetic CPU test cases in `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_v2_scheduler.py`, covering:

- Exhausted and sub-unit budgets after a context chunk: one prefix probe instead of twenty.
- Generation consuming the entire budget before context admission.
- Encoder admission despite insufficient context chunk budget.
- FORCE_CHUNK admission at a snapshot boundary shorter than the chunk unit.
- Unlimited budgets under both chunking policies.
- A budget-only skip preserving an existing context claim and cursor without probing, preparing, freeing, or suspending it.

The existing `unittest/_torch/executor` entry in `l0_cpu.yml` includes this CPU-marked test file.

Validation on the proposed upstream patch:

- Ruff lint and formatting, Python syntax, and diff whitespace checks passed.
- The extracted budget predicate matched the previous inline logic across 2,088 combinations of remaining budget, chunk unit, and policy.
- The scheduler suite could not collect locally because PyTorch is unavailable. Run `python3 -m pytest tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_v2_scheduler.py -q` in a configured TensorRT-LLM environment before submission.
- Prior internal validation: the original six regression cases failed before the fix and the patched scheduler suite passed 226 tests. Those results do not validate this public-main checkout or the three additional cases.

title: [#18609][fix] Do not require encoder tokens for cross prefix reuse
body:
Fixes #18609.

### Problem

Every generation request against `openai/whisper-large-v3` on the PyTorch backend dies in the C++ capacity scheduler, before the forward pass:

```
File ".../scheduler/scheduler.py", line 462, in schedule_request
    return self.impl(
RuntimeError: bad optional access
```

`capacityScheduler.cpp` dereferences the encoder unique tokens at three places, guarded only by the presence of a cross KV cache manager with block reuse on:

```cpp
auto uniqueTokens = *(req->getEncoderUniqueTokens().value());
```

None of the three checks whether the optional holds anything.

### Why it is empty

`mEncoderUniqueTokens` is derived from encoder **tokens** alone (`llmRequest.h:2272`):

```cpp
if (mEncoderTokens.has_value() && mEncoderTokens.value())
{
    ...
    mEncoderUniqueTokens = encoderUniqueTokens;
}
```

Whisper's encoder input is features, not tokens: `modeling_whisper.py:788` passes `"encoder_input_features"`, and `llm_request.py:928-934` leaves `encoder_input_tokens` as `None`. So the optional is never populated.

`enable_block_reuse` defaults to `True` (`llm_args.py:4106`), and an encoder-decoder run must set `cross_kv_cache_fraction`, which is what creates the cross manager. Both guard conditions therefore hold on a default run, which is why the reporter saw it on every request. It is not architecture-specific; the reporter's SM120 box is not what selects this path.

### Change

Add the missing condition at each of the three sites.

Prefix reuse matches on token prefixes, so a features-based encoder has nothing for `analyzePrefixReuse` to walk. Leaving `crossSummary` unset is the state its two consumers already handle:

```cpp
// oneManagerBeneficialToSkip
return summary.has_value() && summary->firstNewBlock.has_value() && ...

// registerContributedBlocks
if (crossSummary.has_value() && crossSummary->firstNewBlock.has_value()) { ... }
```

and it is the state they already see whenever there is no cross manager, block reuse is off, or the manager is variable-window.

The same header already distinguishes the two shapes of encoder input, which is what made the token-only assumption visible (`llmRequest.h:663`):

```cpp
/// @return Encoder input length, or nullopt when this request has no encoder side.
[[nodiscard]] std::optional<SizeType32> tryGetEncoderInputLen() const
{
    if (mEncoderInputFeatures.has_value()) { ... }
    if (getEncoderTokens().has_value())    { ... }
    return std::nullopt;
}
```

### Verification

- `clang-format` 16.0.0, the version pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, reports no diff on the file.
- `grep` finds three dereferences of `getEncoderUniqueTokens().value()` in this file; all three now sit behind `has_value()`.

### What I have not done

I did not reproduce the failure or run this patch myself. I have no SM120 GPU and no Whisper setup; the analysis is from reading `main`, and the reporter's trace is what located it.

**Since writing that, @ravo42-maker has run it.** They applied this hunk onto the `v1.3.0rc25` tag (785c948, where all three sites are identical), built a wheel for `120-real`, and ran `openai/whisper-large-v3` on an RTX 5070 Ti. With `max_input_len=1500` and block reuse left on, stock rc25 raises `bad optional access` and rc25 + this change transcribes the clip in 3.95 s. Their five-run table isolates block reuse as the only variable between the crash and a working run. See the comment below; the verification is theirs, not mine.

I also have not added a regression test. The natural one is a capacity-scheduler unit test with a request carrying encoder input features and no encoder tokens, with a cross manager and block reuse enabled. I would rather add it in the shape this repository prefers than guess, so please say if you want it here.

### Note beyond this fix

The reporter lists four further gaps in the same issue: no `/v1/audio/transcriptions` route, no Whisper chat template shipped, no Whisper example or test in the container, and no release that currently provides a working Whisper path. This change addresses only the scheduler crash.

title: [None][feat] Support attention DP in V2 KV cache connectors
body:
Extend the V2 KV Cache Connector to support attention data parallelism (ADP).

The existing implementation assumes attention tensor parallelism (TP), where all ranks process the same requests and maintain corresponding prefix-cache state. Rank 0 runs the connector scheduler and broadcasts its decisions, while each rank’s worker transfers its local KV-cache shards.

With ADP, ranks process different requests and maintain independent prefix trees, so request-level coordination through a single scheduler no longer applies. This PR gives each ADP rank its own connector scheduler adapter and worker. Request metadata, allocation feedback, and transfer completion remain local to the owning rank, while adapters can share a common external cache pool.

For more info, see /.coderabbit.yaml.

## Description

Gemma4Attention registers itself into the inner ModelConfig.extra_attrs that is passed to Gemma4ForCausalLM, but PyTorchModelEngine.model_forward publishes the outer wrapper's model_config.extra_attrs to the thread-local before running the model. The two are different objects, so attn_layers never reaches the thread-local and extract_extra_attrs asserts "Attention layer is not registered".

Eager execution is unaffected because the custom inplace attention op is gated on is_torch_compiling() or is_in_breakable_cuda_graph(), so the lookup only runs under CUDA graph capture. The visible symptom is that both prefill_cuda_graph_backend=piecewise and =breakable fail to initialize on Gemma4.

Propagating the inner config's extra_attrs to the outer one after the decoder is constructed fixes both paths.

Measured on gemma-4-E4B-it (BF16, TP1, 1x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, SM120) with prefill_cuda_graph_backend=breakable, ISL 25 / OSL 5:

  concurrency 1: TTFT 48.3 -> 14.5 ms, request latency 83.0 -> 50.5 ms,
                 throughput 11.9 -> 19.4 req/s
  concurrency 4: TTFT 93.3 -> 23.2 ms, request latency 129.8 -> 61.3 ms,

title: [TRTLLMINF-336][infra] Enable BOLT postmerge consume
body:
Pass boltPublishCanonical=true from the postmerge pipeline's BOLT-Profile-Gen launch, so the tarball that run re-BOLTs is pushed back to its artifactPath under the canonical name and the un-BOLTed original is preserved as unbolted-<tarball>. Canonical now means BOLTed for the postmerge build, matching what premerge consume already does to the premerge build (Build.groovy's applyLatestBolt) and what the overlay does to published images.

The scaffolding landed in 0beff32139 with the toggle off. publishBoltedCanonical, the unbolted- snapshot, the idempotent re-run handling, and the boltPublishCanonical parameter are all already in place, so this only changes the answer to "should this run republish a canonical".

The helper still requires applyProfiles=true and promote=true, both of which only the postmerge launch sets: an on-demand or premerge generate-and-consume run (promote=false) publishes nothing even with the toggle on. applyProfiles is passed explicitly here rather than left to its default, since publishing silently does nothing without the merge job's BOLT_APPLY=1 step.

In-run effect: the SBSA test stages sequenced after BOLT-Profile-Gen pull the canonical tarball from this same artifactPath, so postmerge tests now exercise the BOLTed build -- test coverage on the very bundle the run promotes for premerge to consume. Scoped to aarch64/SBSA, the only triple the producer profiles; TensorRT-LLM.tar.gz is untouched. The stage stays best-effort under the existing catchError(buildResult: 'SUCCESS'), so a failed publish leaves the canonical un-BOLTed instead of failing postmerge.

Also reports the previously silent skip when the toggle is on but a precondition is unmet, a path only reachable once postmerge sets it.

Rollback: drop boltPublishCanonical from the launch, or set the job parameter to false. Already-published canonicals are recoverable from unbolted-<tarball>.

- `tests/unittest/inputs/test_async_media_loading.py`: `TestDataUriMimeCheck` covers data-URI MIME validation for all three modalities. Integration test-list registration is not applicable.
- `tests/unittest/inputs/test_url_validation.py`: Covers private-URL policy, redirects, multicast addresses, unsupported schemes, and pre-request rejection. Integration test-list registration is not applicable.
- `tests/integration/test_lists/waives.txt`: Waives `unittest/usage/test_llmapi_config_telemetry_docs.py::test_build_capture_manifest_matches_committed_golden` for NVIDIA bug 6811958.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Two small hardening fixes for multimodal media input handling:

1. **Reject data URIs whose declared MIME type mismatches the content part modality.** A data URI in an `image_url` (or audio/video) content part was decoded even when its declared media type said something else entirely (`text/plain`, `application/pdf`, ...): the per-modality loaders sniffed the payload bytes and ignored the declared type. Silently decoding mislabeled payloads hides client bugs and diverges from reference OpenAI-compatible servers, which return 400. Now each media IO class declares its expected MIME prefix (`image/`, `audio/`, `video/`) and `BaseMediaIO.async_load` validates the declared type before dispatching to `load_base64`. Data URIs that omit the media type are still accepted for backward compatibility.

2. **`TRTLLM_MEDIA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=1` opt-in for media URLs resolving to private addresses.** Media URL validation requires resolved IPs to be global, so every internal or loopback http(s) media URL is rejected with no opt-out. That is the right SSRF default for internet-facing servers, but it blocks legitimate airgapped and intranet deployments, forcing `file://` workarounds. The new env var skips only the non-global-address rejection; default OFF, so the SSRF posture is unchanged unless the operator sets it. Scheme, hostname, and multicast checks still apply, the opt-in covers redirect hops through the same validator, and enabling it logs a one-time warning. The rejection message now names the variable so operators can find the switch.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/inputs/test_async_media_loading.py`: data-URI MIME reject/accept/missing-MIME cases for image, audio, and video.
- `tests/unittest/inputs/test_url_validation.py`: the opt-in admits private/loopback/link-local/CGNAT addresses (including redirect targets); default and non-"1" values still reject; multicast and non-http(s) schemes rejected either way.

title: [None][fix] Share speculative capture buffers across CUDA graph buckets
body:
## Description

`DFlashSpecMetadata`/`DSparkSpecMetadata` allocate a hidden-state capture buffer sized for the full token budget (`max_num_tokens x hidden_size * num_capture_layers`). `create_cuda_graph_metadata()` shallow-copies the metadata and re-runs `__post_init__` for every CUDA graph bucket, so each bucket allocated its own full-size buffer even though model forwards and their consumers are ordered on the same execution stream and never need more than one.

This change keeps the existing buffer when it is already compatible (same shape, dtype and device) and reallocates only on a real mismatch, so all graph buckets share one full-token-budget scratch buffer. Behavior is unchanged; per-bucket memory for the capture buffer drops to a single allocation.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/_torch/speculative/hw_agnostic/test_capture_buffer.py` (cpu_only): buckets share the parent buffer, incompatible buffers (rows/width/dtype/device/missing) are reallocated, no-capture configurations stay `None`.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/speculative/test_capture_buffer_cuda.py` (CUDA): graph capture/replay across alternating buckets writes through the shared buffer and replays correctly, including after the parent metadata is garbage-collected; multi-device allocation follows the current device.

title: [None][feat] Kimi K3: unlock the CUTEDSL MoE backend for NVFP4 SiTU
body:
## Description

Enable explicitly selected CUTEDSL routed experts for Kimi K3 NVFP4 on SM100/SM103. The Blackwell kernel already implements SiTU in the rebased main; this change enables it through the MoE capability declaration and K3 backend selection, forwards both soft-caps, and rejects an explicit CUTEDSL request that cannot be served instead of silently selecting CUTLASS.

The Blackwell custom op and fake schema use `Optional[float] = None` directly. SiTU constants must be finite and positive. SM107 end-to-end SiTU integration remains gated; existing Rubin ops retain their separate legacy sentinel API.

## Review coverage

- Compare the NVFP4 output with a SiTU reference and a **plain SwiGLU** negative reference, using dequantized checkpoint weights and a SiTU relative-L2 bound of **0.20**.
- Derive backend admission candidates from `BACKEND_FAMILY` and check exact agreement with the K3 allow-list.
- Exercise the real `KimiK3MoERuntime` / resolver call chain with CUTEDSL ineligible and CUTLASS eligible; require an explicit rejection, with an allowed-degradation positive control.
- At fixed outer/FC1 tactics, independently change each soft-cap across `(4,25)`, `(2,25)`, `(4,10)`, `(2,10)` and verify distinct runner identities and numerical outputs.
- Register the regressions in `l0_b300.yml`. Keep the numerical discriminator's CI selection focused on CUTEDSL as requested; retain the existing TRTLLM selector. Update the upstream Blackwell direct-op test to use `None` for absent SiTU parameters.

title: [None][feat] agent-flow: backend-independent tools and required-tool policy
body:
## Summary

Brings the Codex backend to parity with Claude Code in `agent-flow`, and moves the
pieces that both backends need out of the Claude-specific path.

### Backend-independent tools

Tool definition and MCP result conversion now live in a shared `agent_flow/tools.py`,
so both backends consume one definition format (`from agent_flow import tool`).
Python shorthand and `TypedDict` inputs normalize to JSON Schema. Resource links and
embedded text resources become readable tool output, image results retain their MIME
type, and unsupported result types return explicit tool errors rather than appearing
to succeed with missing output. Existing Claude SDK tool objects still work.

### Required-tool policy on either backend

Workflows previously stacked one Claude `Stop` hook per required tool to get AND
semantics. That is replaced by `AgentLayerConfig.required_tools`, which is
backend-agnostic:

```python
config = AgentLayerConfig(
    backend=BackendConfig(kind="codex", model=CODEX_DEFAULT_MODEL, tools=tools),
    required_tools=("append_reviewer_progress", "update_status"),
)
```

`AgentLayer` observes root-agent tool calls, sends **one** corrective turn on the same
session when calls are missing, and raises `RequiredToolCallError` if that bounded
correction still leaves them missing. Subagent calls and calls from prior invocations
do not discharge the requirement. The policy counts attempts, not successful writes —
tool handlers and workflow validation remain responsible for the outputs. Token
accounting sums both turns, while context occupancy stays the final snapshot rather
than being summed. `require_tool_call_stop_hook` remains available as a Claude-native
alternative for existing callers.

### Codex backend split

`backends/codex.py` is split into `codex_config.py`, `codex_events.py`, and
`codex_transport.py`:

- **config** — session options translate into `thread/start.config` and never edit the
  user's Codex configuration. Unsupported options fail at registration instead of being
  silently ignored, which matters most when they describe tool restrictions.
  `extra_mcp_servers` accepts Claude-style STDIO/HTTP form.
- **events** — the pinned app-server protocol maps onto the shared backend events,
  including subagent activity, structured rate limits, and cache-write tokens.
- **transport** — one isolated notification observer over the SDK's public process and
  request APIs, so descendant turns and account events reach the shared event stream.

Native hooks stay backend-specific: Claude accepts its SDK callbacks, while Codex
rejects per-client hook injection because that trust cannot be verified — configure
Codex hooks natively and prefer `required_tools` for workflow progress/status.

### Other changes

- Context-budget inspection no longer sends a `ping` bootstrap turn, so inspection
  never costs a model turn.
- `UsageInfo.estimated_thread_cost_usd` is reported separately from per-turn `cost_usd`
  and rendered in the console usage line.
- The Claude backend drops its unconditional `can_use_tool` approver; it already runs
  with `permission_mode="bypassPermissions"`.

Also included is the previously staged commit pinning `claude-agent-sdk` 0.2.152 and
`openai-codex` 0.154.0 — the adapters here target those pinned versions.

## Test Coverage

New: `tests/test_tools.py`, `tests/test_codex_config.py`, `tests/test_codex_events.py`,
`tests/test_codex_transport.py`, `tests/test_codex_backend.py` (the oversized
`test_backends.py` is split along the same seams), plus required-tool policy coverage in
`tests/test_agent_layer.py` and per-workflow tests.

```
$ python -m pytest tests -q
1300 passed, 3 skipped in 43.40s

$ pre-commit run --files <changed files>
all hooks passed
```

Transport tests run against the pinned SDK, so a future SDK bump that moves the
notification hook fails here rather than silently dropping child turns.

- [x] PR title follows `[JIRA/NVBUG/None][type] description`
- [x] Commits signed off (DCO)
- [x] Tests added for new functionality
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass

Scope note: all changes are confined to `agent-flow/`; no TensorRT-LLM runtime code is
touched.

title: [TRTLLMINF-381][fix] classify CI failures from originating step logs
body:
## Background

Jenkins shell-step exceptions often contain only an exit code while the actionable failure signature remains in the originating step console log. The shared libraries now expose policy-neutral originating-step evidence and map evidence query IDs back to the existing TRT-LLM failure catalog.

## Changes

- Collect originating-step evidence at Build and L0 classification boundaries.
- Reuse one evidence result within each retry attempt for result suppression and retry decisions.
- Propagate exhausted infrastructure failures as typed InfraFailure values so infra-scoped fail-fast can defer them without cancelling sibling stages.
- Preserve interruption and user-failure behavior, including SLURM/K8s scope isolation.
- Remove the temporary sbatch_output.txt readback path because sbatch output is already printed into the originating Jenkins step log.
- Preserve the primary stage failure when cleanup or result-upload handling also fails.

This also covers the SLURM bring-up classification gap described by TRTLLMINF-415: bring-up failures are classified at the outer SLURM retry boundary after resource cleanup, then propagated as typed infra failures when local retry is exhausted.

## Dependencies

- bloom-jenkins-shared-lib https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/TensorRT/Infrastructure/bloom-jenkins-shared-lib/-/merge_requests/2700
- trtllm-jenkins-shared-lib  https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/ftp/infra/trtllm-jenkins-shared-lib/-/merge_requests/106

Both shared-library changes are merged.

## Impact

No catalog patterns or retry budgets change. Only failures matching the existing scoped catalog, or failures already thrown as typed infra errors, are retried/deferred. Interruptions and unmatched/user failures continue to propagate as their original exceptions.

## Testing

Local checks:

- /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.12 tests/unittest/tools/test_infra_dry_run_pipeline.py (5 passed)
- pre-commit run --files jenkins/Build.groovy jenkins/L0_Test.groovy (passed)
- git diff --check (passed)

- Run the standard PR CI with /bot run.
- Run InfraDryRun=true to verify the successful K8s and SLURM dispatcher paths remain unchanged.
- Use Jenkins Replay or a temporary validation commit to make an originating shell step print a known scoped catalog signature and exit nonzero while its exception remains only script returned exit code N. Verify the matched signature drives the expected retry, intermediate JUnit is suppressed, exhausted infra propagates as typed InfraFailure, cleanup runs first, and sibling stages continue under infra-scoped fail-fast.
https://prod.blsm.nvidia.com/sw-tensorrt-llm-github-4/blue/organizations/jenkins/LLM%2Fmain%2FL0_Test-x86_64-Single-GPU/detail/L0_Test-x86_64-Single-GPU/2774/pipeline/

The normal InfraDryRun is a success-path regression check; targeted failure injection is required to exercise the new evidence-classification path.

title: [None][fix] route AutoDeploy logger severity mapping through _SEVERITY_TO_LEVEL

## Summary

title: [#19362][fix] Name the act fusion in the skip reason
body:
Addresses the second option in #19362.

### Problem

`test_cute_dsl_nvfp4` and `test_cute_dsl_nvfp4_4gpus` skip on anything other than SM 100 or 103 with:

```
CuTe DSL blockscaling mm supports SM 100 and 103 only
```

That reads as though CuTe DSL blockscaling matmul as a whole stops at SM 103. It no longer does: #18761 and #18765 added SM107 CuTe DSL dense GEMM and BMM ops, with their own `*_rubin` test files. What these two tests need and do not have is the NVFP4 GEMM with **fused SwiGLU**, which is gated separately in `cute_dsl_custom_ops.py`:

```
CuteDSL NVFP4 SwiGLU backend requires SM 100 (B200) or SM 103 (B300)
CuteDSL NVFP4 SwiGLU FP4Out requires SM 100 or SM 103
```

Someone reading the skip on an SM107 run is pointed at the wrong thing.

### Change

```diff
-            pytest.skip("CuTe DSL blockscaling mm supports SM 100 and 103 only")
+            pytest.skip(
+                "CuTe DSL NVFP4 GEMM+SwiGLU act fusion supports SM 100 and 103 only"
+            )
```

Two sites, the same string, no behaviour change: the same host states skip, for the same reason, with the reason stated accurately. Both docstrings already describe these tests as "GEMM+SwiGLU fusion for shared experts", so the message now agrees with them.

I kept the message self-describing rather than linking the issue, since the skips in this file reference `https://nvbugs/...` and not GitHub issue numbers.

### Verification

- `grep` finds exactly the two occurrences of the old string in the repository; both are changed.
- `yapf --style pyproject.toml -d` reports no diff on the file.
- The file byte-compiles.

### What this is not

This is the reporting half of #19362. Porting the NVFP4 SwiGLU and FP4Out act-fusion GEMMs to SM107 is the other option there, and it is not this change: #18761 and #18765 added roughly 4,400 lines of SM107-specific kernels and dispatch between them, so that work belongs with whoever owns those kernels. I have not touched any gate.
